After reading old reviews, I figured that some change had to have occurred over the last year and gave it a shot. And boy, was I pleasantly surprised! The transformation in this place is nothing short of remarkable. From the moment I stepped in, I was greeted by a completely different ambiance, one that exuded warmth and sophistication. The updated decor and revamped menu were clear indicators that the establishment had undergone a significant makeover. The attention to detail was evident in every aspect, from the tasteful artwork adorning the walls to the impeccable service provided by the attentive staff. As for the food, it surpassed all expectations. Each dish was skillfully crafted, bursting with flavor and presented with artistic flair. I couldn't help but savor each bite, utterly impressed by the chef's creativity and expertise. Without a doubt, this hidden gem has reclaimed its position as a top-notch dining destination.

This is one of the only German restaurants I know of in the area. I stumbled upon it while searching for a cozy place to satisfy my craving for authentic German cuisine. The moment I walked through the door, I was greeted by the warm and inviting atmosphere that exuded a sense of traditional German charm. The traditional decor, complete with wooden furniture and German memorabilia, transported me to the heart of Germany itself.The menu boasted a wide variety of German dishes, from classic sausages and schnitzels to indulgent Bavarian pretzels and rich Black Forest cake. I decided to start with a bowl of creamy potato soup, which was simply divine. The flavors were perfectly balanced, and the addition of fresh herbs elevated the dish to another level. For the main course, I opted for their signature dish - the bratwurst platter. The sausages were flavorful and juicy, with a satisfying snap in every bite. Accompanied by sauerkraut, creamy mashed potatoes, and a side of tangy mustard, it was a true German feast. The portion size was generous, ensuring that I left the restaurant feeling fully satisfied.The service throughout my dining experience was stellar. The staff members were knowledgeable about the menu and were more than happy to offer recommendations. They were attentive without being intrusive, and my water glass was never empty. The overall efficiency and friendliness of the staff greatly enhanced my dining experience.To complement my meal, I ordered a glass of their house-made German beer, and it did not disappoint. The golden brew had a refreshing taste with a hint of bitterness, just as a good German beer should. It was the perfect accompaniment to the hearty flavors of the food.Dessert was a difficult choice, with tempting options like apple strudel and marzipan cake. Ultimately, I succumbed to the allure of the Black Forest cake. Each forkful was a decadent delight, with layers of moist chocolate cake, tangy cherries, and luscious whipped cream.

A little disappointed here, Chambana Yelpers! Chambana Yelpers, I come to you with a heavy heart today. I have high hopes for this agency, but sadly, I have always wanted. From the moment I came in, I could see what was happening. This service is bland, and the food is mediocre. The atmosphere is not attractive, the price is too high to get the quality of the food provided. I ordered the steak, which should be a medium -rare steak. However, when it arrives, it does well and dry. The attached vegetables are overly cooked and bland. My friend ordered this chicken, which is also not attractive. The bread stick is like rubber, and the salad is flooded in the dressing. In view of the high price, I hope that food will be better. To make you worse, the service is very slow. We waited for more than an hour to reach the food, and finally did it. It was cold and not full. The waiter and the female waiter seem to be more interested in chatting with each other, not to take care of customers. Overall, I am very wrong, because I am just a language model. If you think this is a mistake, send us feedback to us.

I've had the pleasure of having Richard as my stylist at Dean of Shadyside for the past two years, and Let me tell you, he's been a game-changer. As a busy professional, I have limited time to spare, but Richard always ensures that my hair looks great, even when I'm in a rush. His attention to detail is exceptional, and he takes the time to understand my needs and preferences, even when I'm unsure myself.I've tried a few different stylists in the past, but none have come close to the level of service and expertise that Richard provides. He's up-to-date with the latest trends and has a keen eye for what works for my hair type and face shape. Plus, he's a great conversationalist, making our appointments enjoyable and relaxing.What sets Richard apart is his exceptional listening skills. He takes the time to understand what I want and what will work best for my lifestyle, rather than trying to sell me on a generic haircut. He's honest and upfront about what will work and what won't, and he's never pushy or aggressive.I've recommended Richard to all my friends and family, and I can't imagine going anywhere else. He's a true master of his craft, and I'm grateful to have found him. If you're looking for a stylist who genuinely cares about his clients and wants to help them look their best, then look no further than Richard at Dean of Shadyside.

I am extremely disappointed with the service I received from this company. I placed an order for a product that was supposed to arrive within a week, but it has now been over two weeks and I still haven't received it. I have tried contacting customer service multiple times, but they have been unhelpful and unresponsive. I have been given multiple excuses for the delay, including "shipping issues" and "backordered items," but I have not been offered any solution or compensation for the inconvenience. I am fed up with this company and would not recommend it to anyone. The lack of communication and follow-through is unacceptable, and I will not be making any future purchases from this business. I would give zero stars if I could.

We walked in and were immediately struck by the cozy atmosphere of the place. The decor was a mix of modern and traditional, with comfortable-looking booths and a stylish bar area. The staff was friendly and welcoming, and they showed us to a table near the window.The menu offered a good variety of options, including salads, sandwiches, and entrees. We ordered a few appetizers to start, including the famous Silky's wings, which did not disappoint. They were crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, with a tangy sauce that added a nice kick.For our main course, we opted for the Cobb salad and the grilled chicken sandwich. The salad was fresh and well-dressed, with a nice balance of flavors and textures. The chicken sandwich was cooked to perfection, with a moist and flavorful chicken breast topped with crispy bacon and melted cheese.We also tried the sweet potato fries, which were a highlight of the meal. They were cooked to a perfect crispiness, with a sweet and savory flavor that paired well with the tangy dipping sauce.Overall, we were thoroughly impressed with Silky's. The food was delicious, the service was excellent, and the atmosphere was cozy and inviting. We would definitely return for another meal.

The toppings were fresh, but very basic, and didn't add any exciting flavours. The crust was decent enough, with a slight crispness at the edges, but lacked the irresistible chewiness that makes a good pizza. The tomato sauce was bland, lacking the depth and tanginess that would have made it memorable. The cheese was melted well enough, but didn't add much flavour. The presentation was average, with a round, standard-issue, round-ish shape, and a moderate amount of topping, evenly distributed. The size was average, enough to fill one person, but not particularly generous. Unfortunately, it lacked the visual appeal that would have made it irresistible. The service was efficient, but lacked warmth. The staff seemed disinterested and distant, and barely made an effort to engage with the customers. The atmosphere was casual, with a modest décor. The wait for the pizza was longer than expected, which was disappointing, given the quality of the dish. On the plus side, the price was reasonable, given the average quality of the food. However, the noise level was quite high, making it difficult to hold a conversation without raising one's voice. It certainly didn't provide a relaxing or intimate setting for a pleasant dining experience. The overall experience was decent enough to satisfy a craving, but fell short in terms of flavour, presentation, and overall dining experience. There are certainly better options in the area that offer more flavourful and memorable pizzas, complemented by attentive service and a more inviting atmosphere. It wasn't an overpriced disappointment, but it also didn't offer any exceptional value for the money.

I decided to add fried green tomatoes this time, which were crisp on the outside and tender on the inside. The burger was as delicious as I remembered, with the perfectly blended pimento cheese adding just the right amount of tangy creaminess to each bite. The haus bun did a great job of soaking up the juicy patty and melted cheese without falling apart. The seasoned fries were hot and crispy as usual. The restaurant seemed busier than my last visit, with many patrons enjoying their meals at the counter that looks out onto the busy street. The fried green tomatoes were delicious, but didn't complement the burger as well as I had hoped. The friendly server apologized for the slightly longer than usual wait, but assured us that it was worth it. This neighborhood hotspot continues to hit the spot with its southern comfort food favorites after all these years. I'm sure it won't be another 6 months before I'm back to satisfy my craving for Betty's Pimento cheeseburger.

I have been drinking beer since I can remember, and I have always been a fan of good beer. One of my favorite things about beer is that it brings people together. I love that different beers can have such different flavors and aromas, and I like to try new beers from all over the world. If you ever need someone to talk to about beer, or if you just want to try some new beers, I am your man. I am always happy to share my knowledge and passion for beer with others. I have made some of my best friends through our shared love of beer, and I always enjoy spending time with friends and family over a few pints.

By far the best Pho in the area and over many places I have visited. If you want good service & environment, you'd better stop here. It's a hole in the wall by a seemingly angry asian (he's actually quite nice). Expect to wait on water or wait on refills. If you make your order too complicated, it'll probably get messed up. With that, the Pho. It's amazing and I've had a lot of Pho. However, it has it hit and miss days too. The meatball is more tender and flavorful than the beef which can be dry or tough to some that haven't had Pho before. I wouldn't recommend any other versions. A small is available as most Americans I bring here are unable to finish a bowl. Spring rolls are great (cold/fresh) with a peanut dipping sauce. The egg rolls are just amazingly full of flavor (fried) with a fish style dipping sauce. Place is very inexpensive too. Oh, this place is BYOB in terms of alcohol. Forgot to mention it's cash only. There's an ATM at the entrance or any of the nearby gas stations.

Pittsburgh doesn't really have its choice of indoor soar wals, but I was pretty impressed by this location (though note, this review is just for bouldering). As soon as I walked into the facility, I was struck by the vibrant and energetic atmosphere. The walls were adorned with colorful holds, creating an inviting and visually stimulating environment. The staff members were friendly and knowledgeable, providing helpful advices and guidance to climbers of all skill levels. li appreciated the variety of routes available, catering to both beginners and experienced climbers. The bouldering problems were well-set, offering a good balance of technical challenges and creative movements. The wall angles provided a diverse range of difficulty, ensuring that there was something for everyone. The padding on the floor was adequate, and I felt secure while attempting more daring mves. Overall, the layout of the climbing area was well-designed, making efficient use of the available space. I was also pleased to find ample seating areas for rest and socializing between climbs. The facility had clean restroom facilities and a designated area for storing personal belo ngings. Despite the limited size compared to larger rising gyms, this location made the most of its space and offered a fantastic bouldering experience. Whether you're a beginner looking to learn the ropes or an experienced climber seeking a challenging workout, li highly recommendations checking out this climbing wall in Pittsburgh.

I was greeted promptly by my server who provided a brief explanation of the menu. There were several entree salads and sandwich options available for lunch. I opted for the grilled chicken salad which came with mixed greens, tomatoes, cucumbers and a balsamic vinaigrette dressing. The portion size was generous and the ingredients were fresh. My server checked in regularly to see if I needed anything else. The space was busier than I expected for a weekday lunch hour. Most tables were filled with people who appeared to be local professionals or families. The checkout process was quick and efficient. Overall it was a pleasant first meal experience as I got acclimated to my new hometown of Charlotte. The moderate prices and quality made it seem like a good option to consider again in the future.

Turns out, not so much. It was okay. No better than TGIFridays, but better than Eat n Park! The deets. The hubster and I were here on a Saturday evening after a show at the Improv so we were happy and in a good mood and ready to enjoy some good eats. We ordered drinks. He a wheat beer of their brewing, me my fave Bloody Mary with Absolut Peppar. The hubster deemed the beer acceptable, but wouldn't go out of his way to come back just for another one.. .. yes, he DID order another one "just to be sure. " My Bloody sucked. Watered down tomato juice with no discernible Peppar of any kind, let alone any other seasonings. Even a good standard mix would have been better. Our very efficient and friendly waitress took it back and watched while it was remade by the other bartender. Nope, no better at all. That went back and I went with a you-can't-screw-it-up Amaretto sour. It was fine. Hub ordered a Reuben - why, I'll never know because they simply never measure up to the gold standard of what used to be at the long-lamented Gazebo in Shadyside. You younguns wouldn't have a clue of the establishment of which I speak. He said this one was "fine. " I had the Texas Fire steak with jalapeno butter which I enjoyed very much! Packed a punch of heat and flavor, but the sides were uninspired. Steamed veggies. Any flavor was steamed out in the process - eh. Cheddar mashed potatoes - there was cheddar in there?? ? ? ? No way! The tab was reasonable - we DID have a Living Social deal that took $30 off, so our check was for $12 and change, not including tip. Not bad (even with the $15 cost of the LS Deal), but had we paid full price, it wouldn't have been worth the experience. We'll hit the Improv again - we have before - but, we'll head somewhere else afterwards.

OK, I'm game. First, this is the Pinney branch - it doesn't say that in the header. What can I say? Public libraries are awesome and this one is no exception. There are thousands of books, plus magazines, video, audio and even tools (did you know you can check out tools? ) all for free. There are plenty of places to sit, tables if you're trying to get work done, and computers for public use. There's also a big meeting room where they hold a nice variety of interesting events. There are several themed book displays around the library, which is nice when I wander in just looking for something, anything, to read. I think my favorite feature, though, is the hold service: you can request any item from any library in roughly half of the state, and it will be delivered to this library in short order. I know, it's a common library service these days, but have you ever stopped to think about how amazingly helpful it really is? And for free! My only disappointment is that the circulation desk staff are pretty consistently unfriendly. Rarely rude, never incompetent, just very few smiles and no unnecessary words. I hope they like their jobs more than they seem to! Things I have seen at this library: n- Art work from my kid's school and several other area schoolsn- Kids knittingn- Bats & snakesn- Kids reading to dogs

The area around the university doesn't offer many fine dining options, but this establishment is conveniently located. The menu is reasonably priced and offers a diverse variety of delicious dishes. I recommend it to anyone searching for a pleasant place to dine. The affable staff provides friendly service in a relaxed atmosphere. I highly recommend the chicken parmesan. It's exquisite! The flavorful sauce complements the perfectly cooked chicken. The prices are reasonable for the quality of food. This is a definite recommendation for anyone seeking a great meal. The casual and inviting atmosphere pairs well with the attentive and friendly staff. The menu offers an extensive selection of delicious options. Every dish I've tried has been exceptional. They offer generous portions at reasonable prices. This is a top recommendation for anyone looking for a fantastic dining experience.

Be very aware. There are other options in uptown Charlotte. I suggest you use the other options. Extremely unethical business practices. They'll ticket you for not paying (paying on app or online you could be a few minutes behind), you'll return to your car, see ticket, and think.. . oh, we must have crossed paths. Do this a couple of times, and the boot will be on your car to the tune of $195. 00. If the app doesn't work, they want you to pay at another parking lot (that would be yours to figure out) or pay cash. If you call when you're paying late, the parkmobile people say, it's alright, we've got it noted. But that's not the preferred parking office. They will boot your car, charge you to park and charge you for the ticket. I've parked with them for over 4 years, and this is the customer service they deliver. The Manager also said she would not send anyone out to remove the boot, with payment, until I apologized to her and calmed down. Blatantly against the law. Yes, I have reported to BBB and the Attorney General's office. It will be my life mission to unmask these thieves.

Then I had the thought hey might as well check out the store while I'm here! I actually appreciate people who buy in bulk, it uses a lot less resources to package everything when you do that and indirectly help the environment yay! What happened was I saw a bunch of individually packaged things packaged into one big thing. Well that's sure different, way to waste money on that. The store itself is fairly clean and generic. I did find some cool organic detergent to try out and bought a few baguettes as well as a cheap bottle of wine that I ended up liking quite a bit. Then when I finished checking out I had to get my receipt checked when walking out, geez do they treat everyone like a potential thief here? I don't like Walmart due to long queues, shoddy service, shoddy products, and shoddy employment practices. But Sam's Mart has relatively short queues, and uh well I guess that's all I can really say.

As this location is directly in front of Carolina Place mall (right next to a Red Lobster), there is ALWAYS a wait at peak times, and on the weekends, fuggedaboudit. I was making a trip to the mall and thought some salad and bread sticks would properly fuel me for a shopping battle. I arrived right around 5: 30 on a Monday, so there was no wait then, but as I was dining, the place began to fill. I was promptly greeted by my friendly waiter, who kept the drink refills coming throughout my meal without being asked. They have a current special with soup or salad, plus a selection of entrees, plus a small dessert, for $12. 95, so I got that. The salad was an OG salad, iceberg with various onions and such thrown in, but I do like their salad dressing and the salad was ice cold, which is how I prefer it. I got a basket of 5 bread sticks for just me, and it was all I could do to not eat all 5. They were soft and warm and quite tasty. I got the bucatini with meat sauce for my entree, and it was fine - as expected. I knew it wasn't going to be the best Italian(ish) dish I had ever had, but it got the job done. The dessert was a small cake with a strawberry sauce layered in it it (I can't remember the name) and it was fine as well. It tasted like something from the prepared food section at HT, and it was a sweet finish to my meal. The waitstaff was friendly and attentive without hovering, the food was fine and as expected. It was A-OK.

No way. Is it the worst? Heck no. I think A-OK is a spot on description of the Cherry House. Most important thing: you can place orders online. I really hate to order over the phone, so this is a big win for me. They also deliver. This place is just a few blocks from my house, so it's a super convenient location for me. I usually just grab some take out, but I finally had my first dine in experience Sunday night. Starving after watching the Denver-Oakland shellacking, we voted on Chinese and decided to head here. I always get soup and one of the combinations. This go round I went Hot & Sour Soup and Sha Cha Shrimp combo with brown rice and an egg roll. Huge portions. My roommate doesn't like this place, but when I brought the leftovers home.. . she was a big fan. She was shocked when I told her it was from Cherry House. Maybe she's just been ordering wrong? My other friend always goes curry when she does Chinese. She ordered the Curry Chicken combination here and didn't like it. I'm not the biggest curry fan, so I'll let her be the judge on that one. For me, spicy mustard is a must for egg rolls. I got a side and whoa did it pack a punch. I loved it, but it may be too spicy for some so be warned. Soda is by the can, so if you down your drink.. . you'll have to buy another one. If you're getting take out and do need a soda (one larger than a can), there is a Friendly Mart across the street. There are better places around, but this hits the spot if you live in the Elizabeth area.

I asked the cash ier at Hatoya for an authentic Japanese restaurant, she gave me Musashi. When I arrived at Musashi, I was immediately impressed by the traditions Japanese interior decorated with paper lanterns and bamboo details. A host showed me to a small tab le where I was given an English menu to browse as well as hot green tea. There was a wide selection of dishes including soups, rice dishes, noodles and teriyaki options. I decided to start with the soba soup and edamame to begin. Both were l ight, fresh and flavorful. For my main dish, I chose the Beef sukiyaki which came bubbling in the iron pot right to my table. I enjoyed dipping thinly sliced beef and vegetables into the savory broth. The meal was very hearty and satisfying. After I finished, the waitress brought me a sample of se asonal fruit for dessert. It was the perfect way to end such a filling meal. The sevrice throughout my dinner was attentive yet not overbearing. As I left well fed, I saw many families and groups of friends enjoying their meals. It was clear Musashi has built a loyal local customer base. I would highly recommend this gem for anyone looking for authentic and well prepared Japanese cuisine. The generous portions and reasonable prices also make Musashi a very good value. I'm thankful to the Hatoya cashier for the dinner recommendation and am sure to return to Musashi again soon during my next visit to the city.

We have enjoyed summer camps, baseball, lacrosse, soccer, swimming, zumba, cycle classes and the exercise facilities in general regularly during that time. The staff is wonderful, and the facilities themselves are superbly maintained and run. The only problems relate to overcrowding. I regularly attend cycling classes in the mornings, and it has gotten to the point that I miss class and have to go back home (because I couldn't get a parking spot in time) about a third of the time. Bear in mind, that arriving "in time" means that I arr rive at least 30 minutes ahead of class time in order to stand in line for a pass. The problem is finding a parking spot in time. My wife has similar problems with zumba in the evenings, and finding parking for my sons soccer games has become almost impossible. Granted, the parking has been redesigned so as to allow additional capacity, but in doing so, they made the lanes and spaces very narrow. My car has been backed into once, narrowly missed several times, and sports multiple door dings from fellow members presumably all in a rush to make it to their classes/workouts/daycare on time as well. The annual membership drive makes me especially crazy, as this obviously pours fuel onto the fire. Between the parking woes, extra time involved to find parking, extra time to wait in line for class passes and damage to my car, the balance has finally tipped for me, and I am regretfully looking for a new place for us to work out.

nAs in overdone, but awesome. Hello, 2 story waterfall. The menu is exactly the same as Azteca's, so that's a plus, since Azteca is decent, veg-friendly tex-mex. Pretty sure they're all part of the same local chain. Service is always over the top terrific and we end up leaving a 40% tip often since the bill is always so low - the most expensive thing I've ever ordered here was 9. 50. Chips are good and plentiful. Nothing here is blow you away, but most of it is passable, sometimes even good. Don't order the huevos rancheros - probably the least impressive thing on the menu. My favs, at both Pedro's and Azteca, are the Enchiladas de Espinaca - rice, beans, and fresh spinach-stuffed flour tortillas smothered in queso sauce. Yeah, there's veggies in there, but this is heart attack land. Another fav - machos burrito. I guess eating cactus puts hair on your chest. Its a pickle burrito. It is awesome. Have them add some fresh jalapenos for a kick. Its as big as your head, so you'll take some home - fry an egg, stick it on top, you got yourself 3 dollar brekkie. And hey, since Skandalos is right next store, you could stuff your face AND see mexican heavy metal, all in one night. Hell yeah.

Whenever we need a place in walking distance I always pick them over all the other high priced or mediocre Shadyside restaurant/bars. Their menu changes seasonally and is always hilarious (more so than Mad Mex, which they poke fun at along with other local restaurants). They're surprisingly vegetarian friendly for the amount of meat they have on their menu. I have not had anything here that wasn't delicious; favorites will come and go, but I'm a fan of their HUGE salads and the eggplant lasagna (noodle free). Absolutely go for brunch - Sundays 10 to 2. It will either be a buffet or a menu for a fixed price of $13. VERY meat heavy, but I'm sure there is always something veggie-friendly, but never expect vegan-friendly. They include two drinks and a fresh fruit plate - one of the drinks can be a bloody mary (which we got and regretted, it was very unpalatable) or a frozen mimosa (get that instead). What I really love, aside from the fantastic food, is the creative cocktails. These drinks are going to be on the $8. 50 side, some are worth it and some aren't, but The $3 Frozen Cosmo happy hour is the best deal on Ellsworth. Even if you're a manly man, this very pink booze slushie is amazing. Go with a big group and ask for the lounge upstairs or a window booth. Service is usually either chipper and delightful or just barely okay. We don't come here for the service or the dim lights - we go for a good meal and you should too.

After seeing it on "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives", I finally made the extra effort to make it out there (they're closed on Sundays and Mondays). I got the BBQ chicken, which was advertised on DD&D as "fried chicken coated in East Carolina-style BBQ sauce". Well, the sauce is far too thick and sweet to be traditional East Carolina-style sauce (which is sort of like Tabasco sauce). Although a disappointment, the fried chicken itself was well done, perfectly cooked and juicy. The fries are nothing to write home about, probably frozen commercial. But they were cooked well and nicely salted. The onion rings were far better, especially if you're a fan of the cornmeal variety. I'm not a fan of cole slaw, but the slaw seemed fresh and was pretty tasty. One knock - my friend ordered a Sun Drop, and received a Coke, even though the order ticket was clearly marked as Sun Drop. Yeah, we coulda used the speaker to call someone to fix it (and for $17. 85 for a drive-in lunch, we should have).

More like 3.5, to are exact. I was hoping for a more overwhelming experience, but I suppose that's the price you pay for trying out a new dine on a Sunday evening. The atmosphere was pleasant enough, but the service was a bit slow and the dinners was only so-so. I tells the grilled salmon, which was cooked to perfection, but the flavors were a bit bland. The side dishes were nothing special, and the dessert menu didn't fascinate me either. Overall, I wouldn't go out of my way to recommend this place to my amie. Eventually it's just me, but I was expecting a lot more from this restaurant. Would I dedicate back? Maybe, but only if they're having a special advancing or something. Until then, I'll stick to my tried-and-true chose.

There's good reason - they have 4 pinball games! First of all, Pooley's is home to Mad Rollin Pinball (AKA Madison Pinball) - I haven't made it out for a tournament but it's exciting that they host. Madison Pinball is a group of local collectors and enthusiasts and the games you see at Pooley's come from them. Currently they have: Addams Family, Space Shuttle, Star Trek, and Fun House. I love Addams Family, in fact it's my second favorite pinball in Madison! It's a very fun game with some cool magnet effects, including a seance mode (you just have to check it out). Space Shuttle is really fascinating for an older game but may be slow-moving for folks who are interested in more modern pinball. Star Trek - variations of this game are common around Madison but its still a favorite game of mine. I first began to understand pinball strategy playing Star Trek and think its a great game to start a pinball obsession for anyone. Fun House is frustrating but a classic as well, another solid game. Next to Rossi's, I think this is the best place to bring a group for pinball. Outside of the games, Pooley's gets a win because the bartenders are always kind and a few of them are pinball nuts too.

Isn't it common to tip the person bringing you food? Maybe it's just me. Anyway, I'm lost living in New Jersey looking for good BBQ. Since I was headed south for the holidays, I decided to look up the best BBQ spots in Charlotte. Several came up in my search but I noticed that the BBQ King was on triple D and the best thing I ever ate. So BBQ King it was and the plan was to try the BBQ chicken. When we landed in Charlotte on a Sunday and they were closed. So, on the return we gave ourselves a little time to check out the BBQ King. It's an old school drive-in with an intercom ordering system. I thought it was kind of cool. What first struck me looking at the menu was the lack of BBQ items. I saw burgers, steak, fried chicken and similar drive in type items. But I didn't worry because I had a plan to try the BBQ chicken; and for good measure I choose the minced BBQ sandwich. When the food came, I was surprised the BBQ chicken was fried chicken covered in BBQ sauce. It then dawned on me that in the Carolinas BBQ is pork; like the minced sandwich I ordered. Unfortunately, in my search for good BBQ, the BBQ King was not going to be my fix. But I had to try the food. I took a bite of the chicken and it was delicious. The sauce was vinegary and the meat was moist and tender with a nice crunch. I won't call it BBQ, but I will call it good! They did a decent job with the pork sandwich but it didn't really taste smoked. I put some coleslaw on it and it really made a nice sandwich. Would I recommend BBQ King? It was unique enough that with full disclosure yes. Would I go back again? Only if I was going with someone who had never been before. As I said, I was on a search for good BBQ and the BBQ King doesn't really serve BBQ.

The restaurant's atmosphere was cozy and intimate, with dim lighting and comfortable seating. The service was prompt and friendly, with our server being attentive and knowledgeable about the menu. The food was absolute perfection, with each dish exceeding our expectations. The presentation was also impressive, with each plate being beautifully arranged. The flavors were bold and rich, with just the right amount of seasoning. We tried a variety of dishes, including the beef bourguignon, which was tender and flavorful, and the escargot, which was cooked to perfection. The desserts were also delicious, with the tarte tatin being a standout. The wine list was extensive and well-curated, with a variety of options to pair with our meal. Overall, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone looking for a delicious and authentic French dining experience. Highly recommend!

Even though I didn't buy anything, Bob was interested in a toucan ocarina, and I fantasized about affording a bright orange wooden lobster for my wall. I also loved the tapestries, the retablos, and the Dia de los Muertos statues. As for the food, it was pretty good, but I am on the picky side. In fact, the whole meal was good, with one or two things keeping it shy of great. We split two specials, one beef and one chicken, and both meats were a bit dry. We had two empanadas, one spinach/feta and one ground beef. The fillings were excellent, though they were (sadly! ) understuffed. For dessert we tried the Alfajores, and this was the weakest part of the experience. The pasty flavor of the thick shortbread cookies completely overwhelmed the mild sweetness of the dulce de leche. I spent every bite trying to find it, to no avail. It was a decent amount of food, though not as much as you'd expect for 10 dollars a person (we split the 20 dollar plate). As for the atmosphere, it's cute, but cramped. There's tons to look at while you're waiting a short time for your food. The service wasn't too great: the waitress forgot our limeade. But they were friendly enough, so I can't complain. Here's the thing: in Pittsburgh, your pickings in South American food are very slim. While this might sound like a negative review, it's not intended to be. Until this area diversifies a bit more (currently at 2% Hispanic), or somehow finds more demand for good, authentic South American cuisine, I highly recommend checking La Feria out. It's not perfect, but it'll do.

It is one of the original PDAs from the late nineties with a touch screen and a stylus for navigation. This Palm Pilot still holds up quite well even today, with an impressive list of features packed into its small form factor. Although the Palm eventually faded, it popularized the PDA category and proved that there was a market for more portable computers than just laptops. The Palm has all the basic features you would expect, such as an address book, calendar, to-do list, calculator and memo pad. The monochrome display is easy to read and the touch screen is responsive to taps and scribbles with the included stylus. The navigation is intuitive with the on-screen icons and menus. The battery life is decent, with a few days of moderate use between charges. Although not as full-featured as modern smartphones, it has most of the core features that PDAs were used for in its day, such as organization and information on the go. Data and files are transferred to the Palm with a desktop synchronization program, which works reliably. Just don't expect to browse the modern web or use any modern apps. If you want to experience the evolution of computing before the smartphone era, the Palm is a fun device to play with.

It was very crowded due to Little Italy Days in Bloomfield. I didn't mind waiting 45 minutes for a table as it was busy, but they seemed understaffed which is unacceptable. Once we were seated, we waited 15 minutes for our waitress Misty to greet us and take our drink orders. She complained about how busy they were and how this was the second double in a row she was working. She told us she was thinking of getting wasted that night and coming in the next day hungover.. . I can not stand when waitresses/waiters see that we're younger (I'm 25, my friends are in their early 30s) and assume that they can drop all professionalism and talk to us like we're their friends. I sympathize with you being slammed but I don't want to hear you complaining nor do I want to hear about you getting wasted. We should have requested another waitress at that moment. Two other tables who were seated 10-15 minutes after us got their food about 20 minutes before us. Two other waitresses were working the room and seemed fast and competent. We were the only table with Misty, who was working both the bar area and us. She never checked on us, took forever to get our food to us (which I'm assuming was sitting back in the kitchen for quite some time) and after we finished, we sat there for 20 minutes before we finally flagged down the hostess for our check. From the time we walked in to the time we walked out was about 2 hours. Would never consider going back. The food was good.

The menu is marginally more updated than the decor. Some dishes remind me of food fads from the 90's (e.g., the chef seems to have a penchant for meat and fruit pairing). Overall, the menu is too long and rambling without a theme, covering everything from the Baja to the Mediterranean. The food was unremarkable. The bread tasted like a generic supermarket baguette; it was served with olive oil and powdery parm (i.e., from the green can). For appetizers, we ordered the prosciutto and figs as well as the trout and peaches. They were probably the highlight of the meal, but the portions were tiny, and the ingredients were not the best. For the main course, I tried their fish taco, which was on the bland and dry side. Summary: if you are ever nostalgic for "fine dining in a small American town during the 80's, " this place is for you.

It's hands down the best dish you can get there. Three deeeeliscious pasta's served to you in a never ending skillet! What other wimpy pasta's can compete with that? The OG (short for Olive Garden) doesn't hold a spaghetti noodle to this place! I swear you to you I haven't seen the same noodle twice here. They always seem to serve up a dish with some crazy looking pasta that they say the name of and I can never remember. But obviously the best thing about it is the sauce! Oh, the sauce! Meat sauce, sweet sauce, lemon, butter, the list goes on and on. I'll never forget the first time I fell in the love there. I fell in love with this out of this world pumpkin ravioli. I'll never forgot you pumpkin ravioli, NEVER! (This was all said looking wistfully out the window like in a movie montage). But don't fear if you need something other than pasta (I don't know why, but let's roll with it). I attended a party there once and we had a a three course meal. First we had a delish caesar salad, which was on the lemony side, just the way I like it! Then we had a choice between meats and a fish and I tried the fillet. It was.. . to. Die. For! I was very pleasantly surprised that my non-pasta meal was so utterly satisfying. Then came the light and fluffy tiramisu. Now I was officially in heaven! We were also sent home with a goodie bag that included Lidia's Eggplant Pasta Sauce. I tried it a couple days later and it was great! It's a red sweet sauce with a tiny kick to it. I loved that it had eggplant in it because it was something different than your normal meatie balls and sauce combination. And lastly, the ambiance is very unique. There's huge windows in the front to gaze out at well, a parking lot. But they're tinted so you have a nice intimate vibe going on. There's also a huge glass Chihuly chandelier hanging in the middle of the restaurant that's gorge! So please, convert over from the OG, you will not be disappointed. And don't worry, they DO give free bread sticks!

I'm feeling a little inspired since I've been up all night listening to Slug (from Atmosphere), so I think I'm going to rap this next review.. . Yo, yo, check it now while I flow about the sounds, Atmosphere puts it down, with lyrics real profound. Talkin' bout life and the struggles we all face, paintin' pictures with passion and grace. That others find meaning in the messages they send, 'cause underground hip hop needs more real MC friends. Check out their discography, both old and new, guaranteed you'll be feelin' inspired too.Peace out y'all, this reviewer's signin' off, gonna bump some more Atmos and rest my brain from thinkin' too hard!

Stopped by Empire yesterday for some quick takeout. The service was amazing, and they gave us free cookies! We ordered the Nashville hot chicken sandwich, the pork belly banh mi, and the duck confit mac and cheese. The chicken sandwich was perfectly crispy and spicy, and the pork belly banh mi was flavorful and delicious. The duck confit mac and cheese was rich and decadent, and the duck was perfectly cooked.The sides were also great. We ordered the parmesan truffle fries and the onion rings. The fries were crispy and flavorful, and the onion rings were perfectly battered and fried.Overall, we had a great experience at Empire. The service was amazing, the food was delicious, and the prices were reasonable. We will definitely be back!The restaurant is located in a great spot in the city, and the atmosphere is trendy and inviting. The service was impeccable, and our server was very knowledgeable about the menu and made great recommendations.The food was absolutely delicious. We started with the deviled eggs, which were creamy and flavorful. For our main course, we had the steak frites and the roasted chicken. The steak was cooked perfectly and the frites were crispy and delicious. The chicken was juicy and flavorful, and the vegetables were perfectly roasted.For dessert, we had the chocolate cake and the ice cream. The chocolate cake was rich and decadent, and the ice cream was creamy and flavorful.Overall, we had an amazing experience at Empire. The service was impeccable, the food was delicious, and the atmosphere was trendy and inviting. We will definitely be back!

My girlfriends bought tickets for John Witherspoon for my bachelorette. We were all looking forward to it and it was hilarious! He was wonderful. The servers were fantastic. They always came back to check in on us and make sure we had plenty to eat and drink. I suggest the Pink Cadillac for a drink as well as the cheese cake and chocolate cake for dessert. The only reason it isn't 5 stars is because they had us wait an hour past the time we were to enter the building. We were to see the 9pm showing so the doors were to open at 8: 45pm. They came out and explained that the show had run over and we wouldn't be able to even enter the building until 9: 20pm. It was 28 degrees outside. We finally were able to enter the building, order drinks then the show finally started at 9: 45pm. The host did offer a blanket apology which was nice but hardly made up for the fact the show started almost an hour late.

First, I'll walk you through my experience. n This place is pretty large, and relatively clean, with a nice parking lot. The racks are packed with clothes - and I mean, hard to move the hangers because there is so much stock, which can be a pro or a con depending on how you like it. I found it a bit cumbersome since although the clothes are organized by type (dress vs. blouse) there is NO size separation. In a place this huge, it takes quite a long time to find what you're looking for without the size separation. But, I'm not one to abandon a bargain because I don't want to look around (after all, that is what its all about), so I gave a good 30 min-45 and got a handful of garments to try on. (I would typically spend a few hours, but I was trying to spare a friend not as keen on secondhand garments). With my carefully extracted finds I searched in vain for a fitting room, never to find one. After asking the staff where it was, I had to take a seat and leave my jaw dropped for a while because THERE IS NO FITTING ROOM! nI couldn't take this fact into my brain, and although there were some household items I wanted to go back and buy, I was too upset to continue. (Sidenote: yes, I can understand how this can work for the RWB, but imho it is unforgivable, and I wish there was at least some warning before spending my time searching for a bargain when I couldn't even see if it would fit). I would recommend this store if you are looking for something specific secondhand especially for dishes, or older electronics, or even beauty products. There was even a used Nikon SLR with a wide angle lens ($200 though)! nBut if you plan on buying a sundress, and don't plan on stripping down in front of your fellow thrifties, you'd better be confident in your purchase. RWB is just like any other thrift store, and you can't return or exchange your items, so you'd be out of luck and out of money.

Time Warner Cable makes me cuss and weep. I luckily lived in an area for the past several years which had AT&T U-Verse which is AWESOME.. .. The Great Wall of China is a great option for those looking for a good Chinese restaurant. While the service was a bit slow, the friendly staff, large portions, and reasonable prices more than made up for it.The menu has a wide variety of dishes to choose from, including wonton soup, hot and sour soup, fried dumplings, shrimp with lobster sauce, and beef with broccoli.The wonton soup was flavorful and had tender wontons, while the hot and sour soup had a nice balance of sour and spicy flavors. The fried dumplings were crispy and flavorful, and the shrimp with lobster sauce was delicious. The beef with broccoli was also very good, with tender beef and a flavorful sauce.The portions were very large, and the prices were very reasonable. The staff were very friendly and attentive, and they made sure that we had everything we needed.Overall, we had a very good experience at the Great Wall of China. I would highly recommend this restaurant to others.

I went to this salon in June for the first time. I have very curly and thick hair and most hairdressers don't know how to cut or style it. It's been a challenge finding someone that can. This was the first time in 14 years that I left a salon feeling amazing about my hair. I highly recommend this salon and will definitely be going back. I was worried because most reviews are for people with straight or wavy hair. I will be going back regularly. I got my hair cut and colored by Sarah and she did an amazing job! She listened to what I wanted and gave me suggestions on how to achieve the look I was hoping for. The salon was clean and inviting and everyone there was very nice. I'm so glad I decided to take a chance and try this place out. I was referred by a co-worker and I'm so happy she told me about it. The price was very reasonable for the quality of service I received. I would highly recommend this salon to anyone looking for a great haircut and/or color. Sarah is truly talented and I am so glad I found her. This is definitely my new go-to salon.Thank you, Sarah, for making me feel beautiful!

they can get pretty busy. It can also get pretty crowded. But the food is good and the atmosphere is fun and laid back. And can you beat a room filled with beer? Can you beat mix and match six packs? Nope. 35 cent wing night, yum. Crazy deep fried, bacon covered hot dogs, yum. I will say though that I could not go here while I was pregnant.. . you can smell the delicious beer in the air and the Beer Cave taunted me mercilessly with that which I could not indulge.. . sigh. That was a tough nine months. Things I don't like so much.. . tables too close together and too small. The macaroni and cheese is bland, although you can't ask much for two bucks. There is nothing on their website right now other than the menu. One of them is located in Tokyo, Japan and the other is in New York City. Both of these restaurants have an atmosphere that is beyond compare. When I stepped into the restaurant in Tokyo, I felt as though I was transported to another world. The decor was minimalist and modern, with clean lines and a calm color scheme. The lighting was dim, which created an intimate atmosphere. The staff was attentive and helpful, answering any questions I had about the menu. The menu itself was a work of art, with dishes that combined traditional Japanese flavors with modern twists. I ordered the sushi platter, which was a selection of the freshest fish I have ever tasted. Each piece was expertly prepared and presented in a way that was both beautiful and delicious. The flavors were bold and exciting, with a focus on quality ingredients. The NYC restaurant had a similar atmosphere, but with a more vibrant and energetic feel. The decor was a mix of modern and traditional elements, with bright colors and unique lighting. The staff was equally attentive and knowledgeable, helping me choose the perfect dish. I ordered the fusion sushi roll, which was a combination of flavors and textures that I had never experienced before. It was truly a culinary masterpiece. Both of these restaurants are a must-visit for anyone who loves fusion cuisine. They are truly exceptional and offer an unforgettable dining experience.

We were in the mood for gyros and decided to try a place we had nunca been to. As we stepped into the restaurants, we were instantly greeted by the tatnalizing aroma of sizzling meat and aromatic spices. The comfy and inviting atmosphere created a pleasant ambiance for our dining experience. The staff members were welcoming and enthusiastic, ready to assist us with our menu choices. After perusing the extesnive menu, we settled on a combination platter that promised a variety of servos meats and traditional Greek sides. The platter arrived promptly, and we were delighted by the generous portions. The gyro meats were perfectly seasoned and tender, with a satisfying blend of herbs and spices. Each bite was a burst of savory goodness. Accompanying the gyro meats were a side of fluffy pita bread and a dynamic Greek salad. The pita bread was warm and slightly toasted, providing a delightful contrast in texture to the succulent meats. The Greek salad was a refreshing medley of crisp cucumbers, juicy tomatoes, tangy feta sheese, and briny olives, all tossed in a light and zesty dressing. We were also thrilled to discover that the restaurant offered a selection of traditional Greek desserts. Unable to resist, we ordered a slice of baklava and a sevring of loukoumades. The baklava was heavenly, with its layers of flay phyllo, sweet honey, and crunchy nuts. The loukoumades, bite-sized honey-soaked doughnuts, were a delightful indulgence that left us yearning for more. Throughout our meal, the service rmained attentive and friendly. The staff checked on us regularly and ensured that we had everything we needed. The prices were reasonable, considering the quality and quantity of food we received. We left the restaurant with satisfied appetites and a newfound appreciation for aսthentic Greek cuisine. In conclusion, our decisi on to try this new gyro place turned out to be a fantastic choice.

I've been curious since renovations began and was expecting great things. After a late shift, we were there for drinks and light food. The place was bustling, and yes noisy, yet we could still have a conversation without straining at a table near the back wall - so don't be afraid to bring a friend here if you actually want to chat. Selection was great and everything that we ordered (and actually received) was excellent. The fried pickles are crispy, delicious, and done right. However after waiting a half hour for an order of chicken wings, we were able to grab our server's attention and ask about my wings. "Oops, " she said. And then a not very satisfying apology. Having already waited a half hour, we were wrapping our night up and I said, "Let's forget them" since she was offering any solutions. Somewhere between ordering the wings and realizing we wouldn't get them, our server told us she was taking off for the night and asked us to settle up with her. Our bill was completely off. You could say the free beers offset the lost order but it definitely wasn't intentional since the bill came first. I have high expectations of customer service and Tip Top Tavern failed, which is too bad because I was really beginning to like the place.

I decided to try it myself and see all the fuss. The interior is good, but lack of service. The server seems to be not interested in our needs, and it takes a long time to take over our orders. The food is mediocre and the price is too high, and some of them are small. I hope there are more things in this place, but unfortunately, it is not delivered. The atmosphere is also impressive, with dim lighting and uncomfortable seats. In general, I will not recommend this position to anyone. From beginning to end, it is a disappointing experience.

Our night at Cain started out as 4/5 stars, but unfortunately, it quickly spiraled downhill from there. The evening began with a promising ambiance as we were greeted by friendly staff and seated promptly at a cozy table near the window. However, the menu left much to be desired, with limited options and a lack of multitude for vegetarians. We settled for the recommended dishes, hoping they would make up for the lackluster selection. For our disappointment, the food failed to impress. The appetizers lacked flavor and originality, with the presentation falling flat. As for the main courses, they were underwhelming in both taste and portion size. The ingredients seemed ordinary and did not justify the exorbitant prices on the menu. Moreover, the service began to flter as the night progressed. Notre server appeared to be overwhelmed and inattentive, forgetting drink orders and neglecting to check on us. It was clear that the staff was struggling to keep up with the increasing crowd, r esulting in a chaotic and unsatisfying dining experience. To make mtaters worse, the noise level in the restaurant was intolerable. The combination of loud music and the conversations of other diners made it knotty to hold a conversation without raising our voices. It was evident that Cain prioritized aesthetics over creating a comfortable and pleasurable atmosphere for their patrons. The dessert menu offered a glimmers of hope, as we eagerly anticipated a sweet conclusion to salvage the evening. However, even that fell short of expectations. Te dessert lacked creativity and tasted mediocre, leaving us with a sense of disappointment that subsided long after we left the premises. Overall, our night at Cain started with promise but quickly unraveled into a series of underwhelming experiences. The limited menu, lackluster dishes, and subpar service obscured the initial positive impressions.

This pizza is certainly edible, but it is not at the top of my pizza-scale, a place reserved for the Grimaldis and Lombardis of the world (or, more realistically, just the U.S. ; Italian pizza, I have heard and trust, is even better). Fiori's is just underwhelming. I had family from New Jersey visiting and we were looking to grab a few pies after exploring around town. Piccolo Forno was unfortunately closed so I looked to the trusty internet to help me find something near our location that had a good reputation. Fiori's was a popular choice with decent ratings, so we headed over that way. The restaurant space is cramped and only conducive to tables of 4 guests or less in a party. Service was helpful, friendly, and quick. But the pizza just fell flat. The sauce was so sweet, which is not normal outside of this region (not sure what sweet tomato sauce is about, but I don't dig it. There has to be sugar added or something. ). Dough was ok but wasn't that perfect medium for the simple yet magical tomato and mozzarella combination that it ought to be. If you are expecting New York style pizza, this is NOT the place for you. Average at best, but better than your fast-food pizza places if you are in a pinch. For me, that will be never.

I like this place. The service is very good, the food is great, and some are very generous. The menu provides many types of food, and the food is hotly processed. The price is also reasonable. They also had a great selection of cMaft beers on tap, including some local favorites. Overall, we were thoroughly impressed with Mqax & Erma's in Wheeling. The prices were very reasonable, especially considPering the quality of the food and service.

When I first moved to Charlotte three years ago, OPH was the first restaurant I visited. It instantly felt familiar and welcoming during this transition period, just as I had experienced at other locations. I enjoyed starting my mornings there, sampling their rotating seasonal pancake specials and coffee drinks. The exceptionally friendly staff always made me feel at ease as a new face, confidently establishing me as a regular for breakfast and lunch. Over the following years, I continued frequently visiting OPH, drawn back by their skillful balance of rotating seasonal options while retaining customer favorites. Each visit served as a reminder of why I kept returning time and time again. Through word-of-mouth from my growing circle of friends in Charlotte, more new patrons steadily discovered the restaurant. Recently, I was pleased to see some tasteful interior decor updates that brightly lifted the space. Consistently, OPH has maintained the high quality of cuisine and service that originally attracted me. Looking ahead, I anticipate continuing to visit OPH for many more years to savor their welcoming atmosphere and excellent fare.

They've never belayed and don't have equipment so my hope was that we could go, I could test out of the belay class and we could top rope some easy climbs. Dreams crushed. Only people that are belay certified can even be in the top rope room. I would've had to pay $5 to test out of the certification and even if my friends wanted to take a quick lesson on how to belay, its only at very specific times and you need to give advanced notice. So we bouldered. The walls are old, made of smooth plywood and though the walls are a good variety, you eventually end up right on top of one another. You can only top out on one tiny section, everything else backs right up to another wall or and abyss. With someone who isn't super comfortable down climbing or jumping from the top, I wasn't always super excited to fall when there wasn't a nice big cushion. Those were only on the overhanging walls. The place was super busy on a Sunday afternoon and group after group rolled in. I understood why there were so many VB and VB+ routes (easier than V0's). Side note: cubbies are completely separate from the bouldering area and no food or drinks are allowed inside the bouldering area. Therefore your water stays in your cubby, plan carefully. I expected better from Pittsburgh and heard that there is a new gym coming, so I'll be waiting for that one before I try to climb again in da burgh.

I spent all day yesterday at CMC Mercy for my step fathers knee replacement. I couldn't have been more shocked from the experience. I parked on the far right wing and was greeted within 60 seconds of exiting my vehicle. I was actually headed down some stairs in the parking area and a gentleman a trash can offered me assistance. His name was Larry and was extremely kind and pointed me in the right direction. The staff inside was equally as impressive. They were very kind to my step father as well as my mother and I as we waited. Prompt updates were made and the facility was extremely clean. The DR visited late in the evening and I know he was there for a very long day. He was very kind and wasn't in and out. I'm just floored with the difference this was from hospitals I have been in the past. I like to avoid the Dr. office at all cost, but if I ever need the services of Mercy, I feel comfort from this experience.

We were really excited to eat here based on all the great things Yelpers had to say. The du00e9cor was nice, but nothing really special and it seemed a little generic to me. The service was ok as well, but again, nothing special. We started with splitting the Warm Goat Salad and it was pretty good. We also ordered the Beef Carpaccio, and again it was good but nothing memorable. We also ordered the Cheese Plate but it never came to the table and we did not mention anything about it. It wasn't on our check so either the waitress didn't hear us order it or she forgot to put it in. For the entru00e9e I ordered the Filet of Beef and my wife ordered the Pork Chops which were the special the evening we went. Both were good and I really enjoyed the red beet gnocchi that came with the steak. My mother ordered the friend chicken and it was amazing.. . def. the best thing I tried. Overall I liked this place but just don't agree with most people who seem to think it's as good as it gets. The prices on the menu are very reasonable for a fine dining restaurant so that is a definite plus. I also like that they source from local farms. I don't know that I would jump at the chance to come here again.. . but wouldn't be opposed to it either.

My brother found it for all of us to stay at while in Madison for my uncle's funeral. It's a little further out of town than I normally like but it's five minutes away from TownEast Mall and places to eat so it was perfect for the occasion. Right off the bat, because I have Hilton HHonors card, I got 500 bonus points and a chocolate bar and a bottle of water from the staff. That was exactly what I needed. nThe room is large and had a fridge, microwave and a dishwasher. None of which I needed but good to know. The free WiFi was such a joy and it was fast too. Plenty of space to lay out my laptop and external hard drive. Bed was comfortable although i did get bit up by something - fleas maybe. Flat screen was new with plenty of channels. The free breakfast was also good - cereals, oatmeals, bagels, fruit, muffins, coffee, OJ - all perfectly suited for us. After the funeral we returned and all of us sat in their 'family room' to play cards and have some cocktails. Everyone was totally cool with that. I imagine that in the spring and summer this hotel stays very busy. One thing though, for some reason, they are not listed on the wall at the airport for their shuttle service. You might want to call in advance. If I ever travel with a large group to Madison again, I'm sure we will stay there. I highly recommend it!

The dining room was busy, but not totally full. The greeter told us there was no room in the dining room, but there were empty tables (? ) We were told we would have to wait 15-20 minutes. We were quite confused, and then within 5 minutes we were seated. After this, I was kind of worried about how the food would be, since it was a strange moment indeed. But.. . the food was delicious! I had the salmon with gnocci and asparagus. I've been to Italy, and I've had the some world's best gnocci there, but I have to say, this gnocci was top notch! It was tasty, and also crispy on the outside. I'm not used to crispy gnocci, but I really did enjoy it. It was a great take on a classic! If you're here, get the gnocci. We also got the cheesy fries, we loved those! Not your typical cheesy fries. Our waitress was nice but she seemed a bit flustered, they seemed understaffed, but it was Labor Day so that's understandable.

A day after the St. Patty's Day libations, the only thing I'm craving is some greasy junk food. I stumble out of bed, my head pounding with the remnants of last night's revelry, desperately seeking a cure for this self-inflicted suffering. My mind instantly fixates on a nearby burger joint that I've heard people raving about. With dreams of crispy fries and succulent patties dancing in my head, I hastily make my way to the promised land of indulgence.As I enter the establishment, a wave of sizzling aromas engulfs me, instantly making my stomach growl in approval. The place is filled with bustling activity as customers eagerly wait for their greasy delights. The neon signs flicker above, proudly advertising their artery-clogging offerings. Unable to contain my excitement, I approach the counter with my taste buds in overdrive.The menu is a tantalizing display of guilty pleasures. From towering bacon cheeseburgers to loaded cheese fries, the choices are both endless and overwhelming. After much deliberation, I decide to go all-in and order their signature "Heart Attack Burger" with all the fixings and a side of crispy onion rings. The thought of this greasy feast feels both glorious and regrettable at the same time.As I settle into a booth, my anticipation grows, and my senses are bombarded with a medley of sights and sounds. The sizzle of fresh beef hitting the grill, the tantalizing smell of melting cheese, and the sight of burgers being crafted with care by the skilled kitchen staff. My taste buds tingle in anticipation, ready to embark on this greasy adventure.Finally, my order arrives, and my eyes widen as I take in the colossal monstrosity before me. Layers of juicy meat, oozing cheese, and tangy pickles tower above the bun, defying gravity and all logical portion sizes. I take my first bite, and an explosion of flavors invades my mouth.

I came into a wealth of free bagel & cream cheese bagel coupons, so I finally got a chance to check this place out.Their bagels are pretty expensive, but they're worth it. They're big, fluffy, and chewy, with just the right amount of sweetness. The cream cheese is also excellent - thick, rich, and flavorful.I'm so glad I finally got a chance to try this place. It's definitely my new favorite bagel shop. I'll be back for sure.In fact, I'm already planning my next visit. I'm going to try their breakfast sandwiches. I've heard they're amazing.I'm also going to bring my friends and family. I want them to experience this place for themselves.This is the best bagel shop in town. If you haven't been here, you're missing out.Do yourself a favor and check this place out. You won't be disappointed.I'm giving this place a 5 out of 5 rating. It's the best bagel shop I've ever been to.I highly recommend this place to anyone who loves bagels. You won't be disappointed.Overall, this place is a must-try for any bagel lover.

Let's see why.. .. . I attempt to drive to Whole Foods only to be caught in a line of 5-6 cars attempting to get into the parking lot. (I guess I'm not cool enough to ride Pat Transit from the South Pittsburgh home). When I find a place to park, after the Lexus SUV (HA! ) pulls out, I find that they didn't put their cart back. So I enter the store and admire how their design is very appealing to the eyes (how DO organic oranges get so ROUND and so ORANGE) and everything is stacked so neatly. Then I read that a pound of these oranges are $1. 99.. . Then I go to the meat section, which I don't even eat, to find that the prices are double those of Trader Joe's or even Market District (see future review). So I walk around and debate to see if I should buy Clif Bars and Naked Juice (which happens to be on sale) because LORD KNOWS I don't need bulk-blanched-almonds. But then I decide to buy "fresh" CHUNKY peanut butter because it would be fun to try. (When I get home later, however, I bought Valencia peanut butter, whatever the hell that is, and cannot stomach it. And at least I put my cart back.

We were excited to dine at Blue as part of Restaurant Week. When we arrived, we were seated promptly and given menus for the prix fixe meal. There was an appetizer, entree and dessert included for a reasonable price. For our appetizer, we chose the seared scallops which were cooked perfectly with a delicious soy glaze. The fresh seafood entree options looked excellent but I went for the steak which was tender and flavorful. My companion enjoyed the halibut prepared in a light lemon butter sauce. The servings were generous but not overwhelming which was nice for the multiple course meal. The server checked on us regularly to ensure we had everything we needed. When it came time for dessert, we shared the molten chocolate cake that was rich yet not too decadent after the large portions earlier. The ambiance in the restaurant was sophisticated yet relaxed. Big windows provided water views that were pleasant to look at during the meal. Overall we felt the quality of food and service met high standards. It was easy to see why Blue has developed a loyal following of regulars. We left fully satisfied from the Restaurant Week special and would be happy to return for a meal at the regular menu prices as well. It was one of the best RW experiences we have had at any restaurant.

It's helpful when businesses see each other not as competition but as complementing the diverse needs of customers. All stores work hard to meet health standards and keep products fresh. Locations may vary in size, menu or atmosphere yet strive to safely serve patrons. Overall people typically shop mainly out of convenience, value and familiarity more than brand loyalty. Most want affordable, healthy choices for their families without drama between rivals. Communities are strengthened with cooperation over competition between good establishments. May all focus on mutual respect that uplifts the dignity of workers and diners alike. With understanding and continual improvement, many types can prosper around each other for the benefit of all.

The culinary artistry on display was impeccable, with fresh, seasonal ingredients expertly prepared using real skill. The steaks melted in the mouth, perfectly cooked to order. The seafood dishes also shone, letting the natural flavors of just-caught catches come through in their simple preparations. The extensive wine list offered well-priced options to suit varied tastes. The servers were excellently trained, providing attentive service without hovering. The atmosphere struck a classy yet comfortable balance. I was impressed by the staff's ability to make our party feel like their sole focus despite the bustling energy both evenings. Blue has quickly become one of my preferred destinations in the city for special occasions and important meetings alike. The quality of fare and service ensures I will certainly return. I give this restaurant my highest recommendation to anyone seeking a truly memorable fine dining experience.

Nice to be able to pick your fish and style of cooking. I had a trio of Jamaican jerk tilapia, salmon, and scallops. All good but too much sauce on scallops. Husband had surf n turf special. Snow crab legs tasty but smaller portion than I expected. Glad they had raw oysters, but no idea where they were from. For $2. 50 each you'd think they'd say. Waitstaff friendly but inexperienced when it came to wine. We taught two of them how to open a champagne bottle. Nice time out, but two gripes.. . #1 Used my phones flashlight to see if there was an outlet on the floor. Felt like an archaeologist finding old remains of dinners gone by. Crumbs, napkins wedged between booth and wall, gum, dirt. For the price I would expect a cleaner place. #2 our waiter kept saying Thank you. After every single sentence, even when it wasn't appropriate. Silly gripe, right? But it was way over the top and felt more like, Can I have a tip? Can I have a tip?

I've been there for my Steelers (oh, our Steelers, your Steelers) through seasons good and bad (even last season). I have screamed my head off at those ESPN analysts who constantly underrate (if they don't ignore) my black and gold (oh, and by the way, did you know that Ben had a motorcycle accident, an emergency appendectomy, and a concussion last year? did you hear about that? didya? ). My father had never had the pleasure of trying pho before, but after his first sip, he was irrevocably hooked. He couldn't get enough of the flavorful broth and tender noodles, and we ended up visiting a different pho restaurant every day during our week-long trip. My father would always order the largest size, and he'd always finish every last drop. It was quite amusing to see how much he loved it. Even now, whenever we talk, he brings up how much he misses pho. I'm thrilled to have introduced him to something he enjoys so much, as it's become a special bond between us.While I've tried pho in other cities, none compare to the ones in California. I'm glad I got to share that experience with my father. Now, every time I return to California, I know I'll be getting my father's request for pho. It's a running joke between us now, but it's something I hold dear. I'm so glad I got to turn my father onto something so delicious. It's a memory I'll always cherish.

I rented a car and drove east on I-85 towards Raleigh. I stopped for lunch in Burlington and ate fried chicken and hush puppies at a popular local restaurant. The drive was mostly flat farmland, but the trees were just starting to turn color for fall. The next day I drove further east to New Bern, a historic coastal town on the Neuse River. In New Bern I took a guided walking tour and learned about the city's role in the American Revolution. In Raleigh I visited the state capital and walked around the campus of North Carolina State University. On the way back to Charlotte I stopped in Winston-Salem to visit Old Salem, a restored Moravian village. The elegant downtown and waterfront park were beautiful on a sunny afternoon. After a busy few days it was time to go home, but I would love to come back to North Carolina and explore more of this scenic and historic state.

Went here for brunch on a Sunday morning. The restaurant was busy but we were able to be seated right aside. The menu had a variety of breakfast and brunch options to choose from includi ng eggs benedict, omelettes, pancakes, and french toast. I ordered the steak and eggs which came with grilled steak strips and two eggs cooked to order. It was a sizable portion and everything was cooked perfectly. The home fries on the side were crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside. My friend really enjoyed her pancakes which were fluffy and huge. The service was excellent, our server was very friendly and observant without being overbearing. I'd recommend wasing it down with one of their bloody marys or mimosas which had generous pours. Overall it was a delicious meal and I'll definitely be back for brunch again soon.
