While becoming ill is generally unpleasant, I admit that I sometimes find relief in being sick. I know this sounds peculiar, but I appreciate the opportunity illnesses provide to remain indoors and recuperate. As an introvert, it's gratifying to excuse myself from obligations and commitments for a few days' respite. I spend this time cocooned in bed, watching films and napping restfully. One sick-day activity I especially enjoy is preparing homemade chicken soup from scratch. The warmth and comfort of the nourishing soup always seems to speed my recovery. After one or two days of much-needed relaxation, I begin feeling like my usual self again. Overall, though falling ill is far from ideal, it does allow me a break from my typically hectic routine - a silver lining, of sorts.

5 Stars Christos is a sort of charmingly run-down sort of place, particularly given that many of the other offerings in the Cultural District are pretty new joints. The food is better than average. Having just eaten at DC's supposedly cheapest and best Greek restaurant the week I was in Pittsburgh, I found the food to be more authentic, better seasoned, fresher and definitely cheaper. We had a group of 10 on a Sunday night. The restaurant owner/manager/old Greek guy came out onto the sidewalk as we were walking by and practically begged us to come in. I had a grilled fish dish that was nicely cooked along with a glass of the house red wine. At the end of our meals we decided we had to try the famous "Jackie O cake, " which was, sad to say, nothing particularly special. Best of all, we had no problems splitting the check multiple ways when it came time to leave.

I think the location is in a great spot and the atmosphere is also really chill. The inside of this location has that modern rustic feel with light wood and big windows for ample lighting. There is also seating outside if you prefer that. The staff there is always really nice and helpful. My friends and I like to start off with the classic cheese curds and then get our own burgers. The burgers are great and the tots are also crispy and delicious. The beer selection is vast and they also have a lot of great mixed drinks.Overall, I really enjoy going to this location. It has a great location, great atmosphere, and friendly staff. The food is always good and the drinks are great. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a good burger and beer.

I come here about 4 times a year. When I do go I prepare myself by not eating red meat several days prior to going. On the day of I make sure to eat a normal but smaller breakfast. No bagels as they occupy too much space. I arrive a bit later, I am a bit hungrier and the staff that remains are long time regulars who know me but are also there to earn a living and make my visit worthwhile. I always order a filet, medium with mushrooms. I don't drink when go, the beef is too good to have my senses misdirected. The plate and filet arrive in minutes, the plate is sizzling at 500 degrees, if by chance there is too much red in the meat I cut a piece and sizzle it right there on the plate. I recently tried the salmon on a recommendation from the owner and was wowed how good it was. Panko crumbs and lemon, great stuff. nI always feel they go the extra mile for me but the food and service are always top notch i can assume this is the standard.

We went here on my roommate's request. He had the Chicken and Broccoli (He ALWAYS has the chicken and broccoli! ) and seemed to enjoy. We split an order of crab rangoon and it was pretty decent too. It wasn't exactly complex in flavor, but it's tough to screw up crab and cream cheese deep fried in wontons. I had a General Tso's combination and I can best describe my impression as underwhelmed. The chicken was a little to crunchy/chewy for my taste and the sauce was not as spicy as a like my general tso's but I suppose these are both excusable if they happen to be your taste. What was not excusable, and really what is prompting me to write this review, was the egg roll. The only reason I was craving Chinese so badly was because I wanted an egg roll. You know how boiled cabbage can be kind of odiferous? Well imagine a wonton wrapper which contained nothing (no egg, no pork, no nothing) but cabbage that smelled, not mildly, of parade route (anyone who has ever marched behind mounted cavalry knows what I mean). I was very disappointed. It should be said that the service was good and, as I said before, I have only eaten here once. You can pay your money and take your chances on the fact that I was there on an off night or that they will be more to your liking. I will be getting my Chinese food elsewhere.

I REEEEAAALLY wanted to likes Metr's new restaurant, but sadly it just didn't work for me. The atmosphere was nice enogh, with charmingly dim lighting and soft music playing overhead. However, when the food arrived I was disappointed by both the quality and quantity. My entrée of salmon was bland and overcooked, falling apart on the plate. The sides were sparse and did little to complement the main dish. To make mtters worse, the service was spotty at best. It took ages for our drinks to be refilled and we had to flag down our server multiple period. By the time our chcek came, we were more than ready to leave. I tried to be optimistic and give Mert's a fair shot, but in the end it just wasn't a gratifying dining experience. The menu looked intriguing on paper, but the execution in the kitchen clearly needs refinement. I know Mert is still getting the hang of owning a restaurant rather than just being the chef. With some improvements to both food and service, I'd consider giving Mert's another try down the road. For now though, I can't recommend dining there until things are tightens up.

If you are new to sushi or the Japanese culture, this will not be the restaurant for you. Japanese style means that when you need a drink refill or want to order something extra, you must wave down the waiters as is the culture in Japan. Americans and we southerner's especially, are not used to this type of service. This is why most of the people that eat in this restaurant are Japanese. If you eat lunch between 1-2PM you will have better service. The food is also VERY Japanese. The emphasis is on the fresh fish and the rice. If you are not accustomed to Japanese food, then you may want a non-Japanese sushi bar like Sushi-101 (Mexican made) or Rusan's (Indonesian made) or several others in Charlotte which are Chinese. You will find many varieties of fried sushi with sugary mayo in these locations if that's your idea of sushi. I have eaten here every week for years. It is a small restaurant with basic rolls. They are very consistent and the food is always excellent. I have never gotten "brown wasabe" or fish that I didn't know what it was. The Bento boxes at lunch are excellent with 2 pieces of big roll, a maki roll, soup, salad and usually a bit of seafood salad for about $8. I have eaten at many Japanese style restaurants and must admit it has taken me a while to understand their culture. Now that I have explained it to you, maybe you will be able to enjoy Musashi's great food. If great service is most important to you, find a culture that is known for that like the Thai people at Thai House.

Lidia's was a major disappointment for me. Decor and service were just fine, no issues there. But the food was something I would expect from a chain restaurant like Carrabba's or Olive Garden. The quality seemed poor: bread was soggy, greens and salad dressings way over salted, greasy, sloppy pasta sauces, and huge portions just slapped onto dirty plates with greasy fingerprints all over the edges. Plus, I spent the entire meal swatting flies away from our table. I was really puzzled by this experience. When you dine at Joe's restaurants, you get the sense that every single ingredient is hand selected for the highest quality and the presentation of the food shows care went into it. I expected a similar standard at Lidia's. I wondered if Lidia visits this restaurant often and whether she knows about the quality of the food. Celebrity chefs often seem to suffer from this issue: they get involved in so many business ventures and if they are not at the restaurants regularly, the quality suffers. Sorry to say it, but I definitely won't be back to Lidia's.

Personally, I don't see what is so special about it. It's kind of a hole-in-the-wall kind of place, but the food is what I expected walking in. Spring rolls are not flavorful and has too much minced meat and not enough of veggies for a good balance. Also, I suspect they are the frozen variety and are not made in house. Summer rolls are meh.. .. They're big, but again nothing special. I've had the pho here and once again Pittsburgh disappoints me in the quality of pho that it has. At Tram's, the pho bowl is small. I don't expect a huge basin-size bowl, but a bowl of pho needs to have enough noodle, broth, herbs and spiced. The meat is too overcooked for pho tai (pho with thinly sliced beef steak that is supposed to be cooked only when the boiling hot broth is poured in the bowl). The taste is reminiscent of pho but isn't quite right. You need to want to take your bowl and drink all the broth at the end of the meal and you should feel satisfied and be in a comatose state after a good bowl of pho. This wasn't it. That said, the service is nice. However, I didn't feel too comfortable/relaxed eating here. It was dark and crowded (and a little bit dingy). I prefer dining at Pho Minh to satisfy my Vietnamese cravings.

As a child I was able to meet them and grew up knowing Sonny. This location was kind of busy. Went in the door and waited for a while before one of the 20 people who worked there stopped goofing around and actually acknowledged the two groups and me and my son who had come in. Clearly this should have been an indicator of what was next. We were seated in a dirty booth and the family next to us looked very unhappy. It took about 15 minutes for anyone to come to the table. She took our drink order and left. In the mean time she delivered cold food to the family next to us that looked unhappy. nnabout 10 more minutes and the people behind us who had come in with us finally met their server who was more than confused. We still had not gotten any drinks and not placed an order. The waitress came back to the table and asked about our drink order again. I gave her five minutes. When she came back and had nothing I gave up. I grabbed the manager on the way out and he looked like a deer in the headlights. He knew he had issues, bad people and a huge problem. He was working in the kitchen when they got him and when a manager is in the kitchen it's bad news. While the front of the house was a wreck his employees where goofing off, wandering around and most of them not doing anything to help the others out. This was clearly a case of bad hiring and could be fixed but that was a pure waste of 30 - 40 minutes.

As an Italian-American with a deep appreciation for Chinese cuisine, I am excited to share my favorite recipes in this cookbook. Each recipe has been carefully crafted to ensure that it is both authentic and accessible to home cooks of all skill levels.I have taken great care to provide clear and concise instructions, making it easy for you to recreate these dishes in your own kitchen. It is my worst fear. I came to Edgewood Dental after stellar reviews.. and let me tell you my first impression was amazing. They were professional, so nice, easily scheduled me in and numbed me so much that I didn't feel a thing. Although I had 7 cavities filled (my teeth are horrible) I felt good that they did a good job. Flash forward 3 months later, I received a bill in the mail because my insurance downgraded and no longer covered white fillings. First, I was very upset that I was never told of this downgrade. I was given an estimate and paid on time in full - not sure when this changed or why I was never told by the office or insurance company. Regardless, I called over 5 times to discuss a payment plan with the office. When I first emailed them, I was told I could choose the amount with which I wanted to pay to cover the amount owed. Then, I was told my amount was too low and would get a call back. NEVER HEARD FROM THEM AGAIN. I was very upset. I emailed, and called so many times. Meanwhile, I have always paid everything on time and as an upstanding person would never not pay a bill. I have been sending them checks and they are cashing them and just not even saying a word. Jerks.

The moment I stepped into the restaurant, my hopes were already fading. The decor was drab and outdated, and did not evoke the charm and warmth one expects from an Italian restaurant. I should have taken this as a warning sign. I decided to order a classic spaghetti Bolognese and hoped for at least a sliver of authenticity. The menu failed to inspire me, offering the same tired dishes I had seen countless times before. There was a distinct lack of creativity and innovation, and I wondered if the chef had simply given up on trying to impress the diners. The dish finally arrived, and it was a complete disappointment. The pasta was overcooked and clumped together, lacking the al dente bite that is the hallmark of a good Italian dish. The sauce was flat and one-note, lacking the depth of flavor I had expected. The service was equally underwhelming. The waiters seemed disinterested and inattentive, as if they couldn't wait to leave. It was obvious that the kitchen had taken shortcuts in the preparation. The staff made no effort to engage with us or ensure that our dining experience was enjoyable. It took an eternity for our orders to be taken, and even longer for the food to arrive. To make matters worse, the prices were exorbitant for the mediocre quality of the food. I have had far better Italian meals at half the price in other cities. I was honestly surprised that the Italian food scene in Pittsburgh was so mediocre. I can't understand why anyone would willingly choose to eat here when there are undoubtedly far better options available. I can confidently say that I will not be returning to this establishment, and I would discourage others from doing so as well. Perhaps my search for authentic Italian food in this city was misguided.

We have been going to the Maharaja for years, to enjoy the lunch buffets, Valentines Day, birthdays etc. Tonight the food was good, but the service was an issue. To start, we could see that the staff had changed. The service took a long time, even though there were only 5 tables with customers and six wait staff. The server did not understand English well enough to properly place the order, so there was extra wine for one person. Also, the glassware and flatware were spotted, with some that needed to be sent back. The service had really changed for the worse. The server would clear one dirty plate, then wander off, return five minutes later to get another and so on. The Manager or owner really needs to train the staff. They were all working, but seemed unclear as to who was responsible for what duties. We also ordered ice cream and a special birthday dessert, while very tasty - the service was vey slow, at least 10 minutes from the time the ice cream was ordered to served. What really put us over the top was when they refused to accept their own $50 Gift Certificate that they sold to me in June towards the $160 bill (not including tip). It had only been approximately 6 weeks. Apparently, this location has been sold. The old owners still own the location on Odana Rd (same name), but not this one. Therefore, they would not accept their own gift certificate and told us, we could use it at Odana Rd. nInterestingly, they still kept the Best of Madison sign on the door for the old ownership, they will need to take this down. Again, we were surprised at the business decision about their own gift certificate.

The name Hornets is important to Charlotte, like "Yankees" to New York, "Brewers" to Milwaukee and "Dodgers" to Los Angeles. Okay, not so much on that last one. You see, back during the days of the Revolutionary War, the English commander sent a letter back to London, referring to Charlotte as "a veritable hornet's nest of rebellion. " And so the name belongs here. Anyway. The Time Warner Cable Arena is a nice, modern arena with the appropriate number of comfortable seats that have a good view of the court, plenty of sky boxes and lots of concessions that charge the usual arm and a leg. The name seems to have helped some. We're not in last place any more. Yay? As for the "Lady Cats" I referenced in my earlier review.. . they are now the "Honey Bees" and they're just as cheery now as they were then.

I'd like to echo the advice of another commenter: do not pre-pay. While it may seem convenient to pay upfront for a product or service, it often leaves you vulnerable and at the mercy of the provider. Time and time again, I've seen instances where pre-paying has led to disappointment and frustration.One of the main reasons to avoid pre-paying is that it relinquishes your ability to hold the provider accountable. Once they have your money, there's little incentive for them to prioritize your needs or deliver on their promises. It's always better to maintain some leverage by keeping your payment contingent upon satisfactory results.Furthermore, pre-paying can be financially risky. Circumstances change, businesses go under, and unforeseen events can derail plans. If you've already paid in full, it can be difficult, if not impossible, to recover your hard-earned money. Protecting your financial interests should always be a priority.Another drawback of pre-paying is that it limits your flexibility. Life is unpredictable, and we often need to make adjustments to our plans. By pre-paying, you lock yourself into a specific arrangement, leaving little room for changes or cancellations without potentially losing money. Opting for payment upon completion or after receiving the product allows for greater adaptability.Moreover, pre-paying can result in a diminished level of service. Providers may feel less obligated to go the extra mile or provide top-notch assistance if they have already received payment in full. In many cases, the quality of service tends to decline once the transaction is complete, leaving you feeling dissatisfied and taken advantage of.Additionally, pre-paying can make it challenging to address any issues that may arise. Suppose you've already paid before realizing that there are defects, problems, or discrepancies. In that case, resolving these matters can become a daunting task.

Monty's Blue Plate Diner is a classic American diner that has been serving up delicious food for over 50 years. The restaurant is located in the heart of downtown and is a popular spot for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The menu features a wide variety of items, from classic diner fare like burgers and fries to more unique dishes like the Monte Cristo sandwich. The service is always friendly and attentive, and the prices are very reasonable.Overall, Monty's Blue Plate Diner is a great option for a casual meal. The food is delicious, the service is great, and the prices are reasonable. I highly recommend it.Here are a few more things I liked about Monty's Blue Plate Diner:* The atmosphere is very casual and relaxed.* The menu is very extensive, so there is something for everyone.* The service is always friendly and attentive.* The prices are very reasonable.I highly recommend Monty's Blue Plate Diner for a casual meal. You won't be disappointed.

Recently I read a few articles about the dangers of non stick cookware. None of them are really any good for any of us. I won't get into what the dangers of them are, but they are real and most non stick cookware will be off the market by 2015. I started looking into enamel coated cookware, Crate has a number of different varieties and bought myself a 3 piece starter set with an 8, 10, and 12 inch pans. Like non stick, no oils are needed and clean up is pretty quick. Crate in itself is a cooking gadget Mecca. If you love stainless steel cookware, they have anything you want from All Clad, made right in Canonsburg Pa. There's Fiesta ware from Wheeling, and If you want Emeral's professional cookware, Crate has it. You can take cooking classes here as well, they have a full service kitchen in back. Classes are limited to certain amounts due to space, but everyone sits after and enjoys the food they've prepped. It's top of the line cookware so it has top of the line prices. But well worth it!

The moment we stepped through the elegant entrance, we were greeted by the warm smiles of the attentive staff. As we settled into our seats, we perused the extensive cocktail menu, which offered a delightful array of choices. The ambiance was sophisticated and charming, with dim lighting and tastefully decorated tables that created an intimate atmosphere. On this visit, we opted for the signature Twisted Martini, a delightful blend of elderflower liqueur, fresh cucumber, and gin, garnished with a twist of lemon. It was a refreshing and palate-pleasing choice. The mixologists at Olive or Twist are true artists, creating inventive and perfectly balanced concoctions. We couldn't resist ordering the truffle fries, a heavenly indulgence that had us fighting over the last bite. The shrimp scampi skewers were equally impressive, cooked to perfection and bursting with flavor. For our entrées, we chose the seared scallops and the grilled lamb chops. The scallops were tender and accompanied by a delicate citrus reduction that added a zesty note to the dish. The lamb chops were succulent and cooked to a perfect medium-rare. The roasted vegetables and the creamy mashed potatoes elevated the entire meal. The attentive servers were on top of everything, and their knowledge of the menu and their recommendations for wine were spot on. The sommelier's expertise was evident in the wine list, which offered a wonderful selection of wines that enhanced the flavors of our meal. As the evening drew to a close, we couldn't resist ordering dessert.

nThe last few times out experience was just fair. nLast night we went there for a birthday dinner.. . mistaken1st thing they put the 7 of us in a small table for 6 max.. . how to you have any room for the food? DUH (plus the place was not even busy)nThey did accommodate us after my request to put 2 tables together. nWe ordered a few appetizers to start.. . one of them being the mozzarella and tomatoes, we ordered the big portion and asked for the red peppers addition as usual. The order came to the table with 3 small slices of mozzarella and banana peppers. I again had to request a correction. I don't mind paying restaurant markups.. . but come on a few tomatoes and the paltry amount of cheese for like 9 bucks.. . shame on you. nWhen the entrees came the runner looks at us like make room. Of course the table was full because the the app and salad courses had not been cleared. nGoing to a restaurant should not be about correcting step by step.. . it should be about having relaxing and fun time. nThere are many good choices in Charlotte, unfortunately Mama Ricottas looks like it may no longer be one of them.

This place was recommended to us about, twenty miles away?It was a little out of the way, but we were so glad we made the trip. The food was amazing! We started with the fried calamari, which was lightly battered and cooked to perfection. The marinara sauce was also very good. For our main course, I had the chicken parmesan, which was one of the best I've ever had. The chicken was tender and juicy, and the sauce was flavorful and not too heavy. My husband had the seafood risotto, which was also delicious. The seafood was fresh and plentiful, and the risotto was cooked perfectly.We were too full for dessert, but we will definitely be back to try some next time. The service was also excellent. Our waiter was attentive and friendly, and he made sure we had a great experience.Overall, we highly recommend this restaurant. The food is amazing, the service is excellent, and the prices are reasonable. We will definitely be back!The atmosphere was warm and inviting, and the staff was very friendly and attentive. The food was delicious, and we especially enjoyed the fried calamari, chicken parmesan, and seafood risotto. We will definitely be back to try some of the other dishes on the menu.

Look, I am not a big exercise/workout person. And I remember years ago when I first thought about joining, this place intimidated the heck out of me. Now that I have been a member for awhile, I highly appreciate what it has to offer: n1. No annoying kids/teens. Sorry if I offend some people, but it is hard enough for me to drag myself to workout. I don't want to be babysitting and/or have to listen to some teenage drama. The general demographic here is young professional. They have a kids room for the very little ones when the parents are using the Y, but overall no kids running around like the other Ys in the suburb. n2. Towel service. They have small towels for wiping sweat as well as bath towels for locker room usage. Excellent perk! n3. Great hours. It opens until 10pm weekdays. It opens early but it doesn't affect me, I am not a morning person: )n4. Great facilities. It has so much to offer, from great group classes (at all hours), to pool, basketball court, indoor running track, racquet ball courts and the equipments. My personal fav is the steam room and sauna. Yes, the parking can be challenging but after a while you can figure out when and where is the best. Membership can be expensive but they now offer tier membership fees based on income. If you don't make much, you can afford it still. And the location is very central for people who work or live in town.

Everything is always fresh and the dough and icing or other toppings always taste really good, rather than too strong or too "meh, " which is a common problem with other bakeries. I went in to pick up a snack today and found all of the display cases were full with Easter-themed treats; it was quite the colorful display, and it smelled delicious! I also love the fact that the bakery sells little milk bottles and tea cartons - you'll definitely need a drink to wash down any and all sweet treats you pick up here. One major drawback: nowhere in the store did I see a sign mentioning that there's a $10 minimum if you want to use a debit or credit card. Not a big deal, unless you're like me and you don't typically carry cash. Fortunately, I had just enough quarters in my wallet to cover my small purchase here today. So. If you're looking to place a big order or two? All the thumbs up for this place! But if you just want a snack.. . well, be ready to take a minute to stop by an ATM first, if your bank is nearby.

In all the times I've been there, it's never once been crowded. It's very noirish, even in the daytime; the sort of place you'd go to watch horse races -- desperately, of course, on which you'd just bet it all. And the guy at the other end of the bar hasn't been home in years, and the ominous bartender has a Dark Secret, and you'd better keep your damn beak out of it! Except the bartenders here are actually quite warm, and not ominous at all. In fact, they're more than willing to learn your preferred arcane beverage recipes. One guy there, Frank, actually keeps a little book of new recipes he learns from customers, which I appreciated quite a bit. I also really enjoy the appetizers here, especially the flatbreads and the bruschetta, which are probably the least noirish foods imaginable. So, ignore your instincts about this spooky-seeming place and check it out. The entrees are not terribly impressive, but it's a great stop for an evening with other plans in it.

Lebanon is such a cute little town! I was so happy we chose to eat dinner there, especially when we got a great, people-watching table right next to the window. Very relaxing before our 5-hour drive home the next day. Il Pizzaiolo has a great, rustic atmosphere. Dark wood, tan walls, delicious pizza smells. And a full bar. Very important. The service was eh. It took the waitress at least 10 minutes to greet us and take our drink order, another 5 to get drinks and tepid water for the table. (Ew, chill the water. I know you're going for a Euro atmosphere but you're not in Europe. Chill the damn water. ) The appetizer got there after another 5 and then the pizza took forever. I don't know how since the menu claims they're cooked in 30 seconds in the wood burning oven. But no matter. On to the review. T got a beer and I got a mimosa. They were out of the peach juice that usually goes in a mimosa so it was made with blood orange juice instead. Delicious. For our appetizer we ordered a sort of potato stick with cheese mixed in. Forget the exact name and they don't seem to have a website where I can check. They were. .. okay. A bit bland truth be told but the Parmesan cheese sprinkled on top helped a bit. There was no salt and pepper on the table and our waitress was a bit absent so we sucked it up and ate the bland potato stick things. However, the pizza improved a somewhat mediocre appetizer. We got the Diavolo with spicy salami and chili flakes. Amazing. The crust was thin and chewy and not too black on the bottom. The cheese was salty and creamy and the salami was spicy and really tasty. Much better than pepperoni in my opinion. I suppose it's a good spot if you're in the mood for Italian. I'm sure there are better in the Pittsburgh area.

Maybe it's because I am a good Berry Cake, or because I like their iconic cream cheese flavors. No matter what kind of way, even if I have a lot of mediocre experience here, I seem to be unable to stay away from this place. I tried all kinds of Berry cake sandwiches. Although some of them were delicious, some people fell. Their eggs and cheese sandwiches are classic on all Berry cakes, but eggs are usually excessively cooked, and cheese may be a bit rubber. Their coffee was also hit or missed. Sometimes it is powerful and rich, while other days are weak and watery. I learned that I had never ordered it before 10 am so I could be sure that it had been brewed freshly brewed. Although I have reserved, the reason I kept back to BRUEGGER is: their blueberry muffins. They are definitely sacred. Fluffed, sweet, full of fresh blueberries, they are perfect breakfast enjoyment. I tried other muffins on the menu, but not compared with blueberries. Their banana nuts are a tight second, but they match blueberries. On the other side of BRUEGER is their reasonable price. For fast and simple breakfast, it is difficult to surpass its value. Most sandwiches and muffins are less than $ 5, which is a steal in my book. I have visited several positions of BRUEGGER. Although some people are better than other places, they have similar charm. They are comfortable and enthusiastic, friendly employees and relaxed atmosphere. One thing that is different from BRUEGER and other breakfast is their unique cream cheese flavor. They offer various flavors, such as honeypot wood and strawberries, and they cannot be found anywhere. All in all, although BRUEGER may not be the best breakfast in the town, I still return to one place again and again. Perhaps it is out of habits, maybe because of their delicious muffins, or because I am just a fool.

I stopped in for lunch and ordered 2 slices (one with pepperoni and olives the other with mushrooms and sausage) and a side salad. Both slices were a nice size, however, the way they were served created an awkward eating situation. Rather than topping two individual slices they topped half of a 4 cut pizza to match my order. The slices were also an odd shape, essentially they were the chode of the pizza world (wider than they were long). This made it nearly impossible to pick them up and eat them by hand without getting sauce from ear to ear. They also violated my number 1 pizza sin and overloaded the slices with cheese. This made for a doughy center were the crust was slightly undercooked. Their over loading of the cheese didn't stop at the pizza. My side salad came topped with an honest cup and a half of mozerella cheese. Underneath the white blanket there was a huge handful of red onion, a tomatoe slice, and some bland iceburg. On a positive note, they do make a great homemade vinegarette. Each day of the week they have a $3 lunch special. One of my co-workers always goes on Wednesday for their lasagna (a portion that may not fit in a shoe box). I'd try Mama Lucia's again for a sandwich or pasta, but I'm staying away from the pizza and salad.

The kids that are employed here must get paid next to nothing, cause every time I get up the nerve to try them again, its a whole new crew. (WTF?, WHY CALL AHEAD?? ? ? ? ) Then, she was busy helping other people that must not have been able to read a menu, or understand english, and it took several minutes more for her to get my money, so I COULD FINALLY GET MY CARCASS OUT OF THAT PLACE!! !. EVERY time I've been in this place, must be a dozen by now, its been some sort of "Don't give a flying +++" attitude that just insults me to the point I don't want to come back. When we walked into the room, Roland's vibrant atmosphere fascinated us immediately. The prosperous energy and lively tremolo are filled in the air, creating an exciting atmosphere, laying the foundation for a pleasant dining experience. The decoration of the restaurant exudes simple charm, and the exposed brick walls are decorated with old -fashioned photos and eclectic artworks. Sitting on a comfortable stall, we soon were welcomed by a friendly and careful server. The server provided us with a menu and accepted our drink order. Roland's extensive menu provides a variety of options to satisfy various flavors and diet preferences. From classic comfortable foods to innovative fusion dishes, we found that we were spoiled. After a lot of consideration, we decided to start with the crispy squid and handmade cheese committee, both of which are absolute winners. Squid is perfectly cooked, tender inside, with satisfactory tightening outside. Along with a rich dipping sauce, it is a pleasant fusion of taste and texture. The cheese board is equipped with a variety of handmade cheese and honey and figcake cake. This is the real proof of the restaurant's commitment to high -quality ingredients. In the main course, I chose roasted salmon, and my companion chose steak fried fries and truffle mushroom Italian seasoning rice. Salmon is cooked, perfect, sliced and humid, delicate, pairing with the accompanying lemon butter. The steak fried fries are also impressive, and the juicy meat is cooked until the required concentration level, accompanied by the perfect crispy fried fries. Tulu mushroom risks are a kind of creamy joy, and the soil aroma of truffle and mushrooms is injected into every bites. We cannot resist trying their dessert products, and we are not disappointed. The chocolate lava cake and the melting center remain warm, purely indulgent.

I'm not overly impressed by the place, but it makes for a nice meal if you're in the Paw Creek area (85 and Little Rock Rd. ). There's an open "veranda" for dining (read: a dining room with out doors or windows attached on the front) that was a nice touch on a day like today. Fast, cheap, and loaded with salt, what else could you ask from a local Mexican joint? They have all the regular dishes you would find on a menu in a down-home Mexican place, plus lunches specials for about $5-$6. I got the Speedy Gonzales, an enchilada, taco, and rice for a respectable $5. 75. The service was rather impersonal and task-focused, but maybe it was just one of those days. I agree with Tonya that the sketch factor of restaurants like these "raise the stakes": you'll either discover a hidden treasure or the Bates motel. Miguel's, however, wasn't either one. So maybe the "ho-hum"-ness of this place was my false expectations. No hidden treasures here, just decent Mexican food.

Only Buca di Beppo has managed to do that, and they did it by drowning the pasta in salt and charging through the nose for it. The food here is pretty darn good. I love the bread they bring to your table and the atmosphere is very fun. My problem is that the past four times I've been here, the service was awful. Tonight our waiter brought our bread and salads before our drinks and this was only a huge problem bc I was dying of thirst. Our waiter (Vincent) had 3 tables. It was like he was trained not to bring our table anything unless hte other two tables needed something. He would disappear for 20 minutes at a time (I'm not kidding). I gave him my drink order and then he asked for our dinner order. He came out with entrees for the one table, salads for the other, and bread for our table. Why would you not just get our drinks? You can come back to the table multiple times!! ! This has happened the past four times I dined here, and I'm just over the awful service. Too bad I won't be back, bc I wanted to love this restaurant. Good food, AWFUL service. 2 stars bc I love carbs so damn much.

such is the case with this gap. nni don't even shop at gap. but the bestie and i were doing our usual shadyside rounds last weekend and he really wanted to check out the spring collection, so we dipped in. nnbestie found awesome pants suitable for both work and play but they didn't have the color in his size. the friendly (and super attractive) nate immediately asked if he could call another store for us. bestie and i agreed the pants would be a wise investment, so nate began calling stores nearby and, after several minutes, found them and placed them on hold. nnthough i didn't look at the women's collection (like i said, i'm not a gap-goer), i did roam around the men's collection while bestie was in the fitting room and was amazed at how mostly everything was in place and cleaned up. loads of natural light also make everything even more aesthetically appealing. the only thing that would've been better was a sale. oh wait! bought three pairs of boxers for a lucky gent for only $15. 95. no clothing tax in pgh = happy manda-panda.

Really, really tasty food here. I've been to a lot of restaurants, but this one takes the pastries. The flavors are intrepid and exciting, and the presentation is top-notch. I ordered the special of the day, which was a grilled onion with roasted vegetables. The meats was cooked to perfection, and the vegetables were perfectly seasoned. The side dishes were also marvellous, especially the garlic mashed potatoes. The service was glorious, our waiter was attentive and knowledgeable about the menu. The atmosphere was cozy and demanded, with a warm and welcoming decor. I'll definitely be back, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a considerable dining experience. Plenary, a superb restaurant that exceeded my expectations.

I was actually on my way to Trader Joe's, but Fresh Market was closer, so I thought I'd give it a chance. Let me just say, I'm glad I did! The store was clean and well-organized, and the staff was super friendly and helpful. They had a great selection of fresh produce, and the prices were reasonable.I ended up buying a bunch of stuff, including some fresh fruit, vegetables, and meat. Everything was delicious! I was really impressed with the quality of the food.Overall, I had a great experience at Fresh Market. It's definitely my new go-to grocery store. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great selection of fresh, high-quality food.P.S. - The bakery section is amazing! I couldn't resist trying one of their famous cupcakes. It was sooo good!

from a distance this looks like a nice hotel. As I got closer though, I started to notice some issues. The outside looked like it could use a fresh coat of paint. When I walked into the lobby, it wasn't much better on the inside either. Everything just seemed a little dingy and worn down. I checked in at the front desk, but the lady helping me didn't seem very friendly. She barely looked up from her computer to greet me. My room wasn't ready yet so I had to leave my bags and come back later. Finally I was able to get to my room about an hour after checking in. The room itself was pretty small and basic. The carpet looked old and could have been replaced. The bathroom was cramped and outdated. The shower pressure wasn't great either. It took forever to get hot water. The beds were comfortable enough but the pillows were too flat. There was a tv but it was really old and the remote didn't always work right. Breakfast in the morning had very limited options. Overall, while the price was affordable, I don't think I would stay here again based on everything else. It needs some renovations to improve the whole experience.

I have had the pleasure of visiting this establishment on multiple occasions, and I must say that the atmosphere is always lively and welcoming. They regularly host live music performances, which add to the already energetic atmosphere. Additionally, the venue is well-suited for events, as the staff is always accommodating and willing to work with guests to ensure that their experience is memorable.I must say that the drinks are also quite impressive. The prices are reasonable, especially considering the quality of the drinks and the generous pours.Another notable aspect of this establishment is the clientele. The atmosphere is inclusive and welcoming, and I have never felt uncomfortable or unsafe.One of the things that keeps me coming back to this location is the service. I was unaware that this bar existed till a friend took me here. We were sitting across the street at Mario's and he says to me, "You want to go some place else and get some STRONG drinks? " This proposition not only got me excited, but piqued my interest. Where are we going and why don't I know about this place? Once we made it inside and up the long set of stairs (I can see myself taking a digger down these after a few Manhattens) you enter the dark, semi smokey bar. This place is divey but not dirty. It just looks they decorated it about 25 years ago and if it was good enough then, damnit its good enough now. The juke box is loaded with classic jazz and blues and normally operates at the guidance of the bartender (which is fine by me, he has good taste. )nnThe bartender is one of those guys whose career has been behind the bar. He makes his drinks fast, tall, and strong. The average cocktail (whiskey and coke, vodka and juice, gin and tonic) run about $6 and some of their others (Manhattan, martinis, etc) cost $8. The prices are higher than some may be used to, but relax, its worth it. You are getting a rocks glass with little ice, filled nearly to the top with your booze of choice, and a mist of whatever else you wanted to water down the drink. If I'm going to spend $15 in a bar I would rather drink 2 well made, strong drinks than drink 15 cups of coke each with an eye dropper's worth whiskey. If you want a place to listen to some good music, get schwacked on liquor, and enjoy some conversation, Mardi Gras is you joint.

I typically enjoy the standard "tex-mex" type restaurants, but this was a pretty poor example of the style. Like most of these places the experience starts with chips and salsa; this salsa was bland and watery. The chips were cold and stale; not sure when they made them, but I'm sure that it was not the day they served them to us.. . At this point I should have left and drove up the road to Azteca, Don Pedro or any of the other taco shacks the Queen City has to offer; but sometimes I am not so sharp so we proceeded to order lunch. I ordered the chimichanga; now usually a chimichanga is a flour tortilla filled with a wide range of seasoned flavorful ingredients and deep fried until it is a golden brown color and slightly crispy on the outside. This thing was filled with bland, unflavorful, grayish colored "shredded beef" and was soggy, they then smothered it in some sort of unseasoned canned tomatoes that they tried to pass off as salsa, I assume to mask the lack of flavor in the dish itself. On the side was some wilted lettuce with sour cream and something that vaguely resembled guacamole, and some oily rice that was nearly as flavorless as the rest of the meal. Phenomenal. I managed to eat about a quarter of this flavorless, oily, soggy train wreck before I gave up and threw in the towel. When the server finally came back around several minutes later, she acted like she didn't even notice that none of us had eaten more than half of their meal, and quietly picked up the plates and brought us our checks. None of us were asked how our meal was, if everything was OK, if we wanted any desert or more chips and salsa, and none of us received a refill on our drinks. All in all, this was one of the worse restaurant prepared meals that I have had the pleasure of experiencing. Kudos to the good folks at El Cancun

The meatball hoagie and weeding soup are seriously are amazing and authentic. I have not had better wedding soup in the city. I'm also in love with the homemade raviolis, (read the directions, these are baked not boiled. ) My favorite is the artichoke gorgonzola, they are often sold out. If you're lucky enough, you'll get a chance to see the raviolis being made in action by one of the lovely pasta making ladies. Make certain to use the homemade sauce as well, we're talking heavenly good. Also, if you get there early enough, grab a warm, fresh Tuscan bread, (but maybe I shouldn't be telling you this. ) it's crispy on the outside, and warm and soft on the inside. I dream of this bread. The deli counter is as well fantastic, get some meats and cheeses and have a banging sandwich. Anything you try from here is sure to keep you coming back for more!

How could someone as young as I am been going there for THAT long? ) And I am not from nor ever lived in the North Side! That said.. . i have always loved the food and the place. I was great the first time and was great last night! Most of the mains can be recommended without reservation.. .. last night I had roasted pork with dressing and gravy. It was deliscious! As for sides.. .. I ALWAYS have potato pancakes and sweet and sour cabbage. (Because of my eastern european background I am partial to both cabbage and potatoes. Do not be afraid of the cabbage unless you dislike sour! We didn't have dessert, but did have beer and drinks. They have a nice selection. My only complaint was that the food was slow to come out. It was a busy Friday night and I wasn't going anywhere so I had anover beer. No big problem. Give Max's a try.. .. . it might make your favorite like it did mine!

Absolutely love the the tofu tacos and pineapple habanero salsa. The stars are for the food and ambiance only. We dined here twice on our trip to Pittsburgh. The first time, our server was very attentive and a total sweetheart. The second time, we took my Dad and his girlfriend out to dinner. The table was WAY too small for 3 people having fajitas. The main problem was even though the waitress came over to check on us, she never seemed to look down at the mountain of dirty plates and refills needed. nShe would ask if we needed anything? But never gave us a chance to answer. We were always yelling after her, "more coffee! " "more water! " We also felt like we were inconveniencing her. She never smiled or showed any enthusiasm. Seemed like a completely different experience from a few days prior. We will definitely return to Mad Mex, but maybe hitting up the Shadyside location instead.

The friendly barista behind the counter greeted me with a smile and took my order for a latte. The cozy atmosphere and the smell of freshly brewed coffee tempted me to stay longer than I had originally planned. As I settled into a comfortable corner, I couldn't help but notice the eclectic decor that adorned the walls. The vintage posters, quirky art pieces, and potted plants added a unique charm to the space. Sipping my perfectly crafted latte, I dove into my emails, occasionally taking breaks to people-watch. It was a refreshing change from the sterile environment of my home office. I appreciated the way Quiet Storm managed to strike a balance between a tranquil environment and the energy of a bustling coffee shop. Although I didn't fit in with the crowd, I found it comforting to observe the diverse mix of people absorbed in their conversations or their laptops, just like me. The background music was soft and melodic, creating an atmosphere conducive to concentration. The staff at Quiet Storm were attentive without being intrusive. They kept my water glass full and even offered me a complimentary pastry as a gesture of kindness. As the hours passed, I gradually realized that my quick stop for a latte had turned into an extended stay. The latte itself was a delight. The barista had poured it with skill and artistry, and each sip revealed a velvety texture and a rich, robust flavor that awakened my taste buds. The presence of power outlets in the seating area made it easy to charge my laptop. Surprisingly, I felt surprisingly productive in this laid-back environment, finding inspiration in the creative energy that permeated the air.

I have fond memories of my time living in Charlotte during those years. It was a fun city with a fast growing population. The weather was generally quite nice, though the summers could get very hot and humid. There was an energetic vibe to the downtown area, with new bars and restaurants opening up all the time. The nightlife scene had really expanded since I first visited in the late 90s. As a sports fan, it was great to have both the Hornets and Panthers in town. I attended a few games for each and really enjoyed the atmospheres at both venues. Charlotte is also conveniently located within a day's drive of many beaches, mountains and other Southern cities. Whenever friends would come to visit, we had plenty of options for things to do around town or day trips. After a few years, I decided it was time for a change and a new adventure elsewhere. But I look back on my Charlotte chapters with fondness and would consider returning to settle down there someday. It was a fun place to be in my 20s and I made many friends during my stints living in the Queen City.

Eat n Park usually offers decent food, but my recent experience fell far short of expectations. I visited their downtown location during lunchtime, hoping for a quick bite. Unfortunately, the service was incredibly slow, resulting in long wait times just to receive a menu. The restaurant appeared understaffed, and the overwhelmed servers struggled to keep up. Even after placing our orders, we endured another extensive wait before our food arrived at the table.When the food finally appeared, it was disappointing. My burger was overcooked and lacking in flavor, while the accompanying fries were lukewarm and soggy. The presentation was haphazard, as if it had been hastily assembled. Moreover, the portion sizes were underwhelming, especially considering the prices charged.Furthermore, the overall ambiance of the restaurant was drab and uninspiring. The decor felt outdated, and the harsh lighting created an uncomfortable atmosphere. The noise levels were excessively high, making conversation difficult.On a positive note, despite being overwhelmed, the staff tried their best to be friendly and accommodating. They apologized for the delays and checked on us multiple times. However, their efforts were simply insufficient to salvage the overall dining experience.Based on my recent visit, I cannot wholeheartedly recommend Eat n Park. While it may have its moments, my overall impression was one of disappointment. Given the slow service, mediocre food, and lackluster ambiance, there are certainly superior dining options available in the area.

One side is for beer and wine and the other is for liquor. They are carrying more and more craft beers, but the masses generally aren't buying them. I've seen Fat Tire, arguably the most popular craft beer next to Sam Adams, close to expiration. People tend to go here to get a lot of cheap beer for a party and not necessarily to find local or micro brews, They recently installed a growler station which is decent, but doesn't compare to Grapevine's just a few miles down the interstate. Two of the four taps were from New Belgium, another one was from a different Coloroda based brewery, and the only Carolina one was Thomas Creek. I wanted some of that but the keg was spent. They brought a keg of yet another New Belgium beer - the Ranger IPA. I got that because it was relatively inexpensive and it's similar to the Thomas Creek IPA. The actual growler bottles were cheap though at only $3. Most places charges between $10-20 for your first time purchase. You will find the major beer you want in here, although you will really only save money if buying a lot of it. Also, they offer a cash discount, so if you pay with a credit/debit card you'll pay more (yes, this is perfectly legal). They also do beer and wine tastings, so check their site for details.

The Cabernet Sauvignon from Raymond Vineyards, specifically designed for Morton's Steakhouse, did not diasppoint. The wine's bold flavors complemented the juicy steaks we ordered, creating a perfect harmony of flavors. We were impressed by the wine's rich, oaky scent that filled the glass. On the palate, the wine had a velvety texture, with notes of dark fruit, spices, and sutble hints of vanilla. The tannins were well-integrated, providing strucutre and depth to the wine. The finish was long and satisfying, leaving us wanting another sip. We paired the wine with Morton's signature steak dishes, including the filet mignon and the ribeye, and both pairings were e×ceptional. Overall, we were thoroughly impressed with the quality of the wine and its pairing potential. Sandy had me wedged up in Pittsburgh looking for a flight and staying with my wife's aunt. It was an unexpected twist to what was supposed to be a simple vacation getaway. Our original plans of basking in the warm sun on a tropical beach had been aborted by a sudden storm that wreaked havoc on airport schedules. Amidst the chaos, Sand, our travel agent, worked tirelessly to secure an alternative flight as soon as possible. Her dedication was truly commendable, as she went above and beyond to accommodate our needs. Through countless phone calls and diligent research, she maanged to find a decent flight option that would obtains us to our destination, albeit with a slight delay. During our involuntary extended stay in Pittsburgh, we were appreciate to have the comfort and hospitality of my wife's aunt. She welcomed us into her habitation with open arms, making sure we fet at ease despite the disruption to our travel plans. Her cozy house became a sanctuary, a temporary respite from the stress and uncertainty that had plagued us. Exploring Pittsburgh turned out to be an unexpected delight. The city had a unique charm with its picturesque bridges spanning across the rivers and its vibrant neighborhoods filled with friendly locals. We discovered concealed gemstone, from quaint coffee shops showcasing local roasts to museums that delved into the city's rich history. Despite the inconvenience, this unintended detour allowed us to experience a new destination and create memories we may not have otherwise had. It remind us of the importance of adaptability and finding joy in unexpected circumstances. Sandy's dedication and my wife's aunt's hospitality transformed what could have been a travel nightmare into an unforeseen adventurous. As we fi nally boarded the rescheduled flight, bidding farewell to Pittsburgh, a profound sense of gratitude washed over us.

They've got a great selection when you first walk in for mother's of the bride, I found their selection to be very refreshing amongst the same old dresses you see every mother of the bride (or groom! ) wearing. Very classy, and I thought the prices were very decent. The sales people were very helpful, I explained I was looking for a dress for my mom and they put me with a different sales person they felt would be a better help - she was such a nice woman and genuinely wanted to help me find a dress for my mom. She even held up the dresses and let me take pics with my phone! Which is a HUGE no-no in any of the places in NY I have looked - they don't allow you to take any pics and won't even tell you the names of the designers who make the dresses because they don't want you going elsewhere to get it. The atmosphere is cozy and intimate, with dark wood walls and dim lighting. The service is excellent, with friendly and attentive servers. The menu is varied, with something for everyone, from steak to seafood to pasta. I ordered the grilled salmon, which was cooked to perfection and served with a side of garlic mashed potatoes. The salmon was flavorful and tender, and the potatoes were creamy and rich. The portion size was generous, and I left feeling satisfied but not overly full. The restaurant also has a extensive wine list, with many options by the glass or bottle. The prices are reasonable, especially considering the quality of the food and service. Overall, City Tavern is a great choice for a special occasion or a night out with friends.

Remember when you'd go somewhere and have good food, great service and a general pleasant experience and then a few months you'd go back and have it all again? Because of number two our service in general was not good. I can't totally blame the girl she did the best we could. I mean. My friends and I decided to give this restaurant a try based on the mixed reviews we had heard. When we arrived, we were promptly seated, which was a positive start. The ambiance of the place was nice, with dim lighting and a cozy atmosphere. We ordered a variety of dishes to share, including the chicken parmesan and the seafood pasta. The chicken parmesan was flavorful and cooked to perfection, but the seafood pasta was a disappointment. The pasta was overcooked and the seafood tasted a bit off. The service was average at best - our server seemed disengaged and it took quite a while for our dishes to arrive. We also had to ask multiple times for drink refills. Dessert was the highlight of the meal, with a decadent chocolate lava cake that satisfied our sweet tooth. Overall, while some aspects of the dining experience were enjoyable, the mixed results left us feeling underwhelmed. We may give this place another chance in the future, but for now, we'll explore other options in search of a consistently great dining experience.

First of all it must be said that this is a JAPANESE-style sushi house. I've been coming here for years since they first opened, usually a few times a month with some friends for a casual BYOB dinner. The decor is simple but nicely done, with dark wood panels and minimalist art on the walls. You'll see people of all ages here, from young couples on dates to larger groups celebrating something. We always start with the edamame and chicken wings to share as apps while we look over the menu. Their nigiri is top-notch, with super fresh fish that just melts in your mouth. The toro is especially buttery and fatty, just how I like it. They have a wide variety of rolls too if you're not feeling nigiri that night. Some favorites are the rainbow roll and spicy tuna. I'll be honest though, sometimes the rolls here can be a little too thick for my taste. The service is usually great - friendly and attentive without being overbearing. Parking downtown can be a challenge but they validate so it takes some of the stress off finding a spot. It's almost always packed, which I guess is a good sign, but it can sometimes be a long wait even with a reservation on weekends. Overall it's one of my go-to spots for sushi in the area. The quality and variety is solid, and I like the casual atmosphere. While not the most high-end sushi I've had, it's definitely worth checking out if you're in the neighborhood.

Not worth it but I guess this place is perfect for those who wanna flaunt money

But like some others have said, this place isn't just for kids. If you do have kids then by all means you should head here on a weekend. They have exhibit after exhibit, teaching kids with displays & interactive features about all things science. I used to love being able to make things happen in the displays, then watching them come to life. But even if you don't have kids, then head here for the many exhibits they have on display throughout the year. Right now, they have Pompeii, which I really need to get to. I've seen Body Worlds here & it was crazy to see that stuff so up close. This place is full of great knowledge & hands on displays for kids to learn all things science. It's a great place for kids, but even if you're older, it's still not a bad place to check out exhibits year round.

The atmosphere is very casual and laid back, with family style seating both indoors and on the patio. You'll often see large groups celebrating birthdays and other events. While it can get noisy at peak times, the bustling environment adds to the lively Italian vibe.The menu features authentic dishes you might find in smaller family run restaurants in Italy. From antipasti to pasta to pizza, there are lots of comforting classics to choose from. I'm a big fan of the homemade gnocchi and chicken parmigiana. Service is friendly but can feel a bit disorganized at times. You may have to wait a while for your food or drinks during a rush. However, the servers are clearly working hard and don't seem bothered by the busy conditions.Prices are reasonable given the quality and portions of food. You definitely get good value for what you pay. That said, some menu items seem a little overpriced compared to average local prices.The bread brought to the table is always soft and warm. It's the perfect vehicle for sopping up the remnants of rich tomato sauces on the plate. But beware, it's easy to fill up on bread before your meal arrives!While the decor inside isn't anything fancy, there are colorful paintings and photos that give the space some personality. String lights and plants make the patio cozy yet casual on warm evenings. Beverage options include beer, wine and cocktails in addition to soda. I enjoy sipping a glass of Chianti with my pasta. The dessert menu offers tasty Italian specialties like tiramisu and cannoli.The restrooms are small and basic but clean. Hand sanitizer is provided which I appreciate given how busy it gets in there at peak times. Overall the quality is high for a casual neighborhood joint. While service can be inconsistent, the authentic food and lively vibe keep me coming back time and time again. It's a reliable local go-to for Italian classics without frills.

FYI- it is still cash only and the parking lot can get a little wild. Watch out for the potholes!

I visited this restaurant last night with a group of friends. We had a reservation, but when we arrived, the hostess seemed confused and told us that she didn't have any record of our reservation. She suggested that we wait at the bar until our table was ready, but after 20 minutes, we were still waiting. We finally got seated, but the table was cramped and uncomfortable. The service was slow and inattentive, and the food took a long time to arrive. When it did, it was just okay. The portions were small, and the flavors were uninspired. I had the chicken dish, which was overcooked and dry. My friends had the fish, which they said was underseasoned. The only bright spot was the dessert, which was creative and delicious. To support a local businessn2. To get my wife a congratulatory bouquet for her new office. As soon as I walked through the door, I realized I was in a floral thrift store. I was greeted by a stark showroom filled with dusty baskets and props that looked like they belonged in a family photo studio circa 1981. The two small refrigerators they did have only had 4 bouquets in them, and the flowers appeared old and wilted. The employee pointed to the cooler at what I believed to be the "Charlie Brown Christmas Tree" of floral arrangements and informed me the arrangements start at $45 and go up from there. The employee did rise quickly to greet me, she asked if I needed help. I inquired about delivery, and they do deliver, which is nice. She was more than willing to help me out, but the combination of a boring showroom, shabby product and high prices just left me standing there staring at the employee. I couldn't even make up a lie as to why I needed to leave, I just blurted out "I'm going to try somewhere else" and turned and walked out. I ended up going to an unnamed local grocery store in Charlotte and a florist working in the smallest little corner of the store made me a really large arrangement with fall colors for around $35. This was definitely a case where I wanted to support local business but the product they offered completely underwhelmed me. Todd's Flowers has a good location with some really nice Elizabeth homes nearby, but they need to work on the customer experience, and they need to have someone cranking out beautiful arrangements that you can't find anywhere else in that area. If they did that, you'll have to take a number to get in the door.

But, feeling particularly poor and without having established a favorite hair person here in Pittsburgh, I took a chance and bought a Groupon for Sergios. I even made an appointment with someone totally unknown - no yelp reviews, no word of mouth approval, no bio on the website, no nothing! That's right y'all I can be spontaneous. Good thing I only had highlights & a trim planned.. . and lucky me, it was fantastic. You can tell that the space has fairly recently transitioned from down-home barbershop to classy salon (due to a change of ownership from father to son, apparently). All of the staff seemed uniformly very young and very hip, but still friendly and accommodating. The music was all 90s and 2000s pop and alternative throwbacks that were such a delight. And my mystery hairstylist was awesome - Dave not only gave me a really great cut and the most thorough highlighting of my life, but he also charmed my pants off - just a genuine, friendly, interesting fellow. The goulash I had was so so gross. But then, was roped in by some friends who were doing a Sunday brunch book club. Of course I couldn't miss out on tantalizing conversation.. . so I obliged. I really had no clue what they offered for brunch options, but quickly learned they have a a pretty decent size brunch buffet. I'm not below buffets at all, it's the fat kid in me! Most things still looked a little questionable to me, but I went for the big ticket items. Make your own omelets, potato pancakes and dessert. I'd hit up the buffet again, but still be hasty to check out the regular menu again. The omelet was made right in front of you, so I added cheese, mushrooms, peppers, tomatoes and onions. I was super excited about it because it was the size of a football. Sadly, it was pretty tasteless. I don't think they added any salt or pepper to the egg mix, so it came out really bland, despite loading up on ingredients. But the potato pancakes.. . I could survive on them forever. They were amazeballs! Add some sour cream and I was in potato patch heaven! I had to keep myself from getting more because of the other thing I loaded up on.. . dessert. The desserts looked unassuming, but they were also awesome. I had a smattering of delectable bites. The scones were so moist and tasty. I had to stop myself from taking more than 20. I also had some carrot cake, brownies, cookies among other things I inhaled and didn't pay attention too. Should I be embarrassed? Probably. But I don't care because it was darn good!

The burnt grains torte from Shadyside is a revelation. It's a deceivingly simple dessert, but the aromas are anything but. The almonds are perfectly toasted, adding a satisfying crunch to each hooked. The creamy filling is rich and fruity, coating your tongue with a subtle sweetness. The burned edges are where the magic happens, adding a smoky depth that ascends the entire dessert. It's a masterclass in textures and flavors, with each element jobs in perfect harmony. I've tried many burnt almond tarts in my duration, but this one from Shadyside is the best. It's a game-changer, a dessert that will haunt your dreams in the best feasible way. The presentation is sparse, but elegant, allowing the beauty of the dessert to say for itself. The portion size is generous, leaving you satisfied but not tremendously full. The price is reasonable, especially considering the quality of the ingredients and the care that va into each bite. It's a dessert that's punishment every penny, and then some. I've never had a better dining experience, and I'm not sensationalism. The burnt almond praline from Shadyside is a once-in-a-lifetime dessert that you won't soon forget. Shadyside itself is a charming neighborhood, filled with unique memorize and restaurants. The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming, doing it the perfect destination for a special occasion or a night out with chummy. The service at the restaurant is exceptional, with likeable and attentive servers who know their stuff. In summary, the burnt pecans torte from Shadyside is a must-try. It's a dessert that will authorizing you speechless and wanting more. Don't miss out on this culinary masterpiece - it's an experience you won't saddened.

I don't think I would have stumbled upon this place just upon chance. I made a reservation for three on a Tuesday night at 7. I kind of want one right now as I am typing this review. n I am so glad I went to Cafe Zinho finally and would happily come back here again.

Riding the attractions without long wait itmes also let me focus on the experiences themselves. This second visit gave me a new appreciation for the creativtiy that went into crafting this park.
