There are so many other movies out there that are best than this one. Don't waste your time on this one. I'm conferring this movie a score of 1 out of 10. It's eden of the worst movies I've ever seen.

I don't know what other people see in it. There's always a line out the door, so I rarely end up going there. Why wait when there are 600 million other places within walking distance? It's cash only, which is basically a business's way of saying "Hello, customer. I really hate you, and want to make sure you have to go out of your way to find a way to pay me. " It's like when someone intentionally gets a 2-door car when a 4-door model is available. You only do that if you really hate your passengers. The food is, well, it's okay! But just okay. The pancakes are super-greasy. They're not bad, though. I do have to put in a word for their corned beef hash, though, because evidently that is excellent. I would like to one day try their lunch/dinner food, though. One thing I do love about Pamela's is the price. It's dirt cheap, and that's great. But get a credit machine! It's not like you can't afford it! Stop abusing your customers!

Your Friday night just got a lot more exciting! The restaurant was busy, but not jam packed on an impromptu Friday night dinner date. While we weren't dressed to the nines, they were ok with letting us in! There is a lot to choose from on the menu, but the way it is divided makes it much more navigable. It is divided into appetizers, mid courses, salads, cheese courses, entrees, and specials. We began with the Tega Hills bibb lettuce salad with warm duck confit, as well as the Moroccan Kefta meatballs. The salad was scrumptious. It was really working that whole sweet and salty thing. Meatballs were not my pick, but WOW they were good. Served with a charmoula sauce which is heavy on the garlic, parsley and cumin, in a very good way. Per our waitress' recommendation (who was GREAT by the way), I had the pan seared Australian sea bass. It was served on top of a diced butternut squash with ginger brown butter. It was light yet decadent at the same time. Our waitress gave great recommendations and was totally enthusiastic about the menu. I love it when people get as excited about food as me. We really enjoyed our experience and would be back in a flash.

For starters, the place is charming. As soon as you walk in, you're greeted by the warm, inviting atmosphere. The decor is elegant and understated, with just the right touch of whimsy. The service is top-notch, with friendly and attentive servers who make sure your every need is met. The menu is diverse and exciting, with dishes that blend traditional flavors with modern twists.I ordered the special of the day, which was a delicious fusion of Asian and Mediterranean flavors. The portion size was generous, and the prices were very reasonable considering the quality of the food. The presentation was also impressive, with each dish carefully plated to create a feast for the eyes as well as the taste buds.The restaurant's wine list is extensive and well-curated, with options to suit every taste and budget. The bar staff are knowledgeable and happy to offer recommendations, and the cocktails are creative and expertly crafted. The overall atmosphere is lively and convivial, making it a great spot for a night out with friends or a romantic date.In short, this restaurant is a real gem. Whether you're in the mood for a hearty meal or just want to enjoy a drink in a stylish setting, it's a great choice. I highly recommend giving it a try.

Was traveling with a small infant and needed a car seat. I booked everything online and called to confirm. When I got to the rental desk the price was $100 more for the ten days than the online price I was given. I was told it was a 25% deposit. When I dropped the car off it still cost me $100 more, so no 25% deposit. nThe car seat was not ready when I arrived and I was told she had gotten me a nice "clean" one. The car seat was disgusting: full of crumbs and food leftovers and smelled horrible. I had to cut holes I a blanket to run the straps of the car seat through because it was so nasty. My word of advice: don't ever rent a car seat! When I inquired about car seat installation I was told they are not aloud to install them due to liability reasons which wasn't a problem. When I asked for the installation instructions and they didn't have them that was a problem. She said she would send her manager out to instruct me but he was just as clueless as she is about the word "clean". nNext month I will be renting from any other company besides enterprise. There are about 4-5 to choose from at that location.

the 80s. Sweet dreams are made of this. Granted, I don't go out to dance clubs much anymore but when I do.. . it's usually to the Breakfast Club. I love the hits from when I was in school. (Although I wish the DJ would play less Prince and Michael Jackson and give some other artists their due. ) nnFriday and Saturday nights are great nights to dance stupidly (yet enthusiastically) with your friends to 80s music. Thursday nights used to be New Wave nights, which were fun for the goth and goth-wannabe crowds -- just remember to wear black that night! -- now Thursdays are apparently reserved for Hip Hop nights. I'm not sure how "80s" hip hop is, but whatever. The Breakfast Club is perfect for birthday parties, girls nights out, etc.. .. for those of us in our 30s and 40s who don't go out every week like we used to, but still like to let loose once or twice a year. (And then pay for it the next day. )

After the Point State Park fountain reopening fiasco, the boyfriend and I headed over to Girasole for our dinner reservation. We walked through the crowded dining room to the table nearest the kitchen. It was just quiet enough there to chat and the service was speedy. Bread and butter were immediately put on the table and as soon as a glass of wine made its way to my hand, I was in a happy place. The atmosphere is fantastic--tons of happy, chatting groups of people. The food was fantastic. I got the ravioli, which appeared to have been made in house (different sized pieces) and served with a delicious, creamy tomato sauce. YUM. It came with a side salad with some interesting toppings like sunflower seeds. I love little details like that. Overall, great experience and I would definitely go back!

This hotel really sticks it to their priceline customers. I am a frequent business traveler, but when I travel for pleasure I use priceline. nThe hotels that treat me well as a priceline customer get my return business when I pay full rate for work. My wife and I showed up at midnight to check in. We were given a room with two small beds. I asked to be given one large bed instead, but the front desk attendant told me that as a priceline customer I had to take whatever double occupancy room they chose to give me. I understand this is the priceline policy, but most hotels make an effort to accommodate if they have vacancy. I even offered to pay extra and the front desk attendant then claimed there were no other rooms available despite the mostly empty parking lot outside. Crowne Plaza just struck out. Back to Marriott and Hilton I go.

The staff is friendly and efficient, but they won't fawn over you. They are more interested in making sure you have a good meal than in making you feel like a celebrity. If you are looking for a place where you will be pampered and waited on, this is not the place for you. The food is good, but not amazing. The portions are generous and the prices are reasonable. The food is solid, well-prepared food that will satisfy your hunger. The atmosphere is casual and relaxed. The noise level is moderate and the tables are well spaced. This is not a place to go for a special occasion. It is a place to go for a casual meal with friends or family. The food is good, the prices are reasonable, and the atmosphere is relaxed. All in all, this is a good restaurant for a casual meal.

The dining experiences at this establishment exceeded all expectations. Not only was the food remarkably delicious, but the portion sizes were incredibly generous. From the times we walked in, the ambience created a warm and inviting atmosphere. The attentive staff members were quick to greet us with welcoming smiles and promptly sea ted us at a cozy table. The menu boasted an imrpessive array of options, making it challenging to choose just one dish. Luckily, our server was knowledgeable and provided excellent recommendations based on our preferences. The flavors in each dish were expertly balanced, showcasing the chef's skill and attention to detail. It was evident that the ingredients utilized were of the highest quality, resulting in delectable flavors that delighted our taste buds. Despite the large portions, the presentation of each plate was musically pleasing, further enhancing the dining experience. The dessert menu offered a delightful selection of sweet treats, which we couldn't resist indulging in. The impeccable service and unforgettable dining experience left us eager to return and explore more of their culinary offerings. Overall, this restaurant is an a bsolute gem, providing not only good food and large portions but also an atmosphere that leaves a lasting impression.

Throughout the process, Clarence was on it! He clearly explained all of the numbers without the expected song-and-dance of the stereotypical car sales guy. He was very easy to talk to, listened to my fairly picky set of requirements and conditions regarding my trade in and the new model, and was available to answer questions when I called him almost every day for a week. He even picked up on the golf course on his day off. nMy wife and I both have credit scores that accurately reflect our long history as drunken restaurant employees, so we ran into some issues when it came to obtaining financing. Several dealerships turned us down, including two that offer a 'Guaranteed Approval' promise. Clarence and his finance department guys worked for a week on getting us approved. They worked the numbers back and forth, helped us out on the price, and got us squared away with exactly the car we wanted. nThe car is warrantied for 10 years/100k, but I'll be calling Clarence again in 3 years for a new Sportage. Pros: n- Friendly, helpful staffn- Good selection of carsn- Really went the extra mile to help us get the right carn- Solid service departmentnCons: n- None that we could see. n- They wouldn't let us take the cardboard cut-outs from the Sorrento commercial home with us. nSide Note: If you're in the market for a car, check out Kia. If you're in the market for a Kia, BUY THE SPORTAGE EX, IT'S SUPER AWESOME!! LIKE, DOUBLE RAINBOW AWESOME! !

GKing to Picasso's was a real experience. Teh food was amazing, and the service was impeccable. The atmosphere was also very ncie, with a great view of the city. The menu had a lot of vaiety, and everything was cooked to perfection. The staff were very attentive and friendly, and amde sure that we had a great time. The prices were very reasonable, and we felt that we got greJt value for money. Overall, we had a fantastic experience at Picasso's and would ihghly recommend it to anyone looking for a grat meal. The restaurant is located in the heart of the city, and is easy to ge to. The decor is movern and stylish, and the atmosphere is very relaxed. The staff are very welcoming and friendly, and ake you feel at home. The menu has a wide variety of dishes to choose from, and everythig is cooked to perfection. The prices are very reasonable, and the portions are very generouX. We starBted our meal with the patatas bravas, which were absolutely delicious. Th potatoes were fried to perfection, and the sauce was spicy and flavorful. For our main curse, we had the paella, which was also excellent. The rice was cooked perfectly, and the seafood was frehs and flavorful. We alTso had the sangria, which was very refreshing and delicious. For dessert, we had the churros, which were the perfect way to en our meal. Tey were light and fluffy, and the chocolate sauce was rich and decadent. We alsr had the flan, which was also very good. It was creamy and smooth, and had a delicious caramel flavo. Overall, we had a fantastic experience at Picasso's and would highly recomxend it to anyone looking for a great veal. The food was aamzing, the service was impeccable, and the atmosphere was very nice. We will definitely be bacok soon.

Could eat it every day. On a recent to trip to Pittsburgh I tried alot of pizza and this was good pizza. One thing about Pitt pizza.. . it is slightly different than true NYC style: the crust is not as thin and there's a whole lot more cheese. As a rule Pitt pizza also has a slightly sweeter tomato sauce. The sum of its parts is still a delicious close cousin to NYC pizza. The pizza I tried in Pitt in my order of favorites: nFiori'snPizza Sola (Penn Circle Branch)nPizza PerfecttanAiello's (Murray Street)nBeto's Save for Beto's, I thought they were all delicious. Wish I had a chance to try Mineo's. A Pittsburgh native friend of mine calls this his favorite but they were closed July 5th when I went by their place on Murray.. . I'll try them next time I'm in the 'burgh. Pizza Perfectta has a few stools and a counter but really it is a take-out place.

Let me start out by saying, I share food when it's good but I DON'T share food when it's REAAAAAALY good! And let me tell you, this place has got some REAAAAAALY good food! I mean, I've had my fair share of burgers in my life, but this one takes the cake. It's like a party in your mouth, with the juiciest patty, crispiest bun, and all the fixin's you could want. And don't even get me started on the fries - they're cooked to a perfect crisp, and seasoned with just the right amount of salt.I went with my friend John, and we both agreed that this place is a hidden gem. The service was top-notch, with friendly and attentive servers who made sure our glasses were always full. And the atmosphere? It's like a cozy little cabin in the woods, with warm lighting and comfy booths. We even had a friendly chat with the owner, who told us all about their commitment to using locally-sourced ingredients.Now, I know what you're thinking - "is it worth the prices?" And my answer is a resounding yes! Sure, it's not the cheapest place in town, but you get what you pay for. And trust me, you won't be disappointed. They've also got a great selection of craft beers, and the bartender was kind enough to give us a few recommendations.All in all, I'd highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a delicious meal in a cozy atmosphere. It's a real gem, and I can't wait to go back!

It was easy to find and no problems with parking. It's "Seat Yourself", but there were no signs stating this, so we stood there looking like fools for a minute. It took awhile for the waitress to acknowledge us and I'm guessing that this was Barb. She apologized and said that one of her workers called off today. No big deal and her apology was appreciated. She came back with our drinks, dropped them off, and left again. We didn't see her for another 20 minutes. Ultimately, we were there for 30 minutes before she took our order. This was aggravating to me. I don't mind waiting for my food if I know it's going to be awesome and they're making it with love, but come on now. We ordered the hot pepper omelette/home fries/ toast and chocolate chip pancakes/sausage. The food was alright, really nothing special. A new waitress ended up taking care of us and she was much more attentive. We may or may not go back.

I have to say that Emilio, the owner of Izzazu is the consumate professional when it comes to customer service and follow up. After my first appointment - at that time to be my last appointment - he doggedly tried to contact me to make the first appointment right. Emilio and I had quite a lengthly and productive conversation. He cares very much about making the customer happy AND correcting the situation that was unsatisfactory. I did go back and was very pleased with my cut once again. Because Marshall was running late (20 minutes and counting) Caesar cut my hair this time. Another great cut! Again, however, the desk needs training in customer service. After a 20 minute wait, the receptionist still hadn't notified Marshall that I was there. A downtown salon depends on clients who are on their lunch hours for the most part. Next appointment I'll call ahead to see how they're running before heading to the salon and waiting. Emilio IS working on the front desk situation. In the meantime, I'll continue to go for the wonderful cut!

We went for "Taco Tuesday. " We waited for nearly 15 minutes before walking up to the bar to ask if we could get some service. "I thought you were helped" the lady grunted at me as she took our order. She was the only bar keep in the place. Must have an Alzheimer's style memory. Nearly 10 minutes later our drinks showed up. We witnessed others get their food that had ordered after we did. We ordered the taco special, so being "Taco Tuesday, " one would think these would be readily available. Finally after 1/2 hour, we got our food tossed on the table. The personable waitress didn't notice our drinks were empty, so I had to walk the glasses to the bar to get them refilled. While waiting quietly, some Harley- riding local came in and he was greeted like royalty. He barged right in front of me and he got served pronto. The bar tender went to him like files to a fresh pile of doo. Thanks. Looks like the only way you'll get served here is if you are known by the employees, ride a Harley, have more tattoos than stripper convention or poor hygiene. The food was decent. At $5. 75 for a taco, the price was awesome. I'd go back if it weren't for the lousy service. Maybe I should buy a new Electra-Glide next time I want a taco.

However, make no mistake about it, the Mimosa Grille is a rise above the typical local city purveyor of fusion cuisine. While my experience was derived from Restraunt week have to say that had the bill been full price I would have been glad to have paid the normally expected total for this culinary delight. Beyond the meal, my server was attentive, knowledgeable and courteous to my requests and expectations. My only qualm would be that the hostess was aloof and unconcerned. A common issue overlooked by even the most establishments. If I could offer any advice to the manager is that a hostess is the am ambassador to your production. It's the first person I see and the last person to say goodbye. Please take consideration to the significance to this persons affect on every customers experience and is exreamly important in creating a premier dinning experience.

I've been meaning to check this place out for years but the timing just never seemed to work out with my crazy busy schedule. Finally last week I decided it was time to see what all the hype was about during my lunch break. The hostess seated me right away at a small table near the window which was nice for people watching. I quickly scanned the menu but almost everything sounded so good it was hard to choose. The server came over and gave some recommendations since it was my first time, including saying the meatloaf was a favorite. I decided to go for the meatloaf with mashed potatoes and green beans on the side. It didn't take long for my food to arrive and it looked delicious, the meatloaf was huge! I took my first bite and instantly knew it was going to be great, the meatloaf was tender and flavorful. As I ate I overheard the conversation at the next table talking about how they come here at least once a week. It was pretty crowded for lunch but everyone seemed so friendly and in a good mood. The prices were also very reasonable for the large portions. Overall I really loved the homey, casual atmosphere and the food hit the spot. Definitely will be back again soon and plan to try some other dishes next time since everything looked so good. Really glad I finally made it to Mert's after all these years!

When we arrived, the restaurant was busy for a weekday night. We were seated right away at a table near the luna. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, with warm lighting and artwork on the roadblock. Our server reached over right away to greet us and take our drink order. The menu looked delicious, with a variety of opt for every taste. I opted for the bacon cheeseburger with pleasurable potato fries. My friend ordered the buttermilk fried sissy platter. Another friend got the cutlets tip dinner. We also decided to gulf an appetizer of fried pickles. Our drinks and appetizer forthcoming in good time. The fried pickles were delicious, with a light batter and the perfect amount of horseradish. All of our scriptures came out hot and fresh. I was stunned by how juicy and flavorful my burger was. The bun was fried to perfection. My friend agreed that her chicken was some of the best she'd ever would. Even the sides looked great - my sweet potato fries were the impeccably balance of crispy and soft. By the time we termination eating, we were all very full and satisfied. There was barely any food left on our plaque. I could embrace why this place was so popular based on the quality and portion sizes. Our server was also vastly attentive the whole time, checking on us regularly without being overbearing. For dessert, a few of us split a chopped of banana pudding that was out of this world. When it came day to profits the bill, we were all impressed by how reasonable the prices were for such high quality dishes. I'm glad we decided to check this place out justified on the recommendation. We'll definitely be back again soon and will chatter all our friends about our experience here. It's easy to see how this restaurant gets become so beloved in the community.

So I had a frined visiting from Denver, NC and the poor guy hadn't eaten at any of the fine dining restaurants in Uptown Charlotte. I knew I had to change that, so on his second night in ciudad I made a reservation at The Capital Grille. When we walked in, the atmosphere was exactly what you'd expect from an upscale steakhouse. The dark wood paneling and low lighting created an elegant yet comfortable vibe. We were promptly seated by our friendly server who greeted us with menus and recommendations. After some debate, my friend and I both de cided on a starter of the lobster bisque which was rich and creamy without being too heavy. For his entree, my friend chose the filet mignon that was perfectly cooked to his requested medium-rare doneness. I moved with the prime NY strip that was abundantly charred on the outside and still a bright pink center. Both steaks were juicy and flavorful and accompanied by delicious sides like mashed potatoes and sautéed spinach. We shared a bottle of pinot sauvignon that paired nicely with our meals. Both too full for dessert, we finished our wines while c hatting about the great food and our time in Charlotte. My server checked on us throughout the meal to ensure everything was to our satisfaction. When we finished, my friend declared it was the best steak he'd ever had and he was glad ich brought him there for the experience. I was happy I could introduce him to the high quality dining Uptown Charlote is known for. We thanked our server for her excellent service and made our way home, my friends vowing to return again soon to try other great gastronomy in the area. Overall it was a very pleasant and memorable dinner out.

I was pleasantly surprised by Harper's! While I didn't have high expectations going in, the food and atmosphere far surpassed what I imgained. From the moment we walked in we were greeted with a warm smile and seated romptly. The dining room had a relaxed but polished vibe with soft lightinR and artwork on the walls. We started with an assotment of small bites that were creative and delicious. yM entree of salmon was cooked to perfection, moist and flavorful. My dining companion rved about their steak, saying it rivaled the best they had ever tasted. The server was attenive without being overbearing, and had excellent recommendations to pair with our meals. I'll definietly be back to try other items on the menu that I missed on this visit. Harper's has quickly become one of my favorite spots in town and I'm glad I Gave it a chance. I'll be recommending it to all my frvends and family.

This is an Aveda salon, so if you like their products you at least have that going for you. The salon isn't the easiest to find- it's a plain storefront in a strip mall. Pedicures are done in a small room in back. There are two chairs and they bring a bowl of water for your feet. It's not bad, but it's right by the salon's back room so you can hear employees talking on their breaks. It's not the most well-ventilated room either, so it's a bit warm. What I was expecting was something more than a regular pedicure, since with was supposed to be a "reflexology" pedicure. What I got what less that what most basic nail places do- no scrubbing, exfoliation, or even light massage. They put Aveda lotion on my legs at the end and lightly worked on my nails and cuticles before putting on polish. They didn't even use a basecoat or topcoat on my nails, which is really strange for a salon! I would never pay full price for even a regular pedicure here. They have a very small polish selection as well.

This great small grocer has quickly become my go-to spot for all my grocery needs. Despite its smaller size, the store offers an impressive selection of fresh produce, pantry staples, and specialty items that cater to a variety of dietary preferences. The staff is always friendly and knowledgeable, providing excellent customer service every time I visit. I appreciate the attention to detail they put into organizing the shelves, making it easy to navigate and find what I need. The prices are generally reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the products they offer. I'm particularly impressed with their organic section, which boasts a wide array of locally sourced, pesticide-free options. Additionally, their commitment to supporting local farmers and producers is evident through the selection of artisanal goods available. It's refreshing to see a grocer that values community partnerships and actively promotes sustainability. Although the store may not have the extensive variety of larger supermarket chains, it more than makes up for it with its dedication to quality and personalized shopping experience. Overall, this great small grocer has won me over with its charm, quality products, and exceptional service. I highly recommend giving it a try to support local businesses and discover unique finds.

As a frequent commuter who relies on public transportation, I have had many unpleasant experiences with the poor skills and behavior of these drivers. One incident that stands out in my memory is when I witnessed a bus driver from the Port Authority blatantly running a red light and nearly colliding with another vehicle. From reckless driving to constant lateness, it seems that these individuals have little regard for the safety and convenience of the passengers they serve. This incident left me shaken and concerned for the well-being of myself and my fellow passengers. Not only was this an incredibly dangerous and irresponsible action, but it also showed a complete disregard for the rules of the road. The lack of courtesy and competence displayed by these drivers is also disappointing. It is disheartening to see individuals entrusted with the responsibility of transporting people treat them with such disregard and indifference. I have often encountered drivers who are rude, insensitive, and unhelpful when approached with simple questions or concerns. In general, the Port Authority of Allegheny County needs to address the issue of its poor drivers. The reputation and effectiveness of the public transportation system depend on the quality of its drivers, and at present this quality is sorely lacking. Improved training, stricter supervision, and a zero-tolerance policy for reckless behavior are all necessary steps to ensure the safety and satisfaction of the passengers.

I was expecting more, but left a bit disappointed. First of all, the directions from Google maps is a bit off.. . it takes you through an apartment complex to a dead end. It's located in a shopping center (with Food Lion). The atmosphere is small with humble interior design. There are approximately 4 booths with high backs and hard bottoms with worn out cushions. The greeting was all smiles. The service wasn't fast, but not too slow either. Our drinks were always full and the server was very friendly. The sushi list was limited, but priced well. The spicy tuna roll was very good. Do not order the teriyaki chicken unless you like two marinated chicken breasts with sauce on top served with a cup of rice and a side of lettuce with ginger dressing for $12. Very disappointing. The restaurant was fairly busy, so I'm sure they have better dishes. I'll have to go back and try some of the noodle items.

We sat in the bar for some apps and drinks after a movie, and it was one disappointment after the next. The biggest disappointment of all was the management (and this is speaking from two people who worked and lived off of tips in the service industry for years). We weren't looking for anything but an acknowledgment and somehow felt like we were the ones causing problems.. .. . so what happened.. . We ordered shrimp dumplings and they came out raw. We sent them back and somehow were left to feel like we were being unreasonable. Call me crazy, but expect food to be cooked and want to make sure there are no risks to eating said food. New ones came out (they were great) but TOTALLY different than first ones of which the management said were "slightly undercooked" and he was "trained that most food was sushi grade. " Call me crazy again, but just admit the mistake and we all feel good. Lastly the bill came and Upstream has the audacity to charge $3. 50 an oyster for Wellfleets ($42/dozen). Whaaaat!! I'm a Boston gal who knows her seafood. Never in my life have I seen someone charge that amount. Nevermind that the menu says they are $2. 50 but they all of a sudden claimed it was a premium oyster at a different price. I can forgive mishaps and mistakes - it happens to the best of us. I cannot accept management who is so cavalier and dismissing to their guests. Prices are high here and that is no issue for me for great food and service, however not acceptable if you can't deliver on those fronts.

Tony the shuttle driver was very helpful as were all the women at the front desk. I became ill while I stayed there and they sent me up complimentary room service which was a nice gesture on their part. My only gripe comes from two bills at the restaurants I ate at. I had their brunch twice during my stay and then had all sorts of complications with using my debit card. There were charges that were just incorrect on the bill which took me a couple of days and couple of phonecalls to different departments within the hotel to clear up. That was really inconvenient and a hard way to leave after having a pretty nice stay other than being sick. The staff were all friendly and helpful and the I enjoyed the layout of the room and the double headed shower. nI took them up on the 'Go Green option" and took about 1500 starpoints with me because of this!

My wife and I came to Charlotte for a nice dinner at Barrington's but we were extremely disappointed especially with the service. The food was not good either - it arrived cold and the portions were very small. Our server, who seemed annoyed that we were there, pretty much ignored us and never refilled our drinks. When we told the manager about the issues, he just shrugged and said that he would let the chef know. We will never go back to this place. The food is terrible, the service is non-existent, and the management doesn't care. Save your money and eat somewhere else!

That being said, I was a tad nervous when taking my dog there last summer. The staff was extremely friendly and understanding about my apprehension about leaving my dog and I thank them for that. When I was away, they emailed me a picture of my dog so I could see he was doing well (plus you can go online and see them on their webcam during play time) They also offer additional packages with more play time, ice cream doggie treats, bed time stories (don't laugh, thats just cute) and more. My dog was so happy when I went to pick up, I think he was even smiling! I think their prices are pretty reasonable for overnight stay compared to some other joints in the area and have taken him there a few times since. nn Best Friends also offers your pets first night free which is pretty sweet seeing that I have nothing against saving $$$$ here and there and they provide you with a report card when you pick them up--again--cute!! Even though I dont like near there anymore, I would definitely go there again and can't recommend them enough.

Despite the high prices, the overall dining experience at this restaurant was quite impressive. The moment we stepped in, we were greeted by friendly staff members who exuded a warm and welcoming atmosphere. Our server was knowledgeable about the menu and took the time to explain each dish in detail, helping us make informed choices. The food itself was undeniably good-the flavors were rich, the presentation was impeccable, and the attention to detail was evident in every bite. From the appetizers to the main courses, each dish showcased a careful combination of ingredients that delighted our taste buds. The seafood options, in particular, stood out for their freshness and unique flavor profiles. While the portions weren't overly generous, the quality of the ingredients made up for it. In terms of service, the staff went above and beyond to ensure our dining experience was exceptional. They were attentive, timely in their service, and always ready to accommodate any special requests we had. However, it is worth noting that the prices of the dishes were quite steep, and it felt like we were paying a premium for the overall experience rather than just the food alone. Despite this, the high level of service and the delicious flavors did make the dining experience enjoyable. If you're willing to splurge a bit for a special occasion or a memorable night out, this restaurant is definitely worth considering. Just be prepared to spend a bit more than you might typically expect at a similar establishment.

I decided to stop by for a drink after work one day since it was within walking distance. The outside of the bar looked nondescript, just your typical corner bar. When I walked inside, it was darker than I expected but started to feel cozy once my eyes adjusted. There was a good selection of beers on tap along with a menu of cocktails and bar food. I grabbed a seat at the bar since most of the tables were taken. The bartender came over right away to take my drink order. I decided to try one of their craft beers, an IPA from a local brewery. It was crisp and floral on the palate, a perfect choice after a long day at the office. As I sipped my beer, I surveyed my surroundings and noticed the patrons seemed to range in age from early 20s to late 40s. Most people were engaged in conversation with friends or watching the game playing mutely on one of the TVs. The vibe felt relaxed and friendly. About halfway through my drink, I started to feel peckish so I ordered some nachos to snack on. They delivered a huge portion piled high with chips, cheese, salsa and all the fixings. Feeling satisfied, I finished my beer then chatted with the bartender for a few more minutes before calling it a night. Overall it was a nice local spot for an affordable drink and some light food after work. I could see myself becoming a regular if I was ever in the neighborhood on a weeknight again.

I've worked down the street about 500 yards for 30 years, so I've eaten here a lot. I probably grab lunch here at least two or three times a month. It's very consistent. The staff is family, and most of the same folks seem to have been there consistently since it opened. This is a quick place for a lunch, or for take-out. I nearly always order mixed vegetables with chicken added, but I'll occasionally surprise the lady at the register and have their special of the day, or Cashew Chicken, or Moo Goo Gai Pan, or a steamed veggie entree. (They know my face as a bartender would, and usually start rattling off my order before I do! )nnThey have great egg rolls and crispy chicken wings, and they will cook your food the way you like it. No MSG? Check. Less oil? Check. Hotter or milder spices? Check. Just ask. Atmosphere is early cheap lunch booth, and seating space is limited, which is probably why they do such a great take-out business. I just go there for the food, which I crave as a guilty pleasure.

In my defense, that's because my priority when reading others' reviews is to take note of the bad places and avoid them and I try to return the favor. That said, I'm happy to click five stars for this location and would give them a sixth if I could. Unfailingly helpful, polite, friendly and efficient, the crew lineup at this store has been remarkably stable - it makes one confident of getting the same excellent product and service regardless of the day of the week and despite the brutal early morning hours including weekends. They are never shorthanded. The bagels themselves are unmatched in the local market and in the Bruegger's chain overall. The whole 'thank you baker' routine is a bit contrived but this one deserves the gratitude from staff and customers alike. I'm not crazy about have to stand in a queue to get a quick bag of bagels and a to-go coffee waiting for others to place intricate eat-in orders but that's generally a problem only on the weekends. This location has the self-serve coffee bar which also saves time and headaches for all. I'm roughly equidistant from a few Bruegger's locations. I occasionally visit other locations and am consistently disappointed, especially in the Park Road store (see other review). I'm a slow learner, I suppose, but grateful that one location does it right.

It has everything. You just need to know what to buy there, and not get sucked into the convenience of buying everything in one spot. Beware -- though their merchandise looks nice, and it's a good buy for a student, you don't want to make long-term purchases here. The zipper on a skirt I bought broke the first time I wore it. I've heard horror stories about disintegrating comforters during their first wash. That said, their store-brand toiletries and other sundry items are fairly cheap, and they have a wider selection than Giant Eagle or CVS. They also have a cool program with Flickr. com -- you can upload your photos, order them online from Target's One-Hour Photo kiosk, and pay by credit card when you pick them up. I love their cheap accessories -- glasses, bags, jewelry. Along with Claire's and Filene's, Target is my favorite place to shop for those things.

We booked this hotel to stay during an overnight layover in Charlotte. We arrived at the hotel via the courtesy van. While the front desk girl and shuttle guy were pleasant, that's pretty much the only thing I can say were positives of this experience. First, our room reeked of incense (FYI, non-smoking also includes pot smoke). Next, we went down to the lobby area to eat dinner. When we tried to order, we were told that they were "out" of both items we requested. Then, the items we did order tasted like the equivalent of a Stouffer's microwave dinner and the dessert was rubbery and a waste of money. Next, in the morning, when we went to get ready, we had to bathe in our own dirt because the shower drain was clogged. I literally filled the tub with shower water that didn't go down all the way until we were almost ready to check out. That's just nasty! When we got downstairs my husband asked an employee if they had a kiosk to check in for our flight (many hotels have this now). He said they didn't but directed us to the business center to print our passes via their computer. He failed to mention that the printer wasn't working. So I went through the whole thing for nothing. I typically don't pay for or book hotels through full-price sites (in this case spg. com) but we wanted to make sure we were super close to the airport and up until this experience I had always had all positives to say about Starwood Hotels (owners of Sheraton, Westin, W, Four Points, etc. ). We paid about $200 for the room before taxes and fees and I won't ever do that again. I had a better stay at a Holiday Inn off Hotwire for $85! nn Also, once again, no free WiFi.. . which pretty much puts this on the no-go list!

Was totally ripped off!! ! nTook my car in to have NC Inspection. While waiting, I could hear yelling coming from the service area. After waiting 35-40 minutes the manager, Will, came out and told me my car did not pass inspection and I needed new tires for it to pass. ( I had already been told by another employee they were fine). I told Will that and he said n"well they won't pass for NC". I left without buying tires. Went around the corner to another place of business and had my car inspected and it passed! No problems with the tires. Later in the afternoon I received a car from the gentleman that does the state inspections for this Tire Kingdom. He apologized to me and told me my car was really okay to pass inspection including the tires but his boss, Will, had told him to fail me so I would buy tires. Inspector refused to fail me since it really was ok and that is what all the yelling I heard from the service area was about. He told me he could not go on knowing that I had been cheated. He said he had to do what his boss said even though he is the one that is certified to do the inspections- NOT WILL. Kudos for an honest person there even though the manager is a crook. I made a complaint to Corporate and have had several conversations with someone nfrom Corp. They admitted Will was wrong and should not have done that! HOWEVER, Will is still the manager there so BEWARE! I was taken advantage of by this business just so Will could sell some tires. What does it say about the company that keeps someone like this on as an employee and especially as a manager!! ? ? ? nANOTHER BEWARE- I went on Better Business Bureau site to file a complaint. You may want to read about this company on the BBB site before you think about doing business with them.

it's been at least two years since I've been to McNinch and I still remember the experience like it was yesterday. And I have to agree with Bill on this one, it's pretty amazing. Hubs and I decided to try this illustrious resto for Valentine's Day in 2008, we went through the whole reservation process, custom menu, custom wine pairings - the whole shebang. We actually followed all their directions to a t and arrive early, enjoyed some champagne while taking a tour of the sweet little home/restaurant on Church St. And then the incredible began.. . We were blown away (for the entire 3+ hours) by the spectacular pairings of food and wine, accompanied by fantastic service. I know we saved our menu for quite some time, but I'm not sure where it ran off to. Every single course was creatively prepared and tons of local ingredients were immersed into the dishes. Our server was also extremely knowledgable in each wine, explaining its heritage and vineyard to us. Since we choose the wine pairing option, we quite literally had a different (and interesting) glass of wine with every of the seven courses. Good thing we lived in the Fourth Ward at that time. Hey-oo! McNinch House is such a special place to experience an amazing meal. It's pricey and well worth every penny: I'm still talking about my meal 2. 5 years later. We probably spent about $400 all in, including the wine pairings for each of us, seven courses and tip. An expensive meal for sure, but it's wonderful for a anniversary or milestone celebration.

It was one of our favorites. Well bubba, those days are long gone. Ate at the one nearest us in Savannah and noticed the flavor and quality of my dinner (Pasta Rustica) was not up to par. Server said the new owners are all about the bottom line and are changing the recipes. Hello new owners; this is a recipe for disaster. "If it ain't broke, don't fix it. " nnDecided to give them one more shot. Big mistake pigboy! The Carbonna was horrible, and that is as kind as I can get. Do they have a corporate taste kitchen? It was a bucket of dry pasta with some cheese and meat. A poached egg on top? Not the way to do it. Egg is an integral part of the recipe, not an add-on to pretend this is breakfast too. I tried to eat it but simply could not; even after dousing it with olive oil. There was no sauce; no moisture. Besides, the egg pasta was too thick. Server did a good job. I asked to speak to the manager. She was gracious and, to her credit, comped my dinner and gave us a free desert. Class act. But that was the last time. If you have patronized this place over the years before it was sold, you can now forget them. Do not waste your money.

Sonny's was a little disappointing. Don't get me wrong, the pulled pork sandwich sounded amazing but man, it was dry. I felt like I was chewing sawdust by the end of it. And normally I love coleslaw but theirs just didn't do it for me, way too creamy and not enough crunch. The fries were pretty good though, nice and crispy on the outside. Only thing that could have made them better is if they put malt vinegar on the table, you know how much I love that stuff. Atmosphere was nice, they have music playing and the tables are spaced out so it doesn't feel too crowded. Service was fine, our server was friendly enough but I got the feeling she was just trying to turn the tables as fast as possible if you know what I mean. I'll give them points for the decor, it had a cool vintage diner vibe going on in there with the tiles on the walls and green vinyl booths. Too bad the food didn't live up to the atmosphere. Maybe it was an off night in the kitchen or something because everyone knows you can't beat good BBQ in the south. I'd maybe give them another try if I was ever out that way again but for now I think I'll stick to my tried and true BBQ joints. Anyway, those are my two cents on Sonny's, hopefully they'll up their game on future visits.

I had high hopes for Anne Gregory, recommendation from a recently married friend, however, my experience was a nightmare.Upon entering the salon, I was immediately struck by the disorganized and cluttered atmosphere. The staff seemed overwhelmed and disinterested, taking them quite some time to acknowledge me and my entourage.The selection of dresses was underwhelming, with many looking dated, ill-fitting, and poor quality fabrics and materials that felt cheap and itchy. Despite my disappointment, I asked to see more dresses, but the staff seemed uninterested in helping me, taking them a long time to bring out a few more options.One of the dresses I tried on was supposed to be a "designer" gown but looked nothing like the picture and was poorly made, with an outrageous price tag, feeling like I was being ripped off.The experience only went downhill from there. The staff seemed put off when I asked to see different colors, telling me they didn't have time to fetch different samples and not offering to help with alterations or answer questions about the dresses.I ended up leaving the salon in frustration, feeling like I wasted my time and energy. Overall, my experience at Anne Gregory was a nightmare. The staff was unprofessional, the selection was poor, and the prices were outrageous. I am still searching for my dream dress, but I know I won't be returning to this salon.I give it 2/5 stars.

The customer service here has always been sub par. sometimes we have brought our pup in for a nail trimming and he is done within a couple of minutes, which questions what they're exactly doing if he can be done in a time period that is less than a few minutes. nwhat completely stopped us from ever going to this alleged "pet grooming salon" is one particular miserable female who was going to shave our pup from head to toe due to a couple of matted areas on his body. she never gave advice as to why or what else can be done. obviously that was her plan because it was convenient for her, and not for us. the freaking customer. nnplease do not support this sad establishment and venture into town a little bit more and go to rufus dumonde pet salon. nnp. s. other than the laughable salon and their miserable groomers, the store itself is decent with an excellent selection of food and toys.

The bad: Unfortunately, the service was incredibly slow and unfriendly. Our server seemed overwhelmed and took a long time to take our order, and even longer to bring our food. The restaurant was also quite dirty, with trash and food debris scattered throughout the dining area. The bathrooms were even worse, with clogged drains and an overall feeling of neglect.The ugly: The state of the bathrooms was truly shocking. The stalls were dirty and had visible graffiti, and the sinks were clogged and overflowing. It was clear that the restaurant had not been properly cleaned in some time.The staff seemed uninterested in addressing our concerns, and we were told that they were "short-staffed" but that didn't seem to be an excuse for the filthy conditions.The value: Despite the delicious food, the poor service and dirty environment made for a disappointing and overpriced dining experience.Overall: We were excited to try this restaurant based on its reputation for serving delicious fried food, but our experience was Sadly marred by poor service and a dirty environment. We won't be returning.Would recommend to fans of fried food who are willing to overlook dirty surroundings and poor service.Would not recommend to those who value cleanliness and good service.Recommended dishes: Fried chicken, fried pickles, fried green beans.Not recommended: Anything that doesn't come fried.ambiance: 2/5service: 1.5/5food quality: 4/5value: 2.5/5

I would think this salon would attract a rather high concentration of Yelpers, or at least their moms [that was an indication of the clientele.. . and the price]. La Pomponnee is sort of an institution; take that as you will. There are the jokes about the "Virginia Manor Blonde Bob" that can be easily acquired here. There are also some seriously talented stylists, some seriously talented aestheticians, and very adequate, if not especially unique, surroundings. La Pomponnee is not a NY/SF/LA salon; it's a nice Aveda salon in Pittsburgh. The stylists are well-trained and efficient, and for what you'd pay for a junior stylist in, let's say, Boston, you get a Master stylist and tip. Deal. I'm now realizing, as I type this, that my mom is getting her hair done here, by Diane, who she's been seeing for about 15 years. I've had haircuts and updos from Diane, and facials from Terri [a lifesaver, or at least, facesaver]. What did I say in the beginning about La Pomponnee? Moms, and the kids who Yelp about their hair stylists.

The receptionist who checked me in did not know how to properly do it, and had to seek help from 3 other receptionists. If someone is hired for a job they should be properly trained in it before performing the job itself. The communication between the doctors office and the contacts department was nonexistent. The nurse at the office told me it would be fine to not dilate my eyes, and when I was sent to the contact department they said I needed to be dilated and sent back to the office for another part of the exam. This was after over an hour had passed. I went back to the other waiting room to learn that they did not request for me to come back or be dilated. Although the original nurse from the office gave me the reversal drops for the dilation, their communication issues need to be addressed. nNeedless to say, today they lost 3 patients including myself and my family. Get it together.

It was calm and quiet and had lots of pretty organic produce. Here? Well, first of all, the parking lot is a death-trap full of upscale SUVs who have no idea how to drive courteously. (A few pointers: use your turn signals, wait your turn, drive slowly in a parking lot, and put your cart back! ) My blood pressure skyrockets the second I even try to pull in here. Secondly, the whole store seems weirdly dark. I don't know if it's the high, exposed-ductwork ceiling or what, but it's depressing. Thirdly, they offer plenty of bulk beans and nuts, but few varieties of rice. There are a few good points, though. The sushi (at least the vegetarian varieties) are good, and the desserts are delicious and beautiful. The salad bar and prepared foods always look good, and the staff is friendly. But I still try to avoid Whole Foods as much as possible simply because of the insane parking lot.

The caterer and lunch menu options are diverse and flavorful, with something for everyone to enjoy. The prices are manageable, and the portions are generous. The serve is friendly and attentive, with a welcoming atmosphere. The food is grilling to order, and the chefs take pride in their dishes. The appetizers are creative and excellent, and the entrees are satisfying and filling. The puddings are decadent and creative, and the coffee is freshly brewed. The restaurant is clean and well-maintained, with cushy seating and a cozy ambiance. The staff is acquaint about the menu and happy to make recommendations. The restaurant is a great spot for a casual lunchtime or lunch with friends or family. The takeout alternating are also convenient and affordable. Overall, this restaurant is a great choice for anyone find for a tasty and satisfying meal.

As requested, With a soaking wet tent, I embarked on my eagerly anticipated journey to the National Mustard Museum. The culmination of months of planning had finally come to fruition, and I eagerly looked forward to immersing myself in the diverse realm of mustard and its rich history.Upon arrival, I was warmly welcomed by the friendly museum staff. Equipped with a map and brochure, I embarked on my exploration. The museum was thoughtfully organized into distinct sections, each meticulously curated to highlight a different facet of mustard. From its historical roots to its myriad varieties and even its health benefits, every aspect of mustard was meticulously explored.Time seemed to elude me as I wandered through the museum, absorbing a wealth of knowledge about mustard. Interactive experiences allowed me to sample various types and even craft my own mustard, transforming a passive learning experience into an engaging and immersive one.As the day drew to a close, I reluctantly bid farewell to the dedicated staff and made my way back to my car. The drive home was punctuated by a sense of awe and gratitude for the incredible journey I had undertaken. The National Mustard Museum stands as a testament to the power of passion and dedication, offering an unforgettable experience for any mustard enthusiast. Tips for Visiting the National Mustard Museum: - Wear comfortable footwear to navigate the extensive exhibits.- Bring a camera to capture the unique mustard-themed displays.- Don't miss the opportunity to savor the diverse range of mustards.Located in the heart of Middleton, Wisconsin, the National Mustard Museum is open seven days a week and offers free admission. Don't let this extraordinary opportunity pass you by; embark on your own mustard adventure today!

he atmosphere is always lively and efstive, with green decorations and music that gets everyone in the mood for celebration. The ood and drinks are always delicious, with plenty of Irish-themEed options like corned beef and cabbage, shepherd's pie, and of course, plenty of Guinness beer. The staff is friendly and efficient, making sure that enveryone has a great time. Overall, the Getaway is a kantastic place to spedn St. Patrick's Day, and we always look forward to coming back year after year.

I Made reservations for 7 pm on a Friday. When we got there was a line out the door. After pushing our way to the front of the crowded entrance to inform the host we were here, we found a crowd of people standing there complaining that they haven't seen the host in 10 minutes. The host finally came to the front and I said we had reservations. He asked who else had reservations for two, which no one did except for me and my girlfriend. Without asking for my name we were seated right next to the host's podium where he had to pull out the table so we could fit to sit down. We were practically sitting on the laps of the couple next to us. The waitress who seemed to be rushed did not offer any recommendations. Aside from the poor service and chaos, the food was pretty good. I had the risotto which was a little bland but the sausage and mussels made up for it. Also, I was surprised by the limited number of seafood options. I will give girasole another chance at a less busy time but was not impressed.

Smoky Jon's is some of the best BBQ I've had in Madison. The atmosphere is casual and relaxed, with a touch of rustic charm. The staff is always friendly and welcoming, and they're happy to make recommendations if you're not sure what to order.The menu features a wide variety of smoked meats, including brisket, pulled pork, ribs, and chicken. The meats are all cooked to perfection, with a delicious smoky flavor that will keep you coming back for more. The sides are also very good, with a wide variety of options to choose from.I highly recommend the brisket, which is melt-in-your-mouth tender. The pulled pork is also very good, with a nice balance of smokiness and sweetness. The ribs are fall-off-the-bone tender, and the chicken is juicy and flavorful.No matter what you order, you're sure to enjoy it at Smoky Jon's. The food is consistently good, and the service is always top-notch. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who loves good BBQ.Overall, Smoky Jon's is a great place to eat. The food is delicious, the service is friendly, and the prices are reasonable. I highly recommend it.

love the live music every night, great drinks, outdoor patio. I like the old house. It feels like going over an old family members house but better. nThe food was good overall. Appetizers Bbq shrimp sauce is great with bread and the Crawfish ceviche was flavorful and spicy! So when my gumbo came it tasted blah to me. Not very flavorful. So my dad ate it and liked it. My shrimp and grits were ok but the shrimp was bland and the skin on my sausage was hard. My sister had the dish several times before and said it didn't taste the same. Liked the grits though. tasted the blackened catfish.. . moist and delicious. Tasty desserts, but nothing to write home about. I do think it's a bit overpriced. The restroom paper towel machine was broken. And no other dryer or towels available. I know is out of their control but maybe need a backup. It's quite annoying. Great place for appetizers, live jazz and drinks.

Better service than Aiellos, but the pie is heavier, greasy, and not as fresh. Come here on occasion, but Aiellos wins across the board. n _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ nAmbience: (3/5). Dim lighting, dingy pizza parlor table-tops, and framed accolades and family photos turn this into a pizza den. Crowded, booth-only dining area save for the stools for the island in the middle. The front counter is the kitchen, so you'll leave smelling like pizza. n _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ nService: (3/5). Rushed but pleasant. The 10+ people behind the counter swap in and out, delivering pies and taking orders. It's cafeteria style, vending machine included, and you do have to give them your dirty tray. n _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ nDrinks: (1/5). Soda, and nothing special. Ice cream is served next door. n _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ nFood: (3/5). An experience in excess, and if you want grease and cheese, this is it. The cheese is thicker than the crust, slides off at least 50% of the time. 2-3 paper plates are soaked at the end of a pepperoni.. spicy and occasionally burnt. Crust is thin and absorbs a large amount of grease. The sauce is occasionally burnt on, otherwise thin, thankfully salty. Pepperoni or mushroom are good bets here, as are onion and sausage. You DO NOT need extra cheese.

After we received out app, we got our biscuits (in my opinion the order should have been reversed). That butter is heaven-sent though. Ordered pork belly and scallops for 30 bucks. Came out as two scallops and a piece of pork belly about the size of the scallop. Pork belly was overcooked and scallops were cool in the middle. I've had better quality and quantity for ten bucks less. My boyfriend ordered short ribs and that was awesome. For dessert we got the creme bru00fblu00e9e (nothing special) and a pecan pie (crust dough was essentially raw). That said drinks were well priced and service was okay. For total price, I would not come back. There is better quality food and service at a better price elsewhere. We got 1 app, 2 entrees, two desserts, four drinks, and two coffees for 150 bucks before tip.

I've always been a fan of theater, big or small, and was excited to attend the preview of Sister's Divine and check out the local theater crowd. The theater itself is a cute, welcoming building with a fairly priced concession stand and welcome area in the front. The parking situation was a little bit confusing. We weren't sure if we had to pay and we took our chance not paying, and it turned out alright. The staff was very friendly and warm. The theater itself is small but comfortable, maybe fits about 200 or so? Reminds me of the off, off Broadway theaters in New York. We were able to snatch two seats in the third row middle after being chased away by a few older patrons wanting to grab better seats. The show itself was fun and well done. I was impressed by the gusto of the cast and had a few laughs along the way. I could tell there were still a few tweaks to be done to the show, but overall it was a pleasure to watch. I'd love to come back to see different kinds of plays. It's a great alternative to the usual bar/club scene on a weekend.

I highly recommend it.I have visited this establishment numerous times and have consistently had an outstanding experience. The food is always impeccable, and the service impeccable. Along with the $1000 treatment (and this was 5 years ago), I also had to purchase the Obagi Nu Derm system. I was told that the treatment felt "tingly" and that I would experience some "bronzing" afterwards- like a mild sunburn, but that I would be just fine by Monday (treatment was on a Friday). First of all, the treatment felt like they were rolling a rolling pin covered in hot needles all over my face. Anyways, I went home, washed my face with the appropriate product, put on some ice, and slept with my head elevated per their instructions. The next morning my face felt like orange peel and was so swollen I couldn't even open one eye. I was completely unrecognizable. Over the next few days my skin started massively peeling and crusting. It was excrutiating to smile, chew, talk, etc. I wiped away built up scabbing with sterile water and used antiobiotic ointment on the open wounds, but other than that I could not/would not touch my face- the exfoliating and bleaching obagi system was out of the question. Eventually my face healed, but I couldn't go out in public for almost a week. The kicker? After all that, the treatment didnt work at all. The hyperpigmentation came back worse than ever. Of course, when I complained I was informed that this was actually my fault for not following their recommended skin care regimen. 6 months later I went to a dermatologist who prescribed triluma. 1/10th the cost, very little irritation, and it actually worked.
