Giant Eagle: Market District makes great use of their limited space. My favorite things: nn-charmingly confusing store layoutn-happiest store employee I've EVER met -- the guy who hands out cookie samples is so enthusiasticn-polite cashiersn-walk-in cheese closet Transportation is easy for CMU students (B shuttle stops here). It's also on several major bus lines because it's on Centre Ave. Unfortunately, parking is the worst ever. Turning left out of the parking area is a nightmare and takes upwards of 3-4 minutes. Trying to turn left onto Centre during rush hour? Forget it. No matter where you're going, just turn right and resign yourself to driving really far out of your way.

We didn't want the cheese on the salad, and pasta, so we asked for it on the side - and we got exactly that.. .. . then, we get the bill, and my husband noticed that they charged us 50cents each for the salad, and pasta cheese that we asked for on the side.. .. .. . really? We immediately called the manager, and he said that it is the restaurant policy to charge for cheese - I said that is ridiculous because salad, and pasta SHOULD come with cheese, and the fact that we wanted it on the side instead of on the food should not be an issue, and we shouldn't be charged (I know it's only a total of $1. 00 extra for both cheese, but that is not the point.. .. . the point is for what they charge for food, it SHOULD come with cheese). With this said, they do have good food, and I just wish they were not trying to gouge their customers for every penny. We'll have to think about going back to this establishment.

This grocery store is a real gemstone in the city center. Here, you can find the freshest agricultural products, the highest quality meat and the highest quality Italian products. At the moment when I stepped into the room, friendly employees would pay tribute to you, and they are always eager to help. The aisle well is organized, you can easily browse and find what you need. The choice of products is indeed impressive, and you can choose a variety of choices. Whether you are looking for a specific type of pasta, a certain brand of olive oil, or the unique ingredients of special dishes, you may find it here. The price is reasonable, and the quality is always excellent. In addition to other grocery stores, one thing to set Italian grocery stores is that they are committed to purchasing products from local family companies. This means that you are supporting the local community and you can also get the best products. The store also provides a loyalty plan that can reward ordinary customers, which is a good choice. The checkout process is always fast and efficient, and friendly cashier is happy to help you carry your luggage or answer any problems you may encounter. This store is well maintained, and the atmosphere of the aisle and enthusiasm makes you feel home. In addition to the selected grocery selection, italiana grocery also provides various prepared foods, such as fresh bread, delicious pastry and homemade sauce. These are very suitable for fast and simple meals, or as side dishes to supplement fresh ingredients. Overall, Italiana Groceria is an excellent grocery store that provides an excellent shopping experience. Whether you are an Italian enthusiast or just looking for a good place to buy groceries, this store is worth visiting.

Make sure you CALL the restaurant to make a reservation if you have more than 4 in your party because often times a party of 6 or more will allow you to get 2 burners at the table. The menu during RW allows you to try the cheese fondue course (we really like the Spinach Artichoke dip one and the cheddar is really good too! ), the salad (I LOVE the California--- delicious and fresh! ), the main course (be sure you pay the $5 upgrade to try the mojo cooking style) which includes fresh seafood and beef cuts.. .. Along with this ravioli concoction that is truly incredible. The main course comes with an array of sauces.. .. . Green Goddess is my favorite, although our server suggested to try his favorite which is a blue cheese sauce and I LOVED it, especially with the pasta! The service is always divine and they talk you through your entire experience. It ends with the piece de resistance.. .. . The chocolate. We opted for the Flaming Turtle and the Yin and Yang.. .. . Amazing!! ! ! ! I say if you've never "fondued" before.. .. Definitely Do! : )

After getting stuck in Charlotte due to weather in Chicago, we were able to book this hotel for our unexpected stay. As a nursing mother I was hoping for a fridge in my room, however a pageant taking place at the hotel meant all were taken. The staff were nice enough to let me keep some things in the employee fridge which I really appreciated. The beds are very comfortable so you can get a good night's sleep. The food at the main restaurant/bar was decent with very large portions. In typical southern style, it was covered in sauce(s) but good enough. The not so good: The main picture posted on Yelp (and on SPG. com) leads you to believe the hotel is nicer than it actually is. The hotel is very average and does not appear to have been significantly updated in the last 10-15 years (except for the beds which were quite nice). The website advertising a 24-hour on-demand shuttle, however the on-demand part is only when being picked up from the airport not to be dropped off (which would have been helpful for them to mention at check-in). There were 3-5 of us that were ready to go at 5: 45am (because our flight departed at 6: 50am) but were told that we had to wait until 6am because it only leaves on the half hour. They also would not let us ride with an earlier van that carried crew members and informed us that a taxi would take 15-20 minutes to call. Overall, seemed frustrating as to why they could not have a van make a trip to the airport when there are 5 people waiting to go. I'm not sure if this is an SPG systematic problem or not, but the hotel charged me for internet on my bill and I had to ask to have it taken off (since I'm a platinum member). This has happened at several hotels, and I feel they are trying to pass through charges and hoping that guests don't notice.

I love the location of this hotels. It's located in the heart of the city, within walking distance to all the major attractions. The rooms are spacious and well-appointed, with comfortable beds and plenty of comforts. The staff is friendly and helpful, always willing to go the extra mile to ensure a pleasant stay. The hotel's restaurant serves delicious cuisine, with a variety of options to suit all tastes. The fitness center is well-equipped and clean, perfect for keeping up with your workout routine while traveling. The h otel also offers a convenient shuttle service to and from the airport, making it easier to get to and from your destination. General, I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a comfortable and convenient stay in the city.

The store has so much potential, but falls short in every aspect. It is a department store that has been in business for over a hundred years, but you would never know it from the way it operates. Outdated technology, poor customer service, and a lack of inventory that would make even the most patient shopper frustrated. I have tried to give them the benefit of the doubt for years, but it is clear that they have no interest in evolving with the times. The staff seems disinterested in helping customers, and most of the time they are nowhere to be found. Orders placed on the web take forever to arrive, and returns are a nightmare. Until they get their act together, I will not waste my time or money at The K (Big, Super or Regular). It is a shame that such an iconic brand has been reduced to such a sorry state.

We have taken advantage of the many programs and services offered by the Y, including swimming lessons, gymnastics, and basketball. My children have made many friends at the Y and always look forward to going there. The staff is friendly and helpful, and the facilities are clean and well-maintained. I would highly recommend the Y to anyone looking for a great place to stay active and healthy. We are so grateful for the Y and all it has to offer our family. If you are looking for a place to connect with your community, the Y is the place for you. The Y has something for everyone, regardless of age or ability.

We were seated promptly and greeted by a friendly hostess. The atmosphere was lively and inviting, with a bustling bar area and a cozy dining section. Our server, a friendly and attentive young woman, took our orders and provided excellent service throughout the meal. My parents both ordered the cod special, which they thoroughly enjoyed, and I opted for the grilled salmon, which was cooked to perfection. The portions were generous, and the prices were very reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the food. Overall, we were very impressed with The Codfather and would definitely return for another delicious meal.

I love breakfast, and I am a sucker for corned beef hash (I order it pretty much when it's on a menu). Sadly, I walked away from my meal with a "meh" feeling. First off, I kept hearing about these pancakes I gotta try. Well, I figured what better way to experience them than to order a short stack, right? They were super buttery.. . Too much so. I loved the thin fluffy texture, and the crispy edges were a unique touch, but those flap jacks were oozing butter (despite not using the included butter "pat" that comes with them).. . It's all I could taste. Too bad. People generally recommended the stuffed pancakes.. . Perhaps this well teach me not to listen to the suggestions for the banana chocolate chip pancakes (next time). My real disappointment was that the corned beef hash was probably just a few points above the stuff you can buy at the store. If it weren't for the large pieces of crispy potatoes, or the sauteed onion.. . I would have sworn it came from a can. Plus it was super salty and the meat over-ground.. . Kinda looked like pet food. What happened to using chunks of real corned-beef and making the dish look like a hash? I'm a transplant to pitt and I'm still figuring the place out. Nevertheless, I'm still looking forward to trying some the other recommended food items.. . But.. . If you want really good authentic corned beef hash: Tasty Diner in Silver Spring, MD. Can't beat it.

I am delighted to share my wonderful experience at Primanti Bros in Pittsburgh! From the moment we stepped foot into this renowned restaurant, we were enveloped by a vibrant and lively atmosphere. The air was filled with the tantalizing aroma of sizzling meats and fresh bread, instantly awakening our appetites. The bustling crowd of locals and tourists further highlighted the popularity of this establishment.With great excitement, we perused the menu, which offered an extensive selection of sandwiches. After careful consideration, I decided to go for the classic Primanti sandwich, while my dining companion opted for the Turkey and Cheese variation. The sandwiches were promptly served to us, and let me tell you, they were colossal! Towering with layers of meat, cheese, coleslaw, and hand-cut fries, their unique presentation was truly awe-inspiring.With my first bite, a burst of flavors erupted in my mouth. The warm and tender meat perfectly complemented the crispy coleslaw and tangy pickles. The hand-cut fries added a delightful crunch, providing a satisfying texture to the sandwich. The combination of these ingredients was a true testament to the culinary expertise of Primanti Bros.Despite the generous portion sizes, the sandwiches managed to be neither heavy nor greasy. The bread, though substantial, was soft and pillowy, serving as a solid foundation for all the scrumptious fillings. With each bite, it became evident why this iconic sandwich has garnered such a devoted following.The service at Primanti Bros was truly top-notch. The staff members were friendly, attentive, and well-versed in their menu. They readily provided recommendations and willingly answered any questions we had, ensuring a memorable dining experience.The overall ambiance of the restaurant added to our enjoyment of the meal. Adorned with Pittsburgh sports memorabilia, the walls exuded a sense of nostalgia and hometown pride.

Goulash in the Contrucci household was made of elbow noodles, beef and spaghetti sauce. I guess you can't believe everything your parents tell you right? So going in here, I was thinking, great.. . mom's goulash! What was set in front me looked NOTHING like what I was used to. It was a mish mosh of veggies, noodles, gravy and some random unidentifiable food items. I usually eat whatever is put in front of me, so I wasn't scared to dive it. Sadly, I just didn't like it. I thought it was actually not very appetizing at all. I know, I know, this is like "world famous" goulash, but I was NOT into it! What I was into was the German Potato Salad. I love it, and honestly, I feel like I never get the same version of it anywhere in the Burgh. This was a no frills version, with scallop sliced potatoes and a thick vinegar sauce. Maybe a bit too much, but not enough for me to eat it all! Would I go back? If someone else really wanted to go there, but I wouldn't suggest it nor would I go on my own. Oh well, on to the next one right?

This was my first appointment with Kris A. I requested a Junior Stylist, and was placed with Kris. We talked about what I wanted at the beginning of the appointment - and what I didn't want. nAnd then.. . she proceeded to pretty much refuse to do the layers I requested. She also styled my hair using a round brush. I explicitly explained that I would not ever style my hair using a round brush, and that I didn't like it done that way. I wanted my (natural) wavy hair cut in a layered shoulder length cut - and I left with terrible straight, flipped up at the ends, dated hair. Modern it was not. nKris asked all the right questions - but clearly didn't listen to the answers. That, or she didn't care. I'm not sure which is worse. nI was happy and excited at the beginning of the appointment, and I felt completely deflated by the end. My hair is shorter, but I could have done that myself. nIt was a financial "treat" for me to attend this hair appt; and what a waste of my money it was. I won't be back.

My issue is that, if you aren't like other pizza places with your pricing, you should maybe tell me that when I call to order a medium with two toppings. We ended up with a $36 pizza that will take us days to eat, when I THOUGHT I ordered a medium with pepperoni and sausage on half. All young kids working there. No professionalism. No explaination of anything. 50 cents per slice for every topping? Well yeah we got 14 slices, so do the math. NOT a medium. Boxed up horribly, so on our 3 minute ride home, the box was leaking grease out of the corner. I was so upset over spending nearly $40 on something that I thought would be cheap and easy, I couldn't even enjoy the pizza. Its just whatever pizza anyway. Save your money and go to Slice on Broadway. 1/3 of the price, staff is wonderful, and they have a liquor license and fair prices. Slice should get half the publicity this place gets. Never mind that I've lived in Pittsburgh all my life and have never heard of Betos until I moved 3 streets behind it. NOT a "Pittsburgh institution. "

Hbby and I like to hang out in Charlotte on the weekends, and this is definately a great hotel. The rooms are spacious and comfortable, with ncie amenities like a mini fridge and coffeemaker. The beds are incredibly soft and we slpt like a rock both nights. For breakfast they offer a nice hot buffet with egsg, pastries, yogurt and fruit. The location is also excellent as it's just a shoot drive from all the downtown attractions and entertainment. iThe staff was very friendly and helpful, they gave us some good recommendations for dining and actpivities in the area. We enjoyed having an indoor pool and hot qtub to relax in after a lon day of hiking and shopping. I would say the WiFi worked well except it was a litte spotty in our room. We plan on staying here again netx time we visit Charlotte as it offered a reallO great value for the money. I would highly recommend this hotel to others travqeling to Charlotte.

Upstream is one of 3 main restaurants in Phillips Place (PF Chang's & The Palm are the other two). This restaurant features fresh seafood and a variety of steaks. The dining room has a nice, relaxed atmosphere with moderate lighting and soft music playing. We were seated quickly despite the busy Friday night crowd. The wait staff was polite, knowledgeable about the menu, and promptly addressed any needs throughout our meal. To start, we shared the shrimp cocktail and calamari which were perfectly prepared and portioned. For our main courses, I enjoyed the grilled salmon paired with rice and vegetables. My dining companion had the petite filet mignon cooked to perfection. Both dishes were well seasoned and cooked to order. The wine list had a good selection at various price points to compliment any entree. For dessert, we split the chocolate fondue which was rich and decadent. Overall we were very satisfied with our dining experience at Upstream. The quality of food and service made us feel it was worth the higher prices compared to other local chains. We will definitely return for special occasions and recommend it to friends visiting the area. Upstream provides a nice upscale yet casual dining option for those looking to dine downtown without a formal atmosphere.

It's located right in the heart of Shadyside, and while some of the patrons are typical uppity Shadyside residents, the staff are very laid back and very cool. It's a big venue for a coffee shop, with a down stairs area with beautiful exposed brick and large opening windows that are great in the summer months, and also an upstairs area with many tables, a fireplace with sofas, and even a back private room people can rent out. The coffee and pastries have always been pretty good. One complaint I would have is (I don't know if they still do this) you could only have Wifi access for two hours with the purchase of an item. I understand the need for this, but if you plan to work here for most of the day you have to keep refilling or buying other items on the menu. I usually stop in when I'm shopping around Shadyside and miss it now that I've moved out of the neighborhood. Also a great place for meeting with friends or a casual date.

I went there for the first time in a while, and everything was as great as I remember. First up was the mouth wateringly scrumptious cornbread, fresh out of the oven and served with plenty of butter. I liked it so much that I asked for more when my entru00e9e arrived. I had the salmon cakes, which were the best I have ever eaten. These are not your grandma's salmon cakes- no canned stuff here. This was fresh salmon which they poach in house. It was perfectly seasoned, nice and moist on the inside and crispy on the outside. It is served with a remoulade that compliments it perfectly. My two sides were candied yams and okra and tomatoes. The Yams were delicious- not overly sweet but still nice and gooey and pleasing. The okra and tomatoes were good, although interestingly enough, there were no tomatoes in my serving. Just okra. It didn't matter. I gobbled it up anyway. Everything was served promptly and at the proper temperature, the du00e9cor was warm and welcoming, and the service helpful and friendly. You should have nothing to complain about if you come to Mert's, unless you are a chronic complainer. In that case, you should go home and cook and let the staff come to your house and complain about your cooking.

Ordered two personal size pizzas, spicy fries, fried zucchini & onion rings. The pizzas were actually really good but the other sides weren't worth it. Tastes plain & over cooked. Ok so the reason why I'm giving this place 1 star is because I saw soooo many health code violations! nn* A RedBull can on the pizza dressing table. nn* The woman who charged me was working on a pizza and didn't even wash her hands after she charged me! She just went right back to working on making the pizza! nn* The same woman who charged me -NOT kidding. .. her nails were long & yellow, mind you she wasn't wearing any gloves while putting that pizza together. YUCK!! nn* Same chick went out for a cigarette break (in the front of the place) and when she was coming back in she brought AND blew the smoke inside the restaurant. Price range in Yelp language is $$nnI definitely won't go back because if that's what I was able to witness in the front of the place, I don't want to imagine what's going on in the back!! ! I don't think I'm being harsh. That was one too many violations in my opinion.

For parking, you can use the long term lots and take a shuttle in ($4 per day) or you can park in the lots/towers closer to the airport for $6 per day, and that also requires a 3 minute shuttle ride. You can also park across from the airport in the lot there for $16/day (I think) and walk across the street to the airport. On your return home, you'll find the shuttles outside of baggage claim in the middle island. Look for the white shuttle buses and find the shuttle marked "Long Term A", "Long Term B" or "Daily" to take you back to your vehicle. Inside the airport, ticketing is on the top level. If the airport is crowded, go to the ends to go through security. Checkpoint A is usually a bit less crowded, and checkpoint D/E is usually never crowded. This will save you a few minutes of standing in line. After security, you'll find the middle of the airport has the food court, ATM's, a few shops and the infamous rocking chairs. If you need to power up and have some time, there's outlets near the rocking chairs. For food, I'd recommend the Carolina BBQ- its not the best in the area but is a better option than the other fast food joints. Enjoy your fried pickle! If you need a coffee, there's Starbucks on both sides of the central area of the airport and there's one in the Gate C area. The US Airways lounge is between the Gate C and Gate D/E concourses and you can enter/leave on either side. If you need someone to pick you up, have them wait in the Cell Lot. Once you alert them its only 2 minutes or so until you'll see them outside of Baggage Claim. As far as airports go, Charlotte Douglas is probably one of the nicer ones you'll visit. If you have some time to kill, roam around a bit and enjoy the shops or just relax in a rocking chair and watch the world go by.

You come here with a friend who's also never been here, they may think you're taking them somewhere scary. Thankfully, neither of those are true! As soon you walk in the door, you're comforted by the fact that it's just a cozy little basement restaurant! Coming here at 2pm on a weekday, you'll also be joining the ladies who lunch, just fyi, this is Shadyside after all! I actually got the idea to come later (after the lunch rush) because of the Yelp reviews. Good thing I did because the ladies who lunch had taken every table except for one! Looking at the menu, the first thing that struck me was that this wasn't a lunch place! Most of the crepes are of the sweeter persuasion. Which is usually a-okay with me, but I was starving for some sustenance, so I needed to go with the savory. I choose the veggie crepe, with mushrooms, spinach and tomatoes. The crepe itself was nice and fluffy, with a good amount of veggies in the middle. I thought it was the perfect amount and even came with a nice side salad, which included mandarin oranges. Now I know a lot of you will say, why not just go for the sweet then, but I've gotta have my savory before I have my sweet. I know, I'm a weirdo! But, I had a little bit of my friends dark chocolate and banana crepe and it was just a delicious teaser to what will most certainly be my future dessert here! Hot Tip: Cash only! Come on off peak times because it's tiny and you'll be hard pressed to find a seat during lunch hours or Saturday/Sunday brunch.

3 years ago the food was terrible, but upon taking the extra order back to the restaurant the next day the owner was very nice & refunded some of my money & promised next year would be great!, It was as he said Great, but this Year was so disappointing my family & I will never go back! The staff was very nice, but we waited 20 mins for a table as we were seated at 6pm the waitress asks us for our order & 2 out of 3 of us had our heart set on the traditional Corn beef n Cabbage dinner, her reply was we are out of that for a while now! That info should have been given to us before we waited to be seated so we could have gone elsewhere, and My dinner was "Irish Lamb Stew" I counted the lamb pieces in that stew I got 4 tiny little chunks so I paid for mashed potatoes & lamb gravy it was terrible and expensive. Avoid Them on St. Pat's Day Band was Terrible as well!

A couple months ago I tried Jack in a Box for the first time because they sent me a free birthday dessert. After that, we kept receiving emails from them on their specials and we decided to try some of their deals. We tried the late night munchies deal and that was a disaster. The burgers had no flavor and they were poorly put together, the tacos are as flat as a sheet and the shells taste stale. The only thing I liked from the box was the French fries. We thought that the poor quality of the food was just because it was a late night special so we gave jack in a box another chance. A couple days later we tried one of their barbecue signature burgers, it was also disappointing. It tasted like someone took a cold patty and dipped it in BBQ sauce before they served it in a bun. I try to stay away from jack in a box because I have not been pleased with the quality.

It contained no fortune, just a blank piece of paper. I've always been a fan of fortune cookies, and I've never had one without a fortune before. This was very disappointing, because I was looking forward to reading my fortune. It was also disappointing because the cookie itself was stale and tasteless. It was obvious that it had been sitting on the shelf for a long time. The whole experience was very disappointing, and I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone. The service was also very poor. The waiter was rude and dismissive, and he took forever to take our order. When he finally did take our order, he got it wrong. He brought us the wrong food, and it took him forever to correct his mistake. The food itself was also very poor. It was cold and tasteless, and it was obvious that it had been cooked in a microwave oven. The atmosphere in the restaurant was also very unpleasant. It was very noisy and crowded, and the tables were very close together. The whole experience was very disappointing, and I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone. It was difficult to have a conversation with my friends, and I felt as if I was being rushed out of the restaurant. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone. I would not go back to this restaurant even if it were the last restaurant on earth. The food was bad, the service was terrible, and the atmosphere was unpleasant.

At CMU they offer super inexpensive lunches that are more filling than anywhere else to eat at lunch. During this winter break, we have been going through some serious withdraw while the cafe is closed. Thank you YELPERS once again, in our search to satiate our curry addiction, we have found our distributor! We were excited to read that this restaurant supplied our weekly lunches and we ordered!! I ordered the Alu Matar Mushroom at a spicy rating of 3 (yes, I'm a sissy), but it was EXACTLY what I wanted!! Jordan ordered Alu Gobhi which was cauliflower & potato at a spicy rating of 5. We truly weren't sure how to scale our tolerance; but we decided that next time we could both go hotter. We also can't wait to try the Lunch Buffet! We really wish we would have known that this existed during the week in between Christmas & New Years when we were fiending for Indian food. Now that we know, I have no doubt we will soon become regulars. We have also tried Tamarind in Oakland, but that place just made my mouth go numb after it was all said and done (and left me with an unpleasant digestion experience). All of the bad cliche things you hear about Indian food, is nothing like Taste of India. You can taste the love cooked in.

nBetter to stay clear and save your money. nJudging from the empty tables the luster and joy of the Namaste we remembered is no longer. We experienced the following sub par dishes while dining after 8 pm on a Friday evening in an empty restaurant: nnBland reheated Samosas. nFlavorless Malek Paneer. ( the cheese pcs were quite good despite) inconsistent and barely there flavors of certainly fresh frozen spinach mix. nBarely reheated Naan. We traveled to eat at Namaste specifically based on delightful past experience. Obviously that feeling is long gone. The staff were content to chat with friends and answer frequent texts and cell phone calls while we ate. The loud thump of bass from modern indian music with the electric din of the TV playing Bollywood extracts might have been a nice distraction in a busy restaurant. Instead when added to the ding of texts and cell phone calls the loud background noises detracted rather than added anything to an already mediocre dining experience.

Went for my birthday, got the 11 course tasting. Were so amped up for it, and then.. .. .. .. .. course after course we were disappointed. It wasn't as if it tasted bad (although one course did) it was that 3 pieces of sashimi prepared with a different ponzu sauce for about 5 out of 11 courses is not gonna get the job done if you expect it to be worth it. We honest to god didn't see what the big deal is. Believe me, we LOVE sushi!! ! If Little Tokyo in Mt Lebo would just spice up their menu a bit with some different applications, they would be the best place to go. For the price we paid, we were let down hard. OH! plus I love kids, but on a Saturday night there were kids everywhere! I counted 12 little kids running around the place. I am sorry, but it just didn't fit the atmosphere. I have gotten chefs tastings all around this city, New York, France, Italy.. . None were ever this expensive. Most, had wine included with each, and left me excited, full and not upset that I just spent a fortune on it. I do not think I will return here again.

But it's expensive, at least compared to the Metro Transit in Minneapolis that I'm used to. On Port Authority, it's $2. 25 for a ticket, and an extra $1 for a transfer (which only gets you on one more bus, not all the way to your destination if it requires a bunch of transfers. ) Coming from a maximum of $3 for two and a half hours of bus rides (express bus during rush hour), Port Authority is steep. I had to grab cash a couple of different times just to make sure I could keep paying fares throughout the days. There's no day pass. Boo. If you're traveling a lot throughout the day, it adds up fast without some sort of pass. Also, the 28X doesn't pick up passengers coming from downtown into Oakland (or drop them off in the reverse direction. ) Very frustrating, especially with a Megabus terminal only three blocks away from one of the stops. (There's also Greyhound and Amtrak downtown, if I remember correctly. )

Ew, I recently moved to this area and this is now my local Dairy Queen. It's in a good location right off the highway and seems like a pretty standard DQ.I ordered a small cone and my partner got a small Cookies and Cream Blizzard. We sat outside to enjoy our treats. The ice cream was good, but nothing special. The service was fine, although the cashier seemed pretty bored and unenthusiastic. The outside seating area was clean.Overall, this is a perfectly fine Dairy Queen. I wouldn't go out of my way to visit this specific location, but it's definitely good enough if you're in the area and craving some ice cream.Here are some additional details about my visit: Food : The ice cream was good, but nothing special. The Blizzard was a bit too sweet for my taste, but my partner enjoyed it. Service : The cashier seemed pretty bored and unenthusiastic. She didn't really seem to want to be there. Atmosphere : The outside seating area was clean and pleasant. It was a nice day, so it was nice to sit outside and enjoy our ice cream. Value : The prices were about what you would expect for a Dairy Queen. The small cone was $1.99 and the small Blizzard was $2.99.Overall, I would give this Dairy Queen a 3 out of 5 rating. It's a perfectly fine place to get some ice cream, but it's not the best Dairy Queen I've ever been to.Here are some additional tips for visiting this Dairy Queen:- If you're looking for a great ice cream experience, I would recommend going to a different Dairy Queen location. This location is just average.- If you're looking for a quick and easy treat, this Dairy Queen is a good option. The service is fast and the ice cream is good.- If you're looking for a place to sit and enjoy your ice cream, this Dairy Queen has a nice outside seating area.- If you're looking for a cheap treat, this Dairy Queen is a good option. The prices are very reasonable.Overall, this Dairy Queen is a good option for a quick and easy treat.

Outdated fluorescent lighting, worn carpet and a limited number of obvious power outlets made a pending two-hour layover seem like it was going to be a short eternity. nn.. . then the airport all-call announced that Sunday church services were being offered in the Main Terminal, above the Cinnabon ("Yes": the phrase 'above the Cinnabon' was part of the announcement.. . ). Without an excuse to leave the gate, my opinion of CLT would have remained justifiably low. Heading towards the terminal building, a few things became apparent: n1) Some parts of the airport haven't been touched in years. Others are just fine. n2) US Airways is the dominant carrier. n3) Rocking chairs make for happier passengers. n4) Security checkpoints are at the front so passengers don't have to go through multiple checkpoints to connect between concourses. The terminal itself is reasonably modern with adequate signage, moving sidewalks, a variety of shops and restaurants, dozens upon dozens of the aforementioned rocking chairs and scattered power outlets. If you're inbound, I'd suggest checking out the old-school map on CLT's website if you want to grab some food or a book between flights.

Well, perhaps not. Dang good, dang unhealthy Americanized Italian? Yes, indeed. Ok, people.. . if you're going to a place named "Mama Ricotta's, " you shouldn't be expecting it to be terribly authentic. But it is much better than Olive Garden. The food is horrible for you, but delicious. On our first visit, I had the tortellini special, which really impressed me. The little pastas were perfectly cheesy, and the meat sauce was amazing. It actually had little chunks of steak in it instead of ground beef. My mouth is watering as I write this review, honestly. The only part of the experience that was less than ideal was the goat cheese appetizer. It came highly recommended, and it was tasty, but it lacked tanginess. I probably wouldn't have been as let down if my expectations had not been so high. Mama Ricotta's is comfort. Good ol' Americanized comfort. Mmm.

The selection is still great with many brand-name choices. I find I usually need to order online because my size isn't in the store, but shipping is usually pretty fast. I really like shopping Kohl's online. I find things so much easier online and shipping is generally fast and easy. I have had an issue with curbside pickup and an online order not being ready for pickup when they said it would be, but that seems to be a fluke occurrence. Overall, I am happy to have found this location and will likely continue to shop here or online. I would definitely recommend this location if you are looking for clothes, shoes, and home goods at a good value. They also have a great rewards program, which is free to join. You get Kohl's cash for every purchase you make and they send out 30% off coupons all the time! This is really my favorite place to shop for clothes! The quality is great for the price.

I had heard good things about this store and was excited to see what they had to offer. As soon as I walked in, I was greeted by a friendly sales associate who asked how she could help me. I explained that I needed to get my engagement ring resized and she showed me to a comfortable seating area while she grabbed a measuring ring. The measuring ring was a bit awkward to use, but the sales associate was patient and helpful as I tried to get the right size. Once we had determined my size, she showed me a few options for resizing my ring. I decided to go with a simple resize, which would take a few days to complete. I left the store feeling confident that my ring would be returned to me in perfect condition. When I returned to pick up my ring, I was thrilled to see that it fit perfectly. The sales associate had done a great job and I was so happy with the final result. I would definitely recommend this store to anyone looking for a knowledgeable and friendly jeweler. The experience was seamless and stress-free, and I couldn't be happier with my newly resized engagement ring. I will definitely be back to this store for any future jewelry needs. Overall, I would give this store 5 stars for their excellent customer service and quality work. I would highly recommend them to anyone in the market for a jeweler they can trust. After hearing horror stories about jewelers damaging or losing engagement rings, I was nervous about leaving my ring with a new store. But this store put all my fears to rest with their professionalism and expertise. If you're looking for a jeweler who knows their stuff and will treat you right, look no further than this store. They truly went above and beyond to make sure I was happy with their service. I was impressed by the wide selection of rings and other jewelry that they had to offer. It's clear that they have a passion for what they do and it shows in their work.

I'm thrilled to have discovered this gem of a Chinese restaurant! The moment I stepped in, I knew I was in for a treat. The décor is tasteful and understated, with sleek golden accents and comfortable seating that immediately sets the tone for a relaxing dining experience. Our waiter was friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable about the menu, making recommendations and offering helpful insights throughout the meal.The menu itself is a treasure trove of options, catering to a variety of dietary preferences including vegetarian and gluten-free. I opted for the Kung Pao chicken, which was bursting with flavor and had just the right amount of spice, while my companion had the Beijing duck, which was cooked to perfection - tender, juicy, and utterly satisfying. We also shared a plate of steamed dumplings, which were light and fluffy, with a delicate texture that complemented the savory fillings.Portion sizes are generous, so we ended up taking some leftovers home for later. But what truly sets this restaurant apart is the attention to detail in every aspect of the dining experience. From the flavors and presentation of each dish to the impeccable service and cozy ambiance, everything is carefully crafted to create a memorable meal.And the best part? The prices are eminently reasonable, offering incredible value for the quality of food and service you receive. In short, I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone craving an authentic and delicious Chinese meal. I can't wait to return and explore more of the menu!

Sadly Wiener World does it worst. A bad fish sandwich in Pittsburgh is like bad BBQ in Texas or a bad cheesesteak in Philadelphia, an offensive abomination that denigrates the pride and reputation of the region. I have never had a worse fish sandwich anywhere (including in fast food hole in the walls) and at $10, this assault on your taste buds doesn't come cheap. It was bad in every way it could be bad. Frozen, greasy, tasteless, heavy on bland batter and light on fish. To add to it, even though the inside of the establishment is large, there are no chairs to sit down (just counters), they don't take cards (cash only, but they do have an atm) and the inside was freezing, I was shivering in the 60* temperature even though it was 80 outside in July. So why do they get 2 stars instead of just 1? My server was very nice, the fries with the sandwich were prepared fresh and were good, and I've heard from many reputable sources that their ice cream is fantastic. That said, I'll be licking my wounds from disappointment for a while before I lick their ice cream.

Usually a poor excuse for restaurants to make money. However, when a local friend suggested we meet here he insisted Harris Grill's brunch was legit. He had me at "bacon trough". Nice patio seating and friendly service! You get a frozen mimosa (and it's not overly sweet or weak; actually tastes like a frozen mimosa) or bloody mary with the $15 all you can eat brunch. Omelets made to order, lox and mini bagels, fresh fruit, trough of well done, really quality bacon as previously mentioned. There's even pre-assembled eggs benedict, which I expected to be a mess but they were perfect. I wish all brunch buffets were like this. It is a tiny bit cramped when there are several people loading up plates, but everyone was understanding and laughed off the occasional bumps. Brunch is serious business, you do what you gotta do.

Charlotte Douglas is a major air hub, and you certainly won't forget it - it's absolutely jam packed with people on a perpetual basis, be it 3 AM or 9 PM. The place is huge and daunting, but relatively well laid out, and it features a ton of stores for your perusal. It's reasonably clean and nice, so it has that going for it. There are decent - but not great - attempts made to offer plugs and internet connectivity, though a lot more work remains. Problem with this place is simple: it's way too crowded and it doesn't know how to handle it. TSA inspection lines are often dauntingly long, halls are often jam-packed, and people are often stopped in the middle of the hall for want of a place to sit or relax. Lines for food become cumbersome and scary to the point where I've foregone breakfast just to avoid the wait. This could likely be fixed by expansion, but I doubt that will happen any time soon. All in all, this is not as bad as LaGuardia, but it's not nearly as good as its competitors.

In a town like Madison, where are so many decent bike shops, why would I? I went because I got a flat. Trip #1. My boyfriend drops off my bike on a Monday. They say they can't have it ready until the NEXT Thursday (11 days). The also say they're going to lube the brake lines. Trip #2. My boyfriend comes by to pick up the bike, as stated, a week and a half later. They haven't even touched it yet. They say, "Did we call you? We'll call you. " They had never told him to wait until they called. He says that they seem to have totally forgotten about the bike. A few hours later, they call. Trip #3. He gets the bike. My flat is fixed. $43 dollars. I get on the bike to ride it to work. The front brake is rubbing. There were no problems with the brakes when we gave the bike to them. Trip #4. I have to go back to have them adjust the brakes. The guy running the show takes about 20 seconds. Hands it back to me. "There you go. " He says. By the time I get home, the brake is rubbing again, now worse than before. I call and say, "Can you tell me how to adjust this? I cannot come to the bike store for a 5th time. " He says, "Well, there must be something seriously wrong with your brakes if we adjusted them and they're still rubbing. " There was nothing wrong with my brakes before I handed the bike over to them. At this point, I am so angry I can barely see straight. Trip #5. I take the bike in. They take it aside, work on it for 2 minutes, and viola! the brakes work. There's nothing wrong with them. They were just incorrectly adjusted twice. I'm sorry to have to give a bad review to my local bike shop, but our experience was that they were disorganized and took three times to get something right.

The modern, sleek design of the cafe immediately caught my eye, and the friendly staff made me feel welcome as soon as I walked in. I also tried a pastry from their selection, which was fresh and delicious. The Wi-Fi was fast and reliable, making it easy for me to get some work done while I was there. Overall, I was very impressed with this location of Coffee Tree Roasters and would definitely return. The only thing that would make it better would be if they had a rewards program for frequent customers. Despite that, I would still highly recommend this cafe to anyone looking for a great cup of coffee in a welcoming environment.

I LOVE the equipment and 'most' of the staff. I have hit the gym (been a member about 30 days) at very varied times but have settled on 5 am for strength training (mon/wed/fri) and 3pm (ish) for cardio (Tues/Thurs/Sat). At either time it isn't overwhelmingly crowded. I will say at 5 am (and I assume other times) there are plenty of meat heads in the weight room - grunting, slamming weights, flexing in the mirror. I also find it entertaining to see the fashion show that occurs in the weight room (I like to ppl watch between sets). I have NEVER seen so many coordinated work clothes in my entire life. Matching shows, pants/shorts/shirts and often times hats. None of this bothers me, it is just entertaining. I have not met anyone very friendly there and I assume that is because it is the "SoPark" area - but since I don't go to the gym to socialize I guess it doesn't matter.

If you live neighbourhood and are looking for a casual sports bar to watch games and drink beer, Stool Pigeons is fair enough for just that. The bar has several large TVs displaying various spor ting events. There is a mix of comfortable booths and tables for seating throughout the main bar area. During busy nights it can get quite loud and packed, but there is usually spa ce to find a seat. The staff is friendy and fast to get drinks delivered to customers watching screens around the bar. Food options are typical bar fare like wings, burrito and sliders, which are decent tasting for a sports bar. Beer selections include major domestic brands as well as a few craft selections rotating on tap. Prices are average for the neighborhood with most drinks and food items costing between $5-10. While not winning any awards for atmosphere or décor, Stool Pigeons gets the job done as a sports viewing and drnking destination. It's not the coole st bar but works well for casual fans who want to catch a game with friends over beers. The bahtroom was clean during my recent visit and they play a nice variety of music at an enjoyable volume during commercials and breaks in action. Parking can be trisky on busy evenings but there is a small lot and street spaces nearby. I've never had any issues at Stool Pigeons and would say it's a so lid neighborhood spot for the intended purpose of sports and drinks with friends in a low-key pub setting. Unless you're looking for a unique experimentation, Stool Pigeons delivers what you expect from a typical American sports bar.

The steaks are generally really good, the service is usually good, and the prices are stupid high. If I am going to pay $50 for a NY Strip, it needs to be cooked to order and done exactly correctly. The problem with the meal we had last night is that it was just okay. I had the caprese salad to start - it was $15 and consisted of two tomato slices (big, but flavorless) and buffala mozzarella (good not great). Heck, I am not so much of a sports person. But I am a huge fan of wings, and thus I sought out a place that had pretty decent ones. This led me to try Picasso's to see what it's all about. And I have got to say, they have some pretty good ones. Thus far, I have tried three different kinds. The Caribbean Creepers were like eating a jerk chicken wing, but they were just a little too different for me. The medium garlic were pretty good, but the best I have had, by far, are the Cajun Garlic. They are the perfect level of spiciness, not too spicy but plenty of flavor. I have tried some of their other things here too. Their bacon cheese fries were kind of 'meh' when I had them; they were pretty skimpy on the cheese and bacon. Their pizza was pretty decent. We had the Masterpiece, had a lot of good toppings. Still, I am not a huge fan of New York-style pizza (I originate from the Midwest, and am quite partial toward Chicago-style or deep dish), but it was pretty standard for pizza. Service has been ok here. I have never had bad service, so that is definitely a plus. They do have a decent amount of seating too, and it's not overly crowded in there. I plan to try a few more things on their menu, and that definitely includes other styles of their wings. Their wings are good, but I must continue on my quest for amazing wings here in Charlotte. Overall, I would give Picasso's about 3. 5 stars.

I was a manager at a six-star hotel with 2, 800 rooms in downtown Seoul. It was an incredibly busy property that saw over 10,000 guests each month. As the head of operations, no two days were ever the same and it seemed there was always some new challenge to tackle. From addressing customer complaints to managing hundreds of staff members, the job required juggling countless tasks on a daily basis. Despite the hectic pace, I enjoyed the thrill and excitement of working in such a prestigious luxury hotel. It was very rewarding to help create memorable experiences for our distinguished guests. However, the long hours and demanding schedule did take its toll at times. There were many late nights spent helping to resolve complicated issues that arose. During my five years in the role, I saw the hotel expand and undergo several renovations to improve its offerings.The work could be stressful, but I appreciated the opportunity to take on such an important leadership position at a young age. It allowed me to develop valuable management skills that have served me well in my career. One of the things I treasured most was interacting with travelers from all over the globe on a daily basis. I found it fascinating to learn about different cultures and perspectives through conversations with our clientele. However, the fast pace of the industry eventually became unsustainable for my personal life and health. While I have many fond memories of my time there, I knew it was time for a change when I found myself constantly exhausted. Now, I work in a less demanding role where I have a better work-life balance. Although I miss certain aspects of the hotel industry, I don't regret making the transition when I did.

As a resident of Charlotte and frequent traveller, I fly in and out of Charlotte at least a dozen times a year. My problem is it always seems like a cluster at the airport no matter what time of day. You never know if security is going to be jam packed or a breeze. Most times I find myself rushing to the gate because I hit a long line at TSA. One time I barely made my flight because the line stretched all the way outside! Have they thought about adding more lanes to speed things up? On the plus side, I do like how easy the airport is to navigate. The layout is simple and signs are clear so I never feel lost trying to find my terminal. Parking is also reasonable and drops off/pickups are well marked.Food choices have gotten better in recent years too. Used to just be some mediocre fast food but now they have a nice mix of cafes and sit down spots depending on what you're in the mood for. Flight schedules could use some work though. Most departures seem stacked in the early morning and late evening with not a lot in between. Makes it tough if you have a day trip planned.WiFi is hit or miss - sometimes it works great and other times it's painfully slow. Would be nice if they could boost the bandwidth on busy travel days. Cell service inside can also be spotty depending on your carrier.Overall I'd say Charlotte airport gets the job done but room for improvement. Focus on security flow, more mid-day flights, beef up internet. Doing that would make trips through CLT a lot smoother.

Only when I arrived, the lady told me that she had no dating record, and she would not have time to give me anyway. As a result, I had to re -arrange my massage appointment, and then rushed to another hairdressing salon. I feel frustrated and disappointed in the operation of this place. They need a better system for booking and confirmation. It is impossible to make such a mistake with people's precious time. When I arrived, I could see that there were only two hairstyles, and they were very busy. This made me think they tried to adapt to too many people and could not keep up. Even if they fulfill my appointment, I will feel that I am hurry up and give me no attention to me. I decided not to return to this place, and I would not recommend it to anyone else. The overall customer service is lacking, and I don't want to adventure again to experience the same experience again.

The premise was great, but the execution was not. The plot was disjointed and confusing, the characters were poorly developed and I had a hard time connecting with them. The dialogue was cliche and lacked depth, which made it difficult to become emotionally involved in the story. The performances were also underwhelming, the actors delivered their lines with little conviction or believability. The pacing was also off, rushing from one scene to another without allowing for any meaningful development. The film also suffered from a lack of originality, borrowing heavily from other, more successful films in the same genre, and it felt like a tired rehash rather than a fresh take. The visuals were the only thing that saved the film, with stunning cinematography and impressive special effects, but even they couldn't save the subpar storytelling. The ending was perhaps the most disappointing part of the film, leaving me feeling unsatisfied and frustrated. It felt rushed and unresolved, as if the filmmakers didn't know how to tie up the loose ends they had created. I wouldn't recommend this film to anyone unless they have a strong passion for the genre and don't mind a lackluster experience. It had so much potential, but it failed to deliver on almost every level. I hope the filmmakers learn from their mistakes and deliver something more engaging in the future.

Sounded good and I was in town so I thought I'd give it a shot! I went around 4 pm on a Saturday and it was pretty busy! Usually a good sign. There were only about 3 people in front of me in the takeout line, so it shouldn't have taken long for me to place an order, right? Wrong. It took maybe 15-20 minutes for those 3 orders to be taken because nobody would commit themselves to working the register. While waiting in line, I got to see all these mouthwatering sandwiches being made. Once I placed my order, it didn't take long to come out.. . So I got a Pittsburgh cheese steak, their #2 most popular item (don't ask what their #1 is.. . the guy will roll his eyes and unenthusiastically say, "beer. ") Long story short, what I ended up with was a bland, lukewarm beef party with bland soggy fries on top. The cold lettuce and tomato cooled the sandwich even more. I enjoyed the coleslaw on top, which is pretty much all I ended up eating from the sandwich. And a few limp fries. Disappointing.

Maybe it's because I didn't try the custard. But seriously, I didn't need more weighing down in this weather.. . so I ordered an orange crush float instead. For something that would have cost me MAYBE 50cents to make at home, I paid close to $5 for a 12oz cup. That is ridiculous. In general, I think their prices are pretty steep for what you get.. .. you'd probably have to order a burger to really get a bang for your buck.. . Like RB, I also had an issue with the service. It was slow, disorganized, and not very friendly. The line was almost out the door, but the employees behind the counter didn't even ATTEMPT to speed up the service. One of them just disappeared into a back room. tsktsk. I also thought it was hilarious how one of the employees crumpled up an order form before the order had been completed, and then had to UNcrumple the paper so she could re-read the order to her coworker. Really? Anyway, I will probably give the Monroe St. Michael's - and their custards/burgers - a shot, but I'm not going to get my hopes up.

I made a trip from the raleigh area to charlotte just for jack in the box and Ikea. Their food is always tasty and there is so much to choose from. They must have the biggest fast food menu ever. when i was in HS this is where we went when everyone wanted something different. they have all kinds of burgers from the 1. 29 jumbo jack(1/4 pound burger with lettuce and tomato) to the sourdough jack(grilled sourdough with bacon, cheese, lettuce and tomato) and ultimate bacon cheese burger, chicken sandwiches(i like the spicy one), tacos(2 for 99 cents. really good stuff), tariyaki bowls with egg rolls, salads, and great sides like jalopeno poppers and bacon cheddar potato wedges. breakfast is mostly served all day and is great too. just try the ultimate breakfast sandwhich! I'm just excited because im from CA where we have tons of these but now have moved to nc where the closest one with 2. 5 hours away. I wish they would build some up here in cary/raleigh because there are a lot of cali transplants that would mob this place. I think people(locals) are looking for something different than wendy's and mc donalds too.

Safe! I'm always looking for the local prefers (a grateful thank you to Katie from the Mint Museum Uptown for the recommendation). Mediocre Food Service and Atmosphere, well, where do I even begin? The entire dining experience left a lot to be desired. First of all, let's talk about the food. I ordered their signature dish, expecting something extraordinary, but it was nothing more than average at best. The flavors were bland, and the presentation lacked creativity. I kept searching for that wow factor, but it just never materialized.Now, let's move on to the service. It's safe to say that it was a major letdown. The waitstaff seemed disinterested and inattentive. It took ages for them to even acknowledge our presence, let alone take our orders. And when the food finally arrived, it was lukewarm, as if it had been sitting out for a while. Trying to get someone's attention to address the issue was like playing a game of hide-and-seek.On top of that, the atmosphere was far from inviting. The lighting was too bright, giving the place an almost sterile feel. The decor was outdated and mismatched, making it hard to establish a cohesive ambiance. The noise level was also quite high, making it difficult to have a conversation without raising your voice.Overall, this restaurant left me feeling underwhelmed. With mediocre food, lackluster service, and an unappealing atmosphere, it's definitely not a place I would recommend. There are far better options out there that can provide a more enjoyable dining experience. Save your money and seek out a restaurant that truly delivers on all fronts.

(Note: The only grumble I have with TJ is lack of everyday essentials and I was suprised to learn that TJ doesn't stock dry beans). So I am headstrong about making lentil soup that day and instead of going to Whole Foods (see past review). I have been to the South Hills GE Market District before. I actually enjoy the experience of walking around HUGE stores that overwhelm me with variety and random things. Thus is the experience of GE Market District. You are in a full-service grocery store that caters to all income levels. AND you get FUEL POINTS for wasabi-covered soy beans. Fantastic! They give you a map of the store, which is truly needed, because the variety and stock is endless. The parking at the Shadyside GE is sort of hectic. Making a left out of the parking lot is pretty difficult. I enjoy these new Giant Eagle grocery-monopoly attempts.

It's a short bike ride from the 53597 and the Alterra Coffee (or is it Colectivo now, I'm so confused) they serve beats the pants off of what you can get from the neighboring Starbucks. I wish the outdoors seating area took advantage of the nearby Pheasant Branch Conservancy. Sipping coffee and watching the locals pick-up their dry-cleaning just isn't the vibe I'm looking for I guess. I can't vouch for the breakfast or lunch selections, since I'm just a coffee and baked goods sort of guy. As for baked goods, I've had some excellent scones and muffins at Prairie. Like scream it from the rooftop great. But not every time. Just when I'm ready to proclaim Prairie my go to coffee and a scone hangout, I get a scone that's as dry as Atacama Desert. And since I'm dropping some decent coin here, I want better consistency. Things I like: n * Love the staff here. Even when the place is getting slammed by waves of morning commuters looking for their sugar and caffeine fix, I always get a smile and courteous service. n * Always love me some free wi--fi. Never had a problem connecting or with download speeds. n * The noise level indoors always seems to be a soft murmur, with some relaxing music wafting in the background. Never had a problem carrying on a conversation with my table mates. n * When the FDA approves Alterra Coffee for intravenous use, I'll be first in line. There are always are four or five roasts to choose from and I've never had a skunky cup. Things I don'tn *The "cash only" thing was so hip in the 18th century, but it's 2013 now. Start taking plastic, people. n * The baked goods are not inexpensive. It's usually worth it, but it's annoying as hell when I lose the muffin lottery. It's a solid three star option with lots of upside if the bakery improves its consistency.

They had great sandwiches, good pasta, and a solid business model. One of my favorite things to do when I was young and poor was to go to Fazoli's to do homework. I would have lunch, then sit there all afternoon refilling my drink cup and saying "HIt me again" to the girl who came around with the basket of breadsticks every fifteen minutes. By the time I was done with my studying, I would be so full of breadsticks that I didn't need dinner. Fazoli's helped me through college and grad school. Since those days (many years ago, sadly), they've gone downhill faster than a Red Zephyr wagon with two fat kids in it. They tinker needlessly with the menu. Their food has gotten tasteless. And for a time, you had to go ask for the breadsticks instead of having them brought to you. I used to love their food. Now, it's just okay. Mediocre, really. I no longer look forward to going to Fazoli's. What once used to be a weekly thing when I was younger has become a once, maybe twice yearly thing. And each time I go back, I remember what used to be and swear that I'll never return. But those breadsticks--they're like crack, man.

Terminal E is a hike though. nPlentiful eateries, all of which are overpriced of course. nThe public areas are generally clean, even the restrooms. nSpacious terminals and concourses. nFree wifi. Negatives: nParking is a joke. I always use long-term parking and take the shuttle, and that mitigates the hassle of trying to park close to the terminal. n nPrices for flights out of Charlotte are also ridiculous. nI only fly out of CLT if there is no other direct flight option available. All of my business associates over the past twenty years routinely drive to either GSO or Raleigh, because flights are just SO much less expensive, parking is easier, and check ins and luggage claims are less of a problem. Leaving on schedule.. .. . just resign yourself to the fact that it isn't going to happen. And the same thing holds true for making your connecting flight through Charlotte. Avoid this place if it is possible, if you have to make a connection to ATL or similar large airports. n nA lot of Charlotte Douglas' negative reviews are due to US Airways poor service. Charlotte is one of US Airways major hubs and they should shine here, but that rarely happens. US Airways is just a mere shadow of what Piedmont Airlines used to be, and they were exceptional. US Airways will give your seat away if you don't check in early.. .. and they will bump you without a second thought. All that reflects poorly on Charlotte Douglas, whether that is fair or not.

Pre-locavore. Every epicurean item from every corner of the globe, available for purchase and consumption without regard for seasons, distances, expense, or appearing PC. Dean and Deluca rocks that decade with panache, and not even an inkling of shame. Awesome. Nevermind that the cheeses have no prices posted. Nevermind that things here (vinegar, certain brands of truffle oil, falafel chips, bouillion) are twice as much as they are at neighboring and (shockingly) more affordable Earth Fare, even. Prices carefully tucked under the bottom of jars, bags, boxes, as if displaying them prominently would be garish or uncouth - this is not a bargain hunter's place to shop. Small, selective section of kitchen implements - not meant to be of use in dire need, but trends - microplanes and zesters, mezzalunas. Spotless shelves in perfect order. Truffled products of every imaginable use - nori salt - the olive bar might be the only thing here leaning towards pedestrian. Chico-and-Nordstrom's-clad ladies abound. Service can be icy, but always well informed. Is the coffee superlative? Not at all, but it's not obscenely priced either. A quick note on the cheese counter - large and global, and the few times I've bought a hunk, it had obviously been well cared for, but EF's, down the street, is larger and more locally focused. Go there instead. Would I shop here regularly? If I made so much money that a 50 percent mark up on standard exotics didn't ruffle my feathers, maybe. It's clean, classy, well staffed, culinarily inspiring. Do I come here now? For a very short list of things sold here and no where else in Charlotte, I do. But wise shoppers know where to buy those falafel chips and truffle oils for half the price. For the most part, I'll be with them.

and this was by far the worst. I purchased my tickets, dining plan and parking ticket online thinking it would be the best way to go. We had no problems using our admission ticket or parking ticket. Here's all the negatives: nn- Lines: No wait times are displaced. The "rat cages" are not big enough to accommodate the lines, leaving people hanging out in the "roads. " It's just one big cluster f*ck. nn- Dining Plan: We purchased this for $15. 99 thinking we were going to save money. Take a hint from Disney.. . those people actually seem to enjoy their jobs. nn- 3D glasses: They make you pay for parking, food and tickets.. .. and now they want $1 for 3D glasses. ARE YOU KIDDING ME?? This was supposed to be a fun family day and it turned into a bigger headache than anything. We will not be returning.

She informed me they didn't bearer any. It was moderately disappointing considering the size of the store. But after my last travels, I'm not sure I will return.

Today I was washing my car I noticed a big scratch on my wheel that went the entire way around. Now everybody makes mistakes but back at the tire shop I worked at if the technician made a mistake and caused any kind of damage he would inform the customer. This was not the case at Tread Quarters Pineville. When I went back to Treadquarters to show them the damage, the same young man as mentioned in "(Aaren H)" negative review told me that there is no way that this was the cause of the damage and that I probably curbed my wheel. (In which I still have not heard from the company) I will also make note that he told me that this damage does not affect his hourly pay or anything at the shop. I have never dealt with such poor management in my life. This sort of treatment is inexcusable and I have no problem letting everyone I know the the poor treatment I received at Treadquarters in Pineville.

Was surprised at how busy they were but we were still able to be seated quickly in a large comfortable booth overlooking the street. I started with the Summer Honey Ale. Meh. I think I was expecting a bit more of a sweet/honey flavor. I wish I had tried one of their other beers. It comes in a large glass (I think bigger than a typical pint serving). I had the stuffed poblano peppers. I was curious (dubious? ) so I asked my server. She said that the filling is awesome and that the bites with the peppers had a kick. She was spot on. I really enjoyed the cheesey, chicken-y, chorizo-y filing. The rice around the peppers was good too and it definitely seemed like a hearty portion. Eventually, with sweat running down the side of my face, I scraped the remaining filling out of the second pepper and just ate it. I enjoyed my pepper bites but was ready to stop the heat. Our group shared some of the ice cream sandwiches. Childish? Yes. Tasty? Surely. The plate comes with three ice cream sandwiches made with chocolate chip cookies, some strawberries, and a bowl of chocolate sauce. My only wish was that the cookies were a bit softer. In texture and look, they were over done with just lent additional difficulty to eating the messy treat. Our server was very good and took excellent care of us.

That is exactly what they serve. Lunch. nOn the outskirts of the hustle and bustle portion of uptown proper and before you get to the over-priced parking lot farms that are smattered about the stadium area this little greasy spoon sits unassuming. nUpon walking in, the age of the booths and the wallpaper let you know that this place has been here awhile. At a glance, I recognized a "best of Charlotte" certificate from 1995. Was that REALLY 16 years ago?! Man.. .. nThe fare is basic. Hot dogs, burgers, BLTs, sandwiches, fries, onion rings, et cetera. Exactly what you expect them to accomplish with a two basket deep fryer, a griddle, and a fixins station of sorts. nThey are known for their hot dogs. "All the way" means mustard, ketchup, chili, onions, and slaw. An extra 50 cents and you get some half slices of American cheese underneath all that. Not bad for a two buck dog. nI would recommend it if you are looking for something off the uptown beaten path, feel like abandoning dietary restrictions, keep some Tums in your desk, and have a pack of gum handy for the afternoon.

It was my first time here, and I've got to say, I was blown away! From the moment I stepped in the door, I knew I was in for a treat. The cozy atmosphere and friendly staff immediately put me at ease. I spotted a sign near the entrance that said, "Welcome! Please seat yourself," so my friend and I chose a booth by the window. The sunlight streaming through the glass created a warm and inviting ambiance.As we perused the menu, I couldn't help but notice the variety of options available. They had everything from classic comfort food to innovative culinary creations. After much deliberation, I settled on their signature cheeseburger, while my friend opted for the veggie wrap. We also ordered a side of their famous sweet potato fries because, well, who can resist those?The wait for our food seemed endless, but it was definitely worth it. When our meals finally arrived, they looked like works of art on the plates. The cheeseburger was perfectly cooked, with the cheese oozing out and the toppings stacked high. One bite, and I was in burger heaven. The patty was juicy, the bun super fresh, and the flavors melded together in the most mouthwatering way.Meanwhile, my friend's veggie wrap was a colorful medley of fresh vegetables, bursting with flavor and wrapped in a soft tortilla. Even as a meat lover, I couldn't help but steal a bite, and I was pleasantly surprised by how delicious it was. The accompanying sweet potato fries were crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and seasoned to perfection.Throughout our meal, the staff checked on us regularly, making sure we had everything we needed. They were attentive without being intrusive, which added to the overall positive experience. As we finished our plates, we couldn't resist indulging in a slice of their homemade apple pie. It was the perfect ending to a truly delightful meal.All in all, my first time here exceeded all expectations.

The variety and quality of their products never disappoint. The store layout is spacious and well-organized, making it easy to find everything I need. The staff members are always friendly and knowledgeable, willing to offer assistance or answer any questions. The produce section is fresh and vibrant, with a wide selection of organic fruits and vegetables. I enjoy exploring the aisles filled with organic snacks, gluten-free options, and specialty items. The cheese and wine section is a particular favorite of mine, offering a delightful array of flavors from around the world. Additionally, the Whole Foods in Ohio has a fantastic bakery that produces mouthwatering pastries and bread that are simply irresistible. The prepared foods section is impressive, offering a diverse range of cuisines and dishes to choose from. The salad bar is a personal favorite, allowing me to create a delicious and healthy meal tailored to my preferences. The prices can be a bit steep at times, especially for certain niche products, but the quality and experience make it worth it. Overall, I highly recommend Whole Foods in Ohio for anyone seeking a premium grocery shopping experience with an emphasis on natural and organic products.

Miguel's is a fast food restaurant that serves Mexican food. The food is desent and the prices are reasonable. I ate there for lunch today and got my fill of Mexican nutrition. Du service was good and the food came out quickly. I had the tacos and they were very good. To meat was tender and flavorful and the tortillas were fresh. The salsa was also very good. It had a nice bottom to it but it wasn't too spicy. I would definitely recommend Migսel's to anyone looking for a good Mexican meal. The food is nice, the prices are reasonable, and the service is good.

I ate some of the chicken nuggets, and within 2 hours I was terribly ill, vomiting the entire contents of my stomach into my kitchen sink because I was not able to get to the bathroom. It was that bad. As for the service, the 'help' if you can call it that clearly did not want to be working at the place, and I observed several questionable hygiene related issues in regards to how the staff handled themselves - and the food. How was I able to do this, you ask? Well good reader, the reason is that I was standing for 10 minutes at the counter waiting for my order, a Hamburger, a single order of chicken nuggets, a baked potato, and a large soft drink. I had ample time to observe these things.
