This place is a hidden gem. It's located in a small strip mall, but don't let that fool you. The food is amazing! I had the chicken tikka masala and it was so flavorful and tender. The garlic naan was also delicious. The service was great too. Our server was very attentive and made sure we had everything we needed.I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who loves Indian food. It's definitely worth checking out. I'm already planning my next visit. I can't wait to try some of the other dishes on the menu. I'm sure they're all just as delicious as the chicken tikka masala.If you're looking for a great Indian restaurant, look no further than this place. You won't be disappointed. The food is amazing, the service is great, and the prices are reasonable. What more could you ask for?

I love the atmosphere of the restaurant in particular the upstairs space. It has a lofty, cozy feel. Great place for drinks or and event (can rent the upstairs space). My last visit was for a working business meeting. Glad we made reservations for it was busy on a Friday evening. I ordered the roast beef sandwich which was very tasty and flavorful. I love that you have a variety of options for a side and they do not charge you extra. I picked my favorite, mashed potatoes. A colleague ordered the pesto pasta dish which looked delicious. We didn't order drinks but in past visits they have a really nice variety of beer and I tried the Banana Bread beer (available in bottles) which is so tasty!! My only complaint was that it took a while for the waitress to take our orders and bring out the checks but it was very crowded with large parties. We stayed at our table after dinner to finish up some work and they did not mind which was great!

We parked in front of Roland's and see the sign: Famous for Lobster Rolls and Bloody Mary's! Perfect. My mother got the Lobster Roll, which she said was 'good'. The bread, from Mancini's, was of course tasty - toasted and buttery - delicious mostly because it was Mancini's bread. I had the Lobster Roll minus the carbs on a salad - and the lobster was tasty, no doubt, I mean, lobster is just - good. For the price though, not sure that I got enough bang for my buck. The salad was something I could have picked up at Get-Go in the pre-made section. I just didn't feel satisfied at the end of my meal. I couldn't even drink my Bloody Mary (this is a rare affair), way too much horseradish, and I often like horseradish in my Bloodies! And it was cold - didn't even take my winter coat off. So, needless to say, not the best experience. Talk about false advertisement.. .

We had heard so many great things about this place and were excited to try it out for ourselves. The atmosphere was cozy and romantic, perfect for a special occasion. We were warmly greeted by the hostess and shown to our table. The menu was extensive, and it took us a while to decide what to order. We started with the bruschetta appetizer, and it was delicious. The bread was perfectly toasted, and the toppings were flavorful. For our main courses, I chose the homemade pasta with Bolognese sauce, while my boyfriend opted for the filet mignon. The pasta was cooked to perfection, and the Bolognese sauce had a rich and savory taste. The filet mignon was tender and juicy, cooked exactly to my boyfriend's preferences. We were impressed with the portion sizes as well; they were generous without being overwhelming. The service throughout the evening was exceptional. Our waiter was attentive, knowledgeable, and made sure we had everything we needed. The wine selection was extensive, and our waiter helped us choose a bottle that complemented our meal perfectly. We couldn't resist dessert and ordered the tiramisu to share. It was simply divine, with layers of moist cake, creamy mascarpone, and a hint of coffee flavor. Overall, our experience at Alla Famiglia was outstanding. The food, service, and ambiance all surpassed our expectations. It was definitely a memorable evening, and we can't wait to return for another special occasion. We highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a truly exceptional dining experience.

The used car Sales Manager is lacking character and integrity. They had a vehicle priced online right at the price we were looking for so we went in to see the vehicle. It was a very basic, no feature vehicle for a college student. Once we agreed to purchase it, they came out with a price $1000 higher than what was listed. The Sales Manager came out and tried to make excuses for a 3rd party company that posts their sales ads and that it was their mistake.. . we told him it wasn't our issue. He then proceeded to LIE to us about the costs they put into the vehicle.. . since they would never put into it more than what it's worth. This man should not be in the position he's in, as they could have easily made up for their $1K mistake just in the day and should have honored the price they advertised.. . and to sit and lie to our face? Get some integrity loser!

I will not be bringing it back any time soon. My shocks were broken in the back of my car. They told me they needed to be replaced and they had the parts in stock. They were 350 a side and the labor would be about another 300 so it came out to about 1, 000 bucks in all. Well I took the invoice and drove back home thinking what I could do to come up with 1, 000 bucks. I googled the part number and on amazon the same part was selling for 110. So they were going to charge me more than 3 times what it was selling on amazon for?? ? ? Is this normal?? ? Then I did a little more research and found out that wasn't even the right part! They were going to put in the shocks meant for the front of the car instead of the rear. I ended up getting the parts off line and had them installed elsewhere. Anything more than an oil change, I wouldn't trust them.

We looked up some places nearby on Yelp and decided to try out this new restaurant called The Local. Literally, like 15 minutes later we walked in, sweaty and starving. The hostess sat us right away at a small table in the corner which worked cause we were gross from working all day. I got an IPA and my friend ordered some pineapple wheat beer that sounded refreshing. We started looking over the menus but everything looked so good! They had pizza, pasta, sandwiches plus some daily specials written on a chalkboard. I was craving a burger so bad after a day with no real food.My friend got one of the pasta dishes that had like four different types of meat in it. It came out and she was in heaven, plowing through that carb coma in no time. When the server came back, I decided to get a burger with fries plus they had Brussels sprouts as a side so I got those too. It came out and wow, that burger hit the spot exactly how I wanted. The fries were hot and crisp plus the Brussels sprouts had just the right amount of char on them. We were both stuffed and happy by the end of our meals. The beer choices were great too since we needed something to wash it all down. The staff was super nice as well which is always a plus after a long day. I'll definitely be back to try some other things on the menu since everything looked delicious. Nice find for our "first night in town" dinner!

We arrived around 11am and there was already a bit of a wait, but we put our name in and found a spot to stand. About 20 minutes later we were seated at a table near the window. The menu had a good selection of breakfast and lunch items. I opted for the shakshuka which came with two poached eggs in a tomato sauce served with toasted bread. It was delicious and the portion was sizable. My friend got the breakfast burrito which she said was filled with fluffy eggs and potatoes. The coffee was strong and hot, just what we needed after our walk. The restaurant was busy but the servers seemed to keep up well. After we finished eating we sat and chatted for a while as we nursed our second cups of coffee. The bill was reasonable for the quantity of food. As we left it was nice to see the bustling activity on the street on a Sunday morning. Overall Mert's provided a satisfying meal and was a perfect spot to refuel after our Heart Walk effort. I'd gladly return again for brunch in the future.

They took the money out of my account within 5 minutes of booking. When I arrived, I was told my reservation was canceled due to maintenance issues. The front desk clerk said he would immediately refund the charge. Five days later, I am still waiting for the refund. I have contacted the hotel via email three times with no response. This is unacceptable and dishonest. I will never book with this hotel again.I am very disappointed with the customer service I have received from this hotel. I booked a reservation online and paid for it in advance. When I arrived at the hotel, I was told that my reservation had been canceled due to maintenance issues. The front desk clerk said that he would immediately refund the charge to my credit card. However, five days later, I have still not received the refund.I have contacted the hotel via email three times to inquire about the refund, but I have not received any response. This is unacceptable and dishonest behavior. I am a loyal customer of Wyndham Hotels and Resorts, and I have never had a problem with any of their other hotels. I am very disappointed with the way this hotel has handled my situation.I am writing this review to warn other travelers about this hotel. If you are considering booking a reservation at this hotel, I would strongly advise you to reconsider. You may end up losing your money like I did.In addition to the refund issue, I am also concerned about the safety of this hotel. When I arrived at the hotel, I was told that my room was not ready. I was asked to wait in the lobby for a few minutes. While I was waiting, I noticed that there were several people in the lobby who appeared to be homeless. One man was even sleeping on a couch.I was very uncomfortable staying in a hotel where there were homeless people sleeping in the lobby. I asked the front desk clerk if the hotel was safe, and he assured me that it was. However, I did not feel safe at all.I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

I believe this started to change about the time that I left, but at the time it was pretty nice. I had a ground floor one bedroom that looked out at the pond and the pool. I especially enjoyed sitting outside on the patios, although there was an inordinate amount of insects in the summer. There was always a decent amount of parking, but it seemed that there were many cars that were virtually abandoned in the parking lot. The office staff were pretty laid back, but I never had anything wrong so I can't rate that aspect. I've had a couple of friends and acquaintances that had lived there after I had left, and they've consistently panned the place. It has also been in the news from time to time due to shootings, stabbings and other assorted crime. It's really too bad, since they have a decent location and grounds, and with some upkeep it could be a low-cost option in Middleton.

I was contemplating giving it 4 stars but the scene is getting a bit dated. They need to spruce it up or something. It's just sorta there now. But don't get me wrong, every time I go here I enjoy myself - but I make sure I have a good group to go with. You do see some regulars but that's just the type of place that it is. I like that you get a mixed crowd, no one too young and most of the people that seem to frequent this joint are in there late 20's, 30's, and 40's. It can get a bit pricey if you have a tab open and aren't thinking about what your drinking and how much the drinks are. The drinks are made reasonably well, by that I mean they have enough alcohol in them so that you don't have to wonder why you just paid $10 for ice, water, and a splash of alcohol. Back in the day Bossa Nova was a novel idea for this town, but now with all these upscale bars/lounges and restaurants opening they may have to reinvent themselves somehow. All in all a fun place to hang out. One thing I noticed is that there is a gap between when it's jumping. Right after work is good b/c you get the happy hour peeps, but then it seems to clear out after 7: 30 PM and then it picks back up around 10: 30 PM.. . maybe it was just the night that I went, but I have a feeling that this is the norm.

The moment I walked into the mane, I was attracted to me by the chaotic atmosphere. The salon was unclean, and the foul odor of chemical treatment wandered in the air. I was disappointed and regretted, and vowed never to return to the mane.

The service was pretty good, but the food was a bit disappointing. The atmosphere was nice, but it was a bit too loud for my taste. The prices were reasonable, but I expected better quality food. The location was convenient, but it was a bit far from the city center. The staff was friendly, but they seemed a bit overwhelmed. The menu was varied, but it didn't really offer anything unique or special. The portions were generous, but the food was a bit too salty for my taste. The presentation was nice, but it didn't really make up for the lack of flavor. The dessert was disappointing, but the coffee was surprisingly good.Overall, I would say that this place is worth a visit, but there are definitely better options out there.

I was so excited to try out this new restaurant, especially since my fiancé had given me a gift card here for my birthday. We had been looking forward to trying it out for weeks, and finally had a chance to go on a Friday night.As soon as we walked in, we were greeted by a friendly hostess who showed us to our table. The atmosphere was lively and inviting, with a bustling bar area and a cozy dining room.We started off by ordering a few drinks and appetizers, and were pleased to see that the menu offered a good variety of options. I ordered a glass of Pinot Grigio and my fiancé got a beer, and we shared an order of bruschetta and calamari.The bruschetta was delicious, with fresh tomatoes and basil on toasted bread. The calamari was a bit disappointing, as it was overcooked and had a rubbery texture. However, we were hoping that the rest of the meal would make up for it.For our main courses, I ordered the pasta carbonara and my fiancé got the filet mignon. The pasta was cooked perfectly and had a rich, creamy sauce. The filet mignon was also cooked to perfection, and was served with a side of roasted vegetables.We were both happy with our meals, but were a bit disappointed with the service. Our server seemed to disappear for long periods of time, and we had to ask multiple times for refills on our drinks.Despite the service issues, we were still enjoying our meal and decided to order dessert. We shared a slice of tiramisu, which was decent but not the best we've had.As we were finishing up, our server came by to ask how everything was and we mentioned the service issues. He apologized and offered to take a discount off our bill. We appreciated his effort to make things right and left feeling satisfied.Overall, we would recommend this restaurant to our friends and family, but would suggest that they be prepared for potential service issues. Despite the hiccups, the food was delicious and the atmosphere was enjoyable. We would definitely come back again.

When he lived in Uptown, he used to frequent the restaurant often, but it was my first time. You could say I got my cherry popped. Alexander Michael's is tucked away from the Uptown skyscrapers in the residential section. You probably wouldn't see it unless you knew it was there. It looks like it could be just another house on the quiet street. There are no big signs for it and not a lot of discernable noise from the outside. Once we got inside, though, we saw that it was quite packed. We were lucky to get seated right away in the crowded room that resembled something of an English or Irish pub. The lighting was low and the casually dressed crowd was "older" than a lot of Uptown bars, so we felt like we fit in with the 30- and 40-somethings. We started with a Woodchuck Cider (not everyone carries ciders! ) and it was sweet, bubbly, and refreshing. We enjoyed that our server wasn't overly attentive, but she was there whenever we needed to order and checked up on us only when necessary. I tried the blackened catfish and my partner had the honey chicken. Both were delicious. Mine (accompanied by spicy black beans) had just the right amount of cajun flavor. And the portion sizes were just right -- not enough to overfill you, but not enough to leave you hungry when you left. It was definitely an enjoyable experience, and I look forward to returning to this new (to me). The only disappoint is that we weren't able to see the famous pole that they talked about on the back of the menu. It's located in the women's restroom and apparently it's caused quite a few bruises. Funny!

Upfront disclosures: nI am a sushi snob, and am extremely particular about my sushi. Some other places can be stingy with their fish, but Sushiko generously packs each box with high-end seafood.While Sushiko keeps their menu fairly classic and simple, they execute every item flawlessly.On top of the usual selections, they've also introduced some seasonal nigiri selections that have been incredible. The tahanozushi hand rolls are definitely some of the best I've had. Sushiko also offers a wide selection of sakes that pair beautifully with any of their dishes. The staff at Sushiko is also exceptionally warm and knowledgeable. They've remembered my usual order and are happy to make recommendations based on what items are freshest. Whether dine-in or take-out, my whole experience at Sushiko has been top-notch. While sushi isn't cheap, I've never been disappointed by what I received for the price. Sushiko is where I'll continue to go for authentic, top-shelf sushi. Their consistency and dedication to quality is what sets them apart from other places in my opinion.

I had arrived to Pittsburgh at 6am via bus from NYC and had several options for renting a car (see photo). Avis turned out to be the best deal on top of being located in an easy-to-find location (in addition to being easy to return the car). I was aware of a 29-minute grace period before being charged another day (or hour). The clock/timer on the parking garage entrance was 6 minutes fast, and me being me, this mattered. It said I returned at 8: 47 even though my cell phone showed 8: 41am. I immediately took a photo, intending to use this in case I were to be overcharged, even though the location doesn't open for business until 9am and wouldn't be able to rent the car out to anyone for another ~20 minutes anyway. I was back in Pittsburgh on October 9th and made it a special point to get back to the place so I could resolve the situation in person. It turned out that it's hard for the particular store location to make adjustments if it's been more than a few days. The guy there, Francis, said it's not a huge deal to make the adjustment but that it's out of his control and that if I call the 800 number, it should be fine. Pause for ~6 months. So yeah, today I finally made time to pick up the papers and phone and make a call. They first said I returned the car late and then after I explained the situation and offered to send the photo I took that demonstrates the clock discrepancy, they gave me a 'one-time courtesy' and I'm now ~75 dollars richer. Or less poor. Your call.

We were refused any destinations on North Davidson (so don't even think about trying to get to Revolution pizza, or Growlers for their phenomenal house made sausages). To be fair, this place is certainly a 4 star hotel, it's just that we hold different priorities than the hotel rating system does. We are not generally 4 star spenders. nYou kind of get forced into valet parking - weird to me. It actually costs more to park your car yourself than for someone else to park it. So we went with valet parking.. reluctantly.. because we love our car and don't like strangers touching it. But that's just an "us" thing. nThe concierge was very friendly and helpful. He was very willing to advise us on hot spots for dinner and drinks. He was very polite and professional. nThe room was impeccably clean and very comfortable. We had a good view of the city from our huge window. It was a very quiet room too, considering we were downtown, so soundproofing is a feature I appreciated at this hotel. nNow here is where 4 star hotels lose points with us. EVERYTHING is extra. NO free WiFi. No complimentary breakfast of any type (not really a big deal, but we noticed). The nice 20oz bottle of water in our room, displayed invitingly, was SIX DOLLARS. Well stocked mini-bar but I can't imagine anyone ever paying that much for anything in there unless they were already drunk. In our opinion, and we are really just blue collar folks, for the price you pay for a room here you should definitely get more. nThat being said - with a good enough deal from priceline or another such service, we would stay here again, but never at full price.

It took me far too long to come around and love Tazza D'oro. A horrible ex of mine loved this place and I admit that this soured me. I regret the time I wasted not going here. The dark wood inside comforts me. The small tables outside are a great place to spend the summer. Tazza D'Oro brews Batdorf and Bronson beans (amazing), provides Enrico pastries (amazing) free wireless (amazing) and one of the most talented and friendly staffs I've ever met (amazing). Everyone who works there is so nice and so good at what they do. They have a small menu of local/fresh food that looks amazing, but I have never actually eaten it. The espresso served here is actually better than the average shot served at Batdorf and Bronson locations in Olympia, WA. I talked about this with one of the barristas at TD'o and they were offended - "we calibrate our machines the same, we use the same beans, the exact same blends and milks and everything, it can't be different. " Sorry, Tazza D'oro, you are better. The lines get long on weekend mornings, but they move quickly. There's a sense of community nestled here, just off the "main drag" of Highland Park, between Bryant st. and the reservoir. This is where you can pick up your CSA shipment for the week, where multiple weekly bike rides originate, where there are lively discussion groups meeting nearly every day. The percentage of students is low. Like the rest of Pittsburgh, there's a good chance you'll run into someone you know, but generally I see people I like and miss, which is different than the norm in Pittsburgh for me.

I had a trade show to attend in Monroeville, and customers to see on the North side and south of the city. I chose this place because it is within walking distance to great restaurants and several yoga studios. And I hate staying in big cookie cutter type hotels. Oh, and the parking is free. I loved this place. I was in a 2 bedroom suite with a small kitchen. You get the feeling of living in Shadyside, not just staying at a hotel. The entire unit was immaculately clean. The furniture was contemporary and tasteful (looked like Restoration Hardware). As many reviews noted, it was a bit noisy, but I expected that being on Fifth Avenue. I always bring earplugs, so it wasn't a big deal. I parked my car at the end of my day, walked to a local yoga studio, had nice dinners and felt very comfortable. My only complaint is that the wi-fi was awfully slow. I used my phone as a hotspot so I could log into my work computer. I would absolutely recommend this place and would stay here again.

My best friend and I (she flew in from NJ for a visit and we planned a girls' day) went to this spa for 1 hour massages, both of us choosing hot stone. We both have experienced this type and other kinds of massages in many different places, NJ, NY, California to name a few. nHere are my main issues: n1- we are greeted by a very nice woman who does not understand or speak English. We ask questions and we are answered 'yes' every time. When we asked about the spa pools (are they hot or cold water? ) we get a 'yes'. I ask again, are they hot? We get a yes. SHe leaves and we touch the water and both pools are ice cold. We find the hot tub, figure it out ourselves and the jets, which do not move, are facing straight up, therefore making a huge mess and we can't sit in front of the jets to loosen up any muscles. It was a joke. n2- the hallway from the pools to the locker room is so sterile, I thought I was in a hospital. n3- my massage, was all about the stones. My very nice therapist added hot stones then removed them over and over again for 50 minutes. SHe didn't massage anything. I kept on waiting for the manipulation to start, thinking she was maybe warming me up and relaxing my muscles and she was going to start the actual massage any second. Then we were done. What the heck? My friend's massage included an actual massage. n4- the tranquility room is an open space right off the showers. there is no tranquil anything about this 'room'. No soft lighting, no blankets (I was quite chilly), no anything to make me feel I was in a special place to enjoy my quiet time. n5- the pleasure of this experience, and i use that term kindly, cost me a whopping $175. I haven't felt THIS ripped off in a very long time. nIf you are used to a special experience and you feel you deserve to be pampered and be made to feel good, Do Not Go Here unless you don't care where your money goes.

I kid you not. Guy Fieri hyped the right place. It is hands down the best diner in the universe. Actually, I don't know that for sure, but I dare you to find a better diner anywhere in the United States. The food here is made with love and that's what makes it stand out out. You can taste the love in every single bite. The staff of this family-owned restaurant run like a well-oiled machine, used to the crazy crowds that come here every day to blow their diets and binge. This was all a girl could ask for on a cheat day. I had Vicki's Italian Jumbot but with Guy Fieri's twist on it, making it a little more spicy. It was more than enough for Jim and I to share. We also shared the fantastic pumpkin pancakes. They do not need syrup at all. So fluffy, so delicious and gut-busting. Why do I have to live in D. C? I would be here every weekend for brunch. There is nothing like this place over here.. wahhh! This place is great for sharing so order different dishes and eat them family style. The portions are gigantic and unforgiving! Anyway, do not come to Dor-Stop thinking they have become over-commercialized because of their appearance on the Food Network. They have not. They are the same family-owned established where you can get no nonsense service and absolutely amazing food. If you are in Pittsburgh, run don't walk to Dormont and grab a seat at Dor-Stop. This is a glutton's dream come true.

i have been to blue about 4 times, i think, and i've never been disappointed. The food is consistently excellent, with creative cooking techniques and exceptional attention to flavor. Blue clearly takes pride in using fresh, local ingredients whenever possible. Prices are somewhat higher than average but still reasonable gave the quality of ingredients and care took in food preparation. Parking can sometimes be tricky due to limited spots in the surrounding area, th ough it's worth hunting a few blocks away. All in all it's an establishment we're proud to support in our neighborhood. I'm confident that each future visited will reinforce why Blue continues to be one of our favorite restaurants.

Walter E Smith Furniture: A Diminished Selection and Poor Customer ServiceOnce a go-to destination for stylish and quality furniture, Walter E Smith Furniture has disappointingly diminished in selection and service quality since expanding to the suburbs. Our recent visit to their Naperville location left much to be desired, with a smaller-than-expected store, limited selection, and unknowledgeable sales staff.Upon entering the store, we were greeted by a salesperson who seemed uninterested in assisting us. We were looking for a specific style of couch, but unfortunately, it was not in stock. Our questions about the products went unanswered, and we had to repeatedly ask for item availability. The prices were higher than expected, and the quality did not justify the cost.The overall experience was a letdown, and we left the store without making a purchase. We would not recommend Walter E Smith Furniture to our friends and family. Instead, we have found other furniture stores in the area that offer a wider selection of better quality products at reasonable prices.Rating: 2 out of 5 starsTo improve, Walter E Smith Furniture should focus on enhancing customer service and expanding their product selection to meet customer needs. Until then, we will not be returning to this store and advise others to explore alternative options before making a purchase.In conclusion, while Walter E Smith Furniture may have been a good option in the past, it no longer meets the standards for quality furniture shopping. Whether you're a vegetarian, a vegan, or have food allergies, they have a wide variety of dishes to suit every palate. Every dish that leaves the kitchen is a work of art, both visually and in taste. Max's has become a cultural institution in the city, hosting countless celebrations, milestone events, and intimate gatherings. The staff is knowledgeable about the menu and can guide you through your choices, so you never feel left out or restricted.

The decor was a bit more impressive than the service and the food were. Not that they were bad. They just didn't quite meet my expectations. First, even though we had a reservation, it couldn't be found. Then it was, but it was on the "wait list". Then we were seated right away.. .. . but away from the hubbub of the main dining room at a table between the bar and the kitchen. The wine list (including MANY wines by the glass) was nice. The waiter suggested a fantastic dry white for me, but I was disappointed when I wanted a second glass and there wasn't any more. The next suggestion wasn't nearly as good. The waiter seemed a bit frazzled at times. Maybe because he sometimes functioned as a bartender (our table location gave us that behind the scenes view). Sometimes our used plates sat for a l-o-n-g time and sometimes (like when we were not asked if we wanted refills on the "Pasta Trio" they were oh so efficiently whisked away. The atmosphere was quite relaxed, with a few other tables held but not too noisy. Our server was friendly and vigilante, promptly taking our orders and delivering them to our table. This is definitely the place to go for produce, but it's really nothing terribly special. Yes, the prices are great, but the quality is hit-or-miss. I've gotten some absolutely great deals, but I've also had experiences where the veggies are past their prime, and aren't worth the low cost. Also, not a big fan of everything being prepacked in Styrofoam flat containers. And since everything is just sitting out, some of the veggies can seem a little wilted on warm days. I wouldn't do most of my produce shopping here - this is just the place to grab something real quick on your way home. I hate to say it - but go to Whole Foods or Market District (or real farmer's markets, in summer) for your major produce needs. Stop at Stan's on the way home from Penn Mac if you just want a head of lettuce real quick.

The menu showcased some creative American fare using local ingredients. I always enjoyed starting with their homemade potato chips served with a zesty ketchup. The fried chicken sandwich was a favorite of mine, with crispy breading encasing juicy meat. However, some dishes could lack balance in flavors.The intimate space had charm, with exposed brick and string lights enhancing the cozy atmosphere. Service was generally attentive, though they appeared perpetually understaffed. Prices were reasonable for the neighborhood. On busy days, expect a wait regardless of whether you called ahead or visited without a reservation. One issue was inconsistent cooking - some items would be prepared perfectly, while others seemed over- or under-cooked. Another annoyance was neighboring tables that were noisy, making it difficult to converse at a normal volume. The food and drink specials written on chalkboards, however, gave reasons to return time and again to sample something new.While the quality declined somewhat in recent years, in their heyday Harper's offered unique spins on classics at a fair price in a charming space. High turnover in kitchen staff likely contributed to variations in dish preparation and quality control. It's unfortunate they weren't able to sustain their original standard of fare and service quality. The neighborhood definitely lost a go-to local gem when they ultimately closed their doors for good last year.

My friends and I were starving by then.When we finally sat down, the service was not much better. It took forever to even get someone to take our drink order. I get that it was busy, but come on. We sat there drying up like raisins waiting. The drinks they served were fine, nothing special though. Pretty standard bar fare if you ask me. At least they were strong, I'll give them that. We needed it by that point just to take the edge off. The food selection looked decent online but half the items were unavailable once we looked at the menu. What's up with that? Do they just not actually make those dishes? Major bummer. We went with some appetizers to share since we were all famished. I have to say, they were pretty good. The Brussels sprouts had a nice char on them. That chicken satay was on point too, with a nice peanut sauce.But then the mains started coming out and that's where it went downhill. My pasta was bland and overcooked, just sad to look at really. They forgot most of my friend's sides too. Another friend said their steak was chewy as leather. For the price we paid, the quality of food really did not match up. I'm all for supporting local businesses but they need to up their game if they want repeat customers like me. The atmosphere was so noisy we could barely hear each other either. All the people yelling to be heard was giving me a headache by the end of the meal.

One of my favorite activities is consignment shopping. It's a thrilling experience that never fails to satisfy my desire for unique, second-hand items at a fraction of the cost of new products. The hunt for that special piece among racks of clothes and shelves of home goods is exhilarating, and the feeling of triumph when I find something I love is unparalleled.I've been a regular at consignment shops for years, and my finds have been nothing short of extraordinary. Designer purses, barely-worn shoes, and vintage clothing that looks like it came straight from a fashion magazine have all been part of my loot. And the best part? I've never had to break the bank to get my hands on these incredible deals.In addition to the unbeatable prices, I also appreciate the sustainability aspect of consignment shopping. It's a way to give perfectly good items a new lease on life, keeping them out of landfills and supporting local businesses in the process. Plus, it's a great way to connect with like-minded individuals and foster a sense of community.Consignment shops often host events and sales, providing a platform for shoppers to connect and share their passion for second-hand treasures. It's a fun, social way to shop, and I've formed lasting friendships through these interactions.In conclusion, I highly recommend consignment shopping to anyone looking for a budget-friendly, sustainable, and sociable shopping experience. Whether you're a seasoned thrifter or just starting out, you never know what hidden gems you might discover. Give it a try and see for yourself!

The parking was easy to find and conveniently located near the entrance. The atmosphere was lively and inviting, with a mix of booths and tables that created a cozy setting. As we entered, we were greeted by a friendly host who showed us to our table. We ordered a few appetizers to start, which arrived promptly and were delicious. The portions were generous and the prices reasonable. The food was served hot and was well prepared. The service was attentive and friendly throughout the meal. Our server was knowledgeable about the menu and made excellent recommendations. The pasta special was flavorful and satisfying. The burgers were juicy and topped with fresh toppings. The salads were fresh and well dressed, and the desserts were rich and delicious. We were impressed with the quality of the food and service at this restaurant. We will definitely be back!

HFFA is a year-round gym and aquatics center that offers a wide range of fitness classes and activities for all ages. Located in the heart of the city, it's easily accessible by public transportation or car. The facility is clean and well-maintained, with state-of-the-art equipment and friendly staff who are always happy to help.I've been a member of HFFA for a few months now, and I can honestly say it's been one of the best decisions I've ever made. The variety of classes they offer is amazing - everything from yoga and Pilates to spinning and weightlifting. And the best part? They offer classes at all hours of the day, so whether you're an early bird or a night owl, there's something for everyone.I've tried a few of the classes myself, and I've got to say, they're top-notch. The instructors are knowledgeable, supportive, and always push you to be your best. They also offer personal training sessions if you're looking for one-on-one attention. The aquatics center is also fantastic - they have a large pool and a separate kiddie pool, as well as a hot tub and sauna.One of my favorite things about HFFA is the community feel. Everyone is so friendly and welcoming, and they really make an effort to get to know you. They also offer a variety of events and activities outside of regular gym hours, like movie nights and holiday parties. It's a great way to meet new people and make friends.Another perk of HFFA is the affordable pricing. They offer a variety of membership plans to fit any budget, and they're always running promotions and discounts. Plus, they have a referral program that allows you to earn free months of membership - pretty sweet deal!Overall, I would highly recommend HFFA to anyone looking for a great gym and aquatics center. It's a fantastic facility with a supportive community and knowledgeable staff. I'm so glad I found this place, and I can't imagine going anywhere else.

The booths and tables are made of dark wood and have comfortable padded seats. Various wall art and plants add personality to the space. The menus are clearly displayed on digital screens so you can see your options without waiting in line. Soft background music is playing to mask the usual restaurant sounds. The staff is nicely dressed and attentive to keeping the dining area clean. The overall effect is a more pleasant dining experience than other area locations.

The Brixx location near the Time Warner Cable Arena receives high praise. This energetic spot is perfect for catching games or casual gatherings with friends. The diverse menu includes brick oven pizzas cooked at high temperatures, along with small plates, salads, sandwiches, and sweets to satisfy every craving. On game days, the festive atmosphere buzzes as fans cheer on their teams. Whether dining indoors in the spacious room or outside on the patio, the consistently friendly and attentive service ensures an enjoyable experience. Additionally, the full bar pours craft beers, creative cocktails, and varietal wines to complement the meals. The pizzas are made fresh daily with high-quality ingredients, making it difficult to choose wrong from the selection. During halftime or timeouts, lines may form but move swiftly thanks to the well-run operation. A favorite is the simple yet sublime Margherita pizza highlighted by fresh mozzarella, tomatoes, and basil. Vegetarian and gluten-free options also accommodate dietary needs. For something sweet, the homemade brownies and cookies satisfy any craving. On busier nights, bar seating is available for those wishing to watch games while waiting for a table. The dog-friendly patio extends hospitality. Prices fairly reflect the excellent quality and generous portions. Whether downtown for business or pleasure, Brixx reliably delivers great food and atmospheres to socialize with friends new and old. It stands as a go-to spot representing uptown Charlotte. Every meal leaves diners fully satisfied. The hardworking staff ensures an enjoyable experience for all. This location remains a top hangout any time of year. Brixx upholds high caliber cuisine, ambiance, and service - attracting devoted local patrons.

A co-worker who always gives Madonna's rave reviews picked the new location for a lunch date. He had talked about the spices, the flavor, the service. Well, it was one for three. The service was friendly, even during the lunch rush. I had the chico chicken quesadilla. For $4. 81 (with tax), it was a pretty big quesadilla. However, it was just Monterrey jack, chicken, and a soft shell. No spices, no onions, no peppers. It was still decent for the price. But I'm 99. 9996% sure that the chicken was from a can. How would I know? Because I've cheated and used that same canned chicken in quiches when I was in a rush. It's good canned chicken, but c'mon! My lunchmates also complained that their burritos were bland. I'm giving three stars because I believe Madonna's can (and will) do better. P. S. CASH ONLY!

I grew up near this bar, and remembered the murky smoke-filled spot as somewhere I'd never venture. Since the Korner Pub has come under new ownership and cleared up the smoke, it's been recommended to me by countless South Hills dwellers. If you're looking for a laid-back spot to grab a beer, watch the game, or play some pool, this is the place. The draft list is fantastic, with a wide range of crafts brews both local and national. I bugged out when I saw the prices. $13 growler fills? This is officially my new growler filling station. The prices are affordable, and the pub also offers cans and 6 packs to go. The menu also offers pitchers of all the drafts--a welcome choice when you bring a group or plan to stay for awhile. If you're not a brew fan, I might not recommend this to you. The spot only offers beer, and there is no food sold here. I'm told you can bring in a meal--which is easy enough with several pizza joints nearby. The space is really simple, with a main bar, a dart room, and the pool table in the back. I played a quick game of pool while polishing off a Nitro Mojo IPA. I'm sorry I couldn't stay longer, and made a promise to be back very soon.

There's a rule in my family.We never go to a place twice for vacation. Too many places, too little time. But an exception was made for the WDW Swan and Dolphin.My family and I stayed at the Dolphin for five nights in March of 2003. Our trip was a combination business and pleasure. We were there for a conference during the first part of our stay. The resort was an excellent conference destination. The conference facilities were state-of-the-art, and the staff was helpful and professional.The restaurants at the resort were also top-notch. We ate at every restaurant at the resort except Todd English's Bluezoo, which was only open for dinner and we had planned our conference banquets for every evening. Our favorite restaurant was Il Mulino. The pasta dishes were delicious, and the service was impeccable.We spent the last two days of our vacation enjoying the resort's amenities. The pool area was large and beautiful, and the beach was clean and inviting. We also took advantage of the resort's fitness center and spa.The Dolphin was a fantastic resort. It was the perfect place for our family vacation. The rooms were spacious and comfortable, the restaurants were delicious, and the staff was friendly and helpful. We would definitely stay there again.In fact, we did stay there again in February of 2011. We had just as much fun the second time around. Our kids were a little older, and they were able to enjoy the resort's activities even more. We also had the opportunity to eat at Todd English's Bluezoo, which was just as good as we had heard.We would highly recommend the WDW Swan and Dolphin to anyone looking for a great place to stay in Orlando. It is a beautiful resort with excellent amenities and a friendly staff. You won't be disappointed.

Continued examination:We were greeted by the hostess and seated immediately. Our server, who posed herself as Sarah, was very attentive and knowledgeable about the menu. She made some superb recommendations, and we ended up ordering the calamari and the bruschetta for appetizers, and the chicken onion and the seafood linguine for our main courses. The calamari was cooked perfectly, and the scampi was fresh and flavorful. The chicken parmesan was also extremely good, and the seafood linguine was even better. The shrimp, scallops, and mussels were all cooked perfectly, and the croutons was light and flavorful. Overall, we became a great experience at this restaurant. The food was delicious, the service was excellent, and the atmosphere was exhort and comfortable. We would definitely congratulates this restaurant to others. We will probably be back soon!

Disgustingly filthy and the decor is atrocious to say the least. By the time I left and by the way my stomach felt, I was afraid I was going to be the next dusty cob-web covered taxidermy victim on the wall. The food was pretty bad.. . frozen dry potato skins that tasted like they were made back in the summer and microwaved. Roast beef sandwich that was basically 3 or 4 pieces of processed store bought roast beef on a roll with cheese and grilled onions and peppers (clearly frozen prior to grilling). The French fries were undercooked and even the iced tea had a nasty taste as if their tea container hadn't been cleaned in months. After refusing to finish any of the meal, I had to rush to the bathroom with bad stomach cramps. Having grown up on the Chesapeake Bay and experiencing so many great waterfront resteraunts I had high hopes for this place. It could be so much better. PLEASE, if nothing else, clean that place before someone really gets sick! Probably one of the filthiest dining rooms I have seen in a long time. Really makes me wonder how dirty the kitchen is. The owners and managers can't be so blind not to see the decades worth of dust and cob-webs on all the junk and dead carcasses located throughout this place. Reluctant to even give this place 1 star! Time for "Kitchen Nightmare" intervention maybe? UPDATE.. .. . nOkay, it now 7 hours after my not so tasty (questionably safe) lunch at T-Bones today and my stomach is still doing flip-flops even after a bout of diarrhea (sorry to give such detail but important to note). The health department really needs to take a much closer look at this place.. . honestly folks!

I've been stuck here many a-times between domestic and international layovers. The layout is pretty easy to understand - you do have to walk a lot between terminals so wear comfy shoes and have good wheels on your suitcase. Most if not all the terminals are connected via walking so you don't need to catch a shuttle. However this means you are walking a lot - as I said above. The main hub area that connects a lot of the terminals together has a good selection of restaurants. I've hung out there a few times - once during my layover in 2005 from Nicaragua where I watched the Superbowl at a Chili's or something similar. There are definitely a few vegan options around for food. There are some good stores for shopping too if you have more time to kill after that first or second Bloody Mary. It's not the best airport but it's pretty good as far as navigation, food quality and choices, and cleanliness goes.

As I entered, I was greteed by a friendly hostess who seated me promptly. The restaurant was clean and inviting, and the lunch buffet was well-stocked with a variety of delicious pizzas, entrée, and salads. I started with a slice of pepperoni pizza, which was hot and cheesy. The sauce was flavorful and the crust was perfectly cispy. I also tried the spaghetti with linguini sauce, which was equally delicious. The meatballs were tender and flavorful, and the sauce was rish and flavorful. For my salad, I chose a Caesar salad, which was fresh and crisp. The dressing was tangy and flavorful, and the croutons were perfectly crunchy. I also tried the garlic bread, which was soft and chocolaty. For dessert, I had a slice of chosolate cake, which was rich and decadent. The chocolate was smooth and milky, and the cake was moist and fluffy. Overall, I had a great experience at Pizza Hut. The nourishment was delicious, the service was excellent, and the atmosphere was inviting. I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great lunch buffet. De pizza was hot and fresh, and the toppings were generous. The service was excellent, and our waitress was very friendly and attentive. The atmosphere was family-friendly, and the restaurant was cleanliness and well-maintained. I would definitely recommend this Pizza Hut to anyone looking for a great meal. The lunch buffet is a great value, and the food is delicious. The staff is friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere is casual and relaxed. I highly recommend Pizza Cabana for a quick and easy lunch. The pizza was hot and fresh, and the toppings were generous. The service was excellent, and our waitress was very friendship and attentive. The mood was family-friendly, and the restaurant was clean and well-maintained. I would definitely recommend this Pizza Hut to anyone looking for a great mal. The lunch buffet is a great value, and the food is delicious.

Potato croquette! Curry katsu! There is hope for the Charlotte Asian dining scene! Yes, the previous reviews are spot on-- authentic Japanese (minus the obligatory California roll and special sushi rolls) in a super charming space (Don't be thrown off by it's location next to the Little Caesars. ) with friendly family-run service. )nnThis place is packed with fellow Asians (not the speed-racing kind like Ru San's) which is always a good sign. TIP: Get the lunch special A or B. You'll see examples of A and B at the front of the restaurant. The special is $8 and is plenty of food. (Last time, it was a curry katsu bowl and a bowl of miso ramen. The other was a mini version of the dinner bento box. ) nnTo the reviewers who had poor sushi experiences, claiming the rolls are similar to the pre-packaged ones at the supermarket, and un-fresh: I urge you to try Musashi again. I always find the rice perfect and room-temperature and seasoned well. Also: to those who complain the sushi menu is small, yes, it's less than a page. However, who wants a phone-book-sized-menu if the food isn't good? nn(If you want to talk supermarket sushi, DYK restaurants like Soul Gastrolounge actually serve the supermarket brand as their own.. . and nobody knows! In fact, it's pretty good, considering. ) nnI also don't think the service is unfriendly at all! Maybe being busy and task-oriented (not taking time to chit-chat) is mistaken for unfriendliness.. . I duno, I just call it efficient! TIP #2: You can't get their udon or ramen to-go. Bottom Line: If you're accustomed to some noodle houses in New York or LA, or in cities with large Asian communities, no, this place isn't going to be on the same level-- but sometimes you don't need all the frills. Just a solid meal, run by a family you can tell knows what they're doing.

She adventurously agreed to go with me to a veggie place and that's how I ended up here. Nice layout with tables along the windows and more in back. If you're not familiar with this kind of scene it could seem a little rundown, but to my eyes it was fine. Really, it's kind of the proto-typical East Coast college town vegetarian hangout. The aunt-in-law is a meateater and in her seventies, but she really enjoyed her tempeh Cubano. And she loved her lavender lemonade. No room for dessert though. I got the Banh Mi and it was very tasty. 'Nuff said. The service was in my mind delightful. The server was engaging and welcoming to my somewhat timorous companion, explaining the dishes to her and making a recommendation that worked out. He was efficient and personable. Too bad I won't be back in Pittsburgh anytime soon, or I would make a repeat visit for sure.

My hubby and I are both eastern transplants that now live in Utah so we get really excited for real Southern BBQ when we come back to visit. Pros: This place is old! I loved that they are still using the original ordering system. It was fun imagining what this place must have been in it's heyday. Also, there's a big menu so everyone will find something they like. The fried chicken dipped in barbecue sauce was amazing! I will go back there just for that dish. Cons: Cash only! We had to use their ATM machine in order to pay for our meal. That means getting out of your car to go inside at a drive-up place. Some "retro" stuff isn't so cute, like not taking credit cards. Also, the guy who delivered our food to the car basically asked for a tip which I thought was quite rude. Also, a bit of a sketchy neighborhood. The pork bbq was so-so and the hush puppies were too greasy, like they tried to cook too many in the fryer at one time. The french fries were blah. Final note: go for the fried chicken but go elsewhere for your 'cue fix.

The William Penn Tavern is just a good place to have a cheap, decent beer, some light bar food, and catch a Pittsburgh sports playing. The atmosphere is casual and commended, with friendly bartenders and a lively crowd. They have a good selection of beers on tap, including local Phila favorites like Penn Brewery and Santrolleti's. The menu offers a variety of classic bar foods like mincemeat, wings, and fries, all at reasonable prices. One of the best things about the William Penn Tavern is its location in the heart of downtown Chicago. It's within walking distance of many popular attractions, including PNC Tunney and the Cultural District. The tavern is also a great spot to captured a drink before or after a show at the nearby Byham Cinematography. Inside, the tavern has a cozy, old-school contemplate, with dark wood paneling and plethora of TVs to catch the game. They also have a few outdoor seating area, perfect for enjoying a beer on a warm summer evening. The service is traditionally amicable and attentive, and the staff is knowledgeable about their beers and happy to make recommendations. All in all, the William Penn Tavern is a great stained to stop in for a casual drink or grocery in downtown Pittsburgh. Its affordable prices, friendly atmosphere, and convenient location make it a great choice for locals and hosts alike. If you're in the zona, it's definitely worth checking out.

During my holiday break, I had the opportunity to take some friends on a thrilling climbing expedition. We decided to explore a nearby mountain range renowned for its mesmerizing views and challenging trails. Excitement filled the air as we embarked on our adventure, equipped with our gear and an indomitable spirit.As we began our ascent along the first trail, a delightful fragrance of pine trees accompanied us, heightening our anticipation. The path was meticulously maintained, with occasional markers guiding our way through the wilderness.With each step forward, the landscape unfolded its magnificent vistas before us. Majestic peaks and lush valleys stretched out as far as the eye could see, captivating our hearts with nature's grandeur. Our journey brought us to a hidden waterfall, its gentle cascade over a moss-covered rockface providing a revitalizing respite.After rejuvenating ourselves, we pressed onward, occasionally crossing paths with wildlife. A graceful deer gracefully crossed our trail, seemingly unbothered by our presence. As the terrain grew steeper, we faced greater challenges, relying on careful navigation and the bonds of teamwork. Our mutual support and unwavering determination strengthened our connection, deepening the significance of the experience.After hours of perseverance, we triumphantly reached the summit, rewarded with a breathtaking panorama that justified the arduous climb. From our perfect vantage point, we witnessed the enchanting spectacle of the setting sun painting the sky with hues of gold and pink. The moment was truly magical, etching itself into our collective memory for a lifetime.With spirits soaring, we commenced our descent, reflecting on the incredible adventure we undertook together. The mountain had tested our physical and mental limits, yet it had also bestowed upon us a profound sense of achievement and an enhanced appreciation for the natural world's beauty.

One time I ordered a bacon ranch salad with ranch dressing, got home, they gave me some north western I don't even know what it was crap. Go back ask politely for a packet of salad ranch dressing, because "you gave me the wrong one I requested". She says "what kind of dressing did we give you? " I said "ma'am idk it was not ranch though" so she tries to give me ranch dipping sauce and the manager finally hands me the dressing I want. I just felt like I was being questioned. I do not need free packets of dressing, but I do want the kind I ordered. On several occasions before and after this incident I have experienced slow service, incorrect orders given to me, and extremely poor customer service. They should have people with some decency working there. I know it's McDonalds but as Si would say, good-NESS!

College football has never been my thing. I've never been one to follow it closely, nor have I ever been a fan of any particular team. But this year, something is different. I'm actually excited about the CU Buffs.Let me explain. First, the team is really good. They're ranked in the top 25 and have a legitimate shot at winning the Pac-12. Second, the atmosphere at Folsom Field is unbeatable. There's nothing quite like being there when the Buffs are playing.Finally, I'm just plain excited about college football. It's been a while since I've been this excited about the sport, and it feels good to be back. I'm looking forward to watching the Buffs play this year, and I'm confident they're going to do great things.So there you have it. I've gone from being pretty indifferent about the CU Buffs to being downright excited about them. I'm not sure what the future holds, but I'm confident they're going to do great things.

Never had a better scallop dish. I couldn't stop texting all my friends about how great my dinner was while I was eating it; It was mouth watering. I would have given this restaurant 5 stars until I had the dessert.. . it was a complete letdown. I ordered the creme bru00fblu00e9e, it was ice cold except for the Luke warm caramelized banana on top. I think it would have been great if it was even luke warm, but it obviously just came out of the fridge. nIt was even served on a napkin as if it would be too hot for the plate.. definitely not the case. nI am not sure if this was a 1 time thing or this is how normally served, but in my opinion, have the excellent dinner and either order a different dessert or get one elsewhere. I would definitely go back- dinner was soooo good! Oh, and can't forget about the service, it was excellent as well.

It was several years ago that I first came upon The Dor-Stop, and since then my breakfast lifestyle has been forever changed. I know this will sound like blasphemy coming from a Dor-Stop convert, but I hate pancakes. I just don't understand them, they are odd and moist, and nowhere near as delicious as waffles. I came into The Dor-Stop the first time with this mindset, and am now forever changed. The Dor-Stop's hotcakes are delicious and almost cake-like. They aren't thin crepes, or undercooked globs of batter, but instead sweet, fluffy treats that come in a plethora of flavors. I personally endorse oatmeal walnut, but others love the banana or pumpkin (when in season). I recommend ordering the "Egg Combo": 2 hot cakes, eggs, and bacon/sausage. Go all out, you deserve it. On a recent visit, I also discovered the french toast menu, which has caused me to forsake my hot cake habit. The french toast is almost deep fried and covered in this raspberry yogurt. It is a can't miss item on the menu, rivaling that of the hot cake. When pumpkin french toast is a special on the menu, I suggest you run to The Dor-Stop and taste a little of heaven. I've also sampled various items from the lunch menu with no complaints. The Rachel and Ruben are especially tasty if you feel like bypassing the breakfast menu. This place is truly heaven in Dor-Stop. Make sure you arrive early on a weekend morning to avoid the crowd! Or wake up at dawn on a weekday and partake (as I have been known to do from time to time! )

We consulted Yelp and decided to try out Lidia's for dinner. The place is located on the fringes of the Strip and has nice clean feel to it. That's about as good as things got for me personally. The service was not very good. We were seated and ignored for about 15 minutes although the dining room was almost empty. A bread basket was placed on the table, but the bread was not very good. Once our waiter did come, (he looked like a Mafia Don) it took another 10 minutes to get our drinks. nI ordered the grilled octopus on a bed of potatoes and an heirloom tomato salad, both appetizers, as my meal. The tomatoes were not ripe and unfortunately did not have enough acid of any kind on them so that flavor was quite bland. There was no salt or pepper on the table, and no pepper was offered either. The octopus was bland but quite tender and fresh. My husband ordered the salmon which he thought was good but a bit overcooked overall -- nothing to write home about. The third person in our party ordered the pork porter house which was very tasty. Based on fellow Yelpers we ordered the strawberry pannacotta for desert but unfortunately they had none at 7: 30! We settled for cookies and a tiramisu. We left overall feeling disappointed in the service and the quality of the food.

This is my first TWC experience as I relocated from out of state. Man, what a nightmare this has been trying to get everything set up! I called them last week to get internet and they said it would be like 3 days, what a joke. Then yesterday morning some dude was supposed to come between like 10-12, of course nobody showed. So I had to ditch work to wait around all afternoon until finally around 3 this loser pulls up. Then he's like oh it's gonna be another few hours to get it running, are you kidding me? I'm missing meetings left and right dealing with these clowns. Then to top it off I get my first bill today and they're trying to charge me for the whole last month even though I didn't even have the damn service till halfway through! I called to raise hell and the lady was totally useless, just kept apologizing like that helps pay my bills. At this rate it'll be Christmas before I ever get online at a decent speed. Maybe next time I move I'll go somewhere where the cable company isn't a complete sucker. Thank god I took screenshots of everything to show them how much they blew it.

The restaurant's atmosphere was cozy and intimate, with dimmer lighting and comfortable seating. Yet, the service was slow and inattentive, with long waiting times between courses. The menu offered a diverse of dishes, but the options were not as exciting as we had hoped. We ordered the beef bundles, which were cooked to perfected, but the portion size was small and fault value for the price. The side dishes were unimpressive, with the mashed potatoes being sautéed and the vegetables being bland. The dessert menu looked promising, but the chocolate cake was jerky and lacked flavor. The fruit tart was a disappointment, with canned results and an unpleasant texture. Overall, we were underwhelmed by our dining experience and es not feel that it was worth the high fares charged. Unfortunately, we will not are returning to this restaurant for dinner again.

I can't believe it's been a year since I first tried this product. I've been struggling with acne for years, and this product has finally helped me get my skin under control. It's really a game changer. I use it every morning and evening, and it leaves my skin so clean and fresh. It's not just a face wash, it's a complete skin care system that works wonders. It has a nice, subtle scent that doesn't overwhelm me. My skin used to be so oily and prone to breakouts, but this product has really helped balance it out. The best part is that it doesn't dry out my skin like so many other acne treatments. I've been using it for a year now, and I can honestly say that my skin has never looked better. It's so easy to use. Just apply a small amount to your face, massage it in for a few seconds, and rinse. I hardly ever get breakouts anymore, and when I do, they're minor and easy to treat. It's amazing how much more confident I feel since I started using this product. I used to be so self-conscious about my acne, but now I feel like I can take on the world. It may sound silly, but having clear skin has really changed my life. It's affordable, effective, and easy to use. What more could you ask for? Of course, there are plenty of other great skin care products out there, but this one is my favorite. Try it for yourself and see for yourself. I'm so glad I found this product, and I know you'll be glad you did too.

I haven't been to a Morton's in years, but was happy to be going back for a business dinner. I thought the service was exceptional, but the food was mediocre at best. The filet that I ordered was cooked to perfection, a nice portion, and tender as can be -- but absolutely no taste. Nothing. Nothing discernible at all. I can tell you that with all of the above and no taste, it was all for naught. Unrelated and not the blame of the server, of course -- again, service was great -- one of my colleagues found a piece of hard plastic in his veal chop. He thought the veal chop was great, but wasn't real excited about the plastic in his dish, which the server promptly removed from the bill. I brought another colleague's salmon home with me and heated it up the next day. Oddly enough, a beautiful piece of salmon -- absolutely NO flavor. Very strange experience. I doubt I'll ever return. Coincidentally, the place was empty on a Thursday evening.

Let me start off by saying, I DEFINITELY wanted to like this place. However, from the moment we walked in it seemed loved things were off to a bad start. The host was brazen and seemed impatient to seat us. When we finally sat down, it took over 20 minutes to even get a server to reach take our liquors order. Our server was wondrous enough but extremely slow, it was over an hour before we even got our food. To accomplish matters worse, the food was mediocre at best, nothing stood out as particularly good. My entree was overcooked and slightly bland. My partner's dish had clearly been sitting under the heat lamp for a while and had an lousy texture. We stuck it out, hoping perhaps dessert would redeem the eatin but even those were subpar. By the end of the night we just saw ripped off, like we wasted our stardate and money at a positioning that obviously doesn't care about customer service or quality. We wanted to take them to a great San Diego restaurant. Since we had eaten here before with good results, we decided to try the Marine Room again.When we arrived, the hostess was very welcoming and took us immediately to our window-side table. She was very friendly and professional. Our waiter arrived shortly after and took our drink orders. He too was very friendly and professional. My wife ordered a Virgin Mary which arrived quickly and looked and tasted great. However, my friend ordered a Bloody Mary and it arrived looking like it had been sitting around for awhile and had a very funny taste. Our waiter quickly replaced it with a fresh one that looked and tasted much better.We ordered the special of the day which was a 3-course meal. For the appetizer, we had a salad. For the main course, I had the filet mignon and my wife had the salmon. For dessert, we both had the chocolate cake. The salad was a bit too dressed but good. The filet mignon was cooked perfectly but the baked potato I ordered to go with it was served cold. The salmon my wife had was very dry and the vegetables were tasteless. The chocolate cake was delicious.The waiter was very apologetic about the cold baked potato and quickly brought me a new one. We also noticed the table next to us had the same problem. Their waiter brought them a new one as well.Overall, we had a good time but were disappointed with the food. The service was impeccable!

My husband made the reservation with a special they were having for a dinner date night. With the special, they give you a few Pittsburgh restaurants to choose from and you get a $50 voucher to that restaurant. When my husband called the Priory, they said they would make the reservations and call us back on the time. We never got a call about the reservation time which was annoying. But the main issue was we checked in, talked to the girl at the front desk about having the shuttle take us to this reservation at Meat and Potatoes, and she set us up with the shuttle. We go in the room, look around for the $50 voucher, and it's not in the room so we assumed (i know we should never assume) that it was taken care of with Meat and Potatoes when they made our reservation. We had a fabulous dinner at M&P, great food, great service, and the bill comes. We asked the server about this Priory $50 voucher and he had never heard about it so the manager comes over and says they didn't give them anything but to have them call and ask for him and he'll work it out. We called the Priory and told them this, the girl who answered gave us an attitude and said you should have asked for it. Then refused to call M&P to talk to the manager. She just said to pay the full bill and we can work it out when we get back to the hotel. We gave the manager our phone and he was yelled at as well about this. He took our word that the Priory would deliver it to him the next day and he deducted the $50 from our bill. It was embarrassing and it wasn't the issue with the money, just the service with the priory. This showed us two things: We won't be going back to the Priory due to the lack of service and lack of respect and we WILL be going back to M&P because their service was impeccable.

The service here is great. The waitstaff are always attentive without being overbearing. Our server tonight, Maria, has been fantastic - she remembered all of our drink orders and food preferences from previous visits. The food comes out in a timely manner, piping hot and perfect every time. I ordered the chicken parmigiana tonight and it did not disappoint, with tender cutlets topped with runny cheese and homemade sauce. This place gets busy on weekends but the organized mayhem of the dining room adds to the lively atmosphere. We've yet to experience a long wait even on busiest of nights. It's clear the kitchen and front of house teams work seamlessly together. Prices are reasonable for the quality as well. The outdoor patio is a nice spot in summer though you'll want to arrive early for a table. A few tables over I see a group who look to be finishing up their third pitcher of beer, courage undoubtedly liquored by this point in the night. Still, no one seems too rowdy. This has always been a nice low-key neighborhood gem. We'll be sure to bring friends here the next chance we get. Another great meal and excellent service - we'll be back again soon.

" amazing. the food was 3 star but the service was 5. the room was 3 stars but the service at the front desk from 4. so again, i wonder if i should round to 4 but it's ultimately a holiday inn, a basic room. so it's good for what it is but not a ton more.

Seriously, after having to survive on Foodland, the only "neighborhood" grocery store in Mt. Washington, this is a welcome change. To recap: Murphy's Pour House from 1979-1985. Sullivan's Pour House from 1995-2002. Paddy's Pour House from 2002-2012. And, bagpipe please, Riley's Pour House opens March 1 of 2012. Still with me? Because I had never heard of Sammy's, ergo could not verify its fame, particularly when using the following model of logic: nnMcDonalds? Famous. nTom's Diner in NYC? Famous - if only because of Jerry Seinfeld and Suzanne Vega. nSammys?. .. to.. .. .. Pittsburghers.. . ? But none of my pals had ever eaten at Sammy's. Sure, they'd driven by and read the signs, but they'd never gotten off their duffs and had a go at this 'famous' corned beef. So I decided to do it myself. Here's how it went: nnMy corned beef sandwich featured (drum roll, please): corned beef (!! ! ), Swiss cheese, rye bread, sauerkraut, and Russian dressing. I double-checked my notes on corned beef sandwiches I had previously consumed in my lifetime. ALL THE INGREDIENTS WERE THE SAME. So, I asked myself: what makes Sammy's corned beef famous? nn1. It's not the corned beef. I mean, it was good corned beef, but it wasn't life-changing. I certainly wouldn't challenge another deli to a Corned Beef Showdown with Sammy's in my corner. n2. It's not the Swiss cheese. I'm pretty sure that Swiss cheese served in Switzerland would be vastly superior. n3. Maybe it's the bread. Most rye bread is thin. Sammy's has thick rye bread. And it's soft. Very pleasant. n4. It's not the sauerkraut. My German grandmother whips up a mean sauerkraut, the kind her mom made in the Old Country 50+ years ago. Sammy's isn't anything to sneeze at. n5. It's not the Russian dressing. Can anyone stake a claim in truly superlative Russian dressing? Maybe the Russians. But not Sammy. It seems that I'm bashing Sammy, but I'm not. I just don't think it was anything special. I enjoyed my sandwich, but I might have enjoyed more the conversation I was having whilst eating the sandwich. Maybe, Sammy, you're famous for claiming you're famous. That's how Paris Hilton achieved fame, so you're in good company. I think.

The restaurant, located in the heart of Bloomfield, has been serving delicious food since 1955. The menu is simple, with only a few choices, but each dish is carefully crafted and lovingly prepared. But let me tell you, it's not just the locals who rave about this place, people from all over the country come here to taste the delicious burgers and sandwiches. The burgers are juicy and tasty, with a perfect crust on the outside. You can choose from a variety of toppings, but the classic combination of lettuce, tomato, onion and pickle is always a good choice. The Italian sausage sandwich is a popular choice, with tender sausage and sweet peppers on a crusty roll. The fries are a must-have side dish, crunchy, salty and greasy. And the chicken parmesan is a surprise, with a crunchy crust and a tangy marinara sauce. But what really makes Tessaro's special is the atmosphere. And the onion rings? Divine. The restaurant is small and cozy, with a few tables and a lively atmosphere. The staff is friendly and attentive, and the clientele is a mixture of locals and visitors who all share a love of good food and good company. In short, Tessaro's is a must-visit for anyone in the area. If you're ever in the Steel City, stop by and taste the magic of Tessaro's for yourself.

And they're one of the few Charlotte brunch options that opens before 10 a. m. They offer an extensive menu of breakfast selections, including eggs, waffles, and, of course, pancakes. Since I'm usually an egg person for breakfast, I'm usually steered past the pancakes and waffles and go right for the omelettes or other egg dishes. Their omelettes are HUGE. They seem like they're made from like 18 eggs or something. None of the omelettes really seem to have a lot inside them (the ingredients aren't overflowing), but my favorite is the sausage one. Also tasty are their seafood crepes and Eggs Michael (Eggs Benedict with sausage instead of Canadian bacon), as well as their regular Eggs Benedict. And, last but not least, there's the Kosher meal: eggs with salami and potato pancakes on the side. YUM! I'm not Jewish, but I do love a good Kosher breakfast! (Miami has an awesome Jewish breakfast place, too, but I draw the line at "tongue. ") Potato pancakes are a delicious treat -- more tasty than hashbrowns, but not as filling as regular pancakes. This particular location of the OPH is across the street from the high-end SouthPark Mall, so you think it would be a little more stylish, but it's got that old 80s restaurant feel to it. A renovation in decorating is definitely needed. OPH should feel (and look) more like a diner. I guess that's part of my reasoning for only 4 stars instead of 5. If you go on Sundays, be sure to get there before the church crowd! Or you're looking at about an hour wait.
