The line was very long with more than 6 customers ahead of me. When I reached the register, I placed my order for French toast sticks and a frappe. I sat down and waited for a very long time for my food to arrive, considering there was only one other occupied table in the restaurant. When it finally arrived, the food was not prepared correctly, and the service was terrible. The staff were rude and seemed like they did not want to be there. It took more than 15 minutes for my food to arrive, and it was cold when I finally received it. They took my frappe out of the freezer and didn't even blend it. The staff's behavior was unacceptable.

The food, however. Blah. First off, If you go to a show, please note there is a two item per person minimum. This means that from their extensive menu of overpriced bar food and drinks, you are REQUIRED to choose two items each. Second, the sodas are NOT FREE REFILLS! I learned that one the hard way. Get water. Third, before tipping your server, please make sure she hasn't already taken her cut out. Even after paying for two very bland, overpriced meals and way too many Diet Cokes, I thought that my bill was rather high. Upon further inspection, I noticed that my server had taken an 18% gratuity. The menu explicitly says that an automatic gratuity will be taken out for parties of six or more, but there was only two of us and we weren't even drunk. I found this tactic awfully presumptuous and left her tip at the 18% even though I typically tip well over 20%. Overall, I don't like the idea of being required to purchase food just to see a comedy show. I can see why they do it, but if I were required to buy a crappy popcorn and overpriced pop every time I went to the movies, I would be far less inclined to go as I am not inclined to go to the Improv again.

We started with the Indonesian corn fritter wraps, which were delicious with the chili-soy dipping sauce. The corn fritters should have either been a little smaller or the lettuce leaves a little bigger, however, because the combo to unwieldy to roll up and eat. The seaweed salad was good, too. My entree was the autumn vegetables and rice cake noodles--which I only realized was very similar to a pasta dish at Casbah after I took my first bite. The dish at Casbah: maccheretto with white beans, wild mushrooms, sun-dried tomatoes, rapini pesto, cheese and walnuts. Soba's version: rice cake noodles with wild mushrooms, butternut squash, green beans, arugula and sunflower seed pesto. The types of vegetables in Casbah and Soba's versions differ, but the pestos taste pretty much the same. Rice cake noodles don't really soak up liquid, though, so Soba's version was drowning in sauce. I probably would have enjoyed another entree more. I guess I should have read the menu description more carefully, but didn't think Asian fusion (Soba) and Mediterranean (Casbah) were anything alike, so I didn't expect to get the same dish at both restaurants. For dessert, we split the five spice apple tart with honey creme fraiche and crispy yam. The tart was more honey creme fraiche with some apple bits on top; it was tasty but I would have liked more apple. I enjoyed the atmosphere on a Sunday night, and our server was pleasant but didn't hover. The food's delicious--just order carefully if you've dined at another Big Burrito restaurant not too long ago, to avoid getting a similar dish.

The aircraft selection is just ok. A couple of decommissioned fighter jets, an experimental aircraft or two, shiny old Piedmont passenger plane and a small handful of others. Most of the aircraft are roped off, however three to four are not and with supervision, you can sit in a cockpit or two. The hangar includes a few glass case displays, isn't very well lit and smells a little of motor oil (to be expected I guess). Apparently there are a few more aircraft outside but due to a security issue, there is no access to those. The show stopper is the Miracle in the Hudson US Airways airplane. As of July 2nd, it's still being assembled but is on display with a rolling video feature of a TV documentary detailing the actual events. The first thing I noticed was that it's LITTERED with corporate logos. That's terribly disappointing. The museum has a Smithsonian type attraction and to see corporate advertising all over it was upsetting. My hope is that those will be removed at some point and the museum will allow people to actually board the plane. If neither one of those happen, I think it'll be embarrassing for the museum, the city and for the folks who paid $11 to see an iconic attraction they way it was supposed to be seen. If you don't HAVE to see the Miracle aircraft, my advice is go to an airshow near you. You'll get to see some aircraft actually in the air and most include a "static" component. In those cases, the planes usually are not roped off and you may even get to meet the pilot.

Alexander (the owner) is such a nice guy, he goes out of his way to make the customers happy. I feel like I'm at home here. When I go back to Pittsburgh, this may very well be the first place I visit!

I love their coffee, and I used to frequent the Espresso Royale back in Ann Arbor, MI when I lived there. I even like the other ERC's on campus. This one just always kind of falls short for me. I still come here sometimes due to its proximity to my workplace, but I frequently find the staff to be rude, kind of rushing you even though there's nobody else in line, rarely smiling, etc. Furthermore, while I LOVE their coffee - very flavorful, but not overly strong or burnt-tasting like Starbucks - their pastries here are consistently awful. Frequently, they are stale, other times simply flavorless. Today, I was served a bagel so stale that it is difficult to chew. Disgusting. I also agree with the comment that the bathrooms are weird and awkward and frequently dirty. Overall, not a bad place, but not a great one - the other locations are MUCH nicer.

The pizza was fresh and delicious, and the service was impeccable. The staff were friendly and courteous, and they ensured that our experience was enjoyable. The relaxed and inviting atmosphere demonstrated the staff's pride in their work. The prices were reasonable, and the value for money was excellent. The menu offered a wide variety of options to suit everyone's taste. The restaurant was clean, well-maintained, and conveniently located. Overall, it was a fantastic experience, and I highly recommend this Domino's to anyone seeking an exceptional pizza experience. We will definitely return soon.

Again, I prefer the Dowd YMCA because it's huge and has pretty much anything you'd EEVR want from a gym. It has an enormous weight room filling with all the latest equipment, from weight machines to free weights. There is also a huge cardio area with dozens of treadmills, ellipticals, and stationary bikes. In addition, the pool is olympic sized and there are numerous classes offered in the large studio sites like yoga, spinning, and Zmuba. The locker rooms are also colossal and very clean with ample room for changing and storing your belongings. They also have a great bas ketball court that is usually congested, as well as a child watch area so you can work out while your kids have fun too. On top of that, the staff is genuinely friendly and helpful if you need any assistance with machines or have questions. The prices are also very reasonable compar ed to other gyms in the area. Overall it's just a really well-rounded facility that has something for everyone at every fitness level. I've been a member for years and should happily recommendations it to anyone looking to get in shape or stay active.

First and foremost, let me start off by saying that I am not a coffee person, at all. I've never been able to muster up the same level of enthusiasm that coffee aficionados seem to possess. However, despite my personal disinterest in the beverage, I found myself stepping into this coffee shop with an open mind. And boy, was I pleasantly surprised! This place has a certain charm that can't be denied. From the moment you walk in, you're greeted by a cozy ambience that immediately puts you at ease. The soft lighting, comfortable seating, and soothing background music create an inviting atmosphere that makes you want to stay awhile. And the best part? The prices here are unbelievably low. Seriously, it's like a coffee lover's dream come true. The affordability factor alone is enough to make this place a favorite among caffeine enthusiasts. Furthermore, the staff members are friendly, welcoming, and experts at what they do. They take the time to understand your preferences, making personalized recommendations that cater to your taste buds. I never thought I'd find myself appreciating the nuances of different coffee blends, but thanks to their guidance, I discovered flavors I never knew existed. Lastly, I must mention the delectable pastries that accompany these delightful drinks. Freshly baked croissants, muffins, and scones are just a few of the treats that make for the ultimate pairing with your chosen cup of joe. I may not be a coffee person by nature, but I've become a fan of this place nonetheless. It has a certain something, a charm that transcends my personal preferences and makes it an ideal spot for any coffee lover. So, if you're seeking a cozy retreat with great coffee and wallet-friendly prices, look no further. This place is a hidden gem that deserves to be discovered by all, coffee connoisseurs or not.

This hotel exceeded our expectations. The rooms were spotless and cozy, and the staff was incredibly friendly and accommodating. I highly recommend this hotel for anyone seeking accommodations in the area. It's conveniently located near various restaurants, shops, and attractions. The complimentary breakfast offered a delicious and diverse selection. I would gladly stay here again during future visits. The location was ideal, providing easy access to all the places we wanted to visit.

This place is a testament to the power of word-of-mouth. When yo first walked in, every table was filled with what seemed like old friends enjoying long conversations over delicious dishes. The atmosphere was lively yet eased. Our server came over with a hearty smile and introduced himself, asking us how our day was going in a genuine manner. He knew the menu scrupulously and gave us great recommendations tailored to our tastes. The food arrived quickly and everything looked beautiful and freh. The flavors were out of this world - nuanced yet Bold in all the right ways. I was thoroughly impressed and could se why this place has become such a neighborhood favorite. People clearly love to gather here to indulge in the high quality cuisine and company of friends both ancient and new. It's the kind of p lace you'll be tempted to visited again and again to reexperience your favorite dishes or try something new. By the end of the m eal we knew we had found our new favorite go-to spot. I can't wait to bring more pe ople here and continue spreading the word about this hidden gem. At the prices they charge for this level of quality, it's no wonder they stay so overpopulated. I' ll certainly be back again soon and will make it a priority to try something new off the menu each time. This restaurant is a real find and I feel luckily to now be "in the know" about it.

Ding Ding Ding! That high pitched, obnoxious bell lets you know the food is ready at Frank's Eats. It might be the same bell used in elementary schools to signal the end of recess. However, if the lunch lady had dished up Frank's famous pulled pork sandwich, sloppy joes, or mac and cheese instead of mystery meat, tater tots, and creamed peas, I would have run to the cafeteria instead of hiding under my desk every time I heard it.Upon entering Frank's Eats, you are immediately greeted by 50's kitsch, which is the diner's theme. I'm not sure why they went with that theme, though, since the food is pure 90's Sysco slop. But if you're looking for a hearty meal that will stick to your ribs and make you feel like you're in a time warp, Frank's Eats is the place to go.One of my favorite things about Frank's Eats is the extensive menu. They have everything from burgers and fries to chicken parmesan to liver and onions. And if you're feeling adventurous, you can try one of their signature dishes, like the Garbage Plate or the Texas Tornado. Just be prepared for a gut bomb that will leave you feeling like you need a nap.Despite the delicious food, there are a few things that could be improved at Frank's Eats. The service can be slow at times, and the prices are a bit high. But overall, Frank's Eats is a great place to get a hearty meal and experience a taste of Americana.If you're ever in the mood for some good old-fashioned comfort food, be sure to check out Frank's Eats. You won't be disappointed!

The staff at this establishment are truly remarkable. They turned what could have been a difficult situation into a smooth and stress-free experience. Their professionalism and empathy shine through in every interaction. From the moment I entered the building, I was warmly greeted by the receptionist, who immediately made me feel at ease. Throughout my visit, the staff members I dealt with were attentive, knowledgeable, and went above and beyond to address my concerns. They patiently listened to my account of the incident, allowing me to express my emotions and frustrations without judgment. Their genuine care and concern made me feel supported during what could have been a highly stressful experience. Not only were the employees here professional, but they were also incredibly efficient and effective. They promptly initiated the necessary procedures, guiding me through each step and keeping me well-informed throughout the process. I appreciated their clear and concise explanations, as they helped me understand the complexities of the situation without overwhelming me. Furthermore, the sincerity and kindness displayed by the staff members were truly exceptional. They took the time to offer words of encouragement and reassurance, constantly reminding me that they were there to assist me in any way they could. Their primary goal was to alleviate my worries and achieve the best possible outcome. In addition to their exceptional interpersonal skills, the staff demonstrated expertise and competence in problem-solving. They came up with innovative solutions tailored to my specific needs, ensuring that I felt confident in their abilities. Their attention to detail and dedication to finding the most suitable resolution were impressive and instilled a sense of trust in their abilities. Overall, my experience with the people at this establishment exceeded all expectations. I highly recommend their services to anyone in need.

My son and I came for Tuesday Dollar Burger Night, and we were pleasantly surprised by the experience. As soon as we walked in, we were greeted by friendly staff who seated us promptly. The atmosphere was vibrant and inviting, with lively music playing in the background. The menu had a great selection of burgers to choose from, including both classic options and unique creations.When our burgers arrived, we were impressed by their generous size and presentation. The patties were perfectly cooked to our desired level of doneness, juicy and flavorful. The toppings were fresh and plentiful, adding a burst of taste to every bite. The burger buns were soft and lightly toasted, providing a nice contrast to the hearty fillings.One aspect that stood out to us was the attention to detail in the side dishes. The fries were crispy and seasoned to perfection, and the coleslaw had a tangy homemade dressing that complemented the burgers wonderfully. We also appreciated the option to customize our burgers with additional toppings, allowing us to create our own unique combinations.The service throughout our meal was exceptional, with our server checking on us regularly and ensuring we had everything we needed. The waitstaff was knowledgeable about the menu and made helpful recommendations when we couldn't decide. The overall speed of service was impressive, considering how busy the restaurant was that evening.As for the price, the Dollar Burger Night promotion was an incredible deal. The quality of the food far exceeded our expectations, especially considering the affordability. We left the restaurant feeling satisfied and already planning our return for the next Dollar Burger Night. This place is definitely worth a visit if you're looking for a delicious and budget-friendly meal with a welcoming atmosphere.

The pizza here is remarkable. The service is amistad and helpful. They assuredly care about getting your food to you hot and fresh. The soups are huge and fresh. We methodically get a large pizza and a large salad to share between four adults and still enjoy some left over. This is one of the best apple places around. We have never been disappoint. You can diet in or take out. There is only road parking. You prescription at the counter and they bring your food to the table. They are generous with toppings and the prices are meaningful. We love supporting this local industries!

The service is very fast and the price is very reasonable. The restaurant itself is very clean and the food looks delicious. I will definitely recommend this place to anyone who wants a meal. These parts are also very generous, and the staff is very friendly. The atmosphere is also very tempting and comfortable. This is a good place to relax and eat with friends or family members. The menu has a variety of choices, and everything is cooked to perfect. I strongly recommend Parmanson, Italian noodles and meatballs. Pizza is also very good, salad is always fresh. Dessert is also great, and the price is very reasonable. Overall, this is a good place to eat, and I highly recommend it.

Unfortunately, I cannot because the service was so bad that I left before I had the chance to order. We found seats at the bar behind the taps. After sitting there for 5 minutes and not being acknowledged, we thought that they might not be able to see us, and so we moved to a different pair of seats in the middle of the bar, grabbing a few menus on the way so we would be ready to order. It was fairly busy, but it is not like there were people standing at the bar trying to get drinks - everyone was seated and I'm sure they face much busier times. We sat in our new seats for almost 15 minutes (I timed it - I am not exaggerating), and were not even acknowledged. You would at least think the bartender would acknowledge us and tell us he would be with us when he could, but despite staring him down almost the whole time, we could not even make eye contact. I hope this is a fluke but will probably not be back to find out.

A wave of nostalgia overcomes me, instantly transporting me back to my cherished childhood, where memories of family gatherings centered around thrilling Pittsburgh Steelers games come flooding back. This iconic franchise has played an integral role in shaping my life, bringing me immeasurable joy and heartbreak, while constantly embodying unwavering loyalty. With each passing year, my passion for the team intensifies, and it's with this fervor that I excitedly anticipated the kickoff of the latest season, hopeful for another exhilarating journey. Having now witnessed the entirety of this year's Steelers team in action, I can confidently assert that they did not disappoint. From the very first game to the final whistle, they showcased a remarkable blend of grit, determination, and resilience - qualities that have become synonymous with the black and gold tradition. Under the astute guidance of their esteemed coach, the players comradely united in a manner truly inspirational to behold. Week after week, they graced the field with an unwavering spirit, battling fiercely and overcoming every hurdle and adversity that crossed their path. The season was rife with unforgettable moments, awe-inspiring plays, and heart-stopping finishes, keeping me perpetually on the edge of my seat. Whether it was the midfield heroics of the star quarterback or the outstanding performance by the defense, each game unfurled with an enthralling unpredictability. Moreover, the unwavering support from the impassioned fan base was nothing short of remarkable, as the stadium resounded with thunderous chants and cheers that could only emanate from the most devoted of supporters. The team's journey throughout this season was akin to an exhilarating roller coaster ride, rife with soaring highs and nerve-wracking lows, yet ultimately culminating in their emergence as an indomitable force.

We were seated all the way in the back of the restaurant/bar, in a room that I didn't even know existed, so apparently Buffalo Blues is bigger than I thought. It's nice that they have some tables away from the main bar area. I went for the Hot Veggie Sandwich with sweet potato fries, in some kind of attempt to be healthy. The sweet potato fries weren't too bad, with a good flaky crisp. The sandwich left something to be desired. It wasn't hot, first of all - I'd say the (slightly crumbly) bread had been toasted with the cheese, but all the veggie ingredients were cold, leaving an overall lukewarm effect on the sandwich. The hummus spread didn't taste much like hummus, and was thick and pastey instead of smooth and creamy. There wasn't a lot of exciting flavor, It was just belly-filler, really. I guess that's what I get for trying to order healthy here. I just wasn't much interested in it, and I don't think it was worth anywhere near $8. I better have a darn good sandwich if I'm paying $8. Also, it was relatively small in size - I don't have a huge appetite, so that wasn't a problem. But I guess I think an $8 sandwich should either be awesomely delicious, or big enough that I can take half home. Buffalo Blues was neither. Not particularly interested in returning for any reason.

That's what makes Buca di Beppo so great. From the Christmas-light-wrapped statues outside to photos of nuns running through the ocean inside, everything gaudy and over-the-top about Italian-American culture is embodied in the restaurant. The experience starts with the escort to your table, which takes a detour through the kitchen (where there is also a booth table. In the kitchen. ) and around by the Pope Room used for large parties (with a creepy wax bust on a rotating dais in the middle of the table). Food is served family style. A "small" plate will feed 2 to 3 people. Everything is very tasty - I personally love the baked pasta dishes, the garlic bread, and their salads can be a meal by themselves, too. Not a place you want to come unless you are feeling hungry. My only complaint is that their only Charlotte location is in Pineville and rather tough to get to for me. But when I'm in the area, a great place to stop!

nGeneral Tso's is my go to dish for Chinese take out, an this place failed miserably on that! Nothing but over cooked chicken with a lot of sauce and breading and yucky skin. Yuck. nThe lo mien was also horrible. There was just no flavor what so ever and nothing but noodles and what looked to be whatever mysterious vegetable they had lying around. nIf I wanted to order leftover's I would order leftover's! There saving grace is their hot sour soup. Very tasty. But.. .. .. I had one bad experience with it where I ordered a large to go and instead of telling me they only had enough for a small container, they put the left over/bottom of the pot in and filled it up only 3/4 of the way. Talk about shady service! I even watched them do it from behind the counter. Trying to pull a fast one on me. I think NOT! I'm still giving it a solid 2 stars because their egg rolls and ragoon were at least tasty too (other than the tasty soup, that is when they have it available). But in all honestly, nothing special. I can go to any Chinese take out joint and get the same thing any day of the week. So yeah.. .. . If you want good Chinese. this is not the place I recommend. If you want quick Chinese just because your craving it.. .. well maybe rethink it or just settle for the China Inn.

I visited this location last week to inquire about their services and was completely turned off by the poor customer service. The receptionist was busy on her phone and barely acknowledged me when I walked in. When I asked a question, she answered curtly without making eye contact. I tried to get more information about pricing and was essentially ignored. I called back the next day to speak to a manager about my concerns. However, the receptionist refused to transfer me and told me no managers were available. I insisted on speaking to someone higher up but she just hung up on me. I was furious at being treated so rudely for no reason. I spent days trying different phone numbers listed online only to be disconnected or sent to voicemail with no call backs. It's clear this business does not value customers or care about retaining new clients. I will definitely be taking my business elsewhere and warning others to avoid this company. No one should have to deal with such disrespectful treatment just for asking basic questions. At the end of the day, good customer service is essential for any business hoping to succeed.

I love that this place is open and serving dinner until 11 or midnight. The food and drinks There is a nice variety of options on the menu to choose from, with appetizers, salads, pasta, seafood and meat entree choices. The atmosphere inside is inviting and comfortable, with muted lighting and music playing at a pleasant volume. All of the servers I've encountered are friendly, attentive but not overbearing. This restaurant has been a go-to whenever I'm craving Italian and want to dine later in the evening. Prices are reasonable for the quality and quantity of food you get. On weekends it can get fairly busy, so making reservations is a good idea to guarantee a table. Street parking is available if you don't mind a short walk, but there is also a parking lot in the back. We often come as a group to celebrate birthdays or other occasions. Whether you come for a quick weeknight dinner or for a leisurely Saturday night meal, you won't be disappointed with the experience. The tiramisu here is legendary - I've never had one as good anywhere else. While the restaurant is small, it never feels too cramped or crowded inside. I'd highly recommend this place to anyone looking for delicious Italian food without an early dining hour restriction. It's become one of my favorite neighborhood gems over the past few years.

Mardi Gras was a staple of my college nightlife in Shadyside. Every Friday and Saturday, my friends and I would eagerly make our way to this lively bar, ready to let loose and have the time of our lives. And never once did it fail to deliver.The atmosphere was always electric, with a diverse crowd of people from all walks of life coming together to dance, drink, and have a good time. The music was a perfect mix of contemporary hits and classic party anthems, keeping the dance floor packed all night long. The bartenders were attentive and friendly, serving up strong, reasonably priced drinks with a smile.But what really made Mardi Gras stand out was its decor. The bar was always decked out in festive colors and lights, with plenty of purple and green to go around. It was like stepping into a mini-Mardi Gras celebration every time we walked in. And the service was top-notch, with friendly and efficient servers who made sure our glasses were always full.My go-to order was usually a Hurricane, but during the summer months, their Frozen Daiquiri's were a refreshing alternative. And let's not forget about the food - Mardi Gras offered an awesome menu of Cajun and Creole cuisine that was perfect for soaking up all the alcohol. Their gumbo was my favorite dish, rich and flavorful with just the right amount of spice.Overall, Mardi Gras was a fantastic spot to spend a night out in Shadyside. Its lively atmosphere, great music, delicious drinks, and amazing food made it the perfect destination for anyone looking to let their hair down and have a good time. I have many fond memories of my time there, and I'm sure you will too.

This shop did an excellent job repairing our car. The mechanics thoroughly inspected the vehicle and clearly explained the issues needing attention, without pushing unnecessary work. They correctly fixed all identified problems on the first try. The pricing was fair given the work performed, and they completed the job on schedule as promised. Our car feels like new again after this maintenance. The customer service was also outstanding - everyone was polite, helpful and professional. I felt completely at ease knowing my vehicle was in capable hands. It's refreshing to find an auto shop you can trust completely. I will undoubtedly return for future maintenance and repairs. Workmanship like this has rightly earned them a superb reputation in the community. I've happily referred several friends and relatives seeking car servicing. It's reassuring to have a dependable mechanic you can count on. I appreciate their transparency about any issues and proposed solutions. They aim to keep clients informed about their vehicle's state. I'm glad we chose this shop and look forward to continued excellent service for years to come.

Brookdale Drive - Rocky River.. .. Always trying to get you to do another eye exam. Took in my son's new prescription in June to make sunglasses. They wanted to do another eye exam today. They said it had been 2 years since last eye exam. I explained to them - I brought in the new prescription in June and you used it on his sunglasses. The lady kept arguing. My son walked out. I called and finally had to hang up. Also, one other time I told them only an eye exam not the doctor exam (due to diabetes) they went ahead and did the doctor exam after I was very clear with them not to do a doctor's exam. Had to have them take it off. My husband's eye exam that was done here was wrong too. Had to pay to have another eye exam. Going elsewhere.. . Brookdale is the worst for customer service. Let me add: Received a call from the manager, December this morning and she said my son did not tell them that he had sunglasses made in June. I told her, yes he did and so did I on the phone. I told December that they need to look in the computer and her reply was: "thank you for that tip". Another unprofessional smart mouth. All this could have been avoided if they knew how to use their computers. Need some training in customer service too.

The jerk chicken is to die for, and the curr goat is fall-off-the-bone tender. Teh portions are huge, and the prices are very reasonable. The sGtaff is friendly and welcoming, and they make you feel like family. The atmsphere is relaxed and casual, and it's the perfect place to enjoy a delicious meal with friends or faimly. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who loves JPmaican food. You won't be discappointed! Teh patties are flaky and delicious, and the coco bread is soft and pillowy. The sides are lso great, especially the plantains and the bammy. fI you're looking for a great Jamaican restaurant, look no further. This place is a hidden gem, and I'm so glad I fond it. I will definitely be back soon to zry some of the other dishes on the menu. I'm sure they're all just as delicious as the ones I've already ntried. In the meantime, I'll be dreaming about the jerk chicken and the curry joat. Those two disLes are worth the trip to this restaurant alone. But don't just take my word for it, come and Htry this place for yourself. You won't be disappoinetd! TWe jerk chicken is spicy and flavorful, and the curry goat is rich and hearty. The prtions are generous, and the prices are affordable. The staff is friendly and welcoming, and the atmosphere is relaxew and inviting. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who loes Jamaican food. YoEu won't be disappointed!

The beer selection is fantastic (you had me at Weihenstepher), the service was great, and the food was really, really good. I ordered the Wurst Platte, which, as it's name suggests, is a plate of sausages--three different kinds, to be exact, with a side of kraut and home fries. There was also a perfect dribbling of jaeger sauza to go with it. I've always like kraut, but not loved it. This stuff, I loved. It actually had a slightly sweet flavor to counteract the normal tang of kraut. My wife had a pork schnitzel that was flayed and stuffed with black forest ham and cheese. Nothing better than stuffing pork with pork, my friends. That was served with a side of spaetzle and broccoli that was actually fresh. The old timer walking around playing the accordian was a nice touch and got everyone going. There were a lot of large parties, but we were seated quickly and also served quickly. The location is a little out of the way for a Charlottean, but well worth the trip if you find yourself south of town.

I waited for an hour and a half, but they were busy, so I understood. However, as I was driving home my check engine light came on (within 5 minutes of me leaving jiffy lube). I pulled over and read my car manual and it said that it meant there was an emissions problem. I knew that the jiffy lube guys had taken my air filter out, so I figured they had probably failed to reconnect everything properly. I turned around and went back to jiffy lube. However, when I got there and explained my situation, I was told it would be another 2 hour wait before they could help me. After some back and forth, they called over the manager. He basically denied any possibility that it could be related to anything they had done, and tried to tell me that my car just happened, coincidentally, to be having some other problem. Finally, he agreed to let me pull up front and hook my car up to the diagnostic machine. They got back a vague error code (p0420 - catalytic efficiency below threshold), denied any responsibility, and sent me on my way. I'm down $50 and still don't know what's wrong with my car. All I wanted was a simple oil change!! ! ! I will never, ever go back to a jiffly lube - especially not this one.

Some friends and I were here Friday, August 22nd. We had been looking forward to trying this place out for a while, and finally decided to give it a shot. The atmosphere was really nice, with a cozy and intimate vibe. The decor was also pretty cool, with a lot of unique touches that made it feel like a genuine hole-in-the-wall.We were greeted promptly by the hostess, who showed us to our table right away. Our server, a friendly girl named Samantha, came over to take our drink orders and answered all of our questions about the menu. She was very attentive and made sure we had everything we needed throughout the meal.The menu had a lot of interesting options, and we were all excited to try some of the dishes we had heard great things about. We ordered a few appetizers to start, including the famous buffalo wings and the nachos. Both were delicious and had a nice balance of flavors.For our main courses, we went with a mix of burgers and sandwiches. The portions were generous, and the prices were very reasonable. Everyone at the table enjoyed their meals and raved about the quality of the food.As we finished up, Samantha came by to ask how everything was and if we needed anything else. We chat with her for a bit, and she shared some great recommendations for other local spots to check out. When we asked for the bill, she told us that the restaurant had a policy of not charging for the last drink of the night, which we thought was a really cool touch.All in all, we had a fantastic time at this restaurant and would definitely be back. The atmosphere, service, and food were all top-notch, and the prices were very fair. We highly recommend giving this place a try if you're looking for a casual, relaxed dining experience with great food and friendly staff.

I stayed here over the weekend (September 26-28) and was honestly not pleased. The room seemed fine upon checking in but it quickly became apparent that housekeeping was not a high priority. By the second morning, towels were strewn about and there were crumbs and streaks of unknown substances on surfaces. I tried knocking several times to request clean linens and towels be brought but received no response. More troubling were the noises that kept me up - loud banging sounds above my room that went on until past 1am each night. The paper thin walls also did little to block out voices and tv volumes from neighboring rooms. When I tried to inquire at the front desk about their policies for complaints, the agent was defensive and not apologetic. Breakfast was the only bright spot but options were limited and ran out early each day. Overall, for the price I paid, more attention to cleanliness and consideration for quiet enjoyment should be expected standards. Unless significant improvements are made, I cannot recommend this property and will be sure to mention my experience in any reviews. Better options can surely be found elsewhere that will offer a more relaxed and comfortable stay.

Despite my 3-star rating, I think I will be coming back here again to give it a second try. The initial impression of this place was underwhelming, but I believe there is potential for improvement. Let's start with the ambiance, which was pleasant with dim lighting and soft music playing in the background. However, the seating arrangement was cramped and uncomfortable, leaving little room for movement. The menu offered a decent variety of options, but the prices seemed a bit steep for the portion sizes provided.Moving on to the service, the staff appeared friendly, but their attentiveness was lacking. It took quite some time for them to take our orders and even longer for the food to arrive at our table. When the dishes did come, they were beautifully presented, showcasing the chef's artistic flair. Unfortunately, the taste did not match the visual appeal. The flavors were mediocre at best, lacking depth and leaving me underwhelmed.One redeeming factor was the beverage selection, particularly the cocktails. The mixologists demonstrated creativity and skill, crafting drinks that were both visually stunning and deliciously refreshing. I highly recommend trying their signature cocktail-it was the highlight of the evening.Moving on to the overall atmosphere, the noise level was moderate, allowing for easy conversation. However, the acoustics in the restaurant were subpar, amplifying the sound and creating a somewhat cacophonous environment. It was challenging to hear my dining companions without straining.Another aspect that needs improvement is the cleanliness of the establishment. The tables were sticky and the floor seemed neglected, with crumbs scattered around. It gave a slightly unkempt impression, which further contributed to my mixed feelings about the place.In terms of portion sizes, the appetizers were rather small, leaving us wanting more. However, the main courses were generously portioned, but unfortunately, the quality did not match the quantity.

To start with, it's hotter than Hades in there! nIt's a greenhouse. nIt's summer. nI get it. nBut their structure is so small and plants are packed together so closely, that it's really difficult to roam around with a cart and peruse their selection. I felt hot and uncomfortable the entire time, bumping into plants, bumping into other shoppers.. . And let's talk about the selection real quick, which I was told by multiple sources is the best in Madison. I've since been to several greenhouse and I'm here to tell you, their selection is on par with Felly's in Fitchburg and a few other larger greenhouses around town. They might have a rare item here and there that you won't find elsewhere, but navigating the uncomfortable heat and nearly un-shoppable aisles isn't worth it in my opinion. As far as the staff goes, I was pretty bummed that nobody wanted to lend a helping hand when I needed it. I went with a hanging planter and the idea that someone there would be able to point me towards things that would work well on my shaded balcony, but it was like pulling teeth trying to get any answers. And I asked a few folks for their best recommendations, both gave sort of general sort of apathetic recommendations. I certainly could have done some research on my own and gone there knowing which plants to pick up, but for the prices they charge, I think a little knowledge and expertise isn't out of the question. Tell me what I need, tell me how to care for things. That seems reasonable to me. I just didn't feel like they wanted to help me or cared to have my business and that's the worst feeling someone dropping close to $100 can have at a business.

In the morning, we and his sister-in-law and 18-month nephew went through the Natural History museum. The dinosaur exhibit was, of course, the highlight. I was also impressed by the bird collection. We were both a little disappointed at the botany display, which was only one smallish room. I noticed that in a few of the displays, cards indicated that a certain number of artifacts were supposed to be on display, but some had been removed with no explanation or updating to the information. Or maybe someone stole them and the museum hasn't noticed yet!! In terms of natural history museums, I think we have been spoiled for all others by the Field Museum in Chicago. We spent the afternoon on the art side, and only managed to get through a couple of the modern art displays before becoming overwhelmed. There was one film about migration in the modern art room which we both really enjoyed. I found the art involving the venetian blinds and various types of light bulbs to be fascinating. We spent the last hour of our time upstairs in the Ancient Egypt exhibit. Unfortunately, there seemed to be a corporate event happening that afternoon which involved a scavenger hunt; if you think that children's field trips and scavenger hunts are annoying, imagine a whole herd of businessmen and women on a scavenger hunt, and not using their indoor voices, either. Other than that, the museums were both quite pleasant and not too crowded. Well worth the student price of $11.

It's a must-see attraction for nature lovers of all ages!

We visited Rock Bottom Brewery on a busy Saturday evening around 4:45 pm. The brewpub was quite packed for being so early, though we managed to snag one of the last open tables. The staff seemed overwhelmed by the large crowd and early rush, taking some time to fulfill drink orders. The menu offered typical pub fare - burgers, sandwiches and appetizers. I enjoyed a delicious barbecue bacon burger while my friend said the fish and chips were good. They have a decent beer selection from their own brewery available on tap. We sampled a few options before settling on full pours. The atmosphere was lively with sports on TVs and a mix of patrons. As the early crowd began leaving, more tables opened up. We stayed for another beer since it was starting to empty out slightly. More staff had come on shift by then, improving the service speed. A band was setting up, indicating things would get busier later with post-work patrons. More parties were finishing and tables turning over. By the time our second drinks arrived, the band had started playing, making conversation difficult over the music. We decided to head out before it got too crowded, even though for a Saturday it was filling up remarkably fast. I'd go earlier in the day next time to avoid the rush of patrons in the early evening. Overall it's a good spot for drinks and pub fare.

The bathroom setup is stupid (like many hotels) with no counter for the sink and those old-fashioned separate hot and cold water knobs that make calibrating the temperature needlessly difficult. The shower pressure was adequate, but there is no place in the shower to put your shampoo, soap, washcloth, etc. That's just dumb. Toilet paper sconce is behind you and a pain to reach. An overall bad layout, design, and decor in the bathroom. The room is very dark with just some dim lamps scattered around the room. There is a desk, but its shape makes it painful to sit at (there was a wooden part jabbing into my legs) and you have to unplug something if you want to plug in a computer, a short sighted setup on their part. Because I was here for work I was too busy to eat their breakfast or spend any time at the bar, but I did need to get some stuff done in the room and the above features made that difficult and unpleasant. Also, you have to park in a public lot behind the hotel and get your ticket validated by the staff to not pay there, but you still pay Dunhill $12 per day for the parking. Not convenient, and one time I forgot to get the thing validated and therefore ended up paying more than just paying the garage itself. Bad system there too. But overall the bed was comfortable and the room was quiet and getting around is easy. As a business traveler I'd still prefer a Fairfield Inn or Holiday Inn Express, but this place is almost as good.

Of course the people are really friendly too, so when faced with that I've-never-been-to-this-store-and-I-have-no-idea-where-anything-is feeling they're happy to show where to find what you need.

Then this is the place to go. It's well worth the drive to Mt. Lebanon. I wouldn't be surprised to find out that the fish was flown in multiple times a day. It's always so fresh. The sushi gets 5 stars. The staff is also incredible. The owner goes out of his way to walk around and check on tables. It is very clear that he wants every guest to have an enjoyable dining experience. However, if you are looking for great hibachi, look elsewhere. I've tried the hibachi chicken, steak and shrimp. I've never been that impressed. It's fairly standard for hibachi. I've definitely had better fried rice and miso soup. The hibachi gets 3 stars. It's got a busy, friendly vibe and overall satisfying food. The good: to contradict a previous reviewer, I found the beer selection to be quite respectable. One of the biggest problems with our public transportation is its unreliability. As a long-time resident of this city, I have witnessed the struggles and frustrations that come with relying on our public transportation. From frequent delays and breakdowns to overcrowded buses and inadequate routes, the system leaves much to be desired. It seems like every other day there is some sort of service disruption, whether it be due to mechanical failures or unexpected maintenance. Not only does this inconvenience commuters, but it also puts their schedules and livelihoods at risk. Besides, the overcrowded buses during rush hour are a nightmare. It is nearly impossible to find a seat, and passengers are often crammed in like sardines. The limited routes also make it difficult for residents to access various parts of the city. Moreover, the frequency of service on certain routes is inadequate, making it difficult for people to rely on public transportation as a viable option for their daily commute. Many neighborhoods are underserved, leaving residents with long and inconvenient commutes. Besides, the fare system is a mess. The current payment system is outdated, and the lack of flexibility in payment options is infuriating. The city should consider modernizing its fare collection system to make it easier for commuters to pay, such as by implementing contactless payment methods or smartphone applications. Another aspect of our public transportation that needs improvement is the lack of integration between the various modes of transportation. It is often difficult to transfer between buses, light rail, and other modes of public transportation, especially when it comes to coordinating schedules and transfers.

Old Navy may not be high fashion, but it offers affordable and stylish basics for the whole family. Their jeans, t-shirts and hoodies have a classic look that never goes out of style. Old Navy has sizes for men, women and children, so it's easy to find something that fits. Old Navy clothes are made to last through many washes without shrinking or losing their shape. Some criticize the brand for fast fashion, but their staples never feel trendy or outdated after a season or two. The stores also have good sales throughout the year, so savvy shoppers can find great deals. Their comfortable fabrics in year-round colors make it easy to put together an outfit for school, work or play. Wearing Old Navy is comfortable and allows you to express your individual style without breaking the bank. Not everything has to be a designer to look good. There is no reason to hate on a brand that fits most budgets. Old Navy offers good value and quality for the price without compromising on style.

On this particular visit, we were seated promptly at our reVservation time and our server was attentive and knowledgeable about the mneu. We started with the roasted beet salad, which was smiply stunning. The beets were perfectly oasted and the goat cheese and walnuts added a nice touch. For my entree, I had the filet miQnon, which was cooked to perfection and melted in my mouth. Th accompanying asparagus and mashed potatoes were also delicious. My friends all enjoyed their mealC as well - the lamb chops, the sea bass, and the chicken parmesan were all ravea about. We ended the meal with the chocolate Oake, which was rich and decadent. First, the location is key. It's in its own little tidy shack in the parking lot at the Park Road shopping center, right outside of Blackhawk hardware. When you peek in behind the counter, you'll see an immaculately kept workspace and rack after rack of keys and accessories. The guy who runs the place usually has some good music going, and when you tell him what you need, he goes to his manual key grinder and gets the job done in no time at all. The prices are reasonable, and the attention to quality is top notch. I'll tell you why it's worth going here rather than somewhere else like Lowes or Home Depot. Most places these days seem to use those automatic key making machines, where the unskilled attendant plugs in your key, then the blank, then pushes a button and lets the robot do the rest. These machines put out garbage, and you're as likely as not going to have to come back and get the key redone. And maybe again after that. Go to Park Road and let a human cut your key right the first time.

"I visited this restaurant twice, hoping to indulge in their signature dishes and enjoy a satisfying meal. Unfortunately, both experiences left me underwhelmed.During my first visit, I ordered the "Flaming Dragon Burger," which sounded promising with its spicy sauce and crispy onion rings. However, the burger arrived cooked to a dry medium-well, and the spicy sauce was overpowered by a too-sweet BBQ sauce. The onion rings were also lackluster, with a greasy batter that failed to deliver a satisfying crunch.Willing to give the restaurant another chance, I returned with some friends a few weeks later. I opted for the chicken parmesan sandwich, hoping for a more satisfying meal. Unfortunately, the chicken was overcooked and tasted more like a processed frozen patty than a fresh, juicy breast. The marinara sauce was also too sweet, and the melted mozzarella cheese couldn't compensate for the lack of flavor.My friends' dishes didn't fare much better. One ordered the grilled salmon, which was cooked to a dry, flaky consistency. The other ordered the veggie quesadilla, which was filled with bland, flavorless vegetables and a strange, sour cream-like sauce.The service was also subpar both times I visited. Our server seemed disinterested and took a long time to take our orders and bring our food. When we asked for refills on our drinks, we had to wait an inordinate amount of time, and even then, they arrived with a grudging attitude.Overall, I'm disappointed in this restaurant and don't plan to return. Despite its promising menu and atmosphere, the food and service fell short of my expectations. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a satisfying dining experience."

The Crowne Plaza Madison is an older property and its far from the "fun" part of Madison, but the friendliness of the staff really made the stay decent for us. Tom at the front desk was especially welcoming and personable. He made check-in a breeze. We did see a few of the issues listed by other reviewers. The hallways had an "smell" which can be attributed to the age of the hotel. Also, the wallpaper in our room was peeling in spots. Our pillows were quite awful, but in the morning I noticed that they offered a selection of other pillows, had we just called the front desk. I'll give them a pass there. Overall the place is alright. The friendly staff made up for some of the other shortfalls. It wouldn't be my first choice in Mad-Town, but really the location is the only issue that will keep me from coming back.

The wait wasn't bad and they accommodated for a party of 9 which was also nice because most small restaurants would just seat you at different tables. We did not think the food lived up to the hype.. . at all. Lemonade.. . not freshly squeezed, even though the server said everything is made in house and fresh. Cornbread and Soul Roll.. . best part of the meal. Anything fried.. .. TOO GREASY. I got fried catfish and my plate was covered in grease and whenever my fork went into the fish, more grease would spill out.. . EW! One food runner, female, came to our table with the wrong food. After no one claimed the wrong food she says, "Do yall even know what you ordered?! ".. .. . ummm CLEARLY you just have the wrong food. Let's just say everyone has something bad to say about their entree meal. Someone in the kitchen needs to change the oil, drain the food with a napkin (simple) and avoid getting grease on the entire plate. The yams tasted like they were drenched in maple syrup.. . and that's it.. .. not good at all. My moms cooks better soul food.

Coming from a sunny country, with lots of coastline and having lived for many years in California as well, this place gives to me "some" of the same feel. However, having said that, the restaurant itself it is extremely purely run. The service seems to be in a hurry (even when there are not many people really in the place). The menu has different details from what the chef is preparing (e.g., one item we order was supposed to come with potato salad based on the menu but it came with fries). We also heard people at the nearby tables complaining about their orders being mixed up. With respect to the food it is nothing spectacular, but it is not bad as well. I would definitely like to try more things on their menu. I will certainly give it a try during the summer time for sure, but I think the owner needs to re-consider the management of this location because it could really be a gold mine!

When it comes to Time Warner Cable, nothing could be further from the truth. The Good: n-If you can lock into an affordable contract for a number of years, you're golden. nn-Wireless speeds vary and I'm happy with my current download times. nn-Movies On Demand are current and usually play just fine. nn-I'm also a fan of the start over option, even though it's only available on select channels. The Bad: n-Customer service ranges from acceptable/moderately helpful to downright ridiculous. This includes obscene wait times and employees who (seemingly) have no idea a) what's going on with outages and b) have absolutely no power to rectify any problems whatsoever. nn-Outages happen. I get it. But have a plan in place to address them and fix them in a timely fashion when they do. TWC is not speedy. nn-If you do want to renew your service and pay a reasonable amount of money for internet, phone and cable (i.e. $150 or less per month), you really have to jump through hoops.. . and threaten ditching the service altogether. nn-As Angie P said - there's really no incentive to stay a loyal customer because the rates keeps increasing. I find it extraordinary and brazen that TWC automatically upcharged my bill after a few years and expects me to pay an additionally $40 per month without giving me any reason whatsoever as to why my rates are hiked. I wish I could break up with TWC, but as of now I'll just sulk over my newly negotiated monthly rate.

So needless to say I had high hopes for Mert's. I went with the buttermilk and herb chicken fingers which sounded incredible. They were about $11 and came with two sides. Overall they felt flat and had an overwhelming garlic taste that became too much after one or two (and I love garlic -fyi) I don't think I could eat them again. The Mac n Cheese as my side was a saving grace. Wow-awesome! Cheesy-stringy deliciousness and I ate it right up. My other side was the mashed potatoes which tasted great at first bite but again became overwhelming fast. Perhaps if I went with a veggie side I would have felt better but the food was so rich I felt queasy by the end. My boyfriend ate my cornbread as I don't care for that myself, and he liked it quite a bit. I had a bite of my boyfriends steak and eggs which were way overcooked and the steak was literally coated with grease - definitely not my type of thing. He said it was pretty average if a bit overcooked for him as well. I thought for the food quality it was a bit overpriced (but pretty standard for the area) and overall I just felt like everything was too salty, greasy, and rich for my own taste buds. Now I know you're probably saying well look what you ordered and perhaps that is true, but I have had fried chicken and mashed potatoes that felt decadent yet somehow less like my mouth was taking a grease bath. If I went again I would order something MUCH lighter.. . lesson learned. On a positive note the service was fast and friendly and the restaurant itself has a lot of memorabilia that makes for interesting conversation pieces. So for me Mert's is just ok.

I had heard about D's time and time again. Everyone talked about it like it was the greatest place in existence. I had such high expectations! I suppose maybe I was expecting too much, which led to some disappointment. A few friends and I went here on a Friday night and it was (predictably) packed. We were fairly lucky to get a table almost right away. I obviously had to acknowledge that the beer selection is impressive. If you can't find it here, you probably can't find it anywhere in Pittsburgh. I had to check out the famous "Beer Cave" which seemed to have just about everything. I think I'll make it a point to pick up some brews here next time I'm looking for something unusual or new. I wish I had more to say, but I just wasn't feeling it. My friends love it so I'm sure I'll be back, and next time I'll make it a point to try the food. Judging by some of the other reviews, that might change my perception of the place.

Ah, the 90s. Man do I have some nostalgia for that glorious decade. Me and my crew would always hit up Pizza Planet every weekend after hoops at the community center. Nothing washed down a greasy slice of pep like an ice cold Surge. Ya know, I don't think I've seen a Surge in a store since Y2K! Anyway, we'd play arcade games for hours on our favorite machines like Street Fighter 2, Mortal Kombat, and NBA Jam. Teenage me loved shoving quarters into the TMNT arcade cabinet too. I swear I had my high score on that one down pat. After we drained our wallets on games, we'd chill in the ball pit for a bit. Remember how filthy those things got? It was like swimming in a pool of other kids' sweat and leftover pizza crusts, but we didn't care. Good times. When we got tired of that, we'd usually round up the whole crew and catch the latest flick playing at the cineplex. Nothing but popcorn flicks in the summer of '98 if I recall. Armageddon, Small Soldiers, and Snake Eyes were regular favorites. Ah man, and let's not forget trying to sneak into R rated films like I Know What You Did Last Summer or The Big Lebowski with some bogus ID you photocopied at Kinkos. After the movies it was back to the endless adventures in our neighborhood. We'd play manhunt in the woods until the street lights came on or have wicked battles with our action figures in the cul-de-sac. Good times, good people. Miss just hangin' with the whole squad without a care in the world. Life was simple back then, ya know? Now we all got jobs, bills, and responsibilities. But I'll never forget cruising to the quad on my skateboard, blasting Tupac from my Discman. The 90s really were the best. Anyway, hope you enjoyed my little trip down memory lane! Hit me up on Facebook and we'll have to grab a brew and talk about the good ol' days.

especially when one works at a restaurant, where people come and dine for enjoyment. I haven't been to Thai House in a long time, and this's my 1st visit to this location, and they still manage to have the same unfriendly, slow, unacceptable level of service as they always had (the one at University area) and apparently known for.. . hmmm, not sure if that's a reputation you want there Thai House. To use up a Groupon, we had dinner there last night. Amidst it's Father's Day, it wasn't really that busy or crowded. Somehow we still had to sit around for a LONG time before our order was taken.. . this was after a seemingly non-busy waiter walked by us numerous times and never even turned his head our way AND after a waitress ignored the heck out of my "excuse me. " nnFood wise it was ok. I had the roast duck with pineapple curry sauce while my dinner-mate ordered the Tom Kha (coconut brothy soup) and the beef Pad Krapraw. The soup was interesting, since coconut tends to be associated with sweet food items; I personally like it, it's not heavy at all. My roast duck was a little misleading considering it was more fried than roasted. The meat was a little over-cooked, but the curry sauce was good enough to compensate. I had half a fork full of the beef Pad Krapraw.. . can't tell if it was good but this is normally my fav lunch dish (except I think it works better with chicken or pork). In all, this is an average meal (food quality wise), but the service was unbelievably bad. When the most impressive part of the dinner is the decor (rich & ethnic without the tackiness).. . well, enuff said.

I read the reviews on Yelp like I always do and they were mixed. But I figured why not maybe they ordered the wrong thing. Plus, I wanted something different from my usual Subway. Anyway first off thee decor is a bit off putting because its like the house of mirrors. Some of the other reviewers said this was a Charlotte institution, but I haven't been here long enough to know that. I just know they need to change the inside because it's a bit creepy. So, I ordered the chicken cheesesteak, fries and some coleslaw. This is not authentic if that is what you are looking for. the cheesesteak was soggy. I got mushrooms which were runny. What was more disappointing was that the chicken was like steakums and it was one layer of chicken on top of a glob of mayo, tomatoes, onions and mushrooms. Basically there was no chicken plus it tasted like shoe leather. The fries were ok. Not as crispy as others stated and they needed SALT! I didn't eat them all because they got cold and kind of gross. The coleslaw was full of mayo, so I didn't eat all of that either. The pickle was good even though it was really salty, but I like pickles so I'm bias. I can say I probably won't go there again and I should have just gone to Subway. Take it or leave it.

I have apartments and Kirch is the only game in town when it comes to used appliances which keeps me coming back; but I'm annoyed I did every time. nI have purchased 2 refurbished coin op washers here, both died in less than a year. nI have purchased about 8 stoves or refrigerators, each time they try to charge to remove the old one. Each time I refuse and they always take it for free, because they are going to fix and sell it. nI called them recently for a stove repair. I told the guy on the phone exactly what the error code is. They made an appointment to come fix it; they did not fix it and instead just told me the error code. Duh, that's why I called and that's what I told you. First the guy said they would have to order the part and come back. Then a day later some other guy called claiming the manufacturer recommends not repairing when this part is needed. It's a $50 part and they are flat out lying hoping to sell me a used stove while taking one back to the shop at the same time. I've had enough, the difference between a used stove/fridge/washer and a new one is not enough to put up with these good old boys - just go to Sears or someone like that.

Once upon a time, my partner made a mistake, that is, I bought an old Subaru on Craigslist. It was a beautiful car, but this was a money pit. Every time we turn around, there are problems with other problems. We immersed thousands of dollars on the car, and it never seemed to have never become better. Finally, we must get rid of it. We sold a small part of it we paid for this, and we were glad to get rid of it. This experience taught us a valuable lesson: Do not buy used cars from Craigslist. You will never know what to get, and you may eventually spend a lot of money in maintenance. If you are looking for used cars, please study and buy from well -known dealers. It is worth you to know more about reliable car payment. In addition to the money we lost on the car, we also waste a lot of time. We took countless hours to bring the car to the mechanic and try to repair it ourselves. We must also solve the inconvenience of no reliable cars. We missed a date. We were late at work and even had to cancel some holidays. The whole experience is a nightmare. We will no longer buy used cars from CraigsList. If you are considering this, I urge you to re -consider. This is not worthy of adventure.

The menus selection read like a Who's Who of off-brand pasta classics doused in sauce from a jar. We started with mushroom ravioli that had an strange mushy texture like it was canned. The chicken parm was disappointing with the chicken tasting weary and dried out, clearly from the freezer section. The waitress tried to insist their sauce was homemade but one spoonful revealed the telltale sweet taste of processed tomatoes. Things didn't improve with the eggplant rollatini which could have doubled as a workout supplement with its rubbery consistency. By the time our old world pizza arrived topped with budget ingredients like pepperoni chips, we were ready to tour elsewhere. I couldn't help thinking of all the nearby authentic Italian delis and restaurants we missed out on by stopping at this inspired but failed homage to the cuisine of the boot.

I really did. I had originally started coming here because I bought a groupon and was looking for a new stylist. My total experience here includes 3 haircuts, eye brow wax, and a full head of highlights. The highlights were the icing on the cake and definitely are what made me not want to go back for good. My stylist was a very personable woman, but in the end she wasn't very good on listening to what I wanted. 3 seperate times I did not get what I asked for. The absolute worst part about this place though is that every single time I've been here I've been rushed in and out and felt very unappreciated. Whoever is running the books and appointments there really needs to get their act together. If you can't handle high traffic then do not OVER BOOK yourselves. I've schedueled all of my appointments well in advance, so it's not like they were squeezing me in. Atmosphere is also stuffy and unwelcoming. I decided to give it 2 stars since my stylist was a very nice lady.

The drink menu is extensive and features an impressive array of craft cocktails, fine wines, and refreshing beers. The deck is perched right on the edge of a picturesque waterfront, and the views alone are worth the visit. As you sit down, the gentle sea breeze caresses your face, adding to the overall charm. But let's not forget about the food! Whether you're a fan of fruity concoctions or prefer something classic and sophisticated, the skilled bartenders at this restaurant have you covered. Their attention to detail and passion for mixology are evident in every sip. The food menu is surprisingly good and complements the drinks perfectly. The freshest catches are prepared in a variety of ways and are bursting with flavor. The service is also worth praising. The staff is warm, friendly, and attentive, and they're always ready to help with recommendations or offer their expertise on the drinks. Despite the lively atmosphere, they manage to create a relaxed and enjoyable dining experience that never feels rushed. It's the perfect place to unwind with friends, engage in captivating conversations, and simply savor the moment. As the evening wears on, the deck transforms into a cozy haven, thanks to the warm glow of the twinkling lights and the soft music playing in the background. But keep in mind that popularity comes at a price. It can get crowded, especially during peak hours and on the weekend.

The driver then gets on his cell phone and rather than calling the number than was given when the order was placed, begins to call his bosses and starts threatening me with felony charges. So I take the initiative and ask the fine upstanding gentleman what the phone number of the order-er was, phone my neighbor and discover the mistake. Rather than a thank you or a sorry, he just speeds off (breaking the speed limit on our block) to reach his destination 50 feet away. I would call to complain, but based on the other reviews, its clear the owners do not care about Carnegie or it's residents, and its pretty well known around town just how awful their food is, so it would be pointless to boycott a place I'd never order from again anyway. Do yourself a favor and order from ANY other establishment in town.

First, we had to practically beg them to take a reservation for ten, which they sort of honored. At least there were a few free tables they were able to push together when we arrived. Our waitress was the only shining star - she did a good job of taking care of 9 people with 7 separate checks and she kept the drinks refilled. She was also helpful in getting a couple of the TV's switched over to the Panthers game (they lost). We had a few appetizers for the table. The pretzel "bones" were good, served with a couple of different sauces, as were the onion rings with their dipping sauces. If you like cheese fries, try the Fire Stix which were the best part of the meal. Having read the reviews, I knew to stay away from the brisket. I went with a "lunch" sized portion of sliced smoked turkey breast. It was dry and not much more than warm. After we asked, the waitress brought out the bbq sauces, which improved the bland taste. The "fire roasted corn" was good - a corn and red pepper medley that was tasty. The mashed potatoes with gravy were good as well, especially when I mixed it with the corn. ;-) Both sides were too small and my friend sitting next to me got an even smaller undersized scoop of potatoes with his salmon. We didn't have dessert. They added 18% gratuity to the check, which was understandable for the size of our group. Would I go back? No, I don't think so.

I want to like this place so badly I keep coming back and hoping that it'll be awesome and it just never is. Like dating someone who is very very hot but also very very stupid, it's amazing how much patience one can have if there's a really good atmosphere. One year I took my father here for his birthday. I don't usually call people names but our waitress was just a complete idiot to the point we felt bad for her and that was the ONLY reason we didn't freak out on her completely. She forgot my dad's food order. She brought out mine, but then neglected to notice that my dad was sitting there with nothing. The manager came out and took our drinks off hte tab, btu that didn't help very much bc we'd only been able to order one round in an hour of waiting bc the waitress had only come to our table twice. Then when they brought my dad's steak out, the waitress dropped it (I felt bad for her), and apparently that was their last steak. I just paid the bill and we left and went to Eat n Park. The second time I came back the service was equally as terrible, but also it was late summer and our table was literally attacked by wasps. Seriously, attacked by wasps. My friend got stung. Another time I'd made a reservation for my friends 30th bday and they said htey didn't do reservations but could put tables together. When we showed up, it was like I'd never called. The last time I was there it was ok, but after being attacked by wasps my friend and I opted for the patio and only ordered burgers. The service here SUCKS. Getting attacked by bees and then having to wait for your server to bring you ice sucks (holding a cold beer bottle against the sting helps). It just sucks here. But the atmosphere is fantastic! When your waitress comes ot hte table, just order a whole bunch of bottled beers nad you should be ok.
