It is wedged into a small triangular shaped building. They are open for lunch and dinner. Their pizza has been a staple of Downtown since 1980. Their specialty pizzas include spinach and feta cheese pizza, a little too oily for my tastes (it's made with an oil and garlic sauce). A much better choice is Buffalo Chicken Pizza, which is Buffalo sauce topped with cheese and spicy chicken. The chicken has a nice fresh taste to it and while spicy, is never overdone. But I love the hoagies the best here. My favorite is the tuna hoagie, which is served with cheese, lettuce, tomato, & grilled onions. I know, break out the Listerine strips after eating one of those. If I like something a little zestier, I'll get the Capicola or the Genoa Salami hoagie. They have a lunch buffet here too. I've never tried it because I prefer my food made-to-order.

I have been shopping around for a couple months for a new road bike (which was going to be my first road bike ever, meaning that I'm fairly clueless about how to pick one out). Also, since I'm a student, I don't have particularly deep pockets. At Big Bang, I was greeted basically the moment I walked in the door. I'm kind of shy when I know that I don't really know what I'm doing, but I wasn't pressured or harassed in any way by the staff. Even though my price range was pretty low, they still tried their hardest to find a bike that suited my needs, and they found a bike that fitted me perfectly (and gave me an excellent deal on the price). They take a lot of care to make sure you're properly fitted to the bike. Also, this is one of the few bike stores I've been to where test riding is gleefully encouraged, rather than grudgingly allowed. Definitely it's the only bike store where they'll tell you "You haven't tried it out enough, go climb up the hill on it! " -- they definitely put the emphasis on matching rider with bike, rather than making a quick sale. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone who's looking for a road bike, whether they're a seasoned racer or a neophyte rider like me.

While the exterior of Rusty's looks simple, the food is anything but ordinary. Upon walking in, I was impressed by how welcoming the staff was. I decided to start with an appetizer of buffalo wings, which were cooked to perfection with a tasty spice level. My meal was a bacon cheeseburger that came out piled high and hit the spot. The fries on the side were crisp and paired nicely. For my drink I chose a local craft beer that complimented the food well. The interior of Rusty's has a cozy, casual vibe with comfortable booths and tables. It was nice to see families, friends, and couples all enjoying their meals together. Our server was very friendly and attententive to refill drinks or answer any questions. For my companion's meal, she enjoyed a garden salad and chicken tenders that were cooked juist right. The kitchen did a great job accommodating dietary restrictions.Overall the quality and portions of the food made for a very reasonable price. I will definitely be back to try more dishes on the eclectic menu. It was refreshing to find a neighborhood gem like Rusty's. They have clearly found a formula that works through quality ingredients and good service. I'm glad I finally stopped putting off dining here and can understand why it has become a local favorite. The consistently good experience has earned Rusty's repeat customer in me.

Good friends of mine who spent a helluva a lot of money in Pittsburgh that weekend - who work hard and expect good service for good money like everyone else. We were greeted with reserved distant service. The waiter said something nervously like "It's all good, " or something that people don't even say anymore. A round of Patron Margaritas were horrible. They tasted entirely like sour mix and we couldn't even take more than two sips. Of course, when we ask that they be taken away and replaced with shots of Patron, we were got the "oh, you're that type, " look and it took a while to convince the waiter that there was sincerely something wrong with the drinks. Being used to that look, black folks often stomach bad food just to not appear to be complainers, but these drinks were horrible! So in the spirit of good faith, we ordered the some appetizers. Shrimp cocktail, crab bisque, and two oyster samplers. The soup was bland, shrimp were large, but had a wierd texture that didn't seem fresh or like they'd been scrubbed to hide something, and oysters were not evenly sampled on both orders. One appeared to contain mostly one type instead of the 8-9 different types. We plunked down the $200 for the appetizers and drinks with a nice tip and said ciao - went and had dinner at Sonoma - which was much better.. . Fish Market needs some lessons on hospitality and diversity OR new management.

My dad and I came here for dinner last night after finding out that Jimmy Tsangs had closed. Rick had to teach a night class and Mom had a meeting to go to. Besides, I hadn't been Yeah, I know the chow here is Americanized Chinese food. Who cares--it's great stuff! Now when eating Chinese, you should never begin by diving in to your main course right away. First you've gotta have some soup and some egg rolls! Dad and I both began with some r-e-a-l-l-y good hot-n-sour soup. Man, that was good-n-bold. Warmed my insides right away! Now I know that vegetable spring rolls are supposedly better for you. Yeah right--what's a great Chinese dinner without some good old fashioned egg rolls? I like to put a spoonful each of sweet-n-sour sauce, duck sauce, and hot Chinese mustard on my plate, dipping my egg roll in a different one with each bite! I love the names of some of their specialties here, including the Triple Crown, Three Afire, Sizzling Trio, and the Royal Match. Feeling a little adventurous--and why not: the old man was paying--I went for the Jaded Affair. Yum, scallops and shrimp marinated in white sauce. Usually seafood isn't my first choice. My dad went for the Kung Pao Chicken. I've got to give him credit--how a guy his age can eat that and not reach for the Mylanta is beyond me!

The location is perfect, just a short walk from our front door. The building is impressive, with a sleek and modern design that really stands out. The entrance is welcoming, with a friendly doorman always ready to help. The lobby is spacious and well-appointed, with comfortable seating and a stylish decor. The elevators are fast and reliable, taking us quickly to our floor. The hallways are clean and well-maintained, with plenty of natural light pouring in from the large windows. Our apartment is roomy and well-equipped, with plenty of storage space and modern appliances. The bedrooms are quiet and cozy, with comfortable beds and plenty of closet space. The bathroom is spotless, with nice tile work and powerful showerheads. Overall, we're really happy with our choice and feel lucky to have found such a great place to call home.

nThey have an insane wine list, and a decent beer list. Closed on Monday, open for lunch and dinner the rest of the week, Shanghai is better-than-average Chinese fare that has a full page of veg-friendly options. It is also very affordable, with mains coming in at about $9-$10 each. Its a smaller menu than I'm used to, and not everything is available (looking to try the "vegetarian seafood medley" I was informed it was no longer being served, since no one was ordering it). A surprising number of the appetizers are, however. We went with Lettuce Cups, which was pretty standard, except for the sauce that accompanied it. No plum sauce here, but spicy, watery, sweet-sour hot mustard! Wowza! I was happy. Like Donna said, they'll do whatever level of hot you want. I ordered my stuff at a 9 (out of 10) and wasn't satisfied. You can ask for whole chili's rather than dried flakes, and that's my plan for the next time I come, 'cos I crave the heat. I'd have another star to award Shanghai, but I find the lack of veg-friendly soups a little sad, having to pick through their larger-than-what-they-actually-serve menu a bit of a hassle, and the flavors a little far over the "too sweet" line.

From the moment I stepped into Bossa Nova, I was immediately captivated by its vibrant ambiance. The restaurant was adorned with festive decorations that created a lively and cheerful atmosphere. As I entered the treatment room, I couldn't help but notice how clean and organized everything was. The dentist himself was incredibly patient and understanding, explaining each step of the procedure and addressing all of my concerns. He had a gentle touch and managed to minimize any discomfort I felt during the cleaning. One thing that really stood out to me was the advanced technology used in the clinic. but just barely. The food here is good and it's probably one of the places in Charlotte you have to eat, but I will return to other places before returning to Barrington's. After all of the talk about how good the food is at Barrington's, we had admittedly high expectations. To begin with, we were both fairly disappointed with the bread served prior to our meal. I generally think that, while not a significant part of the meal, the bread sets the tone for a meal. Ours tasted and felt like it was either microwaved or warmed in a convection oven. Of all of the really good meals I have had in my life, I would venture than 95% were proceeded by exceptional bread. I thought the tomato soup was very, very good. My wife had a mixed green salad that was good but not exceptional. The entrees were the biggest disappointment. I ordered the lamb chops. This was, again, a good dish but not exceptional. I am a fan of keeping food simple. The hash and greens ended up just being a mix of flavors that didn't necessarily complement the meat. I also love a good sear to the outside of the meat to provide texture, which this preparation lacked. My wife had the rigatoni. This a very rich and abundant dish. I can see what it is popular but think that better pastas can be had at a number of restaurants in Charlotte. Overall, we had a good experience. It definitely suffered from our high expectations, but I would not rank this as Charlotte's best restaurant largely due to my feeling that it wasn't very innovative, the lamb could have been prepared a little better and the rigatoni was just a decadent but not necessarily tasty dish.

Why Go? Because Matador is not just a restaurant, it's an experience that will transport you to another time. The moment you step through the doors, you're greeted by the charm of a bygone era. The place may not have undergone redecoration in years, but that's part of its allure. It's a small, unpretentious establishment that exudes authenticity. Finding parking can be a challenge, but once you're settled at a booth near the window, all your troubles melt away. The soft, indirect light creates a cozy atmosphere that invites you to relax and take in the ambiance. And don't forget the free chips and salsa-they're a delightful treat that sets the stage for the meal to come.While the service may not be the swiftest, it gives you an opportunity to savor the moment and engage in conversation with your companions. I highly recommend trying the combination dinner, where you can choose three delicious items accompanied by rice and beans. Personally, I love indulging in two beef tacos and a cheese enchilada; it's a satisfying platter that never disappoints. If you're feeling adventurous, venture beyond the traditional Mexican fare and try the Greek Gyro platter. It might not be the most authentic gyro you've ever had, but it's certainly worth a taste.To fully enjoy Matador, I suggest visiting during the late afternoon or early evening when it's less crowded. It's a place where you can take your time, relish the mixed salsas, and savor each bite. Lunchtime can get quite hectic, so it's best to avoid the rush. Matador offers a unique dining experience that embraces its history and refuses to conform to mainstream trends. So, if you're looking for a genuine, unpretentious eatery with a touch of nostalgia, Matador is the place to be. Give it a try and let yourself be transported to a different era, one delicious dish at a time.

A latecomer to our group asked another waitress clearing a nearby table if she was our waitress. The woman said "no" and walked away without offering to get our server. It was a little weird. Our waitress also had people at the other end of the table yell their lunch orders, even though it was very loud. She could have easily walked over, so that was odd, too. And in Germany I'd probably never set a foot into a traditionally designed beer house - just because I'm from Berlin and this is more stuff Bavarians would do. But I was in Pittsburgh so different rules. Came here for brunch on a Sunday because of an invite. You're not a member? Sorry no entry. Luckily, my accent gave it away and apparently Germans are always welcome. They serve proper Bavarian food - Wurst, Bacon (? ), Red Cabbage, fried potatoes - pretty solid. You can also get omelettes together with a Krug of German beer. Is that what we Germans do for breakfast back home? Maybe in the Bavarian woods, I'm not sure, but it is definitely something. The interior is quite unique - imagine Oktoberfest in 1935 and you get the idea. Fun fact: not everyone in there speaks German and they have waitresses that work there for over a decade. I do, however, appreciate that this Pittsburgh institution is around for more than 100 years and hope they'll stick around for a while. Maybe, in another 100 years, even the neighborhood won't look as dodgy as it looks right now.

The food was fresh, tasty and well prepared. I especially liked the salad bar, which had a great selection of fresh vegetables, fruits and nuts. There were plenty of vegetarian and vegan options, which made me feel included and happy to have so many choices. The desserts were impressive, with a variety of cakes, pies and other sweets that looked almost too good to eat. On my second visit, I was happy to see that the quality of the food and service had not dropped. The staff was friendly and attentive, refilling my glass quickly and checking in to see how everything was going. The dining room was clean and well organized, with comfortable chairs and plenty of space between the tables. The atmosphere was lively but not overwhelming, making it a great place for a casual lunch or dinner. I also appreciated the attention to detail in the decor. I would definitely recommend People's to anyone looking for a great place to eat in the area. The prices are reasonable, the service is excellent and the food is consistently delicious. I'm looking forward to my next visit!

We took some friends who are vegetarians out to a Chinese restaurant we like. They were skeptical because there aren't many vegetarian options on the menu, only one in fact, a spicy tofu dish. Our friends were right to be skeptical because the tofu was too spicy for one of them. The other had an egg foo yung. I ordered the sesame chicken, which the server said was the most popular dish. He brought a big bowl of steaming white rice for the three of us to share.We started with spring rolls, which were deep-fried to a golden brown and served with the typical dipping sauce. They were delicious. Our entrees also came out fairly quickly. My sesame chicken was tasty, but the breading was a little thick. The white rice was fluffy and moist. Our friend said that it was cooked perfectly. The egg foo yung was light and fluffy with plenty of vegetables. The tofu was nicely fried.Our server was very attentive and friendly. He kept our water glasses full and even brought us more white rice when we asked.Overall, our experience was good. The service was great, and the spring rolls, sesame chicken and white rice were delicious. However, I wouldn't recommend this restaurant to vegetarians since there are so few options.

I pretty much got my dad obsessed with pho when my family came out to California for my graduation in April. He had never tried it before, but after the first bowl, he was hooked. We ended up going to a different pho restaurant every day for a week straight. My mom was a bit skeptical at first, but even she couldn't deny the delicious flavors and savory broth. My sister, who's a picky eater, even tried it and ended up loving it. It was a great bonding experience for all of us, and we still talk about those meals to this day.The best part about pho is how customizable it is. You can add whatever toppings you like, from bean sprouts and lime wedges to fresh herbs and chili sauce. My dad liked to add a ton of Sriracha to his, while my mom preferred a more subtle approach with just a squeeze of lime. I liked to load up on the fresh herbs, like basil and cilantro, to give it a fresh and fragrant flavor. My sister liked to keep it simple with just a sprinkle of bean sprouts and a drizzle of hoisin sauce.Another great thing about pho is how versatile it is. You can have it for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, and it's always satisfying. My family and I would often have it for lunch after a long morning of exploring the city. It was a great way to refuel and recharge for the rest of the day. And the best part? It's usually pretty affordable, so it's a great option for budget-conscious travelers like us.I'm so glad I got to share my love of pho with my family during our trip. It's a memory that I'll always cherish, and I can't wait to go back and try more pho restaurants in the future. If you haven't tried it yet, I highly recommend giving it a shot. You might just find yourself obsessed like my dad!

so I've eaten here a few times now, and I feel it's finally time for a review. I must say, this place is a hidden gem! The noodles are perfectly cooked and the sauce is just the right balance of sweet, sour, and spicy. Another must-try is the Green Curry - it's packed with flavor and has a nice kick to it. For those who prefer something a little milder, the Massaman Curry is a great option. It's creamy and flavorful, with a touch of sweetness. No matter what you choose, you're sure to enjoy your meal here. The prices are also very reasonable, making it a great option for a casual meal out with friends or family. Overall, I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a delicious and authentic Thai food experience. You won't be disappointed!

I like BBQ king for being all of those things, but the food is mediocre. BBQ was not smoky at all. No flavor. I don't think it's even really smoked. I am no connoisseur, but I know this isn't good Q. Regular fried chicken is good. The fried chicken dipped in BBQ is nice. Something new, not my cup of tea, but if I grew up on it, I surely would understand. Service and Cheeseburgers are good though. For the most part, the food is good, and they have been consistent. One item I like about their menu is the "Indo-Chinese" section. My two complaints: n1) something always seems to get miscommunicated to the kitchen regarding the spiciness of the dish. Not too hot--_too mild_! This has been verified when I look at my cheque--they list the spiciness requested next to the dish. nn2) While quick to refill water, if you order any other beverage, it gets forgotten. 5 stars, actually. Would be 4 but I had to knock off half a star because of the parking situation. The lot sucks, I used to work at Whole Foods and I can not recall how many times I almost got hit by a car when retrieving carts. I am one of the lucky ones, I know of a few people who weren't so lucky. I'm a huge fan of the salad and hot bar - not a fan of the price though. To be fair, I can only blame myself for ending up with an $11 salad (but everything is so good and actually fresh I can't stop myself from piling it on). The prepared sandwich's are pretty awesome too and if you go after 9p, they are buy 1 get 1. I now work with a lot of children on special diets and I have no problem finding lots of GFCF treats for them here. Groceries range from expensive to moderate depending on the brand. The WFM's 365 line is an excellent bargain. The bakery is full of tasty treats. You've gotta try the pumpkin pumpkin pie, though I believe it is only available around the holidays. The atmosphere was very nice and relaxed for a business dinner. We were seated promptly and the server was attentive to our needs throughout the meal. The menu offered a variety of tasty sounding options for appetizers, entrees and desserts. We started with an assortment of bruschetta, calamari and spinach artichoke dip which were all excellent. For our main courses we ordered the chicken piccata, salmon and New York strip steak. Everything was cooked perfectly and the flavors were vibrant. My clients especially loved the steak which they said was one of the best they've had. Towards the end of the meal we had some great conversations and everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves. I would definitely come back here for both personal and professional dining experiences. The rest of the night went smoothly and we closed an important deal. A few weeks later, one of my clients contacted me and said they wanted to meet at the same restaurant for another potential business partnership. We went back and had an equally pleasant time, sealing yet another deal over a relaxed and memorable meal. I've now made it a regular spot to take clients whenever I'm in town. The staff knows me by name now too which adds to the comfort level. Whether dining for pleasure or work purposes, this place reliably delivers quality food and a hospitable atmosphere. It's become one of my favorite local restaurants for both business and personal use any time I'm traveling through the area.

Walking into such a huge space, especially coming from the often narrow venues in San Francisco was strange. Un-nerving actually. Because Dave and Buster's is all about excess. Almost obscenely so. As far as food - their stuff is standard. Most of it is fried and as another reviewer pointed out - not very healthy. At all actually. You have to really scour the menu to find some somewhat decent viable and nutritious options. But most people don't come to Dave & Buster's for food. They come for the games. And while I've never been that into video games or arcade games - my brother and sister always have. I was apprehensive about having a good time here - but after awhile - my siblings' enthusiasm about the place became contagious and I found myself really enjoying myself. Especially once i realized that I have mad skills at Skee Ball. And proceeded to dominate. Trust.

The customer service representatives I spoke with were rude and dismissive. It is big. Very big. Too big, almost. It is so easy to get lost in this HUGE multi-level place. The signage and directions for conventions I have attended have been poor. I've spent a lot of time wandering around trying to figure out which halls, etc. There is a nice selection of different little restaurant places inside but - Skip Them! The best thing about this place is its location on College Street. There are so many exceptional restaurants within just a few blocks. And, downtown Charlotte is lovely! So many fountains, open areas, gardens to visit. My other BIG complaint about this place.. .. charging too much for Wi-Fi packages. Look, stop being cheap. Business and trade groups are already paying you huge $$$ for the place and services. Throw in wireless. Why is this such a hassel? Because in many places, something about the building seems to really disrupt wireless data signals to your 3G/4G phone. So, if you're planning on tethering with you cell phone to get wireless, you have to be up in the open common areas to keep from being dropped. Lame. Don't even try to get it in the big exhibition hall.

The beds here are ROCKS! It felt like I was sleeping on a box spring instead of a mattress and a really had and painful one at that. When we "got up" in the morning (that phrase in quotations as it implies we had a good night's sleep, which we didn't) my husband pointed out that the side of the mattress was slumping, so it was probably very old. Definitely not Marriott standard. Wireless internet was slow, but a CAT5 was provided in the room for laptops that got internet up to speed just fine. Breakfast when I had it was good. Perhaps previous reviewer came down late? A little on the crowded side, but the biscuits were delicious. All in all, the stay was great except for the beds, but unfortunately that's a HUGE thing that needs to be good when you're staying at a hotel. Sorry guys.

Nickle and dime you. Not a fan. Hubs went shopping for some sparkle and shine for me. He did very well! He mentioned that once he picked out the earrings he was told that there is an extra charge for the earring posts. What?! How do the posts not come with the earrings (especially when you throw down a lot of Benjamins to begin with)? That is just crazy. Next, the necklace he gave me as a gift was a tad too long. So I went in and had the receipt and asked to exchange the chain for a shorter one. The employee then proceeded to tell me that I would have to drop it off, they would have it the following day, and there would be a charge to shorten it. What?! Paying for a gift given to you is nuts. That's most of a jeweler's business.. . sweethearts buying for their sweetheart as a surprise and they won't always get the size right. In any case, thankfully the two employees that my husband worked with when he was in and the other that helped me when I was there worked with us to comp the earring posts and got my chain corrected that same moment at no charge. The employees and jewelry itself saved this review from being a 1 star. Needless to say, after these recent experiences I'm even more inclined to take my business to the local mom & pops jewelers. I don't appreciate the extra fees and hassle that seems to be part of the process with this company. Jared's has gotten too big and too corporate and lost its focus on building relationships and loyalty with customers. I don't remember Jared's being like this in the past, but I heard they purchased Zales and a lot has changed. Too bad, Jared's. Your jewelry is gorgeous and employees are kind, but the shopping experience you create for the buyer has lost its charm and is now tainted in my book.

The gumbo tasted like the roux had burned and there was no salt whatsoever. I ordered the blackened chicken to be safe thinking "no one can mess up blackened chicken".. .. . I was wrong. None of the food (including the blackened chicken) were seasoned with salt and pepper. This was the most bland, overpriced food I'd ever had in the city. I ordered my toddler the chicken strip little gators meal. The fries were the best thing out of the entire meal. The service was as also dry and not very friendly or inviting from the hostess to the waiter, Brandon. Geez, I know it's a Tuesday night (we arrived at 5: 30) but at least show some enthusiasm as I arrive to spend a whopping $123 (4 entrees, 4 alcoholic bevs, 1 kids meal) on a below average meal. It would've been more had we been charged for the uneaten cup of gumbo.

I've tried this place twice thinking that I somehow had a "lemon" of a burger the first time. And then returned a few months later. Nope. The smoked flavor is okay and the meat seems fresh, but where the hell is the flavor? I can go as far as saying that I don't believe that they even season the burger with salt and pepper. If I closed my eyes, it is possible that I wouldn't even know that it was a hamburger. That is embarrassing. Maybe if you're used to eating 99 cent burgers, Sysco "meat, " or at chain restaurants, then you would find this to be "amazing. " I've had some of the best burgers at many cities in the US and this is an embarrassment to Pittsburgh. Go to BRGR if you want a tasty burger near Bloomfield. On the other end of the spectrum were the sides. The sides were classics, but definitely above average, especially the home fries. I would consider a 1 star rating if it weren't for them. Additionally, the place is overly crowded and had a long wait during the weekend. The decor is old school and seems satisfied in it's current state. Just like the food itself. File this one under Legacy restaurant still living on it's past accolades.

Say it with me now - Krispy Kreme Bread Pudding. What sounds like a dessert catastrophe is actually a sweet dream in your mouth. Despite appearances, this creation works surprisingly well with the salty-sweet doughnuts melding smoothly into the custard. My first bite was apprehensive but I was won over by the brilliant balance of flavors. The softer texture of the bread pudding complements the crunchier bits of Krispy Kreme throughout. While it may seem like overkill on the sugar, the pudding is rich without being cloying. A scoop of vanilla ice cream on the side cuts through the richness. This indulgent dish would be the star attraction of any breakfast or brunch spread. It's a hearty portion that satisfies both a sweet tooth and those looking for something more robust to start their day. Customers rave about how the pudding captures all the best qualities of a Krispy Kreme without needing to eat a half dozen on its own. The doughnuts soak up the custard without losing their signature ring shape. No doughnut goes to waste as even the last bites hold treasures of glazed dough hiding within the pudding. Clean plates are a common sight after this decadent dessert makes an appearance.While not for every day, the Krispy Kreme Bread Pudding deserves to be a special occasion treat. Just be sure to leave room to take leftovers home in a lovely container-it's hard to stop at one serving. This creative spin on classic bread pudding is sure to delight doughnut and dessert fans alike.

Mert's is awesome! They have such great malnutrition from all over the world. You really can't go false with any of their menu items. The portions are also very generous so you indefinitely leave feeling full. The restaurant has a very cozy ambiance that does you feel at home. All of the staff are really friendly and conscious too. Whether you go for lunch or appetizer you're guaranteed to have an enjoyable meal. They also have a charmer selection of beers, wine and cocktails. I've never had a bad savor during any of my many visits to Mert's over the years. It's obviously one of my favorite local restaurants. I highly praises checking it out if you haven't been before. You won't be outraged with anything you order from their diverse menu. Mert's succeeds at what they set out to do which is serve exquisite global dishes to their patrons. They've getting their place as a go-to neighborhood gem. I'm sure they'll continue to be a mainstay for several years to come.

The hostess seemed overwhelmed and confused, and took an incredibly long time to seat us even though the restaurant was not busy. We waited patiently, getting more and more frustrated by the minute. We finally placed our order, hoping that the food would make up for the disappointing service. Unfortunately, it did not. As we looked around, we noticed that other customers were experiencing similar problems. Some were trying to flag down their servers, and others were visibly frustrated with the whole experience. I would strongly advise anyone considering dining at Eat N Park at Waterfront to think twice. The whole experience left us feeling frustrated, dissatisfied, and determined never to return.

We arrived for our dinner reservation right on time. The hostess was very friendly and seated us promptly. The dining room had a nice upscale atmosphere without being pretentious. Our server came over immediately to greet us and discuss the menu and drink options. She had knowledgeable recommendations and answered all of our questions. I had the salmon which was well seasoned and cooked to flaky perfection. The sides were also very tasty, especially the mashed potatoes. Overall it was a very nice meal and our whole group was pleased with the experience. I would certainly come back here for future business dinners or special occasions.

BAD: n- Lots of food choices.. . burgers.. . steak.. . chicken.. . salads. Lots of drink choices.. . beers.. . wines.. . mixed drinks. Come if you want bar food, but keep your expectations low.

I give it a three, but my heart says that they deserve a two-star rating. Biggest reason is the cost. For Indian food paying $8 - 10 for a simple curry is a lot and when you add additional rice, their portion for accompanying rice is skimpy, nan bread you are into a $20+ meal and then add a beverage, esp an Indian lager, you get a bill for a couple of nearly $60. Out take-out orders are at or over $100. So we have cut down. The lunch buffet is skimpy as well. After the first rush of diners many of the courses offered are gone or near gone. There is quite a wait and it takes a number of people asking for more to roust management and the kitchen to put it out. And the selections are not much variety-wise and on the cheap end of their menu. The buffet might be dollar-cheap, but you get what you pay for: not so good. Dining in, which we thought would be a nicer experience and better portions than take-out, turned out to just be the same niggardly fare. The tastes and quality of the goods appears to have remained consistently good, but we are disappointed at the prices, lackadaisical buffet and skimpy portions.

They have a great spot on the lake but it is a pretty dumpy little fish shanty. If that is what you are looking for, you will love it. I was about to get up and leave when someone came over and said, "oh, you haven't been waited on yet? " So she then tried to help things along. nThe menu was average for sandwiches but overpriced, we felt, for entrees as we ordered the Ahi Tuna and the Bluegill. This location needs a lot of work. We went on a Friday evening before a show at the Improv. We were looking to meet up with friends and have drinks and a quick bite to eat. We never got to the food part because of the level of service that we received. We got there at about 6: 40/6: 45 so Happy Hour was wrapping up, but I would say that the bar was not even 3/4 full. There were also plenty of empty tables. This should have been our sign to run in the opposite direction. But we grabbed a table. I am not a clock watcher, so I am not sure how long it took us to get a server but it was at least 5-7 minutes. Then we got our drinks at 7: 04. The only reason that I know is because I was looking at my phone because my husband and I wanted to get some apps ordered before the end of Happy Hour. That went out the window. When our friends for there; they ordered drinks. We finished them and left. The server was nice, that is not the issue. The issue was how GROSSLY UNDERSTAFFED they were. They had two bartenders on (I think) and not nearly enough cocktail servers. The server apologized for the wait on the drinks, but explained it away with "this happens at the end of happy hour because the bar get swamped". That is a sign that you need more staff. I have never had this happen at any other bar before. Get more staff. We ended up passing up on food because we were worried about time, not the fact that we did not get HH pricing. Even though, in my opinion, they should have honored HH pricing since we were ready to order food at 7: 50/7: 55. We ended up going to the Improv and got food there. Bar Louie lost a great deal of my money because their lack of staffing and they will never get our Pittsburgh business again or our friends who live there.

North Carolina's laws on serving alcohol make it nearly impossible to just open a "club", so you see a lot of these in Charlotte, especially downtown. The staff is super friendly and doesn't hassle you for walking in and realizing "Saturday night" hasn't started yet because the dining patrons still haven't cleared out. So don't be afraid to check it at 11pm and then come back again at midnight or 1 if it's still slow. I've never been here to eat but it's a great place to stop in for a late night weekend drink to see what's going on. People dress nice and behave well. So you can actually get an expensive drink and not worry about someone elbowing it across the room. There's plenty of seating on both the first and second floors and they have a respectable, if predictable, Scotch selection that helps me keep them in mind when I'm downtown, so I'm sure the rest of the liquor options are pretty good. Coming from Illinois where you can buy booze at grocery stores, it's depressing to walk into a bar in Charlotte and only have one or two choices. Cosmos expands the horizons and I appreciate that.

Well, except for the lobster bisque, which was a bit too tomato-ey and not enough lobster taste. nThey gladly exchanged it for two of us, and brought us a wonderful warm goat cheese salad. Thus, I decided to test out Umi based on the good reviews I found on the web. Sadly, I was grossly disappointed. The interior decor is pretentious (large water fountain in the middle of the dining room and "Japanese style" paintings and decorations throughout) and dark (who likes eating in a place where you can barely see your food? ). The sushi was okay at best, but the quality of the fish certainly does not even come close to Chaya's. The dishes were overpriced for the quality of the food, basically you'd be paying for the fake ambiance. I guess the waiter was nice in that he tried to explain our dishes, but frankly he does not know too much. This is one of those Americanized versions of an Asian restaurant and not authentic (key indicator: most of the patrons were not Asian). It was nothing that would make me want to come back.

The rooms in the maternity ward were very spacious and clean. The food for mothers was adequate but could be improved with more nutritious choices. All the nurses and doctors I interacted with were very caring, knowledgeable, and made the birthing process as smooth as possible. The only downside was that the wifi signal was weak and it was difficult for visitors to stay connected. It was great that the ward allowed fathers and partners to stay overnight to support the mothers. The view out the windows was a cement wall, so it was depressing to look outside. However, I was very pleased with my experience giving birth and staying in the maternity ward. After a few days, I was eager to go home to my own space with my new baby.

Sure there's some things that aren't as nice as you might find in other hotels, but this is a Comfort Suites, not a Hilton. The lobby area is set up nicely with a living room ambiance and the breakfast area behind it. I had a king room on the fifth floor which was better than I was expecting. Everything was clean, the furniture was in good repair, and there was a little kitchenette with a small sink, microwave, and fridge. I think the only issue I had with my room was the phone. The cable on the handset seemed to be worn out and there was some static when making a call. The biggest issue I had was with two different front desk staff. The first was a gentleman that gave me completely wrong directions on how to get to the light rail station by bus. Had I taken his directions blindly I would have ended up somewhere in South Carolina. The second issue was when I asked for a late check-out. The staff member said that I could have an extra hour and check-out at noon instead of 11. Just after 11 on the day of check-out, housekeeping came knocking at the door. They weren't told that I had asked for a late check-out and she asked if she could come back at 2: 00. It sounded like 2: 00 was a normal time for a late check-out. So is it up to the staff at the front desk to pull a time out of the air or does the hotel actually have a late check-out policy?

ahhh dor-stop. These two words encapsulated a pure pleasure when they stepped into the Pittsburgh gem. DOR-Stop is located in the center of the city. It is a simple restaurant with the charm of the old world, which can immediately bring you to the past. When you walk through the door, you will attract a warm smile and the intoxicating aroma of freshly brew coffee. Decoration with old -fashioned souvenirs and comfortable booths, creating a feeling like a home outside the home. When you settle down, you will read a wide range of menu, which is a true proof of Dor-Stop's cooking ability. From the classic breakfast staple foods such as fluffy pancakes and crispy bacon to the mouth -watering fried egg rolls, it is full of delicious fillings and can satisfy each desire. These ingredients are purchased locally, showing the restaurant's commitment to quality and support for local farmers. The remaining dishes are their iconic Pittsburgh -style French toast. The thick bread is generously applied to the eggs, cinnamon and a trace of vanilla paradise -like mixture, and then bake it perfectly. The result is a masterpiece of golden brown, which has achieved a perfect balance between the soft and seductive tightening of the pillow. There is a group of cream butter and a small rain maple syrup. It is a paradise -like symphony that will make your taste buds sing. The venue was nice enough, with plenty of space for the event. However, the food was somewhat lacking. The appetizers were small and not very flavorsome. For the main course, I had the chicken which was on the dry side. The sides were average at best - the mashed potatoes seemed uninspiring. Service was slow, it took quite a while to get our drinks refilled. The organizers did a good job putting on the fundraiser overall. It was for a worthy cause, though the food left something to be desired. I'm sure they focused more on the event planning than the culinary aspects. In the future, I'd suggest they partner with a caterer that can provide higher quality dishes. While the intentions were good, they may raise more money with better food to keep guests satisfied.

All floors are packed full of great fun for kids, and make this place a nice way to spend a lazy Saturday with your turbo-charged little one - just be sure you are well-rested before you go! The only place that was a bit much was the water zone, but that's to be expected whenever you join a young child and lots of splashy water fun. Buon Giorno is a charming little Italian restaurant that has become my go-to spot during lunch breaks. The proximity to my workplace is undoubtedly a significant fastor in my frequent visits, but it's the delicious food and warm ambiance that keep me coming back for more. Steps inside, you are greeted with a friendly smile from the staff, who are always attentive and eager to assist. The restaurant's comfy interior is adorned with rustic Italian decor, creating a welcoming and relaxed atmosphere that instantly transports you to the streets of Rome. The menu at Buon Giorno offers a variety of mouthwatering options, ranging from classic pasta dishes to delectable pizzas. Somebody of my personal favorites is their signature Margherita pizza, made with a thin and crispy crust, fresh tomato sauce, and the perfect blend of mozzarella and basil. Their pasta dishes are equally impressive, with gene rous portions and rich, flavorful sauces that leave you craving more. The Carbonara, in particular, stands out with its creamy sauce and perfectly cooked pancetta. It's a dish that never fals to satisfy my cravings for a comforting Italian meal. What I appreciate most about Buon Giorno is the attention to detail in their ingredients. They source their produce locally, guaranteeing that each dish is made with the freshest and highest-quality ingredients available. Another standout aspect of the restaurant is their exceptional wine selecion. The knowledgeable staff will gladly recommend the perfect wine matchmaking to complement your meal, elevating the lunch experience to new heights. Service at Buon Giorno is consistently excellent. The waitstaff is attentive, and dishes arrive promptly, allowing for a leisurely lunch without feeling rushed. De restaurant also offers efficient takeout and delivery services for those busier days when enjoying a dinner in-house isn't possible.

Page's Dairy Mart has been a local staple for as long as I can remember. The atmosphere is nostalgic, taking you back to a simpler time. Walking through the door feels like stepping into a time capsule of classic ice cream parlors. The friendly service is always a delight, and the staff treats you like family. I usually go for their signature sundae, the Page's Special, which is a delightful combination of creamy vanilla ice cream, rich hot fudge, and a generous topping of whipped cream and nuts. It never fails to satisfy my sweet tooth. The ice cream itself is unbelievably creamy and flavorful, and they have a wide array of flavors to choose from. Whether you're in the mood for a classic like chocolate or vanilla or feeling adventurous and want to try something like cookies and cream or mint chocolate chip, they have you covered. The portions are generous, and prices are quite reasonable. I love that they use quality ingredients, and you can taste the difference. If you're ever in the area, don't miss the chance to visit Page's Dairy Mart-it's a true gem that has stood the test of time.

Lemon Grass Thai Cuisine exceeded our expectations with its pleasant ambiance, excellent service, and delectable dishes. The modern decor and soft lighting created a warm and inviting atmosphere, while our server's friendly and attentive demeanor made us feel welcome and well-cared for. The menu offered a diverse selection of traditional Thai fare and innovative creations, which promised a delightful culinary experience.We began our meal with the flavorful and savory Tom Yum soup, generously portioned with succulent shrimp and fragrant herbs. For our main courses, we opted for the Green Curry with chicken and the Pad Thai with shrimp. The dishes were expertly prepared and presented, showcasing a focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients. The green curry struck a perfect balance between spicy and sweet notes, while the Pad Thai boasted a delightful texture, subtly sweetened by the tamarind sauce. We also ordered a side of fluffy and well-seasoned steamed rice, which complemented our dishes perfectly.The food at Lemon Grass was not only delicious but also well-executed, with generous portions and reasonable prices. The restaurant's attention to detail and commitment to quality made for a memorable dining experience. We would definitely recommend Lemon Grass to anyone seeking excellent Thai cuisine in a welcoming atmosphere.

Most other passengers with extended layovers also seemed restless. By the time I reached my gate, I was eager to depart for my final destination. Should I have another layover there in the future, I will be sure to arrive prepared with distracting pursuits beyond what the airport can offer. My, how time can change things. We used to go to The Pasta Shop frequently when my children were young. They have since grown up and moved out of the house. We still make it a point to go there at least once a month or so. The food is good and plentiful and the price is very affordable. The service is always good and we never have to wait long for our food to arrive, even when the restaurant is busy. The owner and his wife are very friendly and always make you feel welcome. They have been in business for over 25 years and it is obvious that they have a lot of experience in the restaurant business. They have a wide variety of Italian dishes to choose from and everything is made fresh to order. We have never had a bad meal there. We usually order a pizza, but we have also tried their pasta dishes and salads. Everything is always delicious. The pizza is thin crust and the toppings are generous. The pasta dishes are made with homemade noodles and the sauces are flavorful. The salads are fresh and crisp. The prices are very reasonable. A large pizza is only $15.00 and a pasta dish is around $10.00. They also have a lunch buffet for $7.95. The service is always good. The staff is friendly and attentive. We never have to wait long for our food to arrive, even when the restaurant is busy. The owner and his wife are always there to greet you and make sure that you have a good experience. The atmosphere is casual and family-friendly. The restaurant is decorated in a rustic Italian style with lots of dark wood and brick. There are several tables in the dining room and there is also a bar area. There is also a small patio where you can eat outside when the weather is nice. We highly recommend The Pasta Shop. It is a great place to get a delicious and affordable Italian meal. The service is great and the atmosphere is casual and family-friendly.

We sat at the bar and the female bartender was miserable. We ordered drinks and she was unhappy that we did. She spent 20 minutes sending text messages and took 3 smoke brakes in one hour while our drinks were empty. We ordered appetizers and they never came out. She actually brought us our check and we never got our food. By the way we were the only people at the bar. Finally a bus boy brought us our food after we payed. We payed before our food came because we thought our table was ready. We finally got seated by the windows. Do not sit by the windows because it was very cold. Not horrible, and definitely not spectacular, but just okay. We sat at the bar and the best part of our experience here was the bubbly bartender and the lone businessman sitting next to us. We had good conversation with them. But hey, you are reading this for a food review. So here goes: nnHot N Sour soup = pretty good. I must now admit that I have some insight into the land of PF Chang's, considering I used to be an employee at a NY location. Let's all be serious here; it's a chain, the mcdonald's of chinese food. The kitchen just pumps the meals out, and you will notice that you can have anything on the menu sitting in front of you within 5 or 6 minutes, minus the chilean seabass. They are so busy, and spit the food out so fast, it just isn't the kind of place that you are going to get a quality meal. I do recommend the mongolian beef - the mongolian sauce is excellent. Just be prepared for your hands and feet to swell given the sodium levels in this thing - out of control. I also always get the ma po tofu - this was the dish that got me into tofu in the first place, considering I never used to be able to say the word 'tofu' without gagging. It's very tasty, a bit crispy, and in a spicy/garlicky sauce with steamed broccoli. A third and final recommendation is the lemon pepper shrimp - again, the sauce is what makes this dish. If you have room for dessert, do yourself a favor and order the banana spring rolls - it's a night ender, but so worth it! I didn't find any yucky bugs in my meal, but I will say this: I've worked in plenty of restaurants, fancy and not, and I've seen them everywhere - it is inevitable that roaches will infiltrate. It's pretty unavoidable. That is disturbing though that it made it all the way onto your plate - a quality restaurant, a CLEAN restaurant, will take care of the problem right away before it gets that out of hand, and obviously PF Chang's is just not on that scale.

For a split second after walking in the door, I smelled leather shoes. That smell was quickly overpowered by the smell of cigarettes. While I didn't see any smoke, the smell was pungent. We quickly left the shoes, name, and number, and were out of there. When we returned 4 days later for the shoes, they were ready as promised. I sent my daughter in while I waited in the car. She was in and out in less than 5 minutes (a good thing). When she entered the car, the smell immediately returned. I felt sorry for her. With the windows down for about 5 minutes, the smell finally left the car. This is a great place to take your shoes but you need to be wary of the cigarette odor as it will have a lasting effect on your clothing the longer you remain in the shop. I am rating the business with 3. 5 stars but am not rounding it up to 4.

YUM YUM YUM YUM. I am so happy to have found another great restaurant in Charlotte - we had relatives staying with us last week and didn't want to take them anywhere we hadn't been yet, in case it wasn't good, and we went to Mimosa after they left - were were so upset we didn't take them here! The service was excellent - our waiter was totally on point and had a great personality, and we made excellent recommendations - I'll get to that in a minute. The atmosphere is beautiful - we ate outside, it was a gorgeous night. They have fountains right out front and large plants out on the terrace to create a nice relaxing feel. The restaurant has soft lighting and stone walls, and you could eat inside or out and it will be just as beautiful. For an appetizer we got the mussels, which were in a garlic butter white wine broth - we were scouring the broth for escaped mussels by the end of it because it was so good we devoured it. Of course, even though I say I won't, I dunked the bread in the broth - delish. For the main course I had the horseradish-crusted salmon, which was very good. If you order this be aware that while the salmon is hot, it is served over cold vegetables - cucumbers and green beans. The dish wasn't as great as I thought it would be and I had immediate food-envy when my finacee's dish was placed in front of him - piping hot scallops, shrimp and lobster over grits and brown gravy - WOW! This was so yummy that I totally dipped into his dish after I finished mine. The manager even came over to see how we were because he noticed the switch - he was so nice, and stopped over a second time just to talk once our meal was finished. I can't wait to go back here!

Arrived about 5 minutes early and were promptly seated. Our server, Shannon, was so fantastic throughout the course of the entire experience. She explained things well without belaboring the points, offered valuable pointers, and anticipated our wants and needs before we had to ask. Food was superb. Spinach artichoke cheese fondue was really delicious. We both had the seasonal strawberry caprese salad and the berries were perfectly right, mozzarella and Roma tomatoes perfect in proportion and texture, and white balsamic dressing gave great balance to flavor profile. Entree meats were fillet, marinated sirloin, pork loin, chicken, shrimp, ahi tuna, salmon, and ravioli. All were good but the absolute best part of the meal for me was the 6 doing sauces. As a condiment junkie I was in total heaven. I cooked mushrooms and stuffed them with the green goddess (which is sour cream, cream cheese, parsley, garlic, and maybe Shallots). Server also recommended mixing the teriyaki glaze and curry together and my wife loved that. Spicy cocktail was awesome on shrimp and gorgonzola was creamy and great on the beef. My wife is all about dessert so she wanted the s'mores one.. . milk chocolate, marshmallow creme flambeed with graham crumbles. We added a swirl of peanut butter in it too and it was awesome. I liked doing the blondies and pineapple and she loved the bananas, strawberries, pound cake, brownies, oreo rolled marshmallows.. . she loved it all. 2. 5 hours later we were ready to roll one another out. Come here nearly famished as you will get enough food for a village. Wonderful experience.

Drinks: Had a guy who grew up in Napa picking wines so we had a few very wonderful bottles. He was impressed with the restaurant's selection and we were with his. I also had a microbrew amber ale on draft that was wonderful. nService: Was not over or underdone. Had the flair and attention of a nice establishment without being too snobby/formal. One bottle of wine we particularly liked ran out so the manager came over to talk about similar choices. Nice touch. nAppetizers: Choosing cheese and then pairing them with membrio, walnuts and bread was lovely. The house bread with butter mixed with kalamata olives was a wonderful touch. The calamari rivaled your favorite sports bar (I expected better). The Flavors of the Mediterranean plate was good but not extraordinary. It was a nice option from standard fare for certain though. nMain meal: For the price we each agreed we didn't get anything special. Certainly the seasonal Jumbo Scallops on Risotto was good, but it wasn't lovely. Almost too salty and there was nothing tying the seafood with the grain. And I adore both items. The Bolognese was described as 'eh' and 'standard' and the two who got the pork roasts were equally so-so in review and description. nAtmosphere: A jazz trio started up as we ate and it added a light and fun atmosphere to the experience. Tables around us were in good spirits, the lighting was set just right and there was enough space to move between tables (very uncommon in SF). It was nice. Conclusion: This was a good experience but not great. I don't want to think because this is a smaller town then I'm used to, "nice" local places = lower standards. I tend more to think there were good ideas here not executed to their fullest. 3 stars is all about the food which is ultimately why we pay these prices and go to these places. I think if the ingredients were fresher and the temperatures and spices were watched closer then this could be a 5 star no matter in what city it's located.

Upstream is one of the most well-known restaurants in Charlotte. The restaurant sits along the banks of the Catawba River in Uptown Charlotte. Diners are greet with beautiful views of the flowing water and downtown skyline upon entering. Upstream offers both indoor and outdoor seating depending on preferences and weather. The menu features fresh, local element prepared with creative flair. Dishes showcase the abundance of North and South Carolina with selections like pan-seared trout and pimento cheese grits. The cuisine strikes an excellent balance of refined tastes and accessible favorites. Presentation of the nourishment is just as pleasing to eyes as it is to taste buds. Complimentary biscuits served with ap ple butter are the ideal start to any meal. For lunch or dinner, the selection of smaller plates allows for sampling multiple dishes. Upstream also has an extensive wine lists with Old and New World varietals at a variety of price points. Service is consistently attentive without being overbearing. The atmosphere remains casual de spite the upscale fare. On nice evenings, sitting otside provides a serene ambiance enhanced by live jazz. Cocktails showcase seasonal ingredients in refreshing liberations. Desserts satisfy any sweet tooth with choices like buttermilk pie and bread pudding. The restaurant has earned high praise from both locals and visitors alike for its qualiy, consistency and delightful dining experience overall. Upstream continues to evolve its menu in harmony with the changing seasons. Many users return time and again to enjoy favorites or sample new creations. Weekend brunch offers satisfying options for breaking bread with friends and family. Private dining and catering menus cater to all types of events from business lunches to wedding receptions. Those seeking a romantic night out will appreciate Upstream's sophistication without pretense.

I am the dork-ie kid from your kindergarten class, and boy, do I have a story to tell you! Remember that time we all went on that class trip to the zoo? Well, strap yourself in because this is a tale that will have you rolling on the floor laughing. Picture this: we're standing in front of the lion enclosure, and I decide it would be a brilliant idea to mimic the lion's roar. I let out the loudest, most pathetic attempt at a roar, and what happens next is pure chaos.The lion, who was probably just as amused by my feeble attempt as the rest of the class, suddenly starts pacing back and forth. Panic sets in, and the teacher is shouting for everyone to stay calm. Meanwhile, I'm frozen in place, regretting my decision to entertain everyone with my killer lion impression. The zookeeper rushes over, trying to calm down the agitated lion, and the whole ordeal ends with us being evacuated to a safer part of the zoo.That was just one of the many unforgettable moments I had from our time together in kindergarten. From the silly finger painting sessions to the dramatic naptime tantrums, it was a wild ride. I can't help but chuckle when I think back on those days. We were a bunch of tiny humans, navigating the complexities of the world, one crayon doodle at a time.Looking back, I realize how much I've grown since then. We've all come a long way from those carefree days of sharing snacks and playing tag on the playground. Life has a funny way of shaping us into the people we are today. And hey, if I hadn't been the dork-ie kid from kindergarten, I wouldn't have such entertaining stories to share with you now, would I?So here's to the moments that make us cringe, laugh, and reminisce. To the friendships formed on shaky legs and with peanut butter smeared faces. To the innocence of youth and the vibrant imagination that knew no bounds. Those were the days, my friend, and I'm grateful for every single memory, no matter how ridiculous or embarrassing they may be.

Intimidator and Cobra, and that's all you need to know. While they may lack finesse, these two rides make up for it with simpler thrills. Intimidator launches riders up the lift hill before plunging down the vertical drop at over 85 miles per clock. Per the first second of free fall, all sense of control is stripped away leaving only adrenaline. Cobra on the other hand is a tightly wound spins monstrosity that flings riders through multiple inversions at terrifying speeds. No safety equipment is needed on these machines, just a mort grip on the handles and the ability to preserve your lunch down. Waiting in line provides plenty of time to contemplating this decision, but the moment you're closed in there is no turning back. Each twist and flip pries a new scream from your throat as G forces pummel your body into the borders. Only the brief respite of the brake runs allow ragged breather before the next onslaught. Nearing the end, chivalry cling to hope of surviving the experience intact. But there are still surprises in depots, like Cobra's breathtaking diving loop where the track disappears below. Adrenaline continues to pump even after staggering elsewhere weak-kneed and begging for solid ground. The sheer intensity leaves an indelible mark, and thoughts immediately revolve to facing the beast again for another go. While their breakneck speeds, both rides operate like precise machines. Businessmen dispatch trains with military precision to keep the throughput high. Passing empty trains swoop by like ominous steel ghost hinting at the terror inside. Watching from below provides no sens of scale for how massive these titans truly are. Only from the cockpit does their full size and muscle were apparent. Even seasoned rollercoaster fans uncovered themselves humbled by Intimidator and Cobra.

$7 gets you 2 pieces of deep fried cod, fries, slaw, roll, and soda. Fish was solid - nicely done, especially for the price and speed. Detailed review: nnI'd never visited the Middleton Sport Bowl prior to today, so I wasn't quite sure what to expect. We arrived exactly at noon, parked, and made our way to the bar, where we found two seats and were promptly greeted by a bartender. We both ordered the lunch special - 2 piece deep fried cod plate with fries, slaw, tartar, dinner roll, and soda. The bartender took our order and came back with a complimentary bowl of popcorn, which was a nice surprise. Plates arrived about 10 minutes later - the fish was appropriately sized, as were the fries - no imbalance, and portions were fair. The fish itself had a flavorful beer batter that was a little thicker than what you'll typically find at most places, but it was delicious and I welcomed the extra crunch. Inside, the fish itself was a tad watery with just a hint of grease - not anything outrageous, but just enough to sense that it was there. Flavor of the fish was incredibly mild; the batter stole some of its thunder. The fries were excellent - battered-style and straight cut. I'm told the slaw and tartar were "average. " Dinner roll was hard and dry. Total lunch bill for two: $14. 64, and we were in-and-out within 35 minutes. Totally acceptable and a good lunch, all things considered. Middleton Sport Bowl = NEUTRALnnFood = 2. 75 to 3 stars (average; not bad, not spectacular)nService = 3. 5 stars (prompt and friendly)nValue = 4 stars nMISC = 3 stars (actually seemed to be a nice bowling alley/bar)nnSummary: Not a win, nor a fail. I'd go back for the fish at lunch, and will definitely be back to sample other foods - the sandwiches looked really good.

This station is definitely in need of some renovations and upgrades. The interior is quite dated and run down. The floors are dirty and some areas have stains. ! Sure, it's not a 5-star restaurant, but you can't beat the price or the food!! ! nWhy would you order french fries at a Greek restaurant?
