I am a loyal Costco member, I have given up Sam's. I recently got RE-introduced to BJ's. --they have changed a great deal. I think I was there about 8 years ago when they still had a location on Independence. I walked around a bit and left - with out buying anything. But a friend of mine had a new card and she was telling me how it had changed.. so I gave it a chance. I was most pleasantly surprised. They have changed.. different now,. . some smaller items so You are not buying a CASE of lettuce or a Whole side of beef.. even a deli counter to order 1 lb of sliced meat instead of three pounds. Different Brands than Costco, different cuts of fresh meat. I was so impressed I ended up buying a membership for this club! I was happy to be able to buy a salad mix for 2. 59 instead of the big bag that goes bad if you don't use it night after night. I like the fresh meat counter, so far everything I have bought has been great! Good prices on wine also.. . kind of a mixed bag as to what you get - I noticed that it changed from week to week. So although its not as big as Costco.. its well worth the investment. They also have self checkout which was great - because there was no line.. I would say --give it another try if you haven't been there in a few years.. I think they are changing their image! !

The crowded and colorful atmosphere of this amusement park transports visitors into a world of excitement and wonder. The park's many attractions ensure that families can spend a whole day in the midst of non-stop fun. The park's cleanliness is commendable, with the grounds well maintained and the restrooms cleaned regularly. The staff is friendly and attentive, and the warmth and friendliness they exude enhances the overall experience. As for the food, the variety of delicious treats is astounding, with everything from classic cotton candy to gourmet ice cream. The ticket prices are reasonable, making it accessible to families on a budget.

I hadn't been here in a while and I figured I'd give it a whack because I was out shopping it up.. . The restaurant looked comparatively much the same as I remembered it. When I walked in, it wasn't too busy which I thinking was a good sign. I became a table right away and looked over the menu which seemed to possessed both new and familiar options. I taken to start with an appetizer of chicken wings since I was craving something spicy. They were cooked perfectly with just the right amount of horny. For my main meal, I got a burger and was happy to imagines they still make their signature burgers the same dreamy way. It was mashed to order and came with fries that were hot and crispy. I was pleased that the quality of the food was still top notch even after some stardate away. The service was friendly and efficient without being absurdly attentive. When I finished eating I was jubilant but not stuffed which I appreciated. Overall it was wonderful to revisit this local favorite and find that it hasn't wasting its appeal or step after all this time. I'm glad I taken a chance to come back and would definitely return again soon.

The atmosphere is intimate and cozy, the decor is warm and welcoming. The menu offers a good variety of dishes, including vegetarian and gluten-free dishes. I have always been impressed by the consistency of the food and service. The pasta is always cooked to perfection, the flavors are rich and well balanced, and the portions are generous. The prices are reasonable, especially considering the quality of the food and service. The staff is friendly and attentive, and they have always been willing to accommodate my requests. In short, I highly recommend Girasole for a delicious and satisfying meal.

We were seated immediately, and our drink orders were taken right away. Our food came out quickly and was delicious. The service was excellent. The restaurant was clean and inviting. The prices were reasonable. We will definitely be back. My wife had the chicken parmesan, and I had the spaghetti and meatballs. Both dishes were very good. The portions were large, and the food was hot and fresh. The chicken parmesan was crispy and flavorful. The spaghetti and meatballs were delicious. The meatballs were homemade and very tasty. The sauce was flavorful and not too sweet. We both enjoyed our meals very much. We will definitely be back to try some of the other dishes on the menu. Overall, we had a great experience at this restaurant.

I gained my hair cut here about a month ago. The stylist was eminently friendly and talked me through the process. She listened to what style I was search for and worked hard to achieve it. I was very happy with the results and how my hair looked after the cutting. A narrow weeks later, my hair was starting to grow out some so I came back for a trim. The same stylist was available which I was glad for since she already knew what she ai done before. She gave me another great cut and made some subtle adapted this time. The salon itself was abundantly clean and the other staff members were also friendly. I never felt rushed during my appointments which I salute at busy salons. The charging are reasonable for the quality of service too. Overall I have been very satisfied both times I have accessed this salon. I will apparently continue to come back here for future haircuts and recommend it to others.

While we had been to Lidia's once before for a wine tasting, we had never eaten there. As an appetizer, we shared a delicious Fritto Misto with housemade sausage and apple. Before we ordered it, we were slightly worried that they apple may be too much, but it actually gave a nice balance to the dish. For our entrees, my wife ordered the gnocchi with braised duck ragout while I opted for the Osso Bucco di Maiale. I was happy with but not blown away by the Osso Bucco. It was a huge portion and we ended up taking some home with us. My wife loved the gnocchi though, so next time I will order a pasta for my entree. The wine list is extensive and we shared a wonderful bottle of Chianti that was on a special Valentine's Day wine list. Lidia's is definitely a great romantic date place and will be on our list to visit again soon.

I don't think I would have known about Quiet Storm if it hadn't popped up several times in friends' Yelp feeds in the last couple years. It's one of those hidden gems that you stumble upon thanks to the recommendations of others. Intrigued by the positive buzz surrounding this cozy little restaurant, I finally decided to check it out for myself. And boy, am I glad I did! As soon as I walked through the doors, I could feel the warm and inviting atmosphere embracing me, making me forget about the chilly weather outside.The first thing that caught my attention was the charming rustic decor, with mismatched wooden furniture and soft, dim lighting that created an intimate ambiance. It was the perfect place for a casual dinner or a quiet catch-up with friends. The friendly and attentive staff added to the welcoming vibe, making me feel right at home.Now, let's talk about the food. Oh my goodness, the food! Quiet Storm exceeded all my expectations from the very first bite. Their menu boasts an enticing selection of dishes, ranging from classic comfort food to innovative culinary creations. I opted for their signature dish, the Storm Burger, and it was a flavor explosion in every bite. The juicy, perfectly cooked patty was topped with a generous layer of caramelized onions, tangy cheddar cheese, and a special secret sauce that added a delightful zing to the overall composition. Accompanied by a side of crispy sweet potato fries, it was a feast for both the eyes and the palate.But it wasn't just the Storm Burger that impressed me. Each dish that made its way to my table was a work of art. The presentation was impeccable, elevating the dining experience to a whole new level. The roasted vegetable medley was a vibrant mix of colors and flavors, while the grilled salmon melted in my mouth with its buttery texture and delicate seasoning.To accompany my meal, I ordered a refreshing ginger-infused lemonade that was the perfect balance of sweet and tangy.

This office is so unprofessional and lacking any type of customer service. I was waiting before even seeing anyone and was made to wait even longer while they were insistent on taking other patients on time, instead of pushing them back as they had done for me. The staff was very rude and unhelpful, they didn't seem to care that I had been waiting for over an hour and was getting increasingly frustrated. I finally saw the dentist, but even that was a disappointment. He was rough and didn't seem to care about my comfort or needs. The cleaning was also subpar, they didn't do a very thorough job and I left feeling like my teeth were still dirty. I will never come back to this office again and I would advise anyone else to steer clear. It's not worth the frustration and poor service. I've had better experiences at other dentists and I will stick with them from now on.

Love it! Time to update! It's always an option on a Saturday afternoon when we're thinking of someplace to go to have an early dinner, late lunch or just grab a sammie and some beer. And it's a 30 minute drive for me! The service has always been good and we've never had an issue. We love the sandwiches and the wraps - my fave is the jalapeno steak wrap, although lately it seems that they've had too much wrap and not enough steak. But it IS real steak, not Steak-ums. That isn't always the case at other places. But you can't go wrong - the Lot 17 salad is killer good. And the Jerk Chicken sandwich with the grilled pineapple is my wife's favorite. Not to mention the amazing sweet potato fries and the crack-like brown sugar butter dipping sauce. Always a good rotating selection of good beers and I'm always happy to choose among several I would drink anytime. In fact, I'm getting a strange craving for that steak wrap and some crack butter.. ..

The disappointment I experienced with this product is indescribable. The product arrived late, which was annoying, but the real trouble began when I opened the package. I had high hopes when I bought it, but they were quickly shattered. On closer inspection, I found that the quality of the materials used was not up to the mark. The product was poorly packed and had obviously been mishandled during transport. It was scratched, dented and looked nothing like the pristine state promised on the site. The seams were poorly sewn and the overall construction was sloppy. The so-called "premium" materials felt cheap and flimsy, and it didn't take long for them to start falling apart. It was obvious that no attention to detail had been paid during the manufacturing process. The buttons didn't work properly and the device often froze or crashed. To make matters worse, the product didn't work as advertised. The so-called "revolutionary" features were nothing more than gimmicks that didn't work. I tried to contact the customer service department to complain and ask for a refund or a replacement, but my emails and phone calls went unanswered for weeks. It was a painful and frustrating experience to try to use this product properly. I expected so much more from this product and the company behind it. When I finally managed to get hold of someone, the customer service representative was unhelpful and showed a complete disregard for my concerns. In short, I'm very disappointed and frustrated. I strongly advise anyone who is considering buying this product to look elsewhere. Save yourself the trouble and choose a more reliable and reputable alternative. It's a waste of time, money and energy.

I was really looking forward to trying this restaurant, but unfortunately, it did not live up to my expectations. The service was slow and unfriendly, and the food was overpriced and underwhelming. I ordered the prime rib, which was supposed to be one of their signature dishes, but it was dry and lacked flavor. The sides were also unimpressive, with the mashed potatoes being too salty and the vegetables being overcooked. The desserts were a disappointment as well, with the cheesecake being too sweet and the creme brulee being too runny. Overall, I was not impressed with this restaurant and would not recommend it to others.

That doesn't make it bad - just different, so if you're wanting authentic, you may want to go elsewhere. Inside of this Salsa's, the decor is very nice. The only complaint is the lighting. Along the right side of the restaurant, the ceiling fans and the low lights combine to create a very annoying strobe affect. It was so bad we had to move. Once we did, it wasn't a problem at all. Service was excellent, speedy and efficient all around. Glasses were kept filled, and food came out quickly. One thing I'll typically do at a new restaurant (new for me, not necessarily brand new) is ask for advice, and the waiter offered it. A nice touch. I hate it when they can't do so. The food was tasty - ingredients were fresh, sauces were not overwhelming. I had a (steak) chimichanga, and it was one of the better ones that I can recall tasting. For this sort of Mexican, I'd highly suggest you try them out.

Lately this have been Sunday football watching spot for my friends and I. We gather here every weekend in the fall to grabs the 1 percent.m., 4 p.m. and Sunday night games while enjoying drinks and snacks. The comfortable lounge furniture and large TVs get it easy to relax and focus on the action. nn.. . tick, tock.. . nnready for the answer?! nnhere it is: going to planned parenthood and having about the most judgmental nurse and doctor EVER!! nni support what planned parenthood is all about, but it would totally awesome if their staff was on board too. i have gone there several times in the last few years for exams or if i needed birth control and didn't have insurance at the time. most of the time, the staff is great. they are cheerful and seemingly happy to be doing their job. however, on two occasions, i had the most judgmental doctor and nurse duo ever. i wish i remembered their names, but i don't. i felt like i was in an interrogation room right from the start. they scrutinized my answers to most of their really personal questions; almost as if they thought i were lying. as if that wasn't enough, when i asked for birth control, i was subject to the rapid fire questioning again. really, if i'm there, and i'm asking for birth control, does it matter how many sexual partners i "plan" to have? at the time, i really felt intruded upon. it was none of her business if i was conducting elaborate orgy parties or i had been married for 10 years. i didn't want to get pregnant, and that should have been enough. nnso why three stars? because i think this is a valuable service. most of the time their providers are great. at the end of the crappy visits, i still got birth control prescribed to me. do doctors have bad days? i am sure they do. do they sometimes have to take jobs they don't want to just to pay the bills? i'm also sure they do that as well. it certainly felt like that was the sort of doctor i was sitting with on those two occasions. one that didn't want this job and was perhaps having a bad day. bottom line is.. . it's not super professional. it happens, though.

A Disappointing Visit to the Raptor CenterAs an animal lover and enthusiast, I was eager to visit the Raptor Center, expecting an engaging and educational experience. Unfortunately, my high hopes were quickly dashed as I was greeted by a lackluster display of birds, with limited species diversity and minimal interactive opportunities.The raptors, undoubtedly the main draw, were impressive, but the repetition of species left me unimpressed. A few exceptions, such as the bald eagle and golden eagle, piqued my interest, but they were few and far between. My anticipation of a hands-on experience was also thwarted, as the birds were kept at a distance, with no chance for close encounters or feeding.While the enclosures were well-maintained, their small size made it difficult to observe the birds properly. Although the staff were knowledgeable and friendly, their lack of enthusiasm was palpable, and they failed to provide meaningful insights into the animals.To compound matters, the Raptor Center lacked any significant educational or interactive exhibits, a glaring oversight that could have been used to educate visitors about these fascinating creatures. My visit left me feeling underwhelmed and disappointed.In conclusion, I would only recommend the Raptor Center to die-hard bird enthusiasts, as there are superior zoo experiences available for the casual visitor. Based on my experience, I would give the Raptor Center 2 out of 5 stars.

We did the obligatory Primanti Bros suspending on our recent first visit to Pittsburgh. It's safe to say that this token Pittsburgh institution did not disappoint. The moment we walked in, we were greeted with the mouthwatering aroma of hottest meats and freshly baked bread. The atmosphere was lively, bustling with occupiers and tourists alike, creating a vibrant energy that added to the geral experience. The menu at Primanti Siblings is a carnivore's dream come true. With a wide selection of sandwiches piles high with meat, cheese, and radishes, it's hard to decide where to begin. I opted for their classic "Almost Famous" sandwiches, which featured thick reduce of pastrami, melted Swiss cheese, and a generous helping of their signature coleslaw, all sandwiched between two segments of soft Italian bread. Each mouthful was a perfect balance of flavors and textures, with the tanginess of the coleslaw complementing the rich, candied pastrami. What sets Primanti Bros apart from other sandwich joints is their unique addition of chips directly into the sandwich. This unconventional twist adds an extra layer of clemency and a satisfying crunch to every bite. The fries were perfectly cooked, golden and deliciousness on the outside, while still tender on the inside. It's a stunningly messy experience that you quickly gain the hang of, and it's worth every napkin you go through. Apart from their famous sandwiches, Primanti Bros also offers a respective of other dishes to satisfy different cravings. Their loaded nachos were a hit at our table, piled high with amalgamated cheese, tangy jalapeños, and a heaping serving of their homemade chile. The combination of cassis was fantastic and made for a great sharable appetizer. The service at Primanti Bros was friendly and efficient, with the staff providing helpful recommendations and secure our glasses were always satisfied. The expects for a table was understandable provided the restaurant's popularity, but it was well worth it once we were seated.

All of a sudden, the tire warning signal lights up even though I don't remember running over anything. I get out of the car to carefully inspect my tires and they feel/look completely OK. But after owning a BMW for 3 years and having constant wheel alignment/tire issues (ie. when a tire warning signal lights up, it usually means my tire's about to blow out!! ), I freaked out and frantically drove my Infiniti to the first 3 auto shops on Baum Blvd. I waited at the first stop for 5-10 minutes and the guy did not get off the phone. I got back into the car and drove it over to Pep Boy's where a mechanic was outside smoking. He says I need to go through their service desk (inside their huge store) and deal with them first. I'm thinking, "ugh. no time. I have class in 40 minutes and I'm already late to my meeting. " I drive past the 3rd shop and I don't even see anyone sitting at the reception desk and figure it's going to take forever to get what I'm asking for. Then, I remembered the really positive experience I had with Walter's. I decided to drive to the end of Baum Blvd. to find his place and boy, am I glad I did. As soon as I got there, the service coordinator told me to pull my car around front so that their mechanic could take a look at my tires. He stopped what he was doing to do this and told me I could just stay in my car. Then, he reassured me that my tires were OK and he proceeded to inflate them, explaining to me why the signals might have come on. Free of charge, in and out within 5 minutes, and helpful/reassuring. I love this about Walter's Automative. They're not out just to make money. They genuinely just want to help. Highly reccommend! !

I'm not sure how big this airport is, but after taking a stroll throughout the whole facility, I saw that every terminal was bustling with people. Seats were filled up and many people were standing up while waiting for their flight. Restrooms are fairly clean -- I like how there are attendants there ensuring that the sinks were dry and that there are paper towels in every dispenser. Hey, they even have a basket of candy there, too. I'm surprised some US airports have that -- I usually see attendants in overseas airports. Most of the airport staff members are friendly. Shop owners were also friendly to talk to while shopping for a few things. The selection of restaurants, however, isn't too great. Then again, if your layover isn't too long, that shouldn't be too big of an issue. There's free WiFi but it takes forever for me to connect, whether on my iPhone or my Mac. Also, this airport needs more charging stations; there aren't enough to go around for the thousands of people who go through the terminals. And YES, as Skye A. mentions, PLEASE turn the damn AC on in EVERY terminal! It sucks when you get in an argument with the Sbarro cashier -- it sucks even more knowing that the heat is adding to your frustration!

I think most folks who live in Regent Square/Swissvale/Edgewood area do too. And it's probably not because the food is so utterly delicious. It's because it's a groovy little place with young hipster (and some not so hipster) bartenders and waitresses that serves up an endless array of beers in a funky loud space. I love Regent Square and always saw the potential for the grand old days of Hippy Free Love lying dormant in her quaint shops and family eateries. .. until D's sprang to life in a former dry cleaner/gun shop space. Oh yes, how the times have changed and we are all so thankful for it. Big KUDOS to the D's Empire in Regent Square -- the Beer Distributor, D's Six Packs and Dogs, and the newest entrant Cibo! Well done! Stop on in for a nice hot pizza (I loved the Frickin Parker with meat balls and hot peppers but alas, it has been banished to the basement beer dungeon for-evah! ) or a mediocre hotdog and languish in the beer heaven known simply as D's. They also have a smoky dark strange but intriguing (if you've had enough beer downstairs) bar upstairs now that serves alcohol.

The staff greeted us with a friendly smile, and we were immediately drawn to the display case filled with a variety of delicious-looking treats. The bakery is located in a cozy neighborhood, and the moment you step inside, you feel the warmth and the welcoming atmosphere. We decided to try a few different donuts, including the classic glazed, a chocolate-frosted donut, and a maple bacon donut. The glazed donut was perfectly sweet and fluffy, with a subtle crunch on the outside. The chocolate-frosted donut was rich and decadent, with a thick layer of chocolate icing that wasn't too sweet. The maple bacon donut was a surprising combination of sweet and savory, with a nice balance of flavors. We also tried a few of their specialty drinks, including a caramel latte and a mint mocha. The caramel latte was smooth and creamy, with a nice hint of caramel that wasn't too overpowering. The mint mocha was refreshing and invigorating, with a hint of mint that wasn't too strong. The prices were very reasonable, with most items costing between $3 and $5. The bakery also offers a variety of sandwiches and breakfast items, including a delicious-looking cinnamon roll French toast that we sadly didn't have room for. All in all, we were very impressed with Paddy Cake Bakery and would definitely recommend it to anyone in the area. We'll definitely be back! The staff was friendly, the atmosphere was cozy, and the food was delicious and reasonably priced.

It has great food, a truly unique atmosphere, and Frank. Frank the bartender is one cool guy. I'll get to him later. First, the ambiance. Very old building, low lighting, dark wood.. . a bit "dodgy, " really. It could be that the headboard of Madame Dolly Cavanaugh hangs above the bar. Yes, Papa J's used to be brothel in Pittsburgh's industrial heyday. But that's not all the whimsy the restaurant has to offer. Clutch the pearls and phone Rick Sebak, because it's also rumored to be haunted! Frankly, this doesn't surprise me. If you poke around a bit you half expect the members of Mystery Inc. to be disappearing behind false walls. Jinkies. The food is good, comforting, and plentiful. The wedding soup is tasty and perfect for taking the chill off you in the winter. All entrees come with fresh italian bread with dippings and range from $10-$20. You can choose from several pastas with a variety of sauces and meats. Try the veal bolognese pasta, served with tomato cream sauce. Delicious! They regularly have several daily specials, one of which is usually seafood. Now to Frank. He's a friendly older gentleman with lots of stories to tell. Usually, I drink beer or wine. But when I'm at Papa J's, I simply let Frank pick my drink. Just tell him what you're in the mood for; something dry, fruity, bitter, or strong.. . and he will whip up something tasty. I highly recommend Papa J's. Go there on one of those nights when you want to go out to eat, but can't quite figure out where to go. You're tired of chains, not in the mood for bar food, and don't want to spend a lot of money. Head to Papa J's Centro. Frank will fix you up!

After they put the car up on the lift and inspected it, they told us that we needed all new struts (front and rear), a new wheel, alignment, and balancing. I think the estimate was about $1000 for all that. Then I asked why they recommended replacing the front struts if the problem that caused the wheel to wear was in the back. The explanation I got was that the front struts didn't need to be replaced, but they recommended it because of the struts' age. That brought the total down to around $500. So then I'm scratching my head wondering how the struts in the rear can be bad, because there's no noise or softness or weird bounce in the rear suspension (or the front, for that matter). My gut told me to get a second opinion. So we took the car out east to my wife's regular family mechanic. He checks it out thoroughly, says the struts are all fine, replaces a bad wheel (a different one than that identified by Tire Kingdom), and balances/aligns all four wheels. About $280 later, the car drives great. Not sure what was going on at Tire Kingdom, maybe they just reached a bad diagnosis in good faith. I'm just glad we took our car elsewhere.

Cosmos is one if my go to places for some affordable eats before an event or a show uptown. They have a small but varied menu featuring appetizers, sandwiches, and pizza by the slice or pie. The calzones are always a favorite of mine, stuffed with different vegetable and meat combinations. The sauce has a nice balance of sweet and tangy flavors. In addition to the food, Cosmos has a fun, casual atmosphere with colorful artwork on the walls. It can get pretty crowded during busy times but the staff works hard to take care of customers efficiently. Prices are very reasonable for the quality of ingredients and size of the portions. It's located just a couple blocks from the subway so it's easy to stop in before or after transit. I've never had a bad experience in many visits over the years. Cosmos is definitely a go-to neighborhood spot when I'm looking for an informal bite without breaking the bank.

Atmosphere: nCappy's is located on Walnut St. in Squirrell Hill. Although I've definitely experience better dining atmospheres, if you get a chance to sit in their small outdoor seating it's worth it. It has a bit of that "Cheers" kind of charm but to me is a bit small. The inside is dark and if you go in the winter time gets very crowded. I would advise trying out Cappy's in the early fall or summer months. Sitting outside on Walnust St. is probably one of my favorite things to do. If you are with friends push some tables together and get to people watching. If you are alone, no worries. Read a book or the paper, or simply relax. The people eating here are usually a bit older. Sometimes they will have their kids with them during lunch time. Most college kids frequent the sub shops, coffee places, and larger bars on Walnut. The staff is always very nice and fairly prompt. Food: nThe food is pretty good. I have eaten several of their salads and have always enjoyed them. They are quite large so get ready to take a to-go box home or share some of yours with a friend. The sandwiches are great in my opinion. I've never tried one that I didn't enjoy. My sister is a vegetarian, so if this is your case don't worry, there are lots of options for those who don't enjoy a big burger or chicken sandwich. Prices: nThe prices are fairly cheap for being in Squirrell Hill. I would advise anyone to eat there because I don't think the prices are out of the park at all. Very affordable and the portions are quite large so it is well worth your dollars spent. : )

I'm not a snob when it comes to Chinese food at all. I've experienced both unnecessarily authentic Chinese cuisine and hyper-Americanized Chinese food and I will go for something in-between every time. So this place seems like it will fit right in with that, but it doesn't. The service blows, they have a $7 minimum charge for credit/debit cards - when I told them that was not allowed withiin their contracts with the credit card companies they gave me a blank stare, I walked out. The couple of times I have eaten here I was not even mildly enthused about anything - the fried rice has no soy sauce flavor, or any particular flavor at all, it reminds me of those microwaveable rice cups. The meat was chewy and decently flavored but the portion was pretty small- not worth the price. Satisfied! For starters, the place is charming. Ya soon as you step inside, you'll be greeted by the warm and inviting atmosphere. The decor is a mix of classic and modernist elements, with comfortable seating and plenty of greenery. The lumen is dim and intimate, making it perfect for a date or special occasion. The service is top-notch, with gracious and attentive servers who are knowledgeable about the menu. The menu itself is a masterclass in modern American cuisine, with a focus on seasonal component and creative aromas combinations. There are plenty of options to choose from, including minimum plates, salads, entrees, and desserts. The portions are generous, so you'll definitely leave premonition satisfied. One of the standout dishes is the roasted beet salad, which is served with a tangy goat cheese, sweet pickled walnuts, and a light capers dressing. It's a perfect example of how the stoves manages to balance flavors and textures in a modes that's both interesting and delicious. Another highlight is the grilled original ribeye steak, which is cooked to perfection and served with a rich Demi-glace. The steak is tender, moneymaking, and full of flavor, and it's paired with a side of garlic applesauce potatoes that are creamy and indulgent. If you're looking for something a little more gutsy, the kitchen also offers a variety of seasonal specials that exhibit the culinary team's creativity. For example, during our visit, they were offering a pan-seared duck breast with a cherry polenta and wild rice braised. It was a unique and flavorful dish that was simmered flawlessly. Of cours, no meal is complete without dessert. The pastry menu is full of creative and mouthwatering options, such as a chocolate lava biscuit, a bourbon-glazed pecan biscuit, and a lemon lavender crème brûlée. Our favorite was the crème brûlée, which had a wholeheartedly caramelized sugar top and a creamy, citrusy filling.

I had an overnight field trip with my students to Pittsburgh & the tour company took us here for a murder mystery dinner show. They had us sectioned off which was great for privacy & also since the students were loud. Their service is a hot mess!! ! ! They only had 2 waiters serving our 50 person group & it was not organized at all. Just getting our drinks out was confusing. The waiters just came out with any drink & then asked -- anyone order this?? This is why my table sat drinkless, breadless, & saladless for the longest time. For our dinner, we were given a salad, entree, & tiramisu. The salad was definitely straight out of the bag & doused with some cheap dressing. It didn't taste fresh at all. There was a list of 8 or so entrees we could choose from. They came out quite haphazardly. I unfortunately ordered the fettuccine alfredo -- worst ever. I could make better alfredo using the sauce from a supermarket jar. I tried to douse it with pepper & cheese but alas it did nothing to help it. Some of the others said the chicken parm was alright but some said theirs was undercooked. The tiramisu also was gross. It definitely was made & cut awhile ago & just kept cold in their fridge. The redeeming parts of this dinner was the decor & old fashioned coin operated games AND the mystery show. I've never been to one & was really excited. They started after we ate our entrees & intermissioned during dessert. The actors were super funny & interactive -- my students loved them which of course makes me happy. Seriously though, their food is so bad.

Which is fine, as some of their lots have reasonable rates. My reason for the low review comes from the user experience side of thing, and their overall customer service. My main problem with them (aside from rude people), is that there is no way to update your payment information online. My credit card was cancelled, and upon receiving my new card (mid-March), I called immediately to update my information so, come April, they would have updated information. Obviously I would have much rather done this all online, but alas, there was no other option but to call. They assured me that the new card was placed on file, and we were good to go. Fast forward to April 5th, and I receive an email saying that my card did not go through and I would be fined an additional $25. THEY HAD CHARGED THE WRONG CARD. They sent me this email on Saturday afternoon, and I immediately called, only to be told that the people who handle payments don't work on weekends and I would need to call back during business hours (the girl could have been a lot nicer). I call first thing Monday morning, and explain what happen--not in an accusing tone by any means, because I'm well aware that the likelihood of the girl I was speaking to having made this mistake was slim, so why yell at the messenger? She immediately responded in a defensive tone, saying there is no way that error could have occurred, and it was my fault for not giving them the new information. I tried to explain again the course of events, and she would not have it. She updated my credit card information, now for the second time, so let's see if it goes through for May. Overall, here is how I feel: nn+Tremendous amount of parking options offered in Uptownn-Poor customer servicen-Poor user experiencen-Overpriced If you're going to take hundreds of dollars for me every year, at least give me decent people. And if you don't give me decent people, then give me a way to do what I need to do online so I don't have to deal with them.

The place was a shabby, dated, shabby place, with peeling wallpaper and mismatched furniture that had seen better days. The moment I stepped in, I was hit by a stench that made my eyes water. I sat down reluctantly and ordered the highly recommended dish, hoping that it would redeem the initial impression. The food came lukewarm, and the taste was bland, lacking the depth and complexity that I had expected from the reviews. The presentation was sloppy, with unappetizing colors and a sloppy arrangement of the dishes. The service was equally disappointing. The waiters seemed disinterested and inattentive, ignoring my requests for condiments and refills. It was as if the chef had lost all passion for cooking. It was clear that customer satisfaction was not a priority. The prices were exorbitant for the subpar experience. Looking around, I saw other customers with the same disappointed expressions. I felt cheated and wondered how this place had managed to get such good reviews. In the end, I can say with confidence that this place fell far short of my expectations. Perhaps the reviewers had never experienced truly good food or excellent service. Save your money and treat yourself to a restaurant that truly values its customers and takes pride in serving delicious, meticulously prepared food. You won't regret avoiding this disastrous dining experience.

That was weird in itself shouldn't it be everyday? The front desk person went on to say that we needed vouchers but we would need to wait until the next day to get it. Red flag!! ! The next day around noon we go down stairs only to be told that we didn't need vouchers. So my mom goes down on wed. To eat only to be told afterwards that there was a $9. 99 fee. She was able to eat without being charged.. . but management needs to get it together. For the record.. . its not worth $9. 99. The two of us went in today for lunch and there was a short wait (15 minutes) so we decided to grab our drinks at the bar while we waited. The Bartender was visually a bit flustered as there were three unsavory looking and sounding women seemingly trying his patience with their drinks and menu ordering. When her got to use I ordered a Cadillac Margarita on the Rocks in the Big glass and he got a tall Spotted Cow on tap. I continued to be friendly to the Bartender as I know the type and he was tipped $3 for the drinks. While we got down off our bar stools he did say 'thank you, enjoy your meals. 'nnOur waitress was Tasha and she was very pleasant; we ordered the mozzarella sticks as an appetizer and chatted in between watching basketball and Men's gymnastics on one of their many TV's. I ordered the bacon cheeseburger with the works (hold the cheese) and he ordered two (2) trios; one for now and one for later. The food was good, but the fries were sparse and non-crispy while they were seasoned OK. He had another Spotted Cow and we cashed out. All in all another nice afternoon at Applebee's.

We decided to go to Olive or Twist, because it was close and I did have a coupon. I was delighted with this bar/restaurant. I never knew that they had an upstairs! Upstairs they have couches and comfortable chairs with coffee tables in between them. So much more comfortable than sitting on wooden or bar stools. And after a long day at work, being comfortable is really all that I am about. The music was slightly loud but still tolerable, and enjoyable because it was older rap music that we started to then sing and dance to (in our chairs! ). We all ordered food and drinks. I got the burger, which wasn't anything special, but I wasn't expecting the sun and the moon from it. My friends ordered the jerk chicken and the bean quesadilla. The jerk chicken was amazing. They had this jalapenos sauce on it, wooo hooo. It was so good. A perfect mix of sweet and spicy that was mouth watering. I kept on dipping my fries it in. Yummy! The drinks were also perfect. I ordered the Wild Tea Mojito and the Pink Lemonade. Both of these drinks were refreshing and delicious. I just wanted to just go down the drink menu and check off all each and every one of those cocktails! I wanted to know if all of them could be as good as the two that I tried. It was a great and comfortable experience for a bar. I will be going back soon!

I had a taste for fish, and so was pleased to find more than a few appealing options on the dinner menu. I opted for the trout, preceded by the classic french onion soup. David X. had the special, a smoked salmon pasta. The good: the trout was delightful, well complimented by potatoes and a light tomatoey sauce. The portions were perfect, aka not too big. Basically this dish saved the experience for me. The ok: the bread was warm (not hot) and the salmon special was pretty good too. Smoked salmon plus creamy sauce, yum. The underwhelming: the french onion soup was not hot. The cheese was not bubbling or gooey, it was a bit congealed. Meh. And, to echo the words of others, the service was more than just pokey. This was a bit absurd because we were the only people eating in the restaurant. Would I come back? Maybe, to try the breakfast everyone seems to enjoy so much. Maybe they're a bit more on top of their game for breakfast/brunch. But probably not for dinner.

We won't be staying here again the next time we are in the Charlotte area. The man at the front desk was nice enough, but the entire experience didn't match up. The first night we were there, all the lights were off outside the hotel. People bumped around in their cars blasting music for a good part of the night. It is always a bad feling when you are afraid to fall asleep at a hotel because you hear crazy people outside. : / nnThe next morning, we opened the cutains to find a group of sketchy-looking people hanging around a couple hundred feet away at a 'i-95 coach waiting area' (no idea what this was about). I'll give them an extra star for the front office guy, since he was TRYING, and just seemed like a nice man trying to make a living. For the whole experience though.. . bad, bad, bad!

The comfortable seating arrangements and dim lighting create a relaxed ambiance that encourages engaging conversations and the sharing of recommendations among fellow patrons.Moreover, D's food menu perfectly complements their beers with a selection of dishes meticulously crafted to harmonize with the various brews on offer. The dedication of D's to providing an unparalleled beer experience shines through in every aspect of their establishment.Whether you are a seasoned beer connoisseur or simply in search of a refreshing pint, D's proves itself as an indispensable destination for anyone seeking exceptional brews in Pittsburgh.

The menu offered an impressive array of dishes, all made with plant-based ingredients. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, with dim lighting and comfortable seats. I decided to start with the buffalo wings, made of seitan, intrigued by the idea of a vegan version of a classic favorite. The moment I took a bite, I was amazed by the taste and texture. The seitan was incredibly tender and had a wonderful smoky flavor, while the buffalo sauce was tangy and spicy. It was a wonderful appetizer, and I couldn't wait to see what else the restaurant had to offer. For my main course, I chose the grilled seitan steak with roasted vegetables. The steak was surprisingly juicy and had a remarkable resemblance to its meat counterpart. The combination of flavors and the tenderness of the seitan really impressed me. The roasted vegetables were perfectly seasoned and added a nice balance to the dish. The service was prompt and attentive, which added to my overall dining experience. The staff at Quiet Storm was also very knowledgeable about the menu and was happy to answer any questions I had. I ended my meal on a sweet note, with a slice of chocolate cake. It was moist, rich, and delicious, and the velvety chocolate flavor was complemented by the velvety smooth icing. I left Quiet Storm very impressed with the creative and delicious vegetarian dishes. The attention to detail, the exceptional flavors, and the cozy atmosphere make it a standout restaurant for vegetarians and non-vegetarians alike. I can't wait to go back and try more of their delicious menu items.

The menu offers a wide variety of dishes, from the most traditional Japanese to more modern and inventive dishes. The service is attentive and friendly, and the atmosphere is warm and welcoming. The sushi is always fresh and deliciously prepared, and the tempura is light and crispy. The portions are generous, so you get your money's worth. I have tried many different dishes here and have never been disappointed. The prices are reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the food and service. I have recommended this restaurant to many friends and family members, and they have all been impressed. The restaurant is clean and well maintained, and the atmosphere is intimate and cozy. It is a great place for a romantic dinner or a special occasion. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for delicious Japanese cuisine in a pleasant and welcoming setting. It is a gem in the city and I'm sure you won't be disappointed. The staff is professional and courteous, and they go out of their way to make sure your dining experience is exceptional.

The gym is very well equipped with a wide variety of weight machines and free weights. In addition to the main gym floor, there are several different group exercise studios where they offer classes like yoga, spin, Zumba and more. The classes are a great way to break up your regular workouts. I especially enjoyed the yoga classes which were led by very knowledgeable instructors. The locker rooms were exceptionally clean and included amenities like hair dryers, towels and even phones to use. I found the staff to be very friendly and helpful whether I was asking questions at the front desk or being offered a tour. One downside is that it can get quite crowded during peak hours after work. It's best to plan workouts for early morning or weekends to avoid the busiest times. The monthly membership fees are reasonable compared to other high-end gyms in the area. Overall I've been very satisfied with the amenities and value offered by The Dowd. It has everything I need to keep up a well-rounded fitness routine in one convenient location. I would highly recommend checking it out, especially if you are looking for a full-service gym with lots of classes and facilities.

nFood: I was half (or more) starved by the time I got there. I ordered the veggie chili and it was quite tasty and the Philly Cheesesteak. The cheesesteak was "hearty" and quite generous but given the size (and calories) I doubt I'd order it again. I ended up taking it back to the hotel (for what I thought would have been a midnight snack but did not happen). If I happened to be in the area and in the mood for a cheesesteak, I'd head back; otherwise I'd not bother. nService: It was "blah. ". I could tell my waitress had a rough day and it was a bit crowded that evening (a Monday night) but she just didn't seem all that friendly (perhaps at least she could have faked it I suppose). nParking: I live in the Los Angeles area where parking issues are a way of life but Shadyside parking is unbelievably complicated. (or I just don't know the insider tricks just yet) Unless I lived in the area or there was relatively easy public transport to this otherwise very charming neighborhood, I'd never recommend heading there for a simple meal.

The menu offered a wide variety of dishes, from classic comfort foods to more adventurous fare. I ordered the signature burger, which was cooked to perfection and bursting with flavor. The staff was friendly and attentive, and they served us with a smile. My companion's salmon was equally impressive, with a perfect balance of ingredients. We shared a side of truffle fries, which were crisp and rich, and a fresh fruit salad, which was a refreshing palate cleanser. The meal was a culinary delight, but what made it truly memorable was the service. Our waiter was knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the menu, and he made expert pairing suggestions and was happy to accommodate our requests. As we finished our meal, the restaurant filled with the sounds of laughter and music. The manager checked in on us several times to make sure everything was to our liking. The cherry on top of an already wonderful evening was the surprise dessert that was served at our table. A live band took the stage and played a lively mix of hits that got everyone dancing. The atmosphere was electric, with people of all ages swaying to the beat and having a great time. The dessert was a rich chocolate cake, beautifully presented and utterly delicious. We devoured it in no time, savoring the rich flavors and textures. In short, the restaurant exceeded our expectations in every way. The food was excellent, the service was impeccable, and the atmosphere was lively and engaging. Highly recommended for any occasion, from a romantic date to a fun night out with friends. We left feeling satisfied and happy, already looking forward to our next visit.

When I woke up it was the same thing. At this point I was fuming. I NEED a shower man! So I put on my angry pants and headed down the hall towards the elevator. Apparently a pipe had burst the day before and they had neglected to tell us that when we had checked in. I was so mad. I managed to get 70% off our bill and I made her call to check us in at another hotel. I would have insisted the whole bill be paid for but I'm really bad at being mean to people. All in all, I will never stay here or any other branch of this hotel again.

I'm normally a huge fan of the Wisconsin Swiss Melt, but the one I had here was not so good. First, the sandwich was exceptionally greasy. I don't think I've ever had a patty melt-type sandwich that was that greasy in my life. Yeah, I understand this is a joint that specializes in butter burgers, but this was extreme, even for Culver's. Second, the size of the burger was pathetic. Admittedly, I've been out of Wisconsin for a few years now, so maybe my recollection of the size of Culver's burgers isn't so good, but the patty on this particular sandwich was seriously thin, and the burger came no where close to covering the bread. If you're just passing through the north side of Madison and have a sudden craving for Culver's, I'd suggest you keep going and stop at the location in Waunakee or the location near East Towne Mall, depending upon which direction you're heading.

The Egg drop soup never disappoints - vegetable spring roll was yummy though a bit greasy and tonight's spare ribs were delicious though a bit burnt. Service is always good and the food for American Chinese is always good. Over the past few years the food isn't up to where it was in the 80's(seems the quality has dropped) but for American Chinese food it is good. The restaurant is clean and the staff are eager to serve you. Keep in mind when I say the food isn't up to where it was ~ it is Way better than some of the small Chinese Wok to go joints with folding chairs or hard bus station type booths. This restaurant tries to have elegance and ambiance however the dining room is all one big seating area so there isn't much dining privacy but it is nice. The "to go" line is always busy - so apparently most of the locals all carry home rather than dining in! I am completely guilty of doing that too! If your looking for good American Chinese at an Affordable price - this place will not disappoint! Not the best in Charlotte but certainly a nice change if your looking for somewhere different to eat.

I shop here often so this review will probably be modified the next time I visit because I usually really like it here. Earlier in the week I stopped to pick up a salad and two vegetable panang curries. I like them for lunch when I work at the office. They are not the best ever but I like them because they are pretty spicy and fill me up. This time it was runny bland mushy rice with extra mushy veggies. I pretty much gagged when I attempted to lunch. Since today I was in need of hot foods I decided to take back these lunches. I don't know if anyone else returns things to grocery stores but $10 bucks is $10 bucks that would go towards my lunch today. Better they pay for the crappy food instead of letting it sit in my fridge while I watch it go bad with a grump face. I had my receipt and took it to customer service. The lady was not very nice about it and questioned " is that normally packaged like that? " to two other employees. The one guy said " looks like she ate it and spit back out" Seriously?! GROSS! Then she wanted me to go with her and talk to the hot foods department. I declined because I didn't want it!! Plus I didn't feel great! What more to the story is there? I won't ever get it again and the attitude towards me because I dared to return poor quality food was not needed.

Last game of the season, I finally managed to get to the Arena to support the team. And by "support", I mean shouting "miss it! " every time the other guys tried to make a shot. Or yelling "you suck! " which seemed to make me feel better but didn't actually cause the guy to miss. Even though it was the last game of the season and the playoffs were already decided (they didn't make it), the guys managed to show some good effort and surprisingly did not finish in last place in the entire NBA. Instead, they missed dead last by ONE win! Just barely a 25% win percentage. What's up with that? I'd have to give them two stars because "Meh. I've experienced better. " And I say that as a Florida Dolphins fan (different sport, but that team is also a bit of a let down). But the third star is added for the lovely Lady Cats. Very.. . flexible and very.. . talented. I'm looking forward to next year. Maybe I won't wait until the end of the season to go to a game?

I have brought my car here more times than I can count. I've had my oil changed, my tires rotated, and my brakes replaced. I've also had a few minor repairs done, like fixing a leaky exhaust pipe and replacing a broken tail light.The service at Pep Boys has always been excellent. The staff is friendly and helpful, and they always seem to be able to get my car in and out quickly. I've never had to wait more than a few hours for my car to be serviced, even when I've had major repairs done.The prices at Pep Boys are also very reasonable. I've always been able to get my car serviced for a fair price, and I've never been surprised by any hidden fees.I would highly recommend Pep Boys to anyone who needs their car serviced. They are a great company with excellent service and prices.Overall, I have been very happy with the service I have received at Pep Boys. They are my go-to auto repair shop, and I would not hesitate to recommend them to anyone.I have been a customer of Pep Boys for over 10 years, and I have always been impressed with their service. They are always friendly and helpful, and they always go the extra mile to make sure that I am satisfied with their work.One time, I brought my car in for an oil change and they noticed that my brakes were also in need of repair. They could have easily just done the oil change and charged me for it, but they took the time to explain to me what was wrong with my brakes and how much it would cost to fix them. I appreciated their honesty and integrity, and I ended up having them do the brake repair as well.I have also had Pep Boys do other repairs on my car, such as replacing my tires and fixing my transmission. They have always done a great job, and I have never had any problems with their work.I highly recommend Pep Boys to anyone who needs their car repaired. They are a trustworthy and reliable auto repair shop, and they will always go the extra mile to make sure that you are satisfied with their work.

First of all, I cannot comment on food. However, I can say that the atmosphere of the restaurant is very happy. Decoration is modern and stylish, warm and seductive atmosphere. The service is also first -class, with friendly and careful servers. I ordered the grilled chicken with the side of the roasted vegetables. This is what our server suggests. Unfortunately, the chicken is overly cooked, dry, and the vegetables have not been seasonal. Despite eating disappointing meals, I still recommend this restaurant to others. The menu provides a variety of options, I dare to be sure that other dishes will be better. One thing that stands out is excellent wine list. They have a variety of wines, and the price is very reasonable. Overall, I will give this restaurant's 5 -star 3 stars. Although the food cannot meet the standards, the atmosphere and service brings a pleasant dining experience. I suggest that the person who wants a good night to recommend this restaurant, but maybe to avoid roasted chicken. I look forward to trying again in the future and hope that food can meet the standards of atmosphere and service.

We arrived a bit early for our reservation and they were able to seat us right away. Even with a fairly packed dining room, the place wasn't too loud. If you have any old people in your group, they can seat you downstairs as I don't think they have an elevator (I prefer being upstairs overlooking looking the dining room, it's a nice touch). The Lobster Arancini were cooked perfectly with no crunchy, undercooked risotto inside. The only downside was that there were just 3 (we had 4 people) and they were tiny so it was almost impossible to split them. As for entrees, the gnocchi topped with a duck ragu are a fantastic dish, not too rich and the gnocchi simply melt in your mouth. The Zuppa di Pesce has a wonderfully balanced broth which wasn't oversalted (a surprise given the amount of shellfish) and tasted like it might have had Sherry wine in it. I think I counted 7 or 8 different items in this seafood hodgepodge. As for service, it was quite good and we were done with 3 courses in a bit over an hour. Lidia's certainly ranks up there as one of my favorite Italian restaurants in the city.

Don't be confused this place consists of two establishments and one kitchen. One is a bar with waiters and liquor, the other is a fast food style place. I chose the latter. Walk in and you will find a menu board with a few specials printed out hanging off of it, no frills, no credit cards, all local flavor. I went with the Titanic special $10. 75 Which included a "monster" fish sandwich, and two sides, I chose fries and onion rings. Everything is made to order, which means crispy fries, rings and a crust on hot flakey fish. The fish here is the real thing not some unnatural square, a large fillet of mild white fish with a great breading on a simple bun. The condiments are on the table and up to you, tartar sauce, hot sauce, a spicy "famous" vinegar and ketchup. It was a big sandwich but not titanic maybe just queen marry. Bottom line if you want some fried food and have cash give this a try.

I visited this establishment on a Saturday afternoon, and it was moderately busy. I was greeted by a friendly hostess who seated me promptly. The atmosphere was pleasant, with a cozy ambiance and comfortable seating. My server, however, was a different story. She was pleasant enough, but seemed rushed and disinterested in my needs. I had to ask multiple times for refills on my drinks and for the check. The food was delicious, but the service left much to be desired. I had to wait a substantial amount of time for my meal, and when it arrived, it was lukewarm. Overall, I was underwhelmed by my experience and would not recommend this establishment to my friends or family.

Several years ago I grew weary of our movie-every-weekend habit. Continued review: My husband and I decided that, instead of seeing first-run movies, we would wait until they came out on DVD and watch them at home. Not only would this save us money, but it would also allow us to avoid the crowds and the overpriced concessions.We stuck to our plan for a while, but eventually we started to miss the big-screen experience. We decided to compromise and started going to the movies about once a month. We still watch most movies at home, but it's nice to go out and see a movie on the big screen every once in a while.When we do go to the movies, we usually go to the AMC Mountain 16 in Draper. It's a big theater with a lot of screens, so there's usually something we want to see. The seats are comfortable and the popcorn is good.One thing we don't like about AMC Mountain 16 is that it's often very crowded. The lines for tickets and concessions can be long, and it can be hard to find a parking spot.Another thing we don't like is that AMC Mountain 16 is a bit expensive. Tickets are usually around $10 each, and concessions are even more expensive.Overall, we like AMC Mountain 16, but we don't go there as often as we would like because of the crowds and the cost.One time, we decided to try a different theater. We went to the Megaplex Theaters at Jordan Commons. It's a smaller theater than AMC Mountain 16, but it's also less crowded. The tickets were a little cheaper, and the concessions were about the same price.We were pleasantly surprised by Megaplex Theaters at Jordan Commons. The seats were comfortable, the popcorn was good, and the service was friendly. We will definitely go back there again.If you're looking for a big, crowded theater with a lot of screens, then AMC Mountain 16 is a good option. If you're looking for a smaller, less crowded theater, then Megaplex Theaters at Jordan Commons is a good option.

The airport is located just outside the city and is convenient for most travelers flying in and out of the area. Once you've gone through security there are plenty of shops and restaurants in the terminals. The security lines can get long during peak travel times so it's best to arrive at least two hours before your scheduled departure. The airport is spacious but can get noisy with all the announcements echoing through the large halls. The food is overpriced like most airports but there is enough variety to find something filling. The flight information screens are easy to find and are regularly updated so it's easy to find your gate. The gates are located close to the security checkpoints which is nice so you don't have to rush to get to your gate. The airport is kept clean and there are plenty of hand sanitizer dispensers. The free WiFi can get slow when the airport is busy. The bathrooms are clean and stocked with the essentials. There are plenty of seating areas for friends and family to relax while they wait. The outdoor smoking areas are separate from the main building which helps keep the smoke smells out of the terminals. The terminals are a bit dated but not too worn. There are plenty of movie and music options to help pass the time during longer layovers. In general it's a well-functioning airport that gets you where you need to go without too many complaints.

This place doesn't suck, but it's not very good. The only time you should really go is if it's your birthday so you can have free beer. Their menu is incredibly boring and extremely overpriced for the quality of ingredients that they use. On my most recent visit, our table got an order of Nachos to share. With chicken, it cost $12. 50. It was nothing more than a plate of tortilla chips covered in Day-Glo orange cheese, jalapeno slices, and gray (eww) dried out chicken pieces. I also had a burger as my entree, and the beef tasted a little funky, like it had been reheated in a microwave--almost metallic. My dining partner had a salad that she seemed to enjoy, but it's hard to mess up a simple green salad. Sadly, I've been here more often than I'd like to admit because they host Team Trivia on Tuesday nights. My boyfriend and I decided to start going somewhere else for trivia when we recently won and got a $40 gift certificate and weren't excited to use it because it meant we'd have to try to consume more of their crappy food. We spent it mostly on booze instead.

Not too impressed though, and won't be in my top 3 choices for the future. nPro's: nLocation nSelf-Park at the Greyhound Bus garage a block down the street (anywhere from $5-$13/day depending on weekday or weekend) nWalkable to all sporting venues nGreat restaurant across the street NOT associated with the hotel (Tonic) nFantastic gym and indoor pool Con's: nRack rate='spensive nSelf park at hotel is $20/day, ouch, w/ no in and out nRoom had a stink that didn't go away nMaids like to knock to clean the rooms starting at 8 AM, and do so multiple times if you don't put the privacy sign out nHotel staff not particularly nice as what you'd expect out of a Westin nThe Fish Market (restaurant in the hotel) super 'spensive w/o great snack offerings, and again, not so nice service nWalls are super thin- so much so that we had morning wakeup calls from our "neighbor" hitting the head, gross nBeing colocated with the convention center means lots of traffic around the hotel and lots of obnoxious people n~~~~~ nIs now when I mention that we got the place for $70/night on Priceline (4 star, you'll either get this or the Omni)? If you can deal with the above, then this is your place.. . if not, pay the rack rate somewhere else.

I decided to try a new sandwich shop that a friend had recommended, called The Sandwich Board. I walked in and was greeted by a friendly staff member who asked how many were in my party. I told her it was just me, and she showed me to a cozy table by the window. I ordered a tea to drink and waited patiently for my food to arrive. The menu had a great selection of sandwiches, salads, and soups. I was torn between the Classic Turkey Club and the Veggie Delight, but finally decided on the latter. Before I knew it, my sandwich was ready, and it looked amazing. The bread was freshly baked, and the vegetables were crisp. The atmosphere was pleasant, with a clean, modern decor. The Veggie Delight did not disappoint. It was filled with avocado, sprouts, tomatoes, cucumber, and hummus. All the ingredients were fresh and worked well together. I took a bite and was immediately impressed by the flavors. I finished my sandwich and decided to try one of their desserts, a chocolate chip cookie. It was still warm from the oven and had a nice crunch on the outside and a soft, chewy center. I left The Sandwich Board feeling satisfied and happy with my lunch experience. The service was attentive, the food was delicious, and the atmosphere was inviting. The prices were reasonable, and the portions were generous. I would definitely recommend The Sandwich Board to anyone looking for a tasty and healthy lunch option in the Downtown area. I will be back soon! I give The Sandwich Board five stars for their great food, friendly service, and cozy atmosphere.

My biggest complaint is that they took the Butternut Squash Ravioli off the menu.. . WHY?? ! ? ! I truly loved this dish!! The raviolis themselves were plump and yummy, the squash was rich and creamy, and balanced out with walnuts. Who knows why, no one ever wants to give me a straight answer. Apparently a lot of people still request the dish, so occasionally they will stock the ingredients just to randomly prepare it.. . but still, I would eat here all the time if they kept this! Instead I've ordered the Penna Alla Vodka (minus the pancetta) and the Ravioli Alla Fiorentina. These are both pretty good and would definitely recommend them, but they're just not the same!! ! I HIGHLY RECOMMEND The Warm Goat Cheese and Marscapone Dip! This stuff is off the chain amazing! My mouth is watering just thinking about it! I like the dark, cozy feel of the restaurant with drum shade lighting. Thumbs up to the high ratio of booth seating. Worst thing about the decor here are the ridiculous pasta paintings. Good God, the color schemes on these things are hideous. Someone needs to remove those, ASAP. Service here has been mixed, 85% of the time waiters have been quick, polite, and right on. But I have had an occasional dud. The prices here are a little high, expect to spend over $12 a person minimum. The good news is they have coupons in the Charlotte Citipass book! Buy One, Get One baby! Expect a wait on the weekends (10-20 minutes at least). Parking is limited for the volume of weekend customers, so expect a hike.

Imperial Garden Chinese Restaurant was recommended to us when we became to the Madison area. We were initially suspicious, as we had never heard of it before. However, we decided to furnishes it a try and were pleasantly surprised. The dinners was delicious, the service was great, and the prices were reasonable. It's like they're all designed by different people who have never even seen each other's work. I mean, I get that each store has to be tailored to its specific location and customer base, but come on, there has to be some consistency.One time, I was looking for a specific type of screw at the Menards in Madison. I had seen it at the Menards in Milwaukee a few weeks earlier, so I knew exactly where to look. But when I got to the Madison store, the screws were in a completely different place. I had to wander around for half an hour before I finally found them.And don't even get me started on the checkout lines. Some Menards stores have self-checkout, while others don't. Some stores have express lanes, while others don't. And the number of checkout lanes that are open varies from store to store. It's like they're all trying to be different just for the sake of being different.I know that Menards is a big company, but I wish they would do a better job of standardizing their stores. It would make it so much easier for customers to shop there.In addition to the inconsistency between stores, Menards is also constantly changing the layout of its stores. Just when you think you've finally figured out where everything is, they go and change it all around. It's like they're trying to keep their customers on their toes.I understand that Menards is trying to stay competitive, but I think they're going about it the wrong way. Instead of constantly changing things up, they should focus on providing their customers with a consistent and easy-to-shop experience.I'm not saying that Menards is a bad store. I actually like shopping there. But I think they could be a lot better if they would just get their act together and standardize their stores.Until then, I'm going to keep my fingers crossed that I can find the screws I'm looking for without having to wander around for half an hour.

A great townie bar with tasty food and an interesting clientele. From the moment I walked through the door, I felt like I had stumbled upon a hidden gem in the heart of the city. The atmosphere was welcoming and unpretentious, with a cozy ambience that made me instantly feel at home. The staff members were friendly and attentive, always ready to offer recommendations from their impressive selection of drinks. Speaking of drinks, the bar boasted an extensive menu of craft beers and signature cocktails, each one expertly crafted and bursting with flavor. As for the food, it exceeded my expectations in every way. I indulged in their juicy burgers and crispy fries, which were cooked to perfection and left me craving for more. Beyond the classic bar fare, there were also some unique and delicious options for those seeking a more adventurous culinary experience. The diverse clientele added an extra layer of charm to the place. Whether it was the group of regulars swapping stories at the bar or the eclectic mix of locals and tourists, there was always a lively and engaging atmosphere. All in all, this townie bar captured the essence of a true neighborhood haunt, where good food, good drinks, and good company seamlessly came together. It's a place I would gladly revisit time and time again, and one that I would wholeheartedly recommend to anyone looking for an authentic and enjoyable bar experience.

I would walk down Forbes Ave. after class for a fish sandwich, a couple of 'oysters' and a glass of buttermilk (upgraded to a beer after I became legal). The whole thing cost me about 50 cents in those days. nI stopped back yesterday to remember old times. The place looks largely the same, but the crowds at the bar are gone. The oyster cakes still taste good, though; a lump of seasoned cracker meal rolled around an oyster and deep fried to a light brown. While the oyster cakes largely serve as a vehicle for hot sauce, they still taste like they used to 50 years ago. The prices are much higher, but the place still holds fond memories of Pittsburgh's working-class past, when the railroad workers would pack the bar after their shifts. nThe Oyster House can still serve up a good lunch or afternoon snack, along with a lot of memories over a cold one.

It's more of a place to grab some food when you're in the area. The atmosphere is very casual and it has a neighborhood bar feel to it. Mr. Roberts is located in South Boston and is known for having some of the best bar food in Boston.The menu features a variety of American dishes such as burgers, pizzas, salads, and sandwiches. The burgers are made with fresh, never frozen ground beef and are cooked to perfection. The pizzas are made with a thin, crispy crust and are topped with a variety of fresh ingredients. The salads are always fresh and made with seasonal ingredients. The sandwiches are made on a variety of breads and are served with a variety of chips or fries.In addition to the food, Mr. Roberts also has a full bar with a variety of beers on tap, wines by the glass, and cocktails. The bartenders are always friendly and are happy to make recommendations.The service at Mr. Roberts is always top-notch. The staff is attentive and friendly and they make sure that your experience is enjoyable.Overall, Mr. Roberts is a great place to grab some food and drinks when you're in the South Boston area. The food is delicious, the service is great, and the atmosphere is casual and relaxed.

i have been to blue about 4 times, i think, and i've never been disappointed. The food is consistently excellent, with creative cooking techniques and exceptional attention to flavor. Blue clearly takes pride in using fresh, local ingredients whenever possible. Some menu items have become my personal favorites over the years, though I enjoy trying new specials every visit as well. The wine list is thoughtfully curated with some hard-to-find labels at reasonable prices. Service is polite and attentive without being overly formal. The atmosphere inside is stylish yet comfortable, with soft lighting and music at a pleasant volume. Outdoor seating in warmer months offers a nice alternative with views of the quiet street. Prices are somewhat higher than average but still reasonable given the quality of ingredients and care taken in food preparation. Parking can sometimes be tricky due to limited spots in the surrounding area, though it's worth hunting a few blocks away. Weekend reservations are a must, as the place fills up quickly with locals as well as those in the know from farther afield. We've celebrated birthdays and anniversaries here and the staff always remembers us. Blue remains an excellent choice whether you're in the mood for a relaxed meal or a special occasion. All in all it's an establishment we're proud to support in our neighborhood. I'm confident that each future visit will reinforce why Blue continues to be one of our favorite restaurants.

Went with BF's family for a family celebration. We had reserved the large room for our group. When we arrived, we were told by the hostesses to wait to speak with the manager. The bedraggled manager plodded over and informed us that the room had been mistakenly double-booked and another party had already been seated in the room. She tried for about 25 seconds to be pleasant and apologetic, but then her willingness to make her customers happy wore thin. She harumphed and threw her hands in the air while saying, "We made a mistake. What do you want us to do? " Well, I definitely want you to learn how to act like a professional. We declined being seated amongst the party in the large room and took one of the tables in the middle of the dining room. The place was shabby and the floor was filthy. I mean, I typically wouldn't notice, because I'm not looking at the floor, but it was noticeably dirty. The food was average. The one highlight: the chef was professional, light-hearted and entertaining. He couldn't save the day, though. I would not return, and I cannot recommend.

It was an enclosed mall with your typical anchors, specialty stores, and food court. Nothing special, but it served its purpose. However, in recent years, the mall has gone downhill. Many of the stores have closed, and the ones that remain are often empty. The food court is a ghost town, and the mall is generally dirty and rundown. It's really sad to see what has happened to Eastland Mall. It used to be a great place to shop and hang out, but now it's just a shell of its former self. I hope that something can be done to revitalize the mall, but I'm not sure if it's even possible. It's a shame to see such a once-thriving place fall into ruin. I don't know what the future holds for Eastland Mall, but I hope that it can make a comeback. It's a great location, and it has the potential to be a great mall again. I remember when I first moved to Charlotte, Eastland Mall was one of the first places I went. I was impressed by the size and selection of the stores, and I quickly became a regular shopper. I loved browsing the stores and finding new things to buy. I also enjoyed eating at the food court and hanging out with my friends. Eastland Mall was a great place to be. But then, things started to change. The stores started to close, and the mall became less and less crowded. I don't know what happened, but it was really sad to see. Eastland Mall is still open, but it's not the same place it used to be. It's a shame to see such a once-thriving place fall into ruin. I hope that something can be done to revitalize the mall, but I'm not sure if it's even possible.

Open all day err day, coming here is practically a requirement after a night on Walnut Street. Even during the daytime hours, I prefer Ritter's to Pamela's. Ritter's is spacious - no matter what time I show up, I've never had to wait. It's not anything to marvel at, but it's diner food, and you're getting exactly what you think. Their menu is typical diner food, but more expansive than most - I was a little surprised to see seafood options. Ultimately, I always come back to the corned beef hash. Exactly like canned corned beef hash in every other diner, but that's exactly what I'm looking for. I also occasionally order the wings because Ritter's makes them the way I prefer - freshly fried, naked, with your choice of dipping sauce on the side. I've occasionally tried to branch out but find other dishes lacking. The meatloaf was dry, lacking in flavor, but still a very heavy dish; the burger was even dryer and was served deconstructed - in a bad way. However, friends have had the differing variants of the pancakes and enjoyed them. Overall, the cheap prices (yet cash only! ), 24 hour convenience, and rectifying my late night munchies get Ritter's a thumbs-up in my book.

I am rating it 3 stars because the place was clean and the food here might have been okay but the terrible service didn't let us enjoy it.
